title: Grants Program Administration - BEAD Monitoring Plan Agent Pilot
task: Grants Program Administration - BEAD Monitoring Plan Agent Pilot
problem: The AI system—referred to as the BEAD Monitoring Agent—is designed to enhance the ability of Federal Program Officers (FPOs) to support Eligible Entities (EEs) in monitoring their subrecipients after a Final Proposal (FP) is approved. The motivation for deploying this AI is grounded in NTIA’s need to rapidly and effectively understand the contents of each EE’s FP to support post-award monitoring. Benefits: 1. Faster, More Thorough Review: The AI agent quickly reviews EE subgrantee monitoring plans by comparing them against a “gold standard,” helping FPOs identify best practices, inconsistencies, and gaps 2. Enhanced Risk Mitigation: By providing recommendations on oversight and potential mitigation actions, the AI helps identify areas where closer monitoring or NTIA support may be needed 3. Standardization and Transparency: The AI outputs enable more standardized and data-driven oversight across diverse plans, informing risk assessments and follow-up activities

title: Grants Program Administration - Tiered Environmental Assessment AI Pilot
task: Grants Program Administration - Tiered Environmental Assessment AI Pilot
problem: The NTIA Tiered EA AI Pilot leverages AI to streamline the initial drafting of the “Affected Environment” section in NTIA Tiered Environmental Assessment templates by integrating project-specific data and geospatial resources. The pilot aims to evaluate AI’s effectiveness in drafting content within the tiered EA; if successful, NTIA may expand the use case to provide eligible entities with pre-populated tiered EAs based on submitted information, rather than blank templates, to accelerate permitting. Benefits: 1. Efficiency: Automates a typically time-consuming, manual process, reducing turnaround time for drafting EAs. 2. Consistency and Standardization: By pre-populating sections with structured data and draft text, the AI helps ensure consistency across assessments and adherence to templates. 3. reported_benefits: 'Coherent X-rays are routinely provided today by the latest Synchrotron and X-ray Free-electron Laser Sources. When these diffract from a crystal containing defects, interference leads to the formation of a modulated diffraction pattern called ''speckle''. When the defects move around, they can be quantified by a correlation analysis technique called X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy. But the speckles also change when the beam moves on the sample. By scanning the beam in a controlled way, the overlap between the adjacent regions gives redundancy to the data, which allows a solution of the inherent phase problem. This is the basis of the coherent X-ray ptychography method which can achieve image resolutions of 10nm, but only if the probe positions are known. The goal of this proposal will be to separate ''genuine'' fluctuations of a material sample from the inherent beam fluctuations at the high data rates of XFELs. Algorithms will be developed to calculate the correlations between all the coherent diffraction patterns arriving in a time series, then used to separate the two sources of fluctuation using the criterion that the ''natural'' thermal fluctuations do not repeat, while beam ones do. We separate the data stream into image and beam ''modes'' automatically.'

title: MACO Project: Law Enforcement CAD Data Autocoder
task: MACO Project: Law Enforcement CAD Data Autocoder
problem: MACO is intended to solve the lack of standardization in Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) data across law enforcement agencies. CAD event descriptions are free-text, highly variable, and differ widely in terminology, structure, and coding practices. Because of this inconsistency, it is currently not possible to aggregate, compare, or analyze CAD data across jurisdictions at scale. MACO uses machine learning and language models to automatically classify raw CAD text into a standardized event taxonomy, enabling consistent analysis, cross-agency comparisons, and the development of national estimates of calls for service.
implementation: The system outputs a standardized event-type classification for each CAD record. For each raw text description, the model generates a predicted category from a predefined event taxonomy (e.g., “Property Crime: Theft,” “Traffic Incident,” “Disturbance,” etc.). The final deliverable is a CAD dataset with these standardized classifications appended to each record, enabling consistent analysis and aggregation across agencies.
reported_benefits: The AI provides standardized classifications of CAD event text, allowing BJS and partner agencies to analyze police activity consistently across jurisdictions. For BJS, this enables the production of scalable, comparable national estimates of calls for service—filling a major data gap not addressed by traditional crime measures. For state and local agencies, the standardized schema improves internal organization of CAD data and supports regional or state-level comparisons of police workload and community needs. For the research community and the public, MACO expands understanding of how law enforcement resources are used, the types of events agencies respond to, and broader patterns of community demand for police services. Overall, the tool enhances data quality, improves analytic capacity, and supports evidence-based decision-making across the criminal justice ecosystem.

task: Offense Text Auto-Coder (OTAC) - Automated offense coder from offense charge text strings used for the BJS National Pretrial Reporting Program

title: Sample Refinement: Frame API
problem: BLS establishment-based surveys, such as the Survey of Occupational Injuries and Illnesses (SOII), the National Compensation Survey (NCS), and the Occupational Requirements Survey (ORS), use the Longitudinal Database (LDB) as the frame for their survey samples. For each of these programs, there is a significant time-lag between when the sample is drawn for a program and when data collection begins. A critical and time-consuming part of data collection is sample refinement: checking the latest Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) and LDB data to adjust for any changes to the sampled establishment during that time-lag. problem: This AI solution impacts the process of investigating foodborne disease outbreaks. implementation: The Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) available within SEDRIC provides CDC epidemiologists the power to accelerate their investigations of multi-state foodborne disease outbreaks. It can extract structured data from grocery receipts, shopper card records, and free-text responses in order to catalog the food items purchased by affected patients. It can also map those items to SEDRIC-defined vehicles which categorize the items and highlight commonalities across patients, helping to pinpoint potential outbreak vehicles. AIP can summarize these results to provide insights from information pulled from shopper receipts. Given ingredients can be found in multiple food products, and some ingredients such as herbs like coriander/cilantro may go by multiple names or be reported in multiple languages, this summarization tool provides a faster way to gather summary information from receipts on different food items which may be part of a foodborne investigation.
reported_benefits: SEDRIC's AIP use case provides CDC epidemiologists the ability to accelerate their investigations of multi-state foodborne disease outbreaks by more effectively leveraging data available in a rich data source, such as receipts from grocery stores, that otherwise requires extensive time and human effort to parse through. In addition, this workflow would free up epidemiologists' time and, potentially, increase the frequency with which both CDC and STLT partners could utilize shopper card, receipts, and free text responses to support investigations. title: MERRAMax Automated feature selection
problem: There is growing interest in using Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)-class climate model outputs in ecological research. These models provide realistic, global representations of the climate system, projections for hundreds of variables (including Essential Climate Variables), and combine observations from an array of satellite, airborne, and in-situ sensors. Unfortunately, direct use of this important class of data has been limited due to the large size and complexity of model output collections, internal file complexity, and limited means for dynamically creating derived products of interest. To address these limitations, we have developed an AI-based stochastic convergence technology, called MERRA/Max, that combines HPC and Princeton's Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) software to rapidly subset and identify potential drivers of change among the hundreds of variables in a climate model output collection. MERRA/Max reduces dimensionality by iteratively drawing on MaxEnt's capacity for feature selection to winnow randomly selected climate variables until a stable set of predictors is found. Preliminary work focuses on the MERRA reanalysis, a product of NASA's GEOS-5 modeling framework. At 1 petabyte in size, MERRA comprises over 700 climate variables and spans 1970 to the present at high temporal resolution. We evaluated MERRA/Max by modeling the bioclimatic envelope of Cassin's Sparrow using MERRA and BioClim variables.

title: Remote Coordination, Actuation, and Planning (ReCAP) Cooperative MultiAgent Architecture
task: Remote Coordination, Actuation, and Planning (ReCAP) Cooperative MultiAgent Architecture
problem: ReCAP provides an architecture for lightweight, efficient coordination of highly-capable agents in a comms-limited environment. By providing agents with high-level, lightweight information about the capabilities of other agents in the fleet, ReCAP can facilitate allocation of tasks that are dynamically discovered and assigned via an auction. Auctions are conducted for particular tasks, and agents formulate bids based on encoded subject matter expertise predicting how a given action will affect their operations. For example, one agent may request that two others bid on a sampling task. The two agents bidding may possess different instruments for sampling, one of them able to sample remotely, but at low fidelity, the other able to sample at high fidelity but requiring a physical sample be collected. The auctioneer agent will consider its own mission goals and award the task to what it deems to be the highest bid. Onboard single agents, ReCAP provides a planning/scheduling module and a behavior tree for real-time control. The planning/scheduling module includes the actions of other connected agents, so that any agent may form a plan sequence involving actions from multiple agents – this is what triggers an auction. Finally, the actions that can be executed onboard are handled by a behavior tree, which is more reactive and requires less frequent reconfiguration than a static planner.
implementation: Through communications interfaces, ReCAP outputs (as well as receiving) state and auction information from other agents. The behavior tree additionally outputs control commands at a level tunable to the given use case; ReCAP has been implemented with direct vehicle control, commanding velocity and position changes, as well as at a much higher level, giving commands to an existing onboard controller.
reported_benefits: Compared to existing multi-agent control systems, ReCAP requires no training data, before or during operations, and does not require centralized control. It was conceived alongside a NASA push for extensible mission architectures, intended to provide technology that would allow missions to interoperate as new assets are added or encountered, and to enable on-demand coordination between otherwise separate missions. ReCAP enables this capability by basing coordination on high-level, lightweight communications, and its auctioning system prevents the need for interchange of complex state information between agents. ReCAP has been deployed to success in field, laboratory, and simulated use cases across terrestrial and space applications.

title: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) Neural Network (NN)
task: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) Neural Network (NN)
problem: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) is a NASA mission focused on exploring and finding exoplanets around nearby stars using the transiting method. TESS telescope covers a large field of view of 96 sq. deg in a single exposure. It has four cameras arranged vertically pointing from the ecliptic plane toward the poles.
implementation: This NN has an architecture that uses two 3D U-Nets stacked (W-Net) with skip connections that output a 3D segmentation mask with asteroid detections. We will introduce the NN model and present results from predictions using years 1 and 2 of TESS data. Additionally, we will show preliminary light curves extracted from new asteroids detected by our model.
reported_benefits: Thanks to this configuration and observing schedule, TESS is able to observe asteroids with a high duty cycle. Current techniques to search for asteroid signals on images rely on the shift-and-stack method, which relies on testing all possible combinations of direction and speed an object can move across the image to maximize the detection signal and find the asteroid’s track. This method is computationally expensive, and only attainable when the parameter space (direction-velocity) is constrained, usually to the main direction (e.g. orbits parallel to the ecliptic plane) and low speeds (main belt asteroids). This introduces a bias against fast-moving asteroids and high-inclination orbits (vertical tracks). To solve this, we implemented a rotationally invariant neural network (NN) model that performs semantic segmentation to find moving objects in TESS FFIs.We constructed a custom training set using 64x64x64 cubes of pixel flux time series and truth masks with the tracks of known asteroids from the JPL Horizon Ephemeris system. Our NN model can find known and new asteroids with all kinds of track orientations, showing no bias against objects moving at high inclination orbits, or fast-moving asteroids, or tracks with a change in direction. This NN model detects ~90% of known asteroids down to apparent visual magnitude 20th and has a detection limiting magnitude of ~20.5. This is on par with current implementations of the shift-and-stack method but without the bias introduced by limiting the range of track direction and velocity.

task: Revolutionizing Neutron Star Parameter Inference through Machine Learning

task: Data-Mining Similar Scenarios for Uncertainty Quantification of Solar Wind Predictions at L1
problem: Accurate Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) for space weather forecasts is an ever-important supplementary variable to enable accurate risk response. Modeling uncertainty is itself a “model of a model”, and one of the best datasets to describe a model’s performance is a past database of it’s predictions and after-the-fact observations. In this work, we develop a method based on k-NN and kernel regression to quantify uncertainty in the WSA solar wind model and it’s predictions of the solar wind speed at L1. By constructing state vectors that describe the current forecasting context— recent observations, recent predictions, and future predictions, we build a catalog of “similar scenarios” from past data. With a set of similar scenarios at each timestep, we can base our uncertainty on the performance in those cases. This approach—suitable for low-dimensional datasets such as time series—is extremely fast and interpretable. We find that the resulting uncertainty estimates naturally capture structured patterns in forecast error, such as shifts between solar minimum and maximum, and periodic features on the scale of half a solar rotation.

title: A hybrid machine learning approach for calibration and regionalization of LSM soil and vegetation parameters
task: A hybrid machine learning approach for calibration and regionalization of LSM soil and vegetation parameters
problem: This work explores the combined use of machine learning and traditional model calibration methods to develop a high resolution (1 km) soil and vegetation parameter dataset for North America and Central America. First, we use a traditional calibration method (i.e., genetic algorithm (GA)) to calibrate soil and vegetation parameters to Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) soil moisture at 25 km spatial resolution over the CONUS, Asia, and Europe. Next, we use a series of machine learning algorithms, including Neural Network, Random Forest, and XGBoost, to downscale and regionalize the optimized parameters for the National Land Data Assimilation System - Phase 3 (NLDAS-3) domain (i.e., North and Central America). The goal is to develop high resolution parameters that produce a land surface model (i.e., Noah-MP) soil moisture climatology that is more in-line with SMAP’s SM climatology.
implementation: The system outputs are soil and vegetation parameters at 1 km resolution.
reported_benefits: The ultimate benefit of this work is that it could improve land surface model simulations of the water cycle through more efficient remote sensing data assimilation (DA). Current DA methods rely on bias correction and CDF matching to translate observations (SMAP) into the same climatology as the model. However, this often filters out (as noise) useful signal about the human component of the water cycle, such as irrigation, in the observations. The ultimate goal of our work is to develop parameters that generate a model soil moisture climatology similar to SMAP, possibly bypassing the need for bias correction. As such, it may allow us to more readily incorporate information that SMAP provides about irrigation and other non-geophysical activities that are difficult to model, through DA of NASA remote sensing observations.

problem: The AI system utilizes a sentence-transformer model (all-mpnet-base-v2) and a statistical keyword method (TF-IDF) to perform document similarity tasks. These AI models are designed for natural language processing (NLP) tasks. Via all-mpnet-base-v2, the model will use utilize deep learning models to capture semantic meaning, ideal for conceptual similarity beyond exact wording. Via Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), the model will focus on lexical overlap and is effective for direct technical document comparison. Both models calculate Cosine similarity, with scores ranging from -1 to 1. Scores can be interpreted as follows: identical (1), highly similar (0.8-0.99), somewhat similar (~0.5), mostly dissimilar (0.1-0.3), completely dissimilar (0) and opposite (-1 to 0). Document similarity analysis can significantly boost productivity since a large volume of documents can quickly and efficiently be analyzed for extent of contextual or lexical similarity and can aid in routine planning for proposal administration. task: Open-source topic identification for the Public Engagement with Science Initiative data analysis.
problem: OIA team proposes using unsupervised Natural Language Processing (NLP) to identify topical themes within responses submitted to the NSF public engagement questionnaire. The AI system will include multiple open-source techniques used together to achieve this goal. Details of the system are as follows: To ensure high-quality topics, the system will first programmatically remove responses that are blank or non-informative. The National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) Semi-Automated Non-Response Detection for Surveys (SANDS) model will be used to filter out non-response responses (e.g., ""sdfsdfa,"" "" idkkkkk""). To reduce duplicate responses potentially caused by bots or submitted to boost relative importance, responses with the exact duplicate question wording will be removed over a threshold of three responses per IP address. If an individual has several different questions they would like to submit, all of their questions will be included. The system will use an open-source profanity filter such as Python’'s profanity-filter to identify toxic language. Any responses that are primarily toxic language will be dropped from analysis. To group questions into themes, we will use a word-embedding model to convert text responses into multidimensional space for topic modeling. Because we anticipate responses in multiple languages, the system will use a multilingual will use a multilingual word-embedding model, such as "paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2" or the most up-to-date version of this model at the time of analysis. Embeddings will be reduced in dimensions using a dimension reduction algorithm such as t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) to prepare for clustering. Reduced response embeddings will be clustered into groups using the ClassTfidfTransformer clustering algorithm from the Python package BertTopic. The algorithm will be seeded with words corresponding to a list of NSF programs corresponding to different research areas to map the clusters to these established categorizations. To aid in the review of topics generated by the clustering algorithm, an open-source large language model (LLM), such as Meta Llama, will be used to summarize the responses grouped within a cluster. Using a prompt like the example below, this strategy will produce a plain language summary and title of each of the clusters of responses. The clusters produced will be reviewed by Research Triangle Institute (RTI) staff for accuracy and appropriateness of naming. Staff will make edits to the LLM-generated summaries as necessary and note any clusters that are candidates for merging with other clusters into a single topic. title: NIV Adjudication Review Recommendation Engine (ARRE)
problem: ARRE is used to make post-adjudication managerial quality assurance review time more efficient. The current required managerial review of cases includes a randomly selected portion, which is not optimized to help managers allocate time toward cases where secondary review is most likely to surface documentation gaps, policy-complex adjudications, or process compliance issues. As a result, managers may spend review capacity on routine cases while missing opportunities to identify coaching needs or quality issues within the fixed review window.
implementation: ARRE produces a unitless anomaly score (0–1) for each already-adjudicated case and uses the score to generate a post-level ranked list that bins cases into priority tiers (e.g., high/medium/low) for managerial review. Outputs are advisory: managers may override or disregard the prioritization and may review any case consistent with existing authorities and review requirements. The output is used to help order the managerial quality assurance workload; it is not a decision output and is not used as an applicant risk determination. ARRE is used only after an adjudication is complete to support internal managerial oversight and does not serve as a basis for any visa eligibility determination or other binding action affecting the applicant. ARRE does not make, recommend, or change visa issuance/refusal decisions; all adjudicative determinations remain the responsibility of U.S. government officials.
reported_benefits: The primary purpose of ARRE is to support the post-adjudication, managerial quality assurance review workflow by helping managers efficiently meet existing review requirements through queue ordering and prioritization. This provides more efficient use of manager review time and more consistent post-adjudication oversight by better targeting the fixed, required managerial review effort toward cases with atypical attributes that warrant a second look for quality assurance purposes. title: Treasury Readability
problem: Government contract descriptions are indecipherable to the average American. The IRS has previously funded and published research on the use of models to validate the accuracy of structured contract spending data such as dates, dollar amounts, and addresses. Advances in large language models have made it feasible to automatically assess the quality of unstructured text descriptions of contract purchases. The description “THOMSON REUTERS ANNUAL TAXATION SUBSCRIPTION” clearly identifies a subscription-based contract with Thomson Reuters. While concise, it lacks details about the specific services included, intended users, and usage context, which would improve clarity and understanding of the contract scope. Rating: Marginal. The description “BPA SET-UP FOR ISS ENTERPRISE SERVICE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION SERVICES” is unclear and relies on unexplained acronyms, which may confuse readers. It also omits key context such as the purpose of the service, intended users, and usage location, making the contract scope difficult to interpret and resulting in a marginal readability assessment.

title: Line-Item Consolidation for Form 1120
problem: Large Business & International (LB&I) partnerships have a variety of forms and statements that include text. Filings include semi-structured attachments to returns that consist of many short free text labels paired with dollar amounts. implementation: A Form 1120 Other Deduction line-item description is assigned or consolidated to a consolidation group, which is either a subject matter expert defined deduction category or a deduction description existing in the dataset, based on how semantically similar the descriptions are, measured by cosine similarity. Not only do these line-items become more accessible to examiners, but it facilitates a more robust benchmarking analysis of line-item amounts by creating larger groupings of common line-items. Success in the line-item consolidation stage was defined by how effectively each stage of the text consolidation pipeline could reduce the number of unique line-item descriptions while maintaining an appropriate level of specificity.

title: SCORE (Structured Clinical Output Rating Engine)
problem: SCORE (Structured Clinical Output Rating Engine) uses o3-mini LLM to grade the quality of clinical notes that have either been created by a human or AI and provides feedback to the user. When a transcript of the patient encounter is available, SCORE employs embedding-based semantic analysis to enhance patient safety and documentation accuracy. Embeddings convert text into numerical vectors that capture meaning, enabling the system to measure how semantically similar—or different—statements are between the clinical note and the source transcript. This capability powers two critical safety detectors: Hallucination Detection identifies factual-sounding claims in the note that lack support in the transcript. This is essential for AI-generated documentation, where models may produce plausible but ungrounded statements about medications, allergies, diagnoses, or procedures. Claims with weak transcript support are flagged with risk levels (high/medium/low) based on their potential clinical impact. Contradiction Detection finds instances where the note and transcript discuss the same clinical topic but present conflicting information—such as differing medication dosages, mismatched vital signs, or inverted symptom reports (e.g., "denies chest pain" versus "reports chest pain").
implementation: Output: Quality Score & Actionable Guidance Returns a hybrid quality score (1.0–5.0) and letter grade computed from three weighted components: PDQI-9 Analysis (70%) – AI-driven evaluation of 9 clinical documentation dimensions (up-to-date, accurate, thorough, useful, organized, concise, consistent, complete, actionable) Heuristic Metrics (20%) – Rule-based assessment of length, structure, and redundancy Factuality Verification (10%) – Claim validation against source transcript (when available) Each dimension includes narrative feedback, supporting evidence excerpts from the note, and specific improvement suggestions to guide documentation enhancement.
reported_benefits: Improve clinical documentation quality through standardized evaluation and scoring and create efficiency for documentation audit staff.

task: Deep-Learning approaches to develop candidate lists of terms for use in text searches
problem: The intended use is to increase the comprehensiveness of term lists to be used in text-matching approaches to identifying concepts of interest in free-text medical record notes. Text-matching approaches are an efficient method for identifying text of interest in medical notes. The success of text-matching approaches depends on the quality of term lists used to search for a concept of interest. While humans can generate word lists for text-matching approaches, the generated word lists are likely to be limited and biased by the vocabulary, language habits, population exposure, and local dialects of the human generating the list. Deep learning methods can help to augment candidate term lists to help overcome some of these challenges. Once generated these augmented candidate terms are reviewed by subject matter experts for appropriateness and accuracy of the suggested terms for the concept and use case of interest.
implementation: The outputs of this use of AI is a candidate list of terms related to a concept of interest. This candidate list is combined with suggestions generated by human experts and then these are reviewed by a subject matter expert to generate a final list of terms for use in text-matching algorithms to extract medical record free text mentions of interest. For the pre-trained Large Language model approach, the input is a query prompting for synonyms of terms related to the concept of interest. The output is the answer provided by the LLM, including the suggested candidate terms and the original terms that were stated in the query. source_description: The Flemish Agency for Child and Family (Kind en Gezin), now part of the Opgroeien agency, faced constraints in conducting comprehensive inspections of childcare facilities due to limited inspection capacity and increasing demand for oversight. Ensuring consistent quality and safeguarding child wellbeing required a more targeted and risk-based inspection approach. The use case aims to prioritise inspections by identifying childcare providers with a higher likelihood of non-compliance or quality issues, thereby improving regulatory efficiency and service quality. The solution integrates supervised machine learning techniques, including logistic regression and gradient boosting (XGBoost), applied to a combination of internal administrative records and external inspection data from the Health Care Inspectorate. These models generate risk scores that support inspectors in selecting facilities for inspection. The system is embedded within existing workflows, complementing professional judgement rather than replacing it. As a result, inspection resources are allocated more effectively, enabling earlier detection of potential issues and improving overall monitoring coverage. The approach enhances evidence-based decision-making, contributes to maintaining high childcare standards, and supports a more proactive regulatory framework.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Camera System - Mobile phone usage on vehicles
source_description: The Belgian road safety institute Vias identified the growing risk of traffic accidents caused by drivers using mobile phones while driving, particularly handheld usage. Traditional enforcement methods rely heavily on manual observation by police, limiting detection rates and scalability. This use case aims to enhance enforcement capabilities by automating the identification of such violations and supporting road safety policies. The system uses roadside camera infrastructure to capture images of passing vehicles, which are then processed using computer vision techniques to detect whether a driver is holding and using a mobile phone. Images not indicating violations are automatically discarded, while detected cases are anonymised to protect privacy before further review. Law enforcement authorities validate flagged cases before issuing fines. The solution integrates image recognition models trained on annotated datasets to distinguish relevant behaviours. The pilot demonstrates the feasibility of augmenting enforcement through automated pre-selection of violations, improving efficiency and enabling more consistent monitoring. It contributes to increased deterrence, optimised use of police resources, and enhanced road safety outcomes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: PaveAI 2.0 - Interprets the figures in Google Analytics via machine learning and custom reports
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: VISITFLANDERS explored the use of automated analytics tools to better interpret website performance data and support digital marketing strategies. Analysing large volumes of web analytics data requires specialised expertise and can be time-consuming, limiting the ability to quickly derive actionable insights. The objective of this use case was to enhance understanding of user behaviour and improve decision-making related to tourism promotion. The solution involved the use of a tool capable of transforming Google Analytics data into structured insights and customised reports through machine learning techniques. The system processes web traffic data to identify patterns, trends, and performance indicators, presenting them in an accessible format for decision-makers. It integrates with existing analytics platforms to automate reporting workflows. While the pilot demonstrated potential to improve efficiency and insight generation, no recent evidence confirms continued use or operational deployment within VISITFLANDERS.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Vlaamse Dienst voor Arbeidsbemiddeling en Beroepsopleiding
title: Jobnet - Reskilling, upskilling and retraining of people
source_description: Labour markets change rapidly, and many citizens need support to understand how their existing experience and capabilities relate to emerging job opportunities, especially when they are seeking to reskill, upskill, or retrain. Without tailored guidance, it can be difficult for jobseekers to identify realistic career paths, understand which skills they already possess, and determine which additional competences are needed to move into new roles. The objective of this use case is to enrich job matching and support career transitions by helping citizens connect their own backgrounds with current labour market demand. The implementation consists of Jobnet, a solution used by VDAB since 2018 that combines multiple analytical models into a broader matching system. At a conceptual level, the platform analyses user experience and skill profiles alongside labour market data to identify suitable jobs and highlight relevant skill gaps that may need to be addressed through training or development. The system therefore links personal profile analysis with market intelligence to support guidance and transition planning. The impact includes more informed career decisions, better targeting of training pathways, and improved matching between people and available work. It also supports employability, makes career services more scalable, and delivers public value by helping align workforce capabilities with changing economic needs.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Vlaamse Dienst voor Arbeidsbemiddeling en Beroepsopleiding
title: VDAB Chatbot for job seekers - Chatbots to better match jobseekers with the right vacancies
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Jobseekers often need timely, practical support when searching for vacancies, yet traditional guidance channels can struggle to provide immediate and personalised assistance at scale. This creates a challenge for employment services that aim to help large numbers of users navigate vacancies, ask questions, and receive relevant direction throughout their search process. The objective of this use case is to improve the quality and accessibility of job-search support by using conversational tools that can answer questions and guide users towards suitable opportunities. The implementation involves chatbot technology designed to participate in typed conversations with jobseekers, automatically responding to enquiries and helping users progress through their search. At a conceptual level, the solution uses conversational language processing to interpret user input, provide answers, and support matching-related interactions between jobseekers and the employment service. The chatbot is positioned as part of a broader exploration of how conversational systems can strengthen vacancy discovery and candidate guidance. The impact includes quicker access to support, a more responsive user experience, and better assistance outside the limits of traditional one-to-one service models. It also increases service scalability, reduces pressure on human support channels, and creates business value by helping more jobseekers engage effectively with vacancies and employment services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Departement Cultuur, Jeugd en Media (CJM) - Wallonia
title: Quickscan Organisaties
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Grant-making bodies often face a heavy administrative burden when assessing subsidy applications, particularly where they must judge not only the substantive quality of a proposal but also whether the applicant has sufficient organisational and business maturity to deliver it successfully. In this case, the Department of Culture, Youth and Media sought to streamline the admissibility and assessment of grant applications, reduce the time required from both applicants and evaluators, and improve consistency in decision-making. The objective is therefore to support faster, more standardised, and less labour-intensive screening of applications without weakening the underlying governance process. The implementation centred on the development of the Quickscan Organizations tool and its supporting algorithm through an innovative public procurement project. At a conceptual level, the solution analyses structured and textual application information to automate elements of admissibility checking and organisational assessment, enabling public officials to compare applicants against defined criteria more efficiently. The tool was developed through a proof-of-concept phase involving selected suppliers and positioned as a digital support layer for grant evaluation workflows. The expected impact includes shorter assessment cycles, lower administrative effort, and more efficient processing for both applicants and reviewers. It also offers improved scalability and greater consistency in handling large numbers of applications, creating business value through better use of public-sector resources.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

It is there for the visitors 24/7 in Messenger and provides information about the city Point of Interests pf the city. title: Andrija - Virtual assistant supporting advising suspected COVID-19 infections
source_description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, public health authorities faced high volumes of citizen enquiries regarding symptoms, testing and protective measures. In Croatia, the digital assistant Andrija was developed to provide consistent, evidence-based guidance and reduce pressure on health services. Stakeholders include citizens, epidemiologists, public health authorities and technology partners. The objective is to support early self-assessment and disseminate reliable health information. The system combines natural language processing, rule-based medical triage logic and continuously updated epidemiological guidance to respond to user queries via web and messaging platforms such as WhatsApp. Expert-defined decision trees and symptom-check algorithms guide users through structured dialogues. Expected impacts include faster dissemination of accurate information, reduced burden on call centres, improved public awareness and more efficient triage during health emergencies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Hope - Chatbot informing work of the Civil Protection Staff
source_description: Local authorities require effective communication channels to inform citizens during emergencies, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. In Vinkovci, the Civil Protection Staff sought a digital solution to address frequently asked questions and reduce administrative workload. Stakeholders include municipal authorities, citizens and public health institutions. The objective is to provide accessible, real-time information on pandemic measures, symptoms and administrative procedures such as e-passes. The chatbot uses natural language processing and predefined knowledge bases to answer common queries and guide users through structured information flows. It is integrated into municipal communication channels and can be updated with new guidance as regulations change. Expected impacts include improved citizen access to reliable information, reduced call volumes for public offices and enhanced responsiveness during crisis management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: The Water Development Department, The Water Development Department, Cyprus
title: WaterAnalytics - Water quality monitoring
source_description: The Water Development Department in Cyprus is responsible for monitoring water resources, including quality and distribution efficiency, in a context of increasing environmental pressures and resource scarcity. Traditional monitoring approaches generate large volumes of heterogeneous data that are difficult to analyse in a timely and integrated manner. This use case aims to improve water management by enabling more effective analysis of hydraulic and quality-related data to support operational and policy decisions. The system employs data analytics techniques to process inputs from monitoring infrastructure, including sensors capturing parameters such as flow, pressure, and chemical composition. Machine learning algorithms are applied to identify patterns, detect anomalies, and support predictive assessments of water system performance. The solution is designed to integrate multiple data streams into a unified analytical framework. Expected benefits include improved detection of water quality issues, more efficient resource management, and enhanced decision-making capabilities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI in social service to improve long term stay
source_description: Social-care systems face growing pressure to support older and vulnerable people in ways that preserve independence, quality of life, and continuity of care, while also reducing unnecessary institutionalisation. This use case addresses that challenge by using digital support in social services to help citizens remain in their natural home and community environment for as long as possible. The objective is to strengthen person-centred care, improve early identification of support needs, and enable more sustainable care planning that balances individual wellbeing with public-service capacity. The implementation is described at a high level within the Czech AI strategy context, where AI is envisaged as a support tool for social services rather than as a replacement for professional judgement. At a conceptual level, such a solution would draw on relevant care and contextual data to help identify risks, support care coordination, and guide interventions that make independent living more viable over time. The expected impact includes improved quality of life for service users, reduced pressure on long-term institutional care, and more efficient allocation of social-service resources. It also supports a more scalable and preventive approach to care by helping public services intervene earlier and tailor support more effectively to individual circumstances.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Corti's AI - Emergency medical services real-time speech analysis for cardiac predictions
source_description: Emergency call handlers must identify cardiac arrest within seconds, yet callers often describe symptoms unclearly and high-pressure conditions can lead to delayed recognition or missed warning signs. This use case addresses that operational problem by supporting dispatchers and call-takers during emergency calls so that out-of-hospital cardiac arrests can be recognised faster and with fewer errors. The broader objective is to improve emergency medical response, reduce avoidable mortality, and strengthen the reliability of call-centre decision-making in time-critical situations. The implementation uses real-time speech analysis on live emergency calls, applying predictive models trained to detect linguistic and behavioural patterns associated with cardiac arrest. At a conceptual level, the system listens to the call as it unfolds, analyses speech signals and conversational content, and produces immediate decision support for human operators. The approach is intended to work alongside dispatch professionals rather than replace them, feeding alerts and clinical suggestions into the emergency response workflow. Reported performance from the original deployment described detection accuracy of up to 95 per cent, and the Copenhagen implementation was sufficiently promising to support wider piloting with the European Emergency Number Association. The impact includes quicker diagnosis, reduced error rates, faster dispatch decisions, and stronger overall service quality, with clear public value in improving survival chances during medical emergencies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Erhvervsstyrelsen - Detection of errors in business statements
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Supervising corporate filings and financial statements at scale is difficult for regulators because manual review cannot easily keep pace with the volume of submissions, while material errors and potentially fraudulent reporting may remain hidden among routine cases. The Danish Business Authority developed this use case to strengthen risk-based supervision by identifying suspicious patterns and highlighting significant errors in business and financial statements more efficiently. The objective is to improve control quality, target inspections more intelligently, and reduce unnecessary burdens on compliant businesses by focusing attention where risks are highest. The implementation uses machine learning models within the authority’s data and control environment to analyse company filings and financial statements for indicators of fraud, irregularities, or non-compliance. At a conceptual level, the solution combines administrative and statement data with digital risk-scoring methods to prioritise cases for review and support supervisory decision-making. This fits into a broader risk-based control framework used by the authority in relation to company law and accounting oversight. The impact includes more effective detection of problematic filings, better allocation of inspection resources, and stronger trust in business reporting. It also supports scalability in regulatory control, improves consistency in case selection, and creates value by enabling more proportionate and data-driven oversight across very large filing volumes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Kiri - chatbot for citizens' enquiries
source_description: Municipal websites receive large numbers of routine citizen questions, yet residents increasingly expect immediate answers without having to wait for office hours or contact staff directly for simple matters. Kiri was introduced in this context as a pilot chatbot for several Danish municipalities, including Frederiksberg, to improve access to general information in citizen service areas such as passports and driving licences. The objective is to provide instant responses to common questions, reduce pressure on front-line service teams, and test whether conversational digital assistance can improve the overall citizen experience without handling sensitive case-specific issues. The implementation uses a public-facing municipal chatbot that interprets natural-language questions and returns answers drawn from predefined service information. At a conceptual level, the system relies on conversational language technology, structured municipal knowledge content, and website integration so that users can obtain immediate guidance directly on the municipality’s digital channels. The pilot was inspired by similar Scandinavian trials and was intentionally limited at first to frequently asked, general enquiries rather than individual case handling. The impact includes quicker access to information, more convenient self-service, and reduced demand on municipal staff for repetitive queries. It also offers a scalable support mechanism across municipalities and contributes to more consistent communication with citizens across digital service channels.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CHAIN - Smart Water optimising energy consumption
source_description: The municipality of Aarhus sought to address inefficiencies in water and energy consumption within its water management infrastructure. Traditional systems lacked the capability to dynamically optimise operations based on real-time demand and system conditions. The objective of this use case is to improve energy efficiency and water quality monitoring through data-driven optimisation of water systems. The solution relies on sensor networks that collect detailed data on water consumption, flow, and quality parameters. Advanced analytics and machine learning techniques are applied to process these large datasets, enabling optimisation of pumping operations and early detection of anomalies. The system integrates sensor outputs with analytical models to support operational decision-making. As a pilot project, it demonstrates the potential to reduce energy consumption, improve system efficiency, and enhance sustainability in municipal water management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Estonian Agricultural Registers and Information Board (ARIB)
title: SATIKAS - Detecting the agricultural grasslands changes
source_description: Agricultural agencies need reliable ways to verify whether grasslands have been mown, since this affects compliance with land-management and subsidy rules, yet traditional inspections are costly, selective, and difficult to scale across an entire country. SATIKAS was developed for the Estonian Agricultural Registers and Information Board to automate this monitoring task and improve oversight of grassland management using remote sensing. The objective is to support more efficient compliance checking by replacing or reducing manual inspection with systematic, data-driven observation of mowing activity. The implementation uses deep learning and convolutional neural network techniques to analyse satellite imagery from the Copernicus programme, particularly Sentinel data, together with reference information on farmer fields, historical inspection logs, and meteorological data. At a conceptual level, the system fuses geospatial imagery and administrative datasets to classify whether mowing has taken place on specific grassland parcels. The solution is one of Estonia’s earliest government uses of such methods and was described as still under development, with plans to expand its capabilities further. The impact includes broader and more frequent monitoring coverage, reduced inspection effort, and more consistent evidence for subsidy control. It also improves scalability and reliability in agricultural supervision while supporting better use of public resources and more targeted field verification where necessary.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: e-Residency - Chatbot for customer assistance
source_description: As the Estonian e-Residency programme grew internationally, customer support demand increased and response times risked lengthening unless more staff were added. The challenge was to provide faster answers to common enquiries while maintaining service quality for a global user base seeking information on applications, digital identity, company creation, and programme processes. The objective of this use case was to improve responsiveness and customer experience without proportionally increasing support headcount. The implementation introduced an AI-powered customer service assistant with a live-chat interface, designed to answer common questions instantly and support users as they navigated the e-Residency journey. At a conceptual level, the solution combined conversational automation with structured support content, allowing the organisation to handle routine queries through a chatbot while reserving staff effort for more complex cases. The service was integrated into the programme’s broader digital support model and aligned with an evolving customer strategy focused on accessibility and end-to-end assistance. The impact includes faster first-response times, better support scalability, and lower pressure on human support teams. It also contributes to a more seamless user experience for international applicants and creates operational value by enabling a public digital service to serve growing demand more efficiently across borders.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Enhanced Care Management - Prediction model for hospitalisation/assistance
source_description: The Estonian Health Insurance Fund, in collaboration with the World Bank, initiated a programme to improve the management of patients with chronic conditions by strengthening preventive care and reducing avoidable hospitalisations. General practitioners often face challenges in identifying high-risk patients who require intensified monitoring and intervention. The objective is to support risk-based care management by identifying patients most likely to experience adverse health events. The solution uses predictive modelling techniques applied to healthcare utilisation data, particularly medical billing records, to identify patterns associated with hospitalisation risk. Algorithms analyse patient histories and selected diagnoses to generate risk scores, enabling GPs to prioritise care interventions such as counselling and follow-up. The model is integrated into primary care workflows to support decision-making. Pilot results indicate improved targeting of high-risk patients and potential reductions in unnecessary hospital admissions and healthcare costs. However, the initiative remains at pilot stage with limited evidence of nationwide implementation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: EE Parliament- A system for preparing of verbatim reports
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Parliamentary administrations are often required to publish accurate verbatim records very quickly after sittings conclude, yet doing so manually places significant pressure on stenographers and can limit both speed and consistency. In Estonia, the Chancellery of the Riigikogu needed a more efficient way to produce official transcripts within one hour of the end of a sitting and to open up these records for wider digital reuse. The objective of this use case is therefore to improve transcript production efficiency and accuracy while enabling parliamentary speech records to become machine-readable open data. The implementation uses a speech recognition system called Hans, developed with Estonian-language recognition technology, to transcribe speeches delivered from the parliamentary rostrum. At a conceptual level, the system converts live spoken contributions into draft verbatim text that can be processed and published more quickly than through manual transcription alone. It is integrated into the parliamentary reporting workflow and supports both operational publication and downstream data use. The impact includes reduced manual workload for stenographers, faster delivery of official reports, and improved accessibility of parliamentary proceedings. It also increases the scalability and reusability of legislative records by supporting their publication as structured, machine-readable data for use in other systems and public services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ITI - Chatbot for Statistics Estonia
source_description: The virtual assistant called ITI, created in collaboration with the Estonian start-up AlphaBlues (now AlfaChat, part of a larger company), shared knowledge regarding the population of Estonia, the size of the pay gap, average wages and consumer price changes, and many other things. Iti also assisted the data provider, whose typical questions are related to activities in the electronic data submission portal and filling in questionnaires. If Iti did not know the answer, it would redirect the query based on its content to either the customer support specialist of the data provider or the user of the statistics. Iti obtained its knowledge from the questions sent through online chats over one year and gets wiser with every query. ITI helped to find information faster thus allowing the customer support of Statistics Estonia to focus on answering more complicated and detailed queries. ITI is know not in use as it has been substituted by Bürokratt, the Estonian national chatbot.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: OTT - Predicting employment pathways
source_description: Employment services must decide how best to support jobseekers with very different skills, histories, and barriers to work, yet this can be difficult to do consistently when advisers are handling large caseloads and labour market conditions are changing. OTT was developed by the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund to improve understanding of client needs and to help identify the most suitable employment pathways for individual jobseekers. The objective is to support more accurate job recommendations, better targeting of retraining or reskilling measures, and more effective allocation of staff attention across client groups. The implementation uses machine-learning methods trained on more than 100,000 client records to estimate the probabilities of different employment outcomes and suggest appropriate positions or interventions based on qualifications and profile characteristics. At a conceptual level, the system combines client data, pathway prediction, and recommendation logic within a tool used by civil servants rather than as a fully autonomous public-facing service. It helps structure client segmentation, identify likely needs, and distribute workload more effectively among advisers. The impact includes more tailored support for jobseekers, improved matching to vacancies, and better-informed retraining guidance. It also enhances service efficiency, supports prioritisation of cases where intervention is most needed, and creates business value by making employment support more targeted and data-driven.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Texta Toolkit - Identifying documents published without authorisation
source_description: Public institutions manage very large document collections, and identifying files that have been published without authorisation, or that still contain personal or restricted information, is difficult to do manually at scale. In Estonia, this challenge arose in relation to document management audits and the need to detect internal documents, personal data, and other content that should not have been publicly disclosed. The objective of this use case is to strengthen information governance by automating large-scale document review, supporting anonymisation, and enabling safer republication of sensitive materials where appropriate. The implementation used the Texta Toolkit, a no-code natural language processing and machine learning platform, to analyse more than 1.2 million documents, convert them into machine-readable form, and identify or remove personal data. The same toolkit was also used in collaboration with justice-sector bodies to anonymise nearly 80,000 court decisions before republication. At a conceptual level, the system combines document ingestion, text extraction, classification, and anonymisation functions within a scalable analysis environment for public-sector records. The impact includes much faster auditing of large repositories, lower manual effort, and reduced risk of unauthorised disclosure. It also improves compliance, supports open-data publication in safer forms, and creates sustained operational value by giving institutions reusable tools for document governance and privacy protection.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Datel - Speed cameras for detecting speeding violations
source_description: Road safety enforcement depends on the rapid and consistent identification of speeding offences, yet manual processing of camera evidence can be slow, resource-intensive, and difficult to scale across large traffic networks. In Estonia, this use case was introduced to strengthen the handling of speeding violations by automating the recognition of number plates, the retrieval of case data, and the preparation of administrative steps needed to initiate proceedings. The objective is to improve the efficiency, consistency, and timeliness of speed enforcement while allowing police officers to focus on validation and final decision-making rather than routine processing. The implementation uses machine learning and image recognition to analyse photographs captured by roadside speed cameras, identify licence plate numbers, match them with the relevant vehicle and owner records, and prepare draft penalty decisions where appropriate. At a conceptual level, the solution links visual detection, administrative data access, and case-generation functions into a semi-automated enforcement workflow, with the Police and Border Guard Board carrying out verification before finalising the process. The impact includes faster handling of offences, reduced manual workload, and more scalable traffic enforcement operations. It also improves procedural consistency, supports more reliable road safety monitoring, and creates public value by enabling authorities to respond more efficiently to speeding violations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Public Transport and Traffic Management Transport Board in Tallinn
title: Traffic load - Machine vision for collecting information on traffic load
source_description: Urban transport planning requires accurate information on how vehicles move through the city, yet municipalities often lack detailed, continuous data on traffic flows across key entry and exit points. In Tallinn, this created a practical challenge for planning decisions related to congestion, parking, road construction, and other transport measures, as authorities needed better evidence on how many vehicles entered and left the city each day. The objective of this use case is to generate a clearer picture of traffic load in order to support more informed and timely planning decisions. The implementation uses machine vision developed in collaboration with Sifr OU, with cameras placed at selected intersections to detect and count different categories of vehicles passing through monitored areas. Because no ready-made solution matched Tallinn’s local conditions, the system required a dedicated training phase to adapt the model to the city’s environment and traffic patterns. At a conceptual level, the application combines image capture, object recognition, and traffic counting to classify buses, cars, lorries, and motorcycles, with the potential to expand later to pedestrians and cyclists. The impact includes the creation of traffic intelligence where little or no such information previously existed, enabling better planning, more data-driven decisions, and improved scalability in how the city monitors and manages transport demand.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SUVE - Chatbot for questions about emergency situations
source_description: During public emergencies, citizens need quick access to trustworthy and consistent information, yet official websites and helplines can struggle to keep pace with rapidly changing demand and the spread of misinformation. In Estonia, this challenge became particularly acute during the coronavirus outbreak, when several government agencies needed a way to answer frequently asked questions efficiently across different audiences and languages. The objective of this use case is to improve public access to reliable crisis information, reduce confusion, and support coordinated communication during emergency situations. The implementation took the form of Suve, an automated chatbot developed rapidly through a hackathon involving government bodies and the Estonian start-up community in the early phase of the pandemic. At a conceptual level, the chatbot uses conversational language processing to answer questions in Estonian and English, drawing on official information published by government agencies so that responses remain aligned with authoritative sources. The system is integrated across the websites of several public institutions, allowing users to access guidance through familiar digital channels. The impact includes faster dissemination of official information, reduced pressure on manual support services, and a better user experience during crisis conditions. It also strengthens the reliability of government communication and helps counter misinformation by making verified answers easier to obtain.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Helsinki HUH - Intensive care for premature baby
source_description: Citizens, visitors, and businesses increasingly expect public services to be available at any time and through multiple digital channels, yet municipal support is often fragmented across websites, offices, and service teams. In Oulu, this created a need for a more accessible way to guide users across everyday matters relating to tourism, business services, and municipal information without depending solely on working hours or manual support. The objective of this use case is to provide continuous, multilingual access to guidance and electronic services while improving the overall availability and convenience of city support. The implementation resulted in OuluBot, a virtual assistant developed through a project co-financed by Business Finland. At a conceptual level, the chatbot retrieves and combines information from city websites, prior chat interactions, guidance materials, databases, and other information sources in order to answer questions or direct users to the right service. It operates continuously across channels and, when it cannot resolve a request, can pass the conversation during office hours to the city’s general counselling service. The impact includes faster access to municipal and business information, reduced dependency on staff for routine questions, and a more seamless digital experience for users. It also improves service scalability, supports more consistent communication, and strengthens the city’s ability to offer responsive support across time, place, language, and device.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: OuluBot - Virtual assistant for business
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The City of Oulu initiated a project co-financed by Business Finland, which brought to the development of a chatbot service, OuluBot. OuluBot is a virtual assistant in all everyday issues, whether they concern tourism, companies or city services. The answer or guidance to an electronic service is provided regardless of time, place, medium and language. Technically, chatbot retrieves information e.g. relevant City of Oulu websites, chat history, guidance information, databases, and other information sources. OuluBot is available 24/7, independently of working hours. If the user is looking for information that OuluBot would not be able to answer, then during office hours the discussion could be directed to the City of Oulu chat service (Oulu10 general counseling customer service).

title: AuroraAI - Programme with many AI examples.
source_description: Public services are often organised around administrative structures rather than around the real-life situations people face, which can make it difficult for citizens to find timely, relevant support across different organisations. Within the AuroraAI programme, one experimental use case focused on the life event of moving to a place of study, where students may need help that cuts across housing, mobility, wellbeing, and local services. The objective was to understand student needs more holistically and to design a cross-cutting public service offering that responded better to the factors shaping wellbeing during this transition. The implementation combined wellbeing survey data collected in Tampere and Turku with clustering and analytical methods to identify groups of students requiring different kinds of support. The findings showed that issues such as the reliability of public transport and the quality of the natural environment played an important role in student wellbeing. Based on these insights, a bot was created to provide information on the topics students considered most important. The impact of the experiment lies less in large-scale uptake than in the lessons learned: it demonstrated the value of user insight, data analytics, and life-event-based service design, while also highlighting the need for stronger user experience capabilities and more proactive engagement if municipalities are to make cross-cutting digital services more effective and widely used.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: French Fraud - Fraud detection value declarations
source_description: Customs authorities process very large numbers of import declarations and must identify potentially fraudulent cases without slowing down legitimate trade unnecessarily. In France, this created a need for a more effective way to detect irregularities in declared values and identify possible cases of identity fraud or import trafficking within complex customs workflows. The objective of this use case is to strengthen risk detection, support targeted enforcement, and improve the efficiency of customs operations by focusing attention on the declarations most likely to involve non-compliance. The implementation uses a supervised deep learning model to analyse customs value declarations and related data for anomalies, suspicious patterns, and indicators of fraud. At a conceptual level, the solution combines historical enforcement knowledge with predictive analysis to assess declaration risk and help customs officers prioritise cases for further examination. Rather than replacing investigative judgement, the model functions as a decision-support layer within a broader customs control process, enabling staff to concentrate resources where the likelihood of irregularity is highest. The impact includes improved capacity to detect fraud, faster identification of high-risk transactions, and more efficient allocation of control resources. It also supports the scalability of customs supervision, contributes to stronger border and revenue protection, and creates operational value by helping enforcement teams manage growing declaration volumes with greater precision and consistency.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Interministerial Center for IT Services Relating to Human Resources
title: RenoiRH - Chatbot in HR management rules to facilitate access
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The French Interministerial Centre for IT Services Relating to Human Resources (CISIRH) manages complex HR systems across the public administration, where staff must navigate extensive regulatory frameworks governing careers, mobility, and administrative procedures. Accessing accurate and timely information can be challenging due to the volume and complexity of rules. This use case aims to simplify access to HR information and improve administrative efficiency for public employees. The solution includes a conversational interface that enables users to query HR rules and procedures in natural language. Natural language processing techniques are used to interpret user queries and retrieve relevant information from structured HR knowledge bases and regulatory documents. The chatbot is integrated into existing HR information systems, providing real-time assistance. organization: Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Recovery - General Directorate of Enterprises (DGE) / Ministry of Labor (DGEFP)
title: SignauxFaibles - Predictive analysis of business difficulties
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Companies in financial difficulty often show warning signs before a crisis becomes visible, yet public support bodies may identify those signals too late to offer effective assistance. In France, this use case was developed to help public actors detect vulnerable small and medium-sized enterprises earlier and intervene before deterioration becomes irreversible. The objective is to strengthen preventive support for businesses by identifying weak signals of distress, improving coordination between institutions, and enabling more timely outreach to company managers. The implementation combines a detection algorithm with an automated data-loading system capable of refreshing information regularly from operational databases such as URSSAF, DIRECCTE, and Banque de France. At a conceptual level, the solution analyses relevant variables associated with business fragility, generates alerts on firms likely to be entering difficulty, and feeds these insights into the work of decentralised public actors responsible for business support. The approach was designed to identify a small but meaningful number of new at-risk SMEs each month within a regional context, demonstrating a targeted and dynamic monitoring capability. The impact includes earlier detection of companies needing help, more effective use of support resources, and stronger public coordination around economic resilience. It also supports digital transformation in state action by creating a more proactive, scalable, and evidence-based way to assist weakened businesses.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Aria - Chatbot answering retired people
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Retirees often need straightforward access to information about payments, declared income, and direct debits, yet conventional customer-service channels may be available only during limited hours and can struggle to respond quickly to large volumes of recurring enquiries. The French National Old Age Insurance Fund introduced this use case to make support more accessible and to help pensioners obtain practical information without waiting for standard service windows. The objective is to improve the availability, speed, and convenience of pension-related assistance while reducing pressure on traditional customer-support operations. The implementation centres on Aria, a chatbot designed to answer questions from retirees and provide personalised information on topics such as payment schedules, income declarations, and debit arrangements. At a conceptual level, the service combines conversational interaction with access to relevant account or process information, allowing users to obtain responses through a digital interface beyond ordinary office hours. The solution is also being extended to cover a broader range of topics and user groups, indicating a gradual expansion of its role within pension service delivery. The impact includes quicker access to information, a more flexible and user-friendly support experience, and lower demand on human service teams for routine enquiries. It also improves service scalability, supports continuity of access outside working hours, and creates public value by making essential pension information easier to obtain.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Datakalab - Covid-19 Mask wearing detection In some French cities
source_description: During the Covid-19 pandemic, the use of surveillance cameras was authorised to monitor whether passengers on public transport respected the requirement to wear masks. However, France’s data protection watchdog CNIL called out the practice, saying it was not governed by any legal framework and was therefore illegal. The authority began a three-month test of its software from French tech company Datakalab this week at the Chatelet-Les-Halles station in the heart of Paris, normally used by about 33 million passengers per year. Monitors will have access to a dashboard with the proportion of riders believed to be wearing masks. The plan was making mask wearing mandatory in public transport from May 2019. AI was regarded to be able to supplement enforcement agents in stations. Still, CNIL, the government body in charge of privacy, raised concerns that this type of technology carries a risk that the identity of the people being analyzed could be reconstructed.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LaBonneBoîte - Identification of companies with a high probability of hiring
source_description: Many job opportunities are never formally advertised, which means jobseekers can miss suitable openings if they rely only on published vacancies. In France, this use case was created to help people identify employers likely to recruit in the near future, even where no vacancy has yet been posted. The objective is to improve access to hidden job opportunities, strengthen spontaneous application strategies, and increase the chances that jobseekers secure interviews by targeting firms with a high probability of hiring. The implementation takes the form of an online service that predicts which companies are likely to recruit within the next six months in a given sector and area. At a conceptual level, the tool uses predictive modelling over labour market and employer data to estimate hiring probability and then presents these employers through a searchable digital interface. Its code is reusable and an API allows the service to be replicated on other websites, increasing its portability and reach. The impact includes better targeting of job-search efforts, improved access to opportunities beyond traditional vacancy listings, and stronger support for proactive labour-market behaviour. It also enhances scalability by allowing the service to be reused across platforms and user groups, while creating clear business value by helping more people connect with employers likely to recruit in the near term.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: The General Food Directorate (DGAL) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Food
title: IAlim - Targeting restaurant health inspections
source_description: Food safety authorities must prioritise inspections across large numbers of restaurants, food service businesses, and distributors, yet traditional inspection planning can struggle to identify which establishments present the greatest immediate risk. In France, this use case was introduced to help Ministry of Agriculture inspectors target health inspections more effectively in the direct-to-consumer delivery sector, where the rapid growth of online ordering and platform-based services has made oversight more complex.
