title: FrailCare.AI - Intelligent trajectories of fragility for the Portuguese elderly population
source_description: FrailCare.AI addresses the challenge of supporting elderly citizens at risk of frailty through scalable, preventive and integrated public services. As the population ages, public health systems must detect needs early, prevent adverse health events and coordinate support across health, social and safety dimensions. The proposal aims to support the national upscaling of a telecare screening and intervention service connected to SNS24 for older people with frailty risk. Its objectives include monitoring a group of elderly citizens through a telecare service, preventing health occurrences, detecting emerging needs early, promoting integrated care and contributing to healthy and active ageing. The emerging technology implementation uses intelligent analysis of frailty trajectories to support screening, follow-up and intervention planning. At conceptual level, the system would combine telecare data with risk assessment and predictive modelling to identify changes in frailty status and guide the prioritisation of support. Integration with SNS24 would allow the approach to be embedded in a national public-service context, supporting remote monitoring and coordinated responses. The expected impact is improved early detection of needs, better continuity of care and greater scalability of frailty-related public services. By enabling proactive follow-up rather than relying only on reactive care, FrailCare.AI can contribute to healthier ageing, reduced avoidable health incidents and more efficient allocation of health and social-care resources.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI4Life - Artificial intelligence as a tool to reduce Premature Mortality
source_description: AI4Life responds to the public-health objective of reducing premature mortality from non-communicable diseases, in line with the World Health Organization target of reducing such mortality by 25% by 2025. The project focuses on the infantile-juvenile population and responds to the need for a more complete understanding of the factors associated with health risks across several dimensions. Public-health authorities often hold relevant data in separate systems, limiting their ability to identify patterns and relationships that could support prevention. The project therefore aims to collect and integrate information from several data sources that had not previously been combined, in order to characterise young populations more comprehensively. The emerging technology implementation applies machine-learning techniques to discover patterns, relationships and knowledge from integrated datasets. At conceptual level, the system combines health and related contextual information to confirm existing assumptions, objectify known patterns and identify previously unknown associations that may be relevant to premature mortality. The expected impact is stronger analytical capacity for prevention-oriented public-health policy, allowing authorities to better understand risk profiles and design more targeted interventions. By integrating previously separate data sources, AI4Life can improve evidence generation, support early identification of relevant determinants and contribute to more effective strategies for reducing preventable mortality and improving population health outcomes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Audit +: CHBV artificial intelligence engine and business intelligence system
source_description: Audit + addresses the need to improve information management, analytical capacity and decision support at the Hospital Centre of Baixo Vouga. Hospitals generate large volumes of clinical, administrative and operational data, but these data must be transformed into usable intelligence to support management, quality improvement and service planning. The project is led by the Hospital Centre of Baixo Vouga in partnership with the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Porto and CINTESIS. Its objective is to develop an artificial intelligence engine and business intelligence system that can help the hospital make better use of its data and strengthen evidence-informed governance. The emerging technology implementation combines advanced analytical components with business intelligence capabilities. At conceptual level, the system is intended to collect, organise and analyse hospital data, producing indicators, insights and decision-support outputs for managers and clinical or operational teams. The artificial intelligence engine can support the identification of patterns or anomalies, while the business intelligence layer makes results accessible through structured reporting and visualisation. The expected impact is improved hospital management, better monitoring of performance and greater capacity to support decisions with timely and reliable information. By integrating analytical intelligence into hospital governance, Audit + can contribute to more efficient processes, improved service quality and stronger institutional capacity for data-driven healthcare management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: University Hospital Center of São João, EPE (UHCSJ)
title: Inpatient AI Model Investigation for Procedure and Diagnostic Coding (CliKode)
source_description: CliKode tackles the administrative and clinical-documentation challenge of assigning accurate diagnostic and procedure codes to inpatient episodes. Hospital coding based on the ICD-10 classification system is essential for clinical reporting, financing, statistics and service management, but it requires substantial human effort and continuous monitoring to ensure consistency and completeness. The University Hospital Centre of São João, EPE, developed this project to improve the quality and efficiency of coding processes, particularly where coders must interpret large volumes of clinical text and keep coding practices aligned with evolving rules. The emerging technology implementation focuses on the automatic generation of ICD-10 diagnoses and procedure codes from clinical texts. At conceptual level, the system analyses unstructured clinical documentation, identifies relevant medical concepts and maps them to standardised ICD-10 categories. It is also designed to remain up to date over time, supporting the adaptation of coding outputs as classifications, clinical practices or documentation patterns evolve. The expected impact is higher coding quality, including an increase in the average number of coded diagnoses and procedures, and a reduction in the monitoring structure required for the codification process. By decreasing the time and number of activities dedicated to coding supervision, CliKode can reduce pressure on specialised human resources, improve hospital data quality and strengthen the reliability of administrative and clinical information.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: IPOSCORE - Predict complications from surgical treatment and prognosis definition in cancer patients
source_description: IPOSCORE responds to the need to improve risk assessment and prognosis definition for cancer patients undergoing surgical treatment. Surgical oncology involves complex decisions in which clinicians must consider patient profiles, disease characteristics and clinical data to estimate the likelihood of complications and anticipate disease progression. The project aims to support more informed clinical decision-making by identifying relevant links between patient characteristics and outcomes, including diagnostic and prognostic markers, progression rates and complication risks. The emerging technology implementation consists of a knowledge-discovery system integrating data-mining algorithms and predictive modelling techniques. At conceptual level, the system analyses patient profiles and clinical datasets to identify patterns associated with post-surgical complications in cancer patients. It also supports the exploration of relationships between disease markers, clinical trajectories and patient-specific risk factors. These models can help transform heterogeneous clinical information into structured evidence for prognosis and treatment planning. The expected impact is improved ability to anticipate complications, better definition of patient prognosis and stronger support for personalised clinical management. By identifying high-risk patients earlier, IPOSCORE can help clinicians plan follow-up, allocate resources and adapt interventions more effectively. The case is particularly relevant for public healthcare settings seeking to improve oncology outcomes through data-driven risk stratification and more precise use of available clinical information.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Instituto Português do Sangue e da Transplantação (IPST)
title: LAIfeBlood - Artificial Intelligence for Blood Management
source_description: LAIfeBlood addresses the operational challenge of improving the efficiency and resilience of Portugal’s blood supply chain. The Instituto Português do Sangue e da Transplantação is the public authority responsible for the collection and regulation of blood donation and transplantation at national level, including the quality and safety of donation, procurement, processing, storage, preservation and distribution of human blood, blood components, organs, tissues and human-origin cells. Because blood is scarce and perishable, effective planning is essential to avoid shortages, minimise wastage and use collection teams and resources efficiently. The emerging technology implementation focuses on extracting temporal and geographical patterns from historical collection and transfusion data, developing predictive models for expected collections and transfusions across different time periods and regions, and creating software tools to optimise national collection planning. At conceptual level, the system combines forecasting, optimisation and dynamic supply-chain management to help IPST plan collection events according to resource availability and demand expectations. The expected impact is improved blood-service effectiveness, reduced wastage and more efficient daily inventory rebalancing. The project also aims to generate implementable policies for IPST, strengthening national capacity to manage collections, allocate teams and respond to changing demand. By supporting evidence-based planning, LAIfeBlood can improve the reliability, scalability and sustainability of blood supply operations in Portugal.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Modelling, Prediction and Decision in the Context of Jurisprudence
source_description: This pilot project addresses the need to support magistrates in managing legal information more efficiently and reaching conclusions more rapidly when handling inquiries or documents submitted by lawyers. Judicial decision-making requires the analysis of previous court decisions, legal arguments and procedural documents, which can be time-consuming and may slow access to justice for citizens. The Ministry of Justice use case aims to provide magistrates with an additional analytical tool that helps them consult relevant jurisprudence and process incoming legal material more effectively. The emerging technology implementation uses past court decisions as a knowledge base for decision support. At conceptual level, the system analyses judicial texts and identifies relevant patterns, precedents or similarities that may assist magistrates when examining new inquiries or documents. It is not intended to replace judicial discretion, but to improve access to structured information and reduce the time needed to locate and interpret comparable cases. The expected impact is faster handling of legal materials, more efficient judicial workflows and improved responsiveness of the justice system. By enabling magistrates to reach well-supported conclusions more quickly, the project can contribute to shorter processing times and better service to citizens. The case is relevant as an example of how data-driven tools may support legal professionals while preserving the central role of human legal judgement.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SIAP - Artificial Intelligence System for detection and warning of risks on Heritage
source_description: Cultural heritage sites face growing risks from environmental stress, structural degradation, and climate-related impacts, while heritage authorities operate with limited inspection resources. The SIAP project was developed to strengthen preventive conservation by enabling earlier identification of risks affecting historical structures. Stakeholders include regional cultural heritage authorities, conservation professionals, research institutions, and local governments. The objective is to improve supervision efficiency, prioritise interventions, and reduce long-term restoration costs. The system combines sensor-based monitoring of physical and environmental parameters—such as vibration, humidity, and temperature—with advanced data-processing tools to analyse trends and detect early warning signals. Sensor data is continuously collected from monitored sites and processed through analytical models that identify deviations from normal behaviour. Alerts are generated when risk thresholds are exceeded, supporting targeted inspections and maintenance planning. The architecture is designed to integrate monitoring data with heritage management workflows and expert assessments. Public sources describe SIAP as a research-driven pilot demonstrated in collaboration between regional authorities and academic partners. While no evidence of nationwide deployment has been reported, the project has shown potential to enhance heritage protection, reduce emergency interventions, and support more sustainable conservation strategies through continuous, data-informed monitoring.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Decoding the Legislation
source_description: Decoding the Legislation addresses the difficulty citizens face when trying to understand and consult legal texts. Legislation is often complex, technical and difficult to navigate, creating barriers to access to rights and obligations. The project sought to facilitate citizen consultation of legal information by improving how legislation from the Diário da República Eletrónico can be searched and interpreted. The selected case studies were Consumer Rights Legislation and the Retirement Statute, both areas where citizens may need practical answers to specific legal questions. The emerging technology implementation involved the creation of repositories containing data sources and metadata from the Diário da República Eletrónico, combined with natural language processing tools. At conceptual level, legal attributes were transformed into code language, and a web application was developed to allow intelligent queries on a given law. A proof of concept demonstrated an intelligent search mechanism through which citizens could ask questions about selected legislative sets and receive automatic answers. The expected impact is improved accessibility of legislation, a better user experience for citizens and reduced friction in finding relevant legal information. By making legal consultation more intuitive, the project can support transparency, legal empowerment and more efficient interaction between citizens and public legal-information systems. It also provides a reusable model for transforming complex legal repositories into citizen-oriented digital services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: IRIS – Application of Artificial Intelligence Techniques in the Supreme Court of Justice
source_description: IRIS addresses the challenge of analysing, summarising and disseminating court decisions within the Supreme Court of Justice. Judicial decisions are complex documents that require careful study by legal professionals, but they are also increasingly relevant to citizens, researchers and other non-specialist users who need understandable access to legal information. The project has two main objectives: to develop automatic summarisation approaches for court decisions and to create a representation of judicial proceedings that can be browsed in a way that supports the decision process. The emerging technology implementation focuses on text-analysis and summarisation techniques applied to judicial documents. At conceptual level, the system is designed to generate both technical summaries, useful for legal study, processing and dissemination, and summaries that are more understandable for non-technical audiences. It also aims to represent the key elements of judicial proceedings in a structured, browsable format, making it easier to explore complex case materials. The expected impact is improved efficiency in analysing court decisions, better dissemination of jurisprudence and stronger support for judicial decision-making. By reducing the burden of navigating lengthy and complex documents, IRIS can enhance access to legal knowledge, improve usability for different user groups and support a more transparent and efficient justice system.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BALCAT – Project on ballistics analysis
source_description: BALCAT addresses the need for faster and more reliable access to information in serious-crime investigations involving firearms. In such cases, collected evidence and information about a weapon’s owner or registration status can be critical for investigative progress. Police authorities require rapid access to structured, accurate and searchable data so that forensic ballistics analysis can be connected with administrative information on weapons. The project, linked to the Agência para a Modernização Administrativa, aimed to create a database for ballistics forensic analysis that would make information on weapon registration and ownership more easily accessible to competent authorities. The emerging technology implementation consisted of a digital database and analytical tool supporting the identification of weapon-related information from available records. At conceptual level, the system links evidence from an investigation with stored data on weapons, owners and registration details, allowing police authorities to retrieve relevant information and analysis more quickly. The expected impact is a substantial reduction in the time needed to access ballistic and registration information, with authorities able to obtain relevant outputs almost immediately. This can improve investigative efficiency, support faster decision-making and strengthen the quality of forensic support in serious-crime cases. BALCAT therefore provides operational value by transforming dispersed weapon-related information into a more accessible and actionable resource for scientific police work.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MEData - AI tools to define a strategy for predicting the behavior of Measurement Instruments
source_description: MEData addresses the need to improve how public administration monitors and anticipates the behaviour of measurement instruments. Measurement instruments are relevant to regulatory, technical and inspection activities because their reliability can affect the quality of controls, certifications and administrative decisions. The available description indicates that the project, linked to the Agência para a Modernização Administrativa, aimed to develop artificial intelligence tools to define a strategy for predicting how such instruments behave over time. The operational problem is therefore the need to move from reactive monitoring or periodic checks towards a more anticipatory approach that can identify potential deviations, deterioration or performance issues before they affect service quality. The emerging technology implementation consists of analytical tools designed to model the behaviour of measurement instruments using available operational or historical data. At conceptual level, the system would use predictive modelling to identify patterns, estimate future behaviour and support decisions on maintenance, verification or monitoring priorities. Given the limited public information available, the exact models, datasets and integration arrangements are not specified. The expected impact is improved planning, more reliable measurement processes and better allocation of technical resources. By supporting earlier identification of possible issues, MEData can contribute to higher-quality administrative and regulatory operations, reduce the risk of failures in measurement-dependent processes and strengthen the evidence base for managing technical assets across the public sector.

title: Artificial Intelligence Prototype-SAF
source_description: Artificial Intelligence Prototype-SAF appears to be an exploratory initiative linked to the Agência para a Modernização Administrativa, but the available information is limited to the project title and does not specify the public service area, institutional user group or operational process targeted. On this basis, the use case can be described only cautiously as a prototype intended to test how advanced analytical tools could support a public-administration function associated with SAF. The business problem is therefore framed as the need to explore whether automation, data analysis or decision-support methods can improve an administrative process, reduce manual workload or strengthen evidence-based decision-making. The emerging technology implementation is identified only as an artificial intelligence prototype. At conceptual level, such a prototype would normally involve testing data-processing, pattern-recognition or decision-support capabilities on a defined administrative dataset, assessing whether outputs are accurate, useful and operationally feasible. However, the specific techniques, data sources, integration with existing systems and intended users are not available from the information provided. The impact and results should therefore be recorded as unconfirmed. The likely value of the prototype lies in experimentation, proof-of-concept development and assessment of whether the approach could be scaled or integrated into public-sector workflows. For observatory maintenance, this case should be flagged as requiring further validation, particularly to identify the meaning of SAF, the responsible body, the functional domain and any evidence of implementation beyond prototype stage.

title: PredictERPgDoc - Integration of ERP and IPB's docs management system for predictive decision making
source_description: PredictERPgDoc addresses the challenge of improving predictive decision-making by connecting structured enterprise resource planning data with document-management information at the Polytechnic Institute of Bragança. Public institutions often hold operational, financial, administrative and documentary data in separate systems, which limits their ability to generate integrated insights for management and planning. The project, linked to the Agência para a Modernização Administrativa, aims to integrate the ERP environment with IPB’s document management system so that institutional decisions can be supported by a more complete view of available information. The emerging technology implementation consists of system integration combined with predictive analytics. At conceptual level, the solution would connect transactional data from the ERP system with metadata and content from document-management workflows, enabling models to identify patterns, forecast needs or support decisions across administrative processes. Such integration can help transform dispersed institutional records into structured inputs for management intelligence. The exact algorithms, datasets and operational modules are not specified in the source description, so the technical implementation should be treated as high-level. The expected impact is improved information availability, stronger organisational intelligence and more timely decision-making. By reducing fragmentation between administrative systems, PredictERPgDoc can support more coherent planning, improve the traceability of decisions and enable public higher-education managers to use data more strategically in operational and institutional governance.

title: GeADAPTalks – Intel service
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: GeADAPTalks addresses the need to improve the availability and quality of services supporting participants in evaluation processes. In public administration, evaluation activities often involve multiple stakeholders, recurring information requests and the need for timely guidance across different stages of a process. The available description indicates that the project applies artificial intelligence tools to improve the service and keep it continuously available in its various aspects for participants. The objective can therefore be understood as enhancing support, responsiveness and accessibility for users involved in evaluation procedures. The emerging technology implementation consists of an intelligent service layer that can assist participants by providing information, guidance or interaction capabilities linked to the evaluation process. At conceptual level, this may involve automated responses, knowledge retrieval, process guidance and service-support functions based on structured information about evaluation rules, procedures and user needs. However, the source does not specify the models used, the data sources, the public body responsible for the evaluation process or the degree of system integration, so these elements should remain unconfirmed. The expected impact is improved user experience, greater continuity of service and reduced pressure on administrative staff who would otherwise respond manually to recurring queries. By making service support more available and consistent, GeADAPTalks could contribute to more efficient evaluation processes, but further validation is required to confirm deployment status, users and measurable results.

title: PAGIRAA - Analytical Platform for the Intelligent Management of Water Supply Networks
source_description: Water utilities and public administrations need reliable operational intelligence to manage supply networks, reduce losses and anticipate service problems across complex infrastructure. PAGIRAA was conceived as an analytical platform for the intelligent management of water supply networks, supporting more informed decisions on system performance, resource use and operational anomalies. The context was public-sector digital transformation in Portugal, with the aim of applying advanced analytics to a critical municipal and regional service. Water networks generate large volumes of operational data from meters, network assets, consumption records and maintenance activity, but this information is often fragmented across systems and difficult to translate into timely management decisions. The platform was designed to consolidate and analyse such data so that authorities and operators could better understand water-flow behaviour, identify irregularities and support planning. At a conceptual level, the solution would combine data integration, analytical modelling, visualisation and decision-support functionality for water-network management. Its expected value was improved efficiency, better detection of network problems, stronger evidence for investment and maintenance decisions, and more resilient management of a scarce public resource. Although the available source provides limited operational detail, the case fits within a wider pattern of using data analytics to modernise essential infrastructure and support more proactive public-service management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LAB BUPi - Creation of the Single Counter Laboratory Simplified Cadastral Information System
source_description: LAB BUPi seeks to resolve the long-standing challenge of identifying land structure and ownership in rural territories in Portugal. Incomplete or fragmented cadastral information can create difficulties for land registration, territorial planning, property management and interaction between citizens and public administration. The reform consists of a pilot project for a simplified national cadastral information system, combined with the entry into operation of the Land Cover Monitoring System and the development of the BUPi digital land registry platform. The objective is to aggregate the information necessary for property registration and provide citizens with a physical and virtual counter that simplifies interaction with public services in the land-register domain. The emerging technology implementation centres on a digital platform using geo-referenced property information. At conceptual level, BUPi consolidates cadastral, registration and land-related data in a single service environment, allowing citizens and authorities to identify, record and manage rural properties more effectively. The reform also establishes the legal framework needed to operationalise the rural property registry and land-cover monitoring investment. The expected impact is improved accuracy and accessibility of property information, easier registration procedures, stronger territorial knowledge and better interaction between citizens and the administration. By combining digital services with geo-referenced data and a simplified counter model, LAB BUPi can improve scalability, reduce administrative barriers and support more coherent land-governance policies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MOPREVIS - Modeling and prediction of traffic accidents in the district of Setúbal
source_description: MOPREVIS addresses the need to improve road-safety planning in the district of Setúbal by understanding where traffic accidents occur, why they happen and which locations are most likely to present future risks. The project aimed to create an information system combining several sources of information on accidents, traffic intensity and climatic conditions. The objective was to classify accident hotspots, identify determinant factors influencing the occurrence and severity of accidents, draw profiles of individuals involved, compare accident types such as collisions, pedestrian accidents and scraping incidents, and construct predictive models for both the number and severity of accidents. The emerging technology implementation consists of a digital platform with distributed architecture for storage, large-scale data processing and management. It includes a data-acquisition module that extracts information from accident documents using natural language processing and artificial intelligence techniques, as well as interfaces for automatic data collection from other systems, including traffic-intensity data in adjacent streets and climate data. An information-retrieval module supports access to the processed results. The expected impact is improved capacity for evidence-based traffic-safety interventions, more accurate identification of high-risk locations and better prioritisation of prevention measures. By integrating multiple data sources and predictive models, MOPREVIS can help authorities anticipate accident risks, allocate resources more effectively and design targeted actions to reduce accident frequency and severity.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Instituto de Engenharia de Sistemas e Computadores, Investigação e Desenvolvimento em Lisboa (INESC ID/INESC/IST/ULisboa)
title: iLU: Advanced Learning in Urban Data with Situational Context for Optimizing Mobility in Cities
source_description: The iLU project addresses the challenge of optimising urban mobility in Lisbon by making better use of heterogeneous data stored in the city’s Intelligent Management Platform. Urban traffic management requires real-time understanding of mobility conditions, but relevant data are often distributed across different sources and may not be systematically connected with situational context. The project aims to consolidate multiple mobility data sources in the Plataforma de Gestão Inteligente de Lisboa, ensure their real-time updatability, discover actionable spatio-temporal patterns and anticipate congestion. The emerging technology implementation combines advanced predictive modelling with deep reinforcement learning. At conceptual level, the system analyses heterogeneous mobility data to detect non-trivial correlations between road traffic and contextual variables, forecast traffic congestion and support real-time mobility decisions. Deep reinforcement learning is intended to help condition city traffic positively by supporting interventions such as traffic-light control and road-message panels. The system therefore connects data integration, pattern discovery, prediction and operational decision support within an urban mobility-management environment. The expected impact is improved traffic anticipation, more responsive mobility management and better use of city infrastructure. By enabling real-time, data-driven interventions, iLU can contribute to reduced congestion, improved reliability of urban travel, more efficient traffic-control operations and stronger strategic capacity for mobility planning in Lisbon.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: PAMWater: Analytical and Predictive Models for Optimization of Multimunicipal Water Systems
source_description: PAMWater addresses the need to improve the efficiency, resilience and sustainability of multimunicipal water systems. Water utilities and public decision-makers must manage complex infrastructures where demand, supply, operational constraints and environmental pressures vary over time and across territories. Inefficient planning can increase costs, reduce service reliability and limit the capacity of water systems to respond to stress events or long-term sustainability objectives. The project, led by the University of Minho, aims to create a predictive and analytical platform that supports decision-makers by giving them access to a broad set of descriptive and predictive information. The emerging technology implementation consists of deep-learning models embedded in a decision-support platform for multimunicipal water systems. At conceptual level, the platform would process operational, temporal and system-level data to identify patterns, forecast relevant variables and provide analytical outputs for planning and optimisation. The use of predictive models can support decisions on resource allocation, infrastructure management, demand anticipation and operational performance. The expected impact is improved decision-making, stronger system resilience and more sustainable management of water resources. By consolidating descriptive and predictive information in a single platform, PAMWater can help public and utility stakeholders anticipate operational needs, reduce inefficiencies and improve the reliability and scalability of water-system management across multiple municipalities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MATISSE - Bivalve health: predictive and early warning system
source_description: MATISSE addresses the environmental, public-health and economic risks created by harmful algal blooms and shellfish biotoxin contamination. Under favourable climate and oceanographic conditions, toxin-producing microalgae can proliferate, reach high concentrations in seawater, accumulate in shellfish and threaten seafood consumers. These events can also cause significant economic losses for shellfish farmers when harvesting or production must be restricted. The project, linked to Universidade Nova de Lisboa, responds to the need for more effective tools that help shellfish producers and public environmental authorities anticipate harmful algal bloom events and manage contamination risks. The emerging technology implementation focuses on statistical and machine-learning forecasting tools for predicting harmful algal blooms and shellfish biotoxin contamination. The reviewed approaches include autoregressive models, support vector machines, random forests, probabilistic graphical models and artificial neural networks, with more complex models increasingly supported by multi-source data. At conceptual level, these models analyse environmental, oceanographic and biological information to forecast bloom events or contamination risks and support early warning. The expected impact is improved decision-making for harvesting, production management and mitigation measures. By providing earlier and more accurate warnings, MATISSE can help reduce production losses, protect consumer health and strengthen the evidence base used by governmental agencies with environmental responsibilities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Associação do Instituto Superior Técnico para a Investigação e o Desenvolvimento
title: GrassData - Identification, verification and quantification of CO2 sequestration in pastures
source_description: GrassData addresses the need to monitor and verify land-management practices that improve soil protection and carbon sequestration in pastures. Public authorities and environmental programmes require reliable evidence to confirm whether declared practices, such as bush management or the existence of harrows, are actually being implemented and producing the expected environmental benefits. Manual verification can be costly, time-consuming and difficult to scale across extensive pasture areas. The project, led by the Associação do Instituto Superior Técnico para a Investigação e o Desenvolvimento, aims to develop algorithms that support monitoring, verification and compliance assessment in relation to soil and carbon-related practices. The emerging technology implementation consists of automated algorithms designed to verify the results of pasture-management practices that contribute to carbon sequestration. At conceptual level, the system would analyse relevant data on land conditions, management activities and environmental indicators to detect whether required practices are present and to support quantification of CO2 sequestration outcomes. The exact datasets and model architecture are not specified in the source description, so the implementation should be understood as an algorithmic monitoring and verification capability. The expected impact is more efficient compliance control, stronger evidence for climate and land-management policies, and improved capacity to scale verification across pasture areas. By automating parts of the monitoring process, GrassData can reduce administrative burden and support more credible environmental reporting.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-4-MUFF - AI for the management of the degree of readiness in urban firefighting
source_description: AI-4-MUFF addresses the challenge of improving strategic decision-making for urban firefighting. Fire services must maintain an appropriate degree of readiness while facing uncertainty regarding incident occurrence, resource availability, operational priorities and urban risk conditions. Decisions on preparedness and response capacity need to be based on empirical evidence and must balance multiple objectives, such as response time, coverage, resource use and operational resilience. The project, led by NOVA.ID.FCT, intends to develop a strategic decision-support system for combating urban fires. The emerging technology implementation combines machine-learning techniques, multi-objective optimisation models and an agent-based simulation environment. At conceptual level, machine-learning methods can be used to extract patterns from historical or operational fire-service data, while optimisation models support the allocation of resources across competing objectives. Agent-based simulation allows the modelling of interactions between units, incidents, urban environments and decision rules, enabling the testing of different preparedness scenarios. The expected impact is improved evidence-based planning for urban firefighting, better readiness management and stronger capacity to evaluate strategic options before they are implemented. By integrating prediction, optimisation and simulation, AI-4-MUFF can support more efficient resource deployment, increase service reliability and improve the ability of fire authorities to respond effectively to urban fire risks.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Associação do Instituto Superior Técnico para a Investigação e o Desenvolvimento
title: RELIABLE - Building occupant risk warning panel during extreme weather events
source_description: RELIABLE addresses the need to protect building occupants during extreme weather events, particularly heat and cold waves. Such events can create significant health risks, especially for vulnerable populations, and public authorities need timely, spatially detailed information to identify where risks are concentrated. Conventional warning systems may not provide sufficiently granular information on building-level or localised exposure, limiting the ability to target prevention and response measures. The project, led by the Associação do Instituto Superior Técnico para a Investigação e o Desenvolvimento, aims to develop a public geographic dashboard providing real-time information and high spatial resolution on the health risks faced by building occupants during extreme weather events. The emerging technology implementation consists of a geographic dashboard supported by real-time data processing and spatial risk modelling. At conceptual level, the system would combine environmental, geographic and building-related information to estimate occupant health risk during heat and cold waves and present it through an accessible public interface. The expected impact is improved situational awareness for authorities and citizens, more targeted risk communication and better prioritisation of preventive measures during extreme weather. By making high-resolution risk information available in real time, RELIABLE can support public-health preparedness, improve the user experience of warning services and strengthen resilience to climate-related hazards.

title: IVDP DATA+ - AI models for processing relevant data for the economy of the Douro Wine Region.
source_description: IVDP DATA+ addresses the need to strengthen data-informed decision-making for the Douro Wine Region, an economically and culturally significant territory where public and sectoral authorities must manage complex information on production, markets and regional dynamics. The project is based on a new model of experimentation developed in close collaboration with the scientific community, with the aim of promoting knowledge transfer and adopting advanced tools and techniques from artificial intelligence and data science. The objective is to support decisions by processing existing data more effectively and transforming them into useful analytical insights for the region’s economy. The emerging technology implementation consists of artificial intelligence models and data-science methods applied to relevant datasets held or used in the Douro wine-sector context. At conceptual level, the models process existing information to identify patterns, generate forecasts or support scenario-based understanding of variables affecting the regional wine economy. The source description does not specify the exact datasets, models or operational modules, so the implementation should be recorded at a high level. The expected impact is improved analytical capacity, stronger collaboration between public institutions and scientific actors, and better evidence for strategic decisions affecting the Douro Wine Region. By creating a data-driven experimentation model, IVDP DATA+ can support more informed governance, improve planning and contribute to the competitiveness and resilience of the regional economy.

title: i-Territory – Intelligent Modeling of Territorial Access to Services of General Interest
source_description: Ensuring equitable access to services of general interest—such as healthcare, education, transport, and administrative services—remains a major challenge in territories affected by demographic change and geographic disparities. The i-Territory initiative, promoted by AMA, seeks to improve how public authorities understand and plan territorial service accessibility. Stakeholders include central and local administrations, regional planners, and service providers. The objective is to support evidence-based territorial planning that reduces inequalities and improves service coverage. The initiative relies on the integration of geospatial data, demographic statistics, service location data, and mobility information into territorial analysis models. These models simulate accessibility scenarios, identify underserved areas, and assess the impact of policy options such as service relocation or new infrastructure. The system is designed to interoperate with public-sector data platforms and geographic information systems, enabling scenario analysis rather than operational decision automation. Public documentation positions i-Territory as an enabling framework and pilot rather than a fully deployed national system. Its value lies in improving analytical capacity, supporting more transparent planning decisions, and helping administrations anticipate territorial needs, even though large-scale operational adoption has not yet been publicly confirmed.

title: SegnalaCI - Transparent management of citizen reports about City status
source_description: SegnalaCI provides the Municipality of Genoa with a digital channel for managing citizen reports on urban problems, such as road damage, waste collection issues or other maintenance needs affecting the city. The administrative challenge is to ensure that reports from residents are received, assigned to the competent office, resolved and communicated back to the citizen in a transparent and traceable manner. The stakeholders include residents, municipal departments, technical offices, maintenance teams, city administrators and service managers responsible for urban quality. The objective is to improve the management of citizen feedback and use the resulting information to support better staff and resource planning. The implementation allows the administration to take charge of a report, notify the relevant office, manage the intervention and inform the citizen of the outcome once the procedure is completed. Machine-learning techniques are used to process the data gathered through reports and provide a smart dashboard for city administrators. At a conceptual level, the system combines citizen-report intake, workflow routing, notification mechanisms, data classification, dashboard analytics and planning support. The expected impact is more transparent handling of local problems, quicker assignment of issues to responsible units, improved communication with residents and better evidence for allocating municipal resources. By analysing recurring reports and operational needs, the municipality can move from reactive case handling towards more informed urban-service management.

organization: City Council of Sant Feliu de Llobregat
title: Brain4it : monitoring the SmartCity
source_description: Brain4it was developed by the City Council of Sant Feliu de Llobregat as an open-source expert-system platform for managing Smart City infrastructure and supporting Internet of Things applications. The operational problem is that connected urban infrastructures generate diverse data flows and require remote, flexible and secure management across multiple municipal systems. City administrations need tools that can automate infrastructure control, support data governance and adapt to new use cases without relying on fragmented or closed technical environments. The stakeholders include the City Council, municipal technical teams, Smart City operators, residents and developers working with urban IoT services. The platform runs as a network service and provides a REST API, enabling remote control and programming of the City-OS platform. It uses a functional language designed to facilitate the implementation of expert systems and machine-learning applications. Conceptually, Brain4it supports modular automation, rules-based reasoning, IoT integration, infrastructure monitoring, security management and adaptable service development. Its open-source character allows the municipality and wider developer community to reuse and extend the platform for different Smart City needs. The expected impact is more efficient infrastructure management, easier integration of IoT services, reduced dependence on proprietary solutions and greater flexibility in developing new municipal applications. By combining expert-system logic with programmable interfaces, Brain4it strengthens the city’s capacity to manage urban systems in a scalable and adaptable way.
