title: Deep Gravity: the algorithm that explains how people move
source_description: Deep Gravity addresses the limitations of traditional mobility-flow prediction models used to estimate how people move between places, both on foot and by vehicle. The conventional gravitational model, inspired by Newton’s law of universal gravitation, estimates flows between two locations as proportional to population and inversely proportional to distance. In practice, this approach is often inaccurate because it relies on only two variables and cannot capture complex relationships between the characteristics of places. The Institute of Science and Information Technologies of the Italian National Research Council, together with the Bruno Kessler Foundation and Argonne National Laboratory, developed Deep Gravity to improve mobility prediction. The emerging technology implementation extends the gravitational model by incorporating multiple variables that describe points of interest in each location, such as restaurants, hotels, hospitals and streets, and by using deep learning to capture complex relationships among these variables. At conceptual level, the algorithm learns how the attractiveness and structure of places influence mobility flows, improving predictions beyond distance and population alone. The expected impact is more accurate mobility-flow estimation, which can support public authorities in transport planning, urban policy, infrastructure design and emergency management. By better explaining how people move, Deep Gravity can improve decision-making in mobility-related public services and provide a more scalable analytical basis for understanding urban and regional movement patterns.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Hospital G.U. Gregorio Marañón | Madrid, Spain
title: FAITH - monitoring mental health with Artificial Intelligence - SPAIN Pilot
source_description: The FAITH Spain pilot addresses the need to improve aftercare for people who have undergone cancer treatment, with particular attention to mental health and quality of life. Cancer survivorship can involve depression, psychological distress and unmet aftercare needs that may not always be detected during routine clinical follow-up. The Spanish pilot, led by Hospital General Universitario Gregorio Marañón in Madrid, focuses on 100 breast-cancer survivors. Its objective is to monitor patients after treatment, evaluate their quality of life and identify possible care needs so that healthcare professionals can provide more personalised interventions. The emerging technology implementation consists of an artificial intelligence application designed to identify and analyse markers associated with depression in people treated for cancer. At conceptual level, the system uses patient monitoring data and related quality-of-life indicators to detect patterns that may signal psychological or cognitive disorders. These insights can support doctors and other healthcare professionals in defining protocols, standards of care and early-intervention pathways. The expected impact is earlier detection of aftercare needs, better personalisation of support and improved patient quality of life. By helping clinicians identify patients who may require additional follow-up, FAITH can strengthen survivorship care, improve continuity between clinical treatment and psychosocial support, and provide evidence for more systematic mental-health monitoring in oncology services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown | Lisbon, Portugal
title: FAITH - monitoring mental health with Artificial Intelligence - PORTUGAL Pilot
source_description: The FAITH Portugal pilot addresses the challenge of supporting the mental health and quality of life of lung-cancer patients during and after oncological treatment. Psychological distress, cognitive changes and broader psychosocial needs can affect patients’ recovery and everyday functioning, but these needs may be difficult to identify consistently without structured follow-up. The Champalimaud Clinical Centre in Lisbon participates as a clinical partner and will involve 100 ambulatory, community-dwelling lung-cancer patients of any type with an indication for oncological treatment over a two-year period. The objective is to monitor patients for 12 months after their first appointment and offer intelligent post-cancer support. The emerging technology implementation consists of an artificial intelligence application that identifies and analyses depression markers in people who have undergone cancer treatment. In the Portuguese pilot, patients receive psychological and cognitive assessments through psychosocial questionnaires, neuropsychological testing and other relevant constructs. At conceptual level, the system uses these data to detect patterns that may indicate aftercare needs or risks to mental well-being. The expected impact is more proactive and personalised post-cancer support, improved early detection of psychological or cognitive difficulties, and better evidence for care planning. By embedding structured monitoring into oncology follow-up, FAITH can support clinicians in improving continuity of care and enhancing quality of life for lung-cancer patients.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FAITH - monitoring mental health with Artificial Intelligence - IRELAND Pilot
source_description: The FAITH Ireland pilot addresses the need to integrate mental-health and well-being monitoring into cancer care for patients undergoing treatment or who have completed treatment. UPMC Waterford is the main Irish pilot test-trial site, focusing on breast-cancer patients as the selected use case and target group. The clinical rationale is that patient well-being and mental health are as important as access to advanced oncology care, particularly when patients may require follow-up from oncologists, general practitioners or local cancer-support services. The objective is to use FAITH to identify patients who would benefit from additional care and ensure that support needs are detected in a timely manner. The emerging technology implementation consists of an artificial intelligence application that identifies and analyses depression markers in people treated for cancer. At conceptual level, the tool processes patient-related information collected through monitoring and assessment to identify signals that may indicate psychological distress or aftercare needs. These outputs can help clinicians decide whether a patient should receive follow-up from the oncology team, a GP or a local Cancer Support Centre. The expected impact is improved identification of patients requiring psychosocial or clinical follow-up, better integration of mental-health support into oncology pathways and a more personalised care experience. By supporting earlier referral decisions, FAITH can contribute to more holistic cancer survivorship care.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: CSI Piemonte (Inhouse ICT of Regione Piemonte)
title: SAFERS - Structured Approaches for Forest fire Emergencies in Resilient Societies
source_description: SAFERS addresses the growing challenge of forest fires, whose impact has increased in connection with climate change and which damage ecosystems, communities, productive activities and air quality through greenhouse-gas and pollutant emissions. Public authorities, emergency services, volunteers and citizens require better information to prevent, monitor and manage forest-fire emergencies. The project, involving CSI Piemonte as the in-house ICT body of Regione Piemonte, aims to develop an innovative platform over three years to improve forest-fire management and reduce the impact of future events. The emerging technology implementation consists of a Big Data platform combined with information systems based on artificial intelligence. The platform uses multiple data sources, including Copernicus Sentinel satellite data, ad hoc monitoring cameras, social media, and mobile-phone inputs from professional users, volunteers and citizens. Citizens and field actors can report observed conditions through chatbots, enriching real-time situational awareness. At conceptual level, the system integrates earth observation, user-generated reports, sensor data and emergency-management workflows to support detection, assessment and response. The expected impact is improved forest-fire preparedness, faster access to operational information, better coordination among actors and stronger capacity to manage emergencies. By combining satellite monitoring with local observations and automated analysis, SAFERS can improve scalability, responsiveness and resilience in forest-fire governance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: CSI Piemonte (Inhouse ICT of Regione Piemonte)
title: AI Autonomation - Automatic classification tools and integration with Robot Process Automation (RPA)
source_description: Public administrations receive large volumes of email and document-based requests that must be routed to the correct office before any substantive work can begin. CSI Piemonte developed an AI Automation prototype to combine automatic classification tools with Robotic Process Automation, using the regional car-tax management service as a concrete test case. The operational problem was that emails arriving in public-service channels required manual reading, categorisation and forwarding, creating delays and repetitive workload. The implementation uses text classification to sort incoming emails according to their content and direct them to the relevant offices. Where the content and process conditions allow, the system can also trigger RPA workflows so that routine responses or administrative actions are handled automatically. At a conceptual level, the solution combines natural language processing, classification models, workflow routing and robotic process execution. The expected impact is faster email handling, fewer manual sorting tasks, improved consistency of routing and greater capacity for staff to focus on exceptions or complex cases. The use case is framed by CSI Piemonte as research and development work from 2019, centred on a prototype for the regional vehicle-tax service. It demonstrates how relatively narrow administrative processes can be automated by pairing AI classification with process automation rather than trying to replace entire services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: CSI Piemonte (Inhouse ICT of Regione Piemonte)
title: Genome representation and artificial intelligence
source_description: The diagnosis and treatment of rare diseases are often hindered by the complexity and volume of genomic data, which require specialised expertise and advanced analytical capabilities to translate raw sequencing results into clinically meaningful insights. Healthcare professionals, geneticists and researchers face challenges in rapidly interpreting whole-genome data to support personalised diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making, particularly in nephrology and other rare disease domains. To address this need, CSI Piemonte, in collaboration with the University of Turin (Departments of Medical Sciences and Clinical and Biological Sciences), the ISI Foundation and GenomSys, launched a research initiative aimed at improving genomic data analysis for clinical use. The objective is to enable faster, more accurate identification of genetic variants associated with rare diseases and to support the design of targeted diagnostic and treatment pathways. The project leverages advanced genome representation techniques to encode large-scale sequencing data into structured, computationally efficient formats. Machine learning models are developed to analyse genomic variants, detect patterns linked to specific pathologies and prioritise clinically relevant mutations. The system integrates genomic databases, clinical records and specialised bioinformatics pipelines, enabling automated variant interpretation and decision support within research and clinical environments. The initiative enhances the speed and reliability of genomic analysis, reducing the time required to reach a diagnosis and improving the precision of treatment planning. By supporting personalised medicine approaches, it contributes to better clinical outcomes for rare disease patients while increasing analytical scalability and fostering collaboration between research institutions and healthcare providers.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: CSI Piemonte (Inhouse ICT of Regione Piemonte)
title: Citizen Conversational AI Platform
source_description: The Citizen Conversational AI Platform addresses the need to make digital public services more accessible through natural-language interaction. Citizens often need to navigate complex administrative information, and traditional interfaces may require users to understand service structures or search terms before finding the right answer. CSI Piemonte developed prototypes to explore how chatbots and conversational interfaces could support interaction with regional services in Piedmont. The objective was to engineer and automate bot production so that new services could be implemented quickly, while improving the effectiveness of conversations through context management and more fluid dialogue mechanisms. The emerging technology implementation consists of chatbot prototypes using conversational user-experience design, context management and artificial intelligence technologies. At conceptual level, the platform supports everyday natural-language requests, maintains elements of the current conversation, manages list references and provides refined responses. CSI Piemonte produced prototypes for searching general practitioners and paediatricians of the Piedmont Region through Alexa and Google Home, including search-refinement capabilities. The expected impact is improved user experience, faster access to information and increased scalability in the production of conversational public-service tools. By making services available through familiar voice assistants and conversational channels, the platform can reduce barriers for users, support more intuitive interaction with public administration and create reusable components for future chatbot-based services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI4EU: Boosting Europe’s artificial intelligence capacity
source_description: AI4EU addresses the strategic need to strengthen Europe’s artificial intelligence ecosystem by bringing together knowledge, algorithms, tools and resources in a common environment. European researchers, innovators, businesses and public-sector users often operate across fragmented communities, which can limit reuse, collaboration and access to technical assets. Launched in January 2019 as a €20 million European Union flagship project involving more than 70 partners across 21 countries, AI4EU aimed to unify Europe’s AI community and make capabilities more accessible to a broad range of users. The emerging technology implementation consists of a European platform designed to share expertise, knowledge, algorithms, tools and resources. At conceptual level, the platform provides an infrastructure for collaboration across research, innovation and business, enabling users to discover and reuse AI-related assets and contribute to collective work. The project was planned to run for three years, with the platform under development at the time described. The expected impact is increased European capacity in artificial intelligence, stronger collaboration across countries and sectors, and easier access to tools for organisations that may lack in-house capabilities. By consolidating resources and supporting a shared ecosystem, AI4EU can reduce duplication, promote innovation and strengthen Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in advanced digital technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DARE: Digital Environment for collaborative Alliances to Regenerate urban Ecosystems in middle-sized cities
source_description: DARE addresses the challenge of supporting urban regeneration in middle-sized cities through a citizen-centred and digitally enabled governance model. The project focuses on the Darsena area in Ravenna and aims to demonstrate an approach that can facilitate, support and accelerate the implementation and evaluation of the regeneration process, with potential replication in other European middle-sized cities. The policy challenge is not only technical, but also organisational: public administration must act as an enabler of collaboration between citizens, economic actors and strategic policy objectives. The emerging technology implementation consists of a three-layer digital environment composed of a data-management platform, an editorial content-management layer and a virtual-realm presentation layer. At conceptual level, this environment enables the collection, organisation and presentation of information needed to activate urban actors and support collaborative decision-making. The project also introduces a process-organisers team to connect strategy, economic opportunities and citizen needs, while promoting digital culture among residents so that they can become digitally aware city changers. The expected impact is improved coordination of urban-regeneration activities, stronger citizen participation and more transparent evaluation of interventions. By combining digital infrastructure with a revised public-administration role, DARE can increase the scalability and replicability of participatory regeneration models in other European urban contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Lepida Spa (inhouse ICT of Regione Emilia Romagna)
title: RainBO (follow-up of BLUEAP Bologna Urban Environment Adaptation Plan for a resilient city)
source_description: RainBO addresses the need to improve Bologna’s resilience to severe rainfall and sudden flooding, particularly in relation to the hydrological response of small watercourses within the urban area. Extreme rainfall can create fast-moving local risks for citizens, infrastructure and municipal services, especially where watercourses react quickly to intense precipitation. As a follow-up to the BLUEAP Bologna Urban Environment Adaptation Plan, the project focuses on improving methods and tools that allow authorities to predict severe rainfall events and assess their likely impact. Lepida Spa, the in-house ICT body of Regione Emilia-Romagna, is identified as the public technology stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation consists of a monitoring and modelling system designed to forecast sudden flooding events. At conceptual level, the system combines rainfall prediction, hydrological modelling and local monitoring data to understand how small urban watercourses may respond to severe weather. These outputs can support early warning, preparedness and operational decision-making by public authorities. The expected impact is higher resilience in vulnerable urban watercourses, improved situational awareness before and during heavy rainfall, and stronger capacity to anticipate flood risks. By connecting monitoring with predictive modelling, RainBO can help authorities move from reactive emergency response towards more preventive and evidence-based management of rainfall-related urban hazards.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GAIA-X: AI-Marketplace: An Ecosystem For Artificial Intelligence
source_description: The GAIA-X AI Marketplace addresses the need to support manufacturing companies, solution providers and artificial intelligence experts in developing innovative applications for product development. Organisations seeking to apply advanced analytical tools in production contexts often face difficulties in finding appropriate partners, accessing relevant data environments and assembling reusable development components. The project establishes a digital platform that brings together AI experts, solution providers and manufacturing companies to promote joint innovation and build on existing infrastructure. Inno-focus Businessconsulting GmbH is identified as the stakeholder associated with the use case. The emerging technology implementation consists of a platform ecosystem providing essential tools for the development of AI solutions. Its core functions include an intelligent partner agency for AI use cases in production development, a data room for production-development data and a construction kit for AI development. At conceptual level, the platform supports matchmaking, data access and reusable development components, enabling actors to design and test solutions more efficiently. The expected impact is faster innovation, stronger collaboration and more scalable development of AI applications in industrial settings. By creating a structured marketplace, the use case can reduce fragmentation, facilitate knowledge exchange and support the emergence of a trusted European data and innovation ecosystem aligned with GAIA-X principles.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GAIA-X: Data Science & Machine Learning (DSML) Hub
source_description: The GAIA-X Data Science & Machine Learning Hub addresses the challenge of making public-administration data more accessible and usable for data-science and artificial intelligence applications while respecting data-protection requirements. Public-sector data are often stored in organisational silos, limiting their reuse by administrations, companies, start-ups and research institutions. The DSML Hub, associated with DataPort GmbH, aims to create a sustainable approach to the use of data science and AI in the public sector and to support innovation and value creation across the wider ecosystem. The emerging technology implementation consists of five building blocks: unlocking administrative data silos and enabling access for third parties; creating infrastructure for data science and AI with modern hardware and common software, including a DSML platform; expanding an ecosystem of start-ups, public IT service providers, regional SMEs, administrations, politics and research institutions; synchronising with GAIA-X; and implementing ten selected innovative projects in administrations and companies. At conceptual level, the Hub combines data access, technical infrastructure and ecosystem governance. The expected impact is improved reuse of public data, stronger innovation capacity and better conditions for public-sector digital transformation. By providing shared infrastructure and connecting diverse actors, the DSML Hub can reduce duplication, improve scalability and enable more evidence-based administrative services and policy applications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GAIA-X: Digital public administration – Chatbot
source_description: The GAIA-X Digital Public Administration Chatbot use case addresses the need to develop and deploy digital assistants in public administration within a legally compliant and trustworthy cloud environment. Public bodies increasingly seek to use conversational services to guide citizens, answer questions and support administrative processes, but they must ensure that data storage, processing and software components comply with public-sector requirements. The project, associated with DataPort GmbH, aims to create the basis for a cloud environment in which digital assistants can be developed and used securely by administrations. The emerging technology implementation consists of modular functional AI building blocks offered as software-as-a-service components and linked with official infrastructure for data storage and processing. At conceptual level, the solution enables administrations to combine reusable chatbot capabilities, natural-language functions and compliant cloud infrastructure rather than building each assistant from scratch. This modularity can support faster deployment and more consistent service quality across public bodies. The expected impact is improved scalability of conversational public services, reduced technical barriers for administrations and a stronger compliance basis for cloud-based digital assistants. By connecting AI components with official infrastructure, the use case can support more accessible citizen services while preserving the governance, security and legal requirements expected in public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GAIA-X: Predictive maintenance for the road infrastructure in South Tyrol
source_description: This GAIA-X use case addresses the challenge of helping public administrations make better-founded decisions on road maintenance and budget planning. Road authorities must manage large infrastructure networks with limited resources, while poor road-surface quality can increase maintenance costs, congestion, downtime and costs for road users. In South Tyrol, GAIA-X is described as a data lake and scalable infrastructure for storing and processing heterogeneous data sources relevant to road-surface quality and maintenance needs. DataPort GmbH is identified as the associated stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation aggregates data from different sensors and other sources useful for assessing road conditions and identifying potential maintenance issues. At conceptual level, the platform processes large volumes of heterogeneous information to generate evaluations within response times suitable for public-administration budget planning. Predictive maintenance methods can then support targeted interventions by estimating where maintenance is most needed and when it should be prioritised. The expected impact includes better management of public funds, more efficient and targeted maintenance, improved road-surface quality, reduced disruption from roadworks, lower agency costs for the administration and lower road-user costs for citizens and infrastructure users. The cloud-based approach is potentially reusable by other European public administrations facing similar road-maintenance challenges.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ConsolONE: proactive monitoring and management system for real-time control of all company resources
source_description: ConsolONE is presented in the AgID data catalogue as a proactive monitoring and management system for real-time control of organisational resources, including technological infrastructure, buildings, IoT devices, environmental systems, data centres, assets, vehicles and people. The operational issue addressed is the fragmentation of monitoring across different technical domains, where organisations may need separate tools for IT infrastructure, building management, environmental control, cloud systems, asset management and safety-related traceability. The stakeholders include public or private organisations using the platform, IT managers, facility managers, security and safety teams, asset-management staff and AgID as the catalogue authority. The solution aims to provide a reliable, intuitive and integrated environment for supervising resources in real time. Its implementation covers monitoring and proactive management of IT infrastructure, BMS and home-automation systems, IoT sensors using IP, radio frequency, LoRaWAN and Narrowband technologies, environmental control systems, on-premise, cloud and hybrid-cloud data centres, and company assets such as PCs, servers, tablets and smartphones. It also supports traceability of vehicles and people within company premises for security and safety purposes. The expected impact is improved operational visibility, faster detection of anomalies, more coordinated infrastructure management and reduced complexity in controlling heterogeneous systems. By integrating multiple monitoring domains, ConsolONE can enhance reliability, support preventive maintenance and strengthen organisational control over critical resources.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: IBM Watson Content Hub
source_description: IBM Watson Content Hub provides a centralised environment for managing web content and digital assets across multiple digital channels. The operational need is to help organisations organise editorial materials, images, documents and other assets in a consistent way, while reducing duplication, improving searchability and supporting coherent publication across websites, applications and other online services. Stakeholders include content editors, digital service teams, communications departments, IT administrators, end users accessing digital channels, and organisations using the service through the public cloud catalogue. The implementation combines a content-management interface with IBM Watson services for automatic asset tagging, allowing digital materials to be categorised and retrieved more efficiently. A SOLR-based search engine supports asset and content discovery, while image rendition and sizing functions help adapt visual materials for omni-channel use. The system also offers REST APIs for editorial functions and content-model reuse, enabling integration with IBM and third-party solutions. Delivery through Akamai’s Content Delivery Network supports reliable digital distribution, while the SaaS model reduces infrastructure-management burdens and allows IBM to maintain updates, enrichment and security levels. The expected impact is lower operating cost, better content reuse, more consistent digital presence, faster asset discovery and improved editorial productivity. By combining centralised content governance, automated cataloguing and API-based distribution, the platform supports scalable management of digital communication services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Amazon Lex: service for creating communication interfaces via voice and text for any type of application
source_description: Amazon Lex is a service for creating communication interfaces via voice and text for any type of application. Amazon Lex offers advanced deep learning capabilities for speech recognition and dictation, as well as natural language recognition and text comprehension, enabling the creation of engaging applications and lifelike conversations. With Amazon Lex, the same deep learning technologies that Amazon Alexa is based on are available to all developers, enabling the creation of sophisticated and natural chatbots quickly and easily. More information: https://aws.amazon.com/it/lex/
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Amazon Polly: Text-to-Speech service
source_description: Amazon Polly is a service that turns text into real conversation, allowing you to build applications that speak and create entirely new categories of voice-enabled products. Amazon Polly is a Text-to-Speech service that uses advanced deep learning technologies to synthesize a human-like voice. With dozens of natural voice types in different languages, you can select the most suitable voice and distribute your applications with voice responses in different countries. More information: https://aws.amazon.com/it/polly/
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Alexacert: Voice application on Alexa for requesting a birth certificate
source_description: Alexacert was developed by the Municipality of Turin as a proof of concept to test whether citizens could request registry certificates through a voice assistant rather than through traditional online portals or physical offices. The administrative problem is that even standard registry procedures can create friction for users, particularly when they require navigation across multiple interfaces, authentication steps and back-office systems. The prototype focuses on birth certificates, which are well suited to experimentation because they are exempt from stamp duty. The solution uses an Alexa voice application activated through the phrase “Alexa, speak with Torino certificates”. The user is identified once by linking the Amazon account with a recognised digital identity, such as SPID, and this authorisation remains valid until explicitly revoked. After recognition, the system uses the email address associated with the Amazon profile, asks the user to confirm the request and, once consent is given, retrieves the PDF certificate from the Registry or ANPR and sends it to the registered inbox. The expected value is a simpler, faster and more accessible interaction with municipal registry services. The prototype also demonstrates how voice interfaces, digital identity, consent management and public back-office integration can be combined in a citizen-facing service.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LombardiaInforma: proactive Citizen Communication
source_description: LombardiaInforma supports Regione Lombardia in managing personalised communications to citizens through a multi-channel and multi-service approach. The organisational need is to help editorial and communication teams disseminate information more effectively, while ensuring that citizens receive relevant content according to their interests and contact preferences. The stakeholders include Regione Lombardia, citizens, editorial staff, communication offices, service managers and data-protection functions responsible for GDPR-compliant profiling. The implementation is based on an omnichannel customer-experience architecture and a public portal, Lombardia Informa, which centralises citizens’ contact data and declared topics of interest. The platform enables the creation and management of personalised communication campaigns across different channels, harmonising data from heterogeneous systems and supporting a coherent browsing experience. It also allows the development of integrated communication tools such as landing pages and surveys, and supports enriched content through image slideshows, videos and PDF attachments. User management and profiling are designed to operate in line with GDPR requirements. The expected impact is more targeted public communication, reduced fragmentation across channels, improved editorial efficiency and a better user experience for citizens receiving regional information. By centralising contact management and campaign delivery, the solution strengthens the region’s capacity to communicate proactively, consistently and in a way that is more responsive to citizens’ interests.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: YUCCA-Smart Data Platform
source_description: YUCCA Smart Data Platform offers Regione Piemonte and other public or private entities an open, pre-competitive cloud environment for experimenting with data-driven solutions. The policy and operational problem is that organisations often hold or generate valuable data from sensors, social sources, public datasets and private systems, but lack a shared infrastructure for aggregation, selective sharing, real-time processing and advanced analysis. Stakeholders include Regione Piemonte, public administrations, private organisations, developers, data users, IoT operators and citizens who may benefit from new digital services. The platform aggregates information from the Internet of Things, including cameras, sensors and weather stations, from the Internet of People, such as tweets, and from public and private datasets. It supports selective data sharing, self-service real-time processing, advanced analytics and access to data and metadata through APIs. Conceptually, YUCCA functions as a data platform that enables ingestion, governance, processing, analysis, visualisation and reuse of heterogeneous information. The expected impact is the creation of value-added services across multiple policy areas, easier experimentation with innovative technologies, and better interoperability between data producers and service developers. By providing end-to-end capabilities, the platform can reduce barriers to data innovation, support evidence-based decision-making and help public and private actors develop scalable solutions using shared digital infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CityFlows-Barcelona
source_description: CityFlows-Barcelona addresses the need to improve the safety and comfort of busy pedestrian spaces in Barcelona. High-density urban areas face operational challenges related to crowding, public-space management, mobility flows and emergency preparedness, particularly in locations affected by tourism, events and changing patterns of pedestrian movement. The CityFlows initiative, developed as an EIT Urban Mobility flagship project, brought together a diverse consortium of partners to create a Crowd Management Decision-Support System for public authorities and managers of pedestrian spaces. The Municipality of Barcelona is identified as the local public stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation centres on the CityFlows CM-DSS, a software solution later licensed through City Analytics, a start-up created to provide the system to government authorities. At conceptual level, the platform uses urban analytics and pedestrian-flow information to support the monitoring, assessment and management of crowded spaces. It can help authorities understand crowd conditions, assess potential risks and select appropriate operational measures. The expected impact is improved situational awareness, safer and more comfortable pedestrian environments, and stronger capacity to manage public spaces during normal operations and periods of disruption. The creation of City Analytics also supports scalability, enabling the solution to be reused by other authorities seeking reliable tools for evidence-based crowd management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CityFlows-Milano
source_description: CityFlows-Milano addresses the challenge of managing busy pedestrian spaces in Milan by improving public authorities’ capacity to monitor crowding, assess risks and support operational decisions. Dense urban areas require tools that can help maintain comfort and safety, especially in places affected by high footfall, public events, commuting flows and changing mobility patterns. CityFlows, an EIT Urban Mobility flagship project, brought together a diverse consortium of partners to launch a state-of-the-art Crowd Management Decision-Support System. The Municipality of Milan is identified as the local public stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation is based on the CityFlows CM-DSS, a decision-support software later licensed to government authorities through City Analytics, a dedicated start-up. At conceptual level, the system combines pedestrian-flow data, urban analytics and decision-support functions to help public authorities interpret crowd conditions and plan responses. It supports the connection between monitoring information and operational management of public space. The expected impact is better safety, comfort and responsiveness in pedestrian areas, with authorities able to rely on more structured information when managing crowd-related risks. The City Analytics licensing model also increases the potential for replication beyond the original project, allowing municipalities and public-space managers to adopt a scalable tool for crowd management, including during crisis situations or periods of unusual pressure on public space.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI4EU-AIPlan4EU
source_description: AIPlan4EU addresses the need to make automated planning technologies more accessible and usable for European innovators, practitioners and public or private organisations using the European AI On-Demand Platform. Planning technologies can support decision-making where actors must sequence actions, optimise resources or coordinate complex processes, but they are often difficult for non-specialists to access and apply. The project, coordinated through LAAS-CNRS, aims to bring AI planning into the AI4EU platform as a first-class capability by creating a uniform, user-centred framework for accessing existing planning technologies. The emerging technology implementation focuses on integrating planning tools, methods and guidance into the European platform environment. At conceptual level, the framework provides common access routes to established planning technologies and supports users in selecting, understanding and applying these tools to concrete innovation problems. The project also develops practical guidelines for innovators and practitioners, helping translate research outputs into usable solutions. The expected impact is broader adoption of planning technologies, reduced barriers between research and application, and improved capacity for organisations to use advanced decision-support methods. By embedding planning capabilities in AI4EU, AIPlan4EU strengthens the platform’s value as a shared European resource and supports more scalable use of intelligent planning across sectors and use cases.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Centre for Research and Technology Hellas (CERTH)
title: AI4EU-AI4Media
source_description: AI4Media addresses the need to strengthen Europe’s research and innovation capacity in artificial intelligence for the media sector while ensuring that future deployments reflect European values of ethics, trustworthiness and responsibility. The media sector faces rapid technological change, including new forms of content production, distribution, verification and personalisation, requiring advanced tools and specialised expertise. Funded under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme, AI4Media is structured as a Network of Research Excellence Centres and is associated with the Centre for Research and Technology Hellas. The objective is to become a Centre of Excellence engaging a wide network of researchers across Europe and beyond. The emerging technology implementation consists of research, training and development activities focused on the next generation of core artificial intelligence advances for media applications. At conceptual level, the network brings together scientific expertise, technical tools and sector-specific challenges to support responsible innovation in media technologies. It also emphasises the embedding of ethical and trustworthy AI principles in future deployments. The expected impact is improved European capacity to develop and apply advanced media technologies, stronger research collaboration and better alignment between innovation and public-interest values. By linking technical excellence with ethical governance, AI4Media supports a more responsible and competitive European media-technology ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: National Center for Scientific Research Demokritos
title: AI4EU-AICopernicus
source_description: AI4Copernicus addresses the need to connect artificial intelligence capabilities with Earth observation data, particularly data generated through the Copernicus programme. Researchers, innovators and public-sector users often face technical and organisational barriers when trying to combine satellite and geospatial data with advanced analytical methods. The project, associated with the National Center for Scientific Research Demokritos, aims to make the AI4EU AI-on-demand platform the digital environment of choice for users working with Copernicus data. The emerging technology implementation focuses on bridging the AI4EU platform with the Earth observation ecosystem. At conceptual level, AI4Copernicus supports access to tools, resources and services that enable users to apply artificial intelligence methods to Copernicus data for research and innovation purposes. This may include support for data discovery, model development, experimentation and reuse of analytical components in geospatial applications. The expected impact is stronger uptake of Earth observation data, improved innovation capacity and easier development of AI-enabled services based on Copernicus resources. By linking two major European digital assets, AI4Copernicus can support applications in areas such as environmental monitoring, climate services, land management and emergency response. The project contributes to a more integrated European data and AI ecosystem, making advanced analysis more accessible to both specialists and applied users.

title: AI4EU-TAILOR
source_description: TAILOR addresses the strategic objective of advancing trustworthy artificial intelligence in Europe by integrating reasoning, learning and optimisation. The project responds to the need for research and innovation that is not only technically advanced, but also human-centred, responsible and aligned with European values. Coordinated through a consortium including Linköping University, TAILOR is committed to demonstrating that expertise, cooperation and diversity can support the European vision of trustworthy AI and position Europe as a global role model for responsible development. The emerging technology implementation focuses on the foundations of trustworthy AI, particularly the integration of symbolic reasoning, machine learning and optimisation methods. At conceptual level, the project brings together research communities that address different aspects of intelligent systems, seeking approaches that are more robust, explainable, reliable and suitable for human-centred applications. Rather than a single operational tool, TAILOR functions as a research network and capability-building initiative that supports methods, knowledge exchange and innovation pathways. The expected impact is stronger European excellence in trustworthy AI, improved collaboration among researchers and better foundations for future applications in public and private sectors. By advancing methods that combine reasoning, learning and optimisation, TAILOR can contribute to systems that are more transparent, dependable and aligned with governance expectations for high-impact digital technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: REDOC - Digital Tutor to make easier learning the STEM subject
source_description: REDOC, based on the Redooc learning platform, addresses the challenge of making mathematics and science education more engaging, accessible, and effective for students while also supporting teachers with structured digital resources. The problem it tackles is not only the difficulty many learners experience with STEM subjects, but also the need for educators to access exercises, explanations, simulations, and lesson materials in formats that are suitable for classroom and independent study. The stakeholders include students across different age groups, teachers, schools, families, and the start-up providing the service. The objective is to encourage learning through practice, motivation, and playful competition, helping students train their reasoning skills in a way comparable to regular physical exercise. The implementation uses a web-based educational platform combining video lessons, interactive exercises, tips, simulations, and game-like learning paths. Technology is applied through digital tutoring functions, adaptive content organisation, gamification mechanics, progress tracking, and online assessment features that allow learners to practise and receive structured feedback. Teachers can use the platform to complement classroom instruction, assign activities, and explain concepts through ready-made multimedia resources. The expected impact includes stronger learner engagement, greater continuity between school and home study, easier access to remedial materials, and improved support for teachers. By presenting STEM learning as an interactive and competitive experience, the platform can increase motivation and broaden participation in scientific and mathematical education.

title: SAMPA - Service of registration and promotion of the adherence to medications in elderly patients
source_description: Medication non-adherence among elderly and chronic patients leads to poorer health outcomes and higher healthcare costs. At the University Hospital Miguel Servet (HUMS) in Zaragoza, outpatient pharmacy processes were fragmented, manual, and prone to dispensing and coordination errors. The SAMPA project was implemented to improve treatment adherence, streamline medication management, and enhance patient experience. Stakeholders include hospital pharmacists, clinicians, outpatient staff, and elderly patients. The solution involved a comprehensive digital transformation of the outpatient pharmacy unit. Core components include an integrated electronic prescription platform, automated storage and dispensing robots, full traceability across prescribing and dispensing stages, appointment scheduling, and adherence monitoring systems. These components are interconnected with hospital information systems, enabling end-to-end visibility of medication flows and patient interactions. Supporting tools such as a patient app, improved web services, and dedicated communication points facilitate engagement and follow-up. The project has been implemented at HUMS and has reduced dispensing errors, improved workflow efficiency, and enhanced accessibility for patients. SAMPA demonstrates how integrated digital systems can deliver measurable operational and quality improvements in hospital outpatient care.

title: Smart Dementia project
source_description: Dementia care requires balancing safety with personal freedom, because residents may benefit physically and mentally from moving around, while care teams must manage risks linked to disorientation or wandering. The Smart Dementia project at Tante Louise uses eHealth technology to give people with Alzheimer’s disease more freedom inside and outside nursing-home settings. The operational objective is to support professional risk assessment: care teams decide how much freedom each resident can safely have, and the technology helps them monitor whereabouts when additional safeguards are needed. The implementation combines a wristwatch, mobile app, sensor technology and GPS-based location tracking, allowing nurses and authorised staff to locate a resident if necessary. At a conceptual level, the device collects location data, communicates it to relevant caregivers and supports a personalised care arrangement rather than imposing uniform restrictions. The expected impact is greater autonomy for residents, improved confidence for staff and families, and longer preservation of physical and mental activity. The project also demonstrates how personal health data can support more precise and individualised care, while raising obvious requirements around consent, proportionality and data protection. Its value lies in using technology as a supportive layer around professional judgement, not as a substitute for person-centred dementia care.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Track AI
source_description: Track AI addresses the difficulty of assessing visual function in children and other non-collaborative patients who may be unable to complete conventional ophthalmological examinations. Reliable early detection of visual impairment is essential for timely intervention, but clinical assessment can be challenging when patients cannot follow instructions or communicate clearly. The project, linked to Miguel Servet Hospital in Zaragoza, uses the DIVE medical device and aims to help physicians determine whether a patient has a visual impairment and, in some cases, estimate the probability of a specific pathology. The emerging technology implementation integrates artificial intelligence into the DIVE device through a dedicated app running on a Huawei P30 mobile phone. The app analyses data from visual explorations, especially patient gaze patterns, and compares them with a database generated from previous diagnoses, available both online and offline. At conceptual level, the system uses pattern comparison and probabilistic classification to support clinical interpretation of visual behaviour. Although focused on non-collaborative patients, it can also be used with collaborative patients. The expected impact is improved support for clinicians, faster and more accessible screening, and better identification of patients who may require further assessment or treatment. By combining portable technology with diagnostic-support capabilities, Track AI can strengthen paediatric and inclusive eye-care services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Osakidetza (Servicio Vasco de Salud/Basque Health System)
title: MasterMind - Basque Country
source_description: MasterMind in the Basque Country addressed the need to make high-quality treatment for depression more widely available to adults with mild and moderate depression. Access to psychological therapy can be constrained by limited professional capacity, distance, waiting times and the need for repeated face-to-face appointments. The project, involving Osakidetza within a broader European collaboration of 23 partners, aimed to use ICT to expand access while maintaining professional oversight. The emerging technology implementation consisted of Computerised Cognitive Behaviour Therapy delivered through the web application “Overcome your depression”, accessible by computer, tablet or smartphone. At conceptual level, the application provides therapy through six modules combining text, videos, images, graphs and interactive tasks. Patients complete tests within the platform, and these results communicate the evolution of their condition to health professionals. Clinicians periodically review the outputs and receive alerts when a patient’s results indicate possible concern. The expected impact is wider availability of depression treatment, fewer required face-to-face appointments and better continuity of monitoring between patients and professionals. By combining structured digital therapy with clinical supervision, MasterMind can improve service accessibility, support efficient use of healthcare resources and provide patients with a flexible treatment pathway that complements conventional mental-health services in the Basque health system.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MasterMind - Southern Denmark
source_description: MasterMind in Southern Denmark addressed the same broader European objective of making high-quality depression treatment more widely available through ICT-enabled care. Adults with mild and moderate depression may face barriers to accessing regular therapy, including service availability, travel, stigma or scheduling constraints. The Region of Southern Denmark participated in the European MasterMind project, which involved 23 partners and focused on implementing Computerised Cognitive Behaviour Therapy as a scalable form of supported treatment. The emerging technology implementation centred on the web application “Overcome your depression”, which can be used through a computer, tablet or smartphone. The application delivers therapy in six modules using text, videos, images, graphs and other structured materials. Patients complete tests during the programme, allowing their progress and condition to be communicated to healthcare professionals. Clinicians review the results periodically and receive alarms when responses indicate a cause for concern. The expected impact is improved access to treatment, reduced reliance on face-to-face appointments and more efficient monitoring of patient progress. By enabling remote therapy while maintaining professional involvement, the solution can help mental-health services reach more patients, use clinical resources more effectively and provide a flexible pathway for people with mild or moderate depression. The case demonstrates how digital therapy can be integrated into regional healthcare provision.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MPAI Community: Moving Picture, Audio and Data Coding by Artificial Intelligence (MPAI)
source_description: MPAI is an international, unaffiliated, non-profit organisation established to develop technical specifications for moving picture, audio and data coding enabled by new digital technologies. The sectoral challenge is that media and data coding systems require interoperable standards, predictable licensing conditions and integration frameworks that allow different components to work together across products, services and markets. Stakeholders include technology developers, media companies, standardisation experts, rights holders, implementers, researchers and organisations seeking clarity on intellectual property arrangements. The initiative focuses on developing data-coding specifications with clear intellectual property rights licensing frameworks, particularly for moving picture, audio and data applications. Its implementation is not a single public service, but a standard-setting and specification-development process. Conceptually, this involves defining coding architectures, technical requirements, component interfaces, conformance expectations and licensing conditions that can support integration of coding components into broader systems. The expected impact is improved interoperability, reduced uncertainty for implementers, and stronger conditions for adoption of advanced coding technologies across international markets. By combining technical specification work with transparent IPR frameworks, MPAI can support innovation while reducing fragmentation in media and data-coding ecosystems. Its value lies in creating common reference points for industry and research actors developing or deploying advanced coding solutions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Trentino Salute 4.0: TREC+
source_description: TreC+ brings together the digital health trials carried out in Trentino with citizens and health professionals, turning them into a single operational ecosystem for online health services. The service challenge is to guarantee citizens continuous, safe and integrated access to healthcare functions through one platform and one app, while maintaining the quality and reliability of care. The main stakeholders include the Autonomous Province of Trento, APSS, citizens, doctors, health professionals and the FBK research centre. The platform is designed around a constant exchange of data produced by patients and clinicians, with health information remaining under public control in APSS archives. Its implementation is based on open-source technologies and an open architectural model that allows proprietary tools and external solutions to be connected without moving health data away from the public system. The more advanced components, developed and experimented with FBK, explore virtual coaches, predictive models, chatbots and other intelligent applications. TreC+ can also integrate with existing healthcare-management systems, including booking services, electronic health records, payment systems and telemonitoring tools. The expected impact is broader access to digital health services, improved continuity of care, stronger data protection, and greater reusability in other regional, provincial, local health authority or hospital contexts. By combining public governance with modular integration, the ecosystem supports scalable digital healthcare while keeping citizens’ data central, protected and available.

title: Seamless Flow: facial recognition of airport passengers
source_description: Seamless Flow supports automated passenger processing in airports by using biometric identification to manage travellers’ digital identities and reduce repeated document checks. The operational issue is that airports must process large passenger flows while maintaining security, identity verification and efficient movement through controlled areas. Passengers, airport operators, border or security authorities, airlines and the technology provider Vision-Box are the central stakeholders. The solution is used in several airports, including Fiumicino, Malpensa and Linate, and aims to allow passengers to move through airport procedures without repeatedly presenting passports and tickets. The implementation uses IoT-enabled access gates equipped with cameras and facial recognition software. These devices capture the passenger’s face and associate it with passport and ticket data, creating a temporary digital identity that is maintained for the duration of the passenger’s stay at the airport. Conceptually, the system combines biometric enrolment, document-data verification, facial matching, passenger-flow management and integration with airport access-control infrastructure. The expected impact is smoother passenger circulation, shorter queues, reduced manual document checks and more consistent identity verification across airport touchpoints. For airport operators, it can improve throughput and service quality, while supporting security objectives. However, because the system relies on biometric data, its use requires strict safeguards on consent, retention, accuracy, access control and proportionality.

title: Shareart: measure the public's satisfaction in front of the works of art exhibited in museum
source_description: ShareArt explores how museums can better understand visitors’ engagement with artworks by analysing behaviour during observation. The cultural-management problem is that museums often rely on indirect indicators, surveys or attendance numbers to assess how the public experiences exhibitions, whereas curators and administrators may need more granular evidence on attention, satisfaction and interaction with specific works. Stakeholders include ENEA’s Sustainability Department of Production and Territorial Systems, the Bologna Museums Institution, museum managers, visitors, curators and cultural-policy actors. The system uses a camera positioned near artworks to detect faces looking towards the piece and collect information about observation behaviour. Its implementation draws on big-data techniques and convolutional neural networks to correlate data on the use and enjoyment of artworks with characteristics inferred from visitors and their behaviour. Conceptually, the tool combines computer vision, behavioural analytics, image processing and data aggregation to infer patterns of public engagement. The expected impact is a more evidence-based understanding of museum experience, helping institutions assess which works attract attention, how visitors interact with exhibitions and how displays might be improved. It may support curatorial planning, audience development and cultural-service evaluation. At the same time, the use of cameras and inferred personal characteristics in a museum setting requires careful attention to transparency, proportionality, anonymisation and visitor privacy.

organization: Multiple Italian Universities (Cattolica, Bocconi, Roma Tre etc.)
title: Respondus: assessment software for remote management of students (university)
source_description: Respondus is a remote proctoring solution used by several Italian universities to supervise online examinations and identify behaviour considered unusual or suspicious during tests. The educational challenge is to preserve exam integrity when assessments are conducted remotely, where universities cannot rely on traditional in-person invigilation. Stakeholders include universities, students, teaching staff, examination offices, technology providers and data-protection authorities or officers responsible for oversight. The software monitors the student’s device and collects visual data during the examination process. Its implementation includes video recording, facial image capture, periodic snapshots and algorithmic flagging of moments that may indicate abnormal conduct. These signals are intended to support decisions on whether a student may have copied, used unauthorised materials or violated examination rules. Conceptually, the system combines device monitoring, identity verification, behavioural analysis, video analytics and automated risk flagging, with human review normally needed to interpret the results. The expected benefits for universities are more scalable remote assessment, reduced need for live invigilators and stronger deterrence against fraud. However, the impact is contested because proctoring systems can affect privacy, create stress for students, and generate false or ambiguous alerts. The use of such tools therefore requires clear rules, proportionality, transparency, human oversight and accessible procedures for students to challenge contested findings.

title: SARI (Automatic Image Recognition System)
source_description: Facial images can be important investigative material when police need to compare a person shown in a photograph or video with people already recorded in law-enforcement databases. SARI, the Automatic Image Recognition System, was introduced in Italy for the Ministry of the Interior and the Central Anti-Crime Directorate of the State Police. The system is supplied by Parsec 3.26 S.r.l. and is structured around two components: SARI Enterprise and SARI Real-Time. SARI Enterprise supports retrospective identification by comparing a facial image already available to investigators with images in police databases of previously photo-recorded individuals. SARI Real-Time, by contrast, was designed to recognise people from a watch list through camera feeds. At a conceptual level, the technology combines biometric feature extraction, facial matching, image comparison and investigative review. Its operational value lies in helping officers narrow searches, identify possible matches and accelerate investigations where visual evidence is available. However, the two components raise different legal and ethical issues: retrospective matching for investigative purposes is different from real-time public-space recognition, which requires stronger safeguards because of its surveillance implications. The system should therefore be understood as an investigative-support tool whose outputs require human validation and legal control, not as an autonomous identification or enforcement mechanism. Current public material most clearly confirms knowledge of SARI Enterprise as the facial-recognition system used by Italian law enforcement for after-the-fact investigative identification.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: ISS- ITALY Istituto Superiore di Sanità
title: EU-JAV European Joint Action on Vaccination
source_description: The EU-JAV vaccine conversation monitoring platform was developed to help public health actors understand how vaccination-related narratives circulate online across different countries and languages. The policy problem is that vaccine debates unfold rapidly through social media and web platforms, making it difficult for health authorities to detect emerging concerns, influential actors and misinformation dynamics in real time. Stakeholders include the Istituto Superiore di Sanità, EU-JAV partners, public health authorities, researchers, online communities and citizens exposed to vaccine information. In its initial phase, the platform operated in Italian, French and Spanish and was accessible via credentials. It monitored information flows from Twitter, Reddit, Wikipedia and Google Trends through a three-layer architecture: a Data layer, an Analysis layer and a Visualisation layer. The Data layer collected and cleaned raw information through platform APIs and keyword filters validated using recurrence and relevance criteria. The Analysis layer generated graphs, geolocated tweets and applied machine-learning processes for influencer analysis and early-signal detection, including the identification of active or influential users and emerging vaccine-related hashtags. The Visualisation layer presented results in an accessible way. The expected impact is stronger real-time monitoring of vaccine conversations, earlier detection of changing narratives, and better evidence for public communication strategies. By structuring online data into interpretable outputs, the platform supports more responsive vaccination policy and communication.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CLIP (Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training) for the Italian Language
source_description: Many advanced multimodal models have been primarily trained on English-language datasets, limiting their performance and applicability in languages with fewer annotated resources, such as Italian. This creates challenges for researchers, public administrations and digital service providers seeking to develop image–text retrieval, content moderation or assistive technologies tailored to Italian users. The project aims to bridge this gap by developing a multimodal model capable of understanding and linking Italian textual descriptions with visual content. The objective is to provide a robust foundation model that enables accurate alignment between images and Italian language inputs, supporting downstream applications in search, accessibility and digital services. The solution builds upon the Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) framework, combining a pre-trained Italian BERT language model (dbmdz) with a Vision Transformer architecture for image encoding. Using approximately 1.4 million paired image–text samples, the model is fine-tuned through contrastive learning techniques that optimise the similarity between matching image–text pairs while distinguishing non-matching pairs. The resulting architecture enables joint embedding of visual and textual data within a shared semantic space, accessible through an online demonstration environment. The Italian CLIP model improves multimodal understanding in a low-resource linguistic context, enhancing the accuracy of image–text retrieval and classification tasks in Italian. By reducing dependency on English-centric models, it strengthens digital sovereignty, supports innovation in language-specific applications and provides a scalable resource for further research and public and private sector use cases.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: iBorderCtrl: Virtual Policeman
source_description: iBorderCtrl, the Intelligent Portable Control System, was designed to address the operational challenge of conducting thorough yet faster border checks for third-country nationals crossing the land borders of EU Member States. Border authorities must balance security, legal compliance, traveller facilitation, and resource efficiency, particularly at road crossings, pedestrian routes, and train stations where flows can be complex and time-sensitive. The stakeholders include border guards, national authorities, EU-level border management actors, travellers, technology suppliers, and backend system operators. The objective was to create a comprehensive and mobile two-stage procedure capable of reducing the time and cost associated with checks while maintaining the depth of control required under Schengen border management. The implementation combined portable readers and scanners, automatic control subsystems, wireless networking, secure backend storage, and processing infrastructure. At a conceptual level, the system brought together hardware for document and biometric capture, software modules for verification and risk-related processing, mobile connectivity for field operations, and centralised data services for secure storage and decision support. The intended impact was to make border control more scalable, consistent, and efficient, particularly in land-border environments where fixed infrastructure may be limited. Expected results included reduced processing time per traveller, lower operational costs, improved mobility for border teams, and more reliable information flows between frontline officers and backend systems. The use case also illustrates the importance of safeguards, transparency, and proportionality in sensitive border-management technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: NUMEL.AI - A communication tool for neurological disorders
source_description: Neurological disorders are often difficult for patients to understand due to the complexity of medical imaging and the abstract nature of diagnostic explanations. Clinicians face challenges in communicating disease progression, anatomical alterations and treatment implications in a clear and accessible manner, particularly when relying on two-dimensional scans and technical terminology. NUMEL.AI addresses this communication gap by providing an interactive visualisation tool that enables doctors and patients to explore neurological conditions using the patient’s own medical imaging data. The objective is to enhance patient understanding, support shared decision-making and improve the quality of clinical consultations through immersive visual explanations grounded in real diagnostic data. The solution processes magnetic resonance (MR) images and other clinical imaging data imported directly from healthcare information systems to automatically generate personalised three-dimensional anatomical models. Computer vision techniques and body-tracking algorithms align these models with the patient’s body in real time using augmented reality rendering. Machine learning methods support image segmentation and the identification of relevant anatomical structures and disorder-related patterns. The system can operate locally or through a scalable, API-based cloud platform that allows secure data storage, retrieval and extensibility across healthcare environments. The tool improves the clarity and effectiveness of clinician–patient communication, enhances patient engagement and understanding of disease evolution, and supports more informed treatment discussions. Its scalable architecture facilitates integration with existing hospital systems, while automated model generation reduces preparation time for clinicians and increases the accessibility of advanced visualisation technologies in neurological care.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI Robort Judge for small claims in Estonia
source_description: Small-claims procedures can absorb judicial time even when the amounts involved are relatively low and the dispute is mainly documentary. Estonia’s proposed “robot judge” was intended to explore whether low-value civil claims, initially under €7,000 and focused on contract disputes, could be processed more efficiently through automated support. The objective was to reduce backlogs for judges and court clerks while preserving the possibility of appeal to a human judge. The implementation concept was that parties would upload documents and relevant evidence, after which the system would analyse the material and issue a decision or recommendation. At a conceptual level, such a tool would require structured digital submissions, document analysis, legal-rule modelling, case classification and clear procedural safeguards for review and appeal. The expected impact would be faster processing of routine small claims, lower administrative burden and improved access to justice for simple disputes. However, many details remained unresolved, including legal responsibility, procedural fairness, transparency and the appropriate boundary between automation and adjudication. Later legal commentary suggests that Estonia has long used semi-automatic procedures for small claims, but public evidence of a fully operational autonomous AI judge remains limited. The use case should therefore be treated as an exploratory justice-automation initiative rather than a confirmed deployed judicial decision-maker.

title: MIREL - Mining and reasoning with legal text
source_description: MIREL was established to advance the mining and formal reasoning of legal texts by creating an international and inter-sectoral network across law, artificial intelligence and computational modelling. The central problem is that legal materials are complex, interpretative and difficult to translate into structured representations that can support querying, compliance checking and decision support. Researchers, legal experts, SMEs, industrial partners and academic institutions are therefore brought together to address both conceptual and computational barriers. The project develops a formal framework and tools for transforming legal texts into representations that machines can process, compare and reason over. Its implementation connects natural language processing, legal ontologies, computational argumentation, formal logic and reasoning methods. It also considers the role of legal interpretation, the handling of large legal datasets and the complexity of regulatory compliance. A distinctive feature is its effort to bridge communities that often work separately: those developing legal ontologies and NLP parsers, and those focused on formal reasoning and logic. Through mobility and staff exchange between SMEs and academia, MIREL aims to build an interdisciplinary and inter-continental knowledge base. Its expected impact is stronger legal technology research, improved foundations for compliance tools and future market-oriented services in legal reasoning.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Predictive maintenance for wind farms
source_description: Wind-power operators need to minimise unplanned downtime because failures in turbines can reduce energy production, increase maintenance costs and require costly intervention in remote or difficult-to-access sites. This predictive-maintenance service applies machine-learning techniques to support more efficient management of wind-power assets, with the objective of anticipating failures before they cause stoppages or major damage. The operational problem is that wind turbines generate large volumes of sensor and operational data, but maintenance decisions often depend on identifying weak signals before they become visible through conventional inspection. The implementation uses a software system that processes machinery, sensor and production data to estimate component health, detect abnormal patterns and forecast the risk of specific failures. At a conceptual level, the system combines IoT or machine data, historical failure records, predictive algorithms, alerts, maintenance planning and reporting. This allows maintenance teams to schedule targeted interventions, prioritise high-risk assets and avoid unnecessary preventive work where a component remains healthy. The expected impact is lower downtime, reduced maintenance cost, improved production efficiency and better quality of asset-management decisions. AIMonitoring’s current Predeep platform describes AI-supported predictive maintenance, integration with 4.0 machinery, IoT sensors and databases, automatic alerts, maintenance planning and reported average results such as reduced downtime and maintenance costs, although those performance figures are supplier-reported.
