The objective of this use case is to improve response times and operational effectiveness by enabling authorised emergency crews to access buildings without manual key handovers or administrative delays. The city conducted a pilot using a blockchain-based access management solution known as SmartKey. The system connects smart contracts deployed on the Ethereum network with physical IoT devices installed in buildings and emergency vehicles. Access rights are managed digitally and activated automatically during emergencies, allowing authorised responders to unlock doors securely and auditable. The trial demonstrates faster emergency response, reduced operational friction, and improved coordination between services. Qualitative benefits include enhanced safety for citizens and responders, greater accountability through tamper-proof access logs, and a scalable model that can be extended to other cities and critical infrastructure environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain-based service to register digital acts at the Court of Cremona
source_description: Judicial systems rely on secure, reliable, and timely registration of legal documents, yet many courts still depend on paper-based or fragmented digital processes that hinder efficiency and continuity, particularly during emergencies. At the Court of Cremona, the Gip-Gup section faced the risk of operational disruption during the COVID-19 lockdown, threatening delays in hearings and case backlogs. The objective of this use case was to ensure continuity of judicial activities while strengthening the integrity and traceability of digital legal documents. In collaboration with Stampiz, the court implemented a service to register digital acts such as judgments, files, copies, and certificates. The solution anchors cryptographic proofs of documents on a blockchain while keeping the files stored securely on the court’s internal servers, ensuring anonymity and preventing unauthorised access. Registration is fully digital and does not require moving files outside the court’s infrastructure. The initiative enabled uninterrupted hearings during the pandemic, accelerated recovery of postponed cases, and improved reliability of registry operations. It demonstrates increased efficiency, stronger evidential integrity, and a robust, scalable approach to digital justice administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital credentials for graduates at University of Lille
source_description: France's largest public university faced substantial administrative burden from diploma verification requests whilst graduates experienced delays obtaining proof of qualifications for employment or further study. The University of Lille partnered with BCdiploma to implement blockchain-based digital credentials through the Dem-Attest project, issuing bilingual (French/English) certificates that are tamper-proof and valid for life. Since July 2021, the university has issued over 80,000 blockchain certificates covering 700 diploma types at approximately 20,000 per year. The system uses the Avalanche blockchain with an estimated energy footprint of just 0.025g CO2 per credential. The University of Lille leads the Fr.EBSI project integrating with the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure and participates in EBSI-VECTOR for W3C Verifiable Credentials deployment. Online verification has been accessed over 132,000 times, demonstrating strong adoption by employers and institutions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: EnergieKnip, Energy Wallet
source_description: European student mobility programmes like Erasmus faced administrative friction from credential verification requirements, with universities unable to efficiently validate transcripts and qualifications from partner institutions across borders. The EBSI multi-University pilot, launched through the Early Adopters Programme in 2021, brought together 11 universities from 11 countries and 2 European university alliances to test cross-border Verifiable Credentials for education. Six scenarios were developed including Erasmus transcript validation, cross-border PhD applications, European student card verification, and diploma recognition for employment. The pilot demonstrated end-to-end exchange of W3C-standard credentials via EBSI-compliant digital wallets, with institutions including KU Leuven and Italian universities testing the Belgium-Italy corridor. The EBSI-VECTOR project (2023-2025) expanded these pilots across 52 partners in 20 countries, advancing toward production deployment of decentralised educational credentials.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Data Valorisation Services
source_description: Smart cities generate vast volumes of data through IoT platforms, yet much of this data remains underused due to limited trust, unclear ownership, and fragmented access mechanisms. In Santander, municipal datasets produced by smart city infrastructures offer significant potential value for public administrations, businesses, and citizens, but require a trusted framework to enable secure sharing and reuse. This use case, developed within the EU-funded TOKEN project, aims to unlock the economic and social value of municipal data while ensuring transparency, accountability, and data governance. Stakeholders include the municipality, data providers, service developers, and data consumers, all seeking reliable access to high-quality urban data. The solution introduces a blockchain-based data marketplace where datasets generated by IoT platforms are registered, described, and exchanged under clear usage conditions. Distributed ledgers record data transactions, access rights, and usage policies, while smart contracts govern permissions and potential monetisation schemes. Data itself remains off-chain, ensuring scalability and compliance. The results include improved trust in data sharing, new opportunities for data-driven services, and more efficient reuse of public data assets. The initiative demonstrates how cities can foster innovation ecosystems while maintaining control, transparency, and public value creation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: The municipalities of Amsterdam, The Hague and Eindhoven
title: The red button: debt pause button
source_description: Individuals facing problem debt often experience escalating stress due to continuous collection actions, while municipalities require time to assess and implement sustainable debt restructuring solutions. In Amsterdam, the “Red Button” pilot was introduced as an innovative instrument in debt counselling to temporarily pause debt collection, giving debtors space to stabilise their situation. Stakeholders include indebted citizens, municipal debt counselling services, courts and collection agencies such as the Central Judicial Collection Agency. The objective is to reduce pressure on vulnerable individuals while enabling more effective and durable financial solutions. The mechanism allows a temporary, legally recognised suspension of collection activities during counselling periods. Digital coordination between municipal services and enforcement bodies ensures that the pause is applied consistently and transparently. The pilot demonstrated improved cooperation between institutions, reduced stress for debtors, and better engagement in counselling processes. Qualitative results suggest higher chances of successful debt restructuring and more humane public debt management. The approach offers a replicable policy tool for municipalities aiming to balance enforcement with social support.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Self Sovereign Attendancy
source_description: Attendance registration at events, classes and conferences is commonly handled through paper lists that expose personal data, are vulnerable to manipulation and fail to meet data protection requirements. The Self-Sovereign Attendance pilot addresses this operational and compliance challenge by rethinking how attendance is recorded and verified. Stakeholders include event organisers, educational institutions, attendees and auditing bodies. The objective is to provide a secure, privacy-preserving and fraud-resistant alternative to traditional attendance lists. The solution enables participants to check in through a decentralised application built on a distributed ledger infrastructure. Attendance records are cryptographically secured, immutable and accessible only to authorised parties, ensuring that personal data is protected while proof of attendance remains verifiable. The proof of concept demonstrated reliable check-in, resistance to data tampering and improved compliance with data protection rules. The pilot enhances trust and fairness for both organisers and participants and provides a scalable foundation for attendance management across education and events.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Generating Health Certificates
source_description: Local authorities are required to verify compliance with health regulations while protecting sensitive personal information, particularly in contexts involving vulnerable groups. In Oldenburg, health organisations faced challenges with fake or invalid registration certificates required under the German Prostitutes Protection Act. The pilot aimed to ensure authenticity and integrity of health certificates while preserving privacy. Stakeholders include municipal health authorities, registered individuals, and regulatory bodies. The objective was to provide a reliable way to prove that health certificates are valid and up to date without exposing personal data. The solution uses a distributed ledger to issue and verify certificates, ensuring that each record is traceable to its source and cannot be altered. A privacy-preserving design allows verification of certificate validity without revealing underlying personal details. The pilot improved trust in certificates, reduced fraud risk and simplified verification procedures. It demonstrated a scalable and secure approach to regulatory compliance in sensitive public health contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Healthy on the Blockchain
source_description: Employers seeking to promote healthier lifestyles among staff often face resistance due to concerns about data privacy and misuse of personal health information. The municipality of Roeselare and HOWEST University launched this pilot to encourage preventive health and physical activity among municipal employees while safeguarding trust. Stakeholders include employees, health coaches, the municipality and academic partners. The objective is to stimulate healthy behaviour without granting employers access to sensitive personal data. Wearable devices track physical activity, and progress is visualised through an application that connects trainees with personal coaches. Blockchain technology is used to secure health data and control access, ensuring that employees retain ownership of their information. The pilot increased participation in wellness programmes, improved trust in data handling, and reduced privacy concerns. It delivers qualitative benefits in employee wellbeing and organisational culture and provides a replicable model for privacy-preserving workplace health initiatives.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain-based Mobiliti App
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Business parks often lack efficient transport connections, limiting access for students and job seekers and increasing reliance on private cars. The Mobiliti pilot was developed to address accessibility challenges in the Deinze business park by enabling trusted ride sharing. Stakeholders include students, employers, local authorities and employment agencies. The objective is to improve accessibility while promoting sustainable mobility. The application provides a ride-sharing platform where participants can coordinate trips securely. Blockchain technology underpins identity and transaction trust, ensuring that participants can share rides with confidence while protecting personal data. The pilot improved mobility options, reduced barriers to employment and education, and supported more sustainable commuting. It demonstrates how decentralised trust mechanisms can enable collaborative mobility services in local economic zones.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain for Maritime Ports
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: Maritime ports involve complex logistics chains where fragmented information systems hinder efficiency, transparency and coordination between authorities and businesses. This pilot investigates the feasibility of using blockchain technology to improve freight transport and government-to-business services in ports. Stakeholders include port authorities, customs, logistics operators and researchers. The objective is to assess whether distributed ledgers can enhance data sharing and service quality in port logistics. The study explores shared ledgers for tracking freight documentation and logistics events, enabling authorised access to consistent and tamper-proof data. Results indicate potential improvements in transparency, reduced administrative friction and better coordination across stakeholders. The pilot provides a knowledge base for future operational deployments in smart port ecosystems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Transparent management of public accounts
source_description: Public administrations face growing pressure to ensure transparency, accountability, and citizen participation in the management of public finances. In the municipality of Katerini, traditional procurement and budgeting processes limited visibility into public spending and constrained meaningful civic engagement. This use case, part of the EU-funded TOKEN project, seeks to enhance trust between citizens and local government by making public accounts more transparent and participatory. The objective is to provide clear insight into procurement processes and enable citizens to actively contribute to decisions on public spending. The solution integrates blockchain technology into existing smart city initiatives to create a tamper-proof system for recording procurement activities and managing participatory budgeting through electronic voting. Transactions related to public spending and voting outcomes are immutably recorded, ensuring traceability and auditability. Citizen participation is supported through secure digital identities and transparent voting mechanisms. The impact includes increased trust in public institutions, reduced risk of fraud or manipulation, and improved civic engagement. The use case demonstrates how transparent digital infrastructures can strengthen democratic processes, improve governance quality, and create more accountable and inclusive local administrations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ONCE project: Sovereign Data and Self Sovereign Identity
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Digital public services often require citizens to repeatedly register and share personal data across different administrations and sectors, leading to inefficiencies and loss of user control. The ONCE project addresses these challenges by enabling citizens to manage their digital identity data directly on their smartphones. Initially deployed in the German state of Hesse and selected regions in Bavaria and North Rhine-Westphalia, the initiative involves public authorities, municipalities, and private sector partners. Its objective is to simplify online registration and authentication across domains such as e-government, mobility, and tourism, while strengthening data sovereignty and trust. The solution combines self-sovereign identity principles with existing identity infrastructures, building on OPTIMOS 2.0 and mobile identity wallets. Identity credentials are issued, stored, and shared under user control, with verification supported by decentralised trust mechanisms. The system integrates with public and private services without centralised identity databases. The project demonstrates reduced administrative burden, faster onboarding to digital services, and enhanced privacy protection. It provides a scalable and interoperable model for secure digital identities, supporting cross-sector use and reinforcing citizen-centric data governance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Cross-border erasmus exchange scenario
source_description: European student mobility programmes like Erasmus faced administrative friction from credential verification requirements, with universities unable to efficiently validate transcripts and qualifications from partner institutions across borders. The EBSI multi-University pilot, launched through the Early Adopters Programme in 2021, brought together 11 universities from 11 countries and 2 European university alliances to test cross-border Verifiable Credentials for education. Six scenarios were developed including Erasmus transcript validation, cross-border PhD applications, European student card verification, and diploma recognition for employment. The pilot demonstrated end-to-end exchange of W3C-standard credentials via EBSI-compliant digital wallets, with institutions including KU Leuven and Italian universities testing the Belgium-Italy corridor. The EBSI-VECTOR project (2023-2025) expanded these pilots across 52 partners in 20 countries, advancing toward production deployment of decentralised educational credentials.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: European Student eCard with blockchain
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Students across Europe face fragmented systems for proving their status and accessing benefits when interacting with public services in different regions. This pilot, led by the Open Government of Catalonia in collaboration with municipalities, universities and technology providers, aims to improve interoperability of student credentials. Stakeholders include students, city councils, universities and service providers. The objective is to enable students to access municipal discounts using a trusted digital identity. The solution leverages a blockchain-based digital identity wallet aligned with European infrastructure standards, allowing students to present verified credentials securely. The pilot enabled students to obtain discounts in multiple Catalan municipalities while maintaining control over their data. It demonstrated interoperability, compliance with European identity frameworks and improved user experience, laying the groundwork for scalable cross-border student services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: EQPR - CoE Refugee Passport
source_description: Refugees often face significant barriers to education and employment due to the lack of formal documentation proving their qualifications. The European Qualification Passport for Refugees (EQPR), developed by the Council of Europe, addresses this challenge by providing a structured and trusted assessment of refugees’ educational background, even when evidence is incomplete. The objective is to support further studies, labour market access, and social integration across Europe. Implemented since 2017 in 15 countries, the EQPR involves refugees, higher education institutions, employers, and public authorities. The digital pilot leverages the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure to issue and verify EQPR credentials securely. The entire workflow has been digitalised, with qualification assessments issued as verifiable credentials through a blockchain-based diploma platform. Holders can store and share their EQPR via a digital wallet, enabling instant verification by universities and employers across borders. The initiative significantly improves accessibility, trust, and efficiency in qualification recognition. It reduces administrative delays, empowers refugees with portable credentials, and supports inclusive education and employment pathways across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: The European Consortium of Innovative Universities (ECIU)
title: Cross-border micro-credentials
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Student mobility within Europe is hindered by the lack of interoperable systems for recognising short learning experiences such as micro-credentials. Universities often rely on manual processes, and achievements obtained abroad are difficult to transfer or verify. Tampere University and Kaunas University of Technology face these challenges within the ECIU university network, particularly for micro-modules and challenge-based learning. The objective of this use case is to enable trusted, transferable, and learner-controlled micro-credentials across borders. The solution is implemented through the EBSI Early Adopters pilot, using self-sovereign identity and verifiable credentials. Universities issue micro-credentials aligned with shared semantic standards, while students store them in digital wallets and share them as needed. The EBSI infrastructure ensures authenticity, legal validity, and compliance with GDPR and eIDAS. The impact includes reduced administrative workload, improved student mobility, and better recognition of skills and achievements. The use case demonstrates a scalable European model for micro-credential exchange, supporting lifelong learning and flexible education pathways.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Bachelor/Master Diploma Credential
source_description: Cross-border recognition of higher education diplomas remains complex, slowing student mobility and increasing administrative costs for institutions and graduates. This use case aims to simplify the issuance and verification of Bachelor, Master, and PhD diplomas across Europe. Involving Romania, Greece, and France, the initiative supports the issuance of Europass diploma credentials that are valid and verifiable across borders. The objective is to provide students, universities, and employers with a trusted and efficient mechanism to exchange academic qualifications. The solution leverages the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure to issue digital diplomas as verifiable credentials. Academic institutions anchor diploma proofs on the shared European infrastructure, while graduates receive credentials they can store and share through digital wallets. Verification can be performed instantly by authorised parties without intermediaries. The results include faster verification processes, reduced fraud risk, and improved interoperability between national education systems. This use case strengthens trust in academic credentials, enhances student mobility, and lays the foundation for a harmonised European digital education ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Neurokõne - provide more accessible e-services
source_description: Estonian-language e-services remained inaccessible to visually impaired citizens and others who rely on screen readers, as existing text-to-speech solutions for Estonian lacked natural-sounding voices and adequate quality for extended use. The University of Tartu's Natural Language Processing research group developed Neurokõne, a neural network-based text-to-speech synthesis system trained on 92.4 hours of speech data from six speakers. Released as open-source software (MIT licence), the system integrates with Android and iOS accessibility features, enabling Estonian speech synthesis across government e-services and applications. The solution significantly outperforms existing alternatives including Google's Estonian speech synthesis in evaluation tests. Neurokõne forms part of Estonia's national language technology programme ensuring digital services remain accessible to all citizens regardless of ability, supporting the country's digital-first government approach.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: HI IBERIA INGENIERIA Y PROYECTOS SL and Fondazione Bruno Kessler
title: WellCo - Wellbeing and health virtual coach
source_description: Supporting citizens in maintaining long-term physical, cognitive, mental, and social wellbeing is a growing societal challenge, particularly in ageing populations where lifestyle-related risks accumulate over time. Individuals often lack personalised guidance and sustained motivation to adopt healthier behaviours, while health and social care systems face increasing pressure to deliver preventive, user-centred support at scale. The WellCo project, funded under Horizon 2020, addresses this challenge by empowering users to make informed and sustainable lifestyle choices across seven wellbeing domains, including physical activity, nutrition, cognitive stimulation, and social participation. Stakeholders include citizens, healthcare and wellbeing service providers, and public authorities seeking preventive, cost-effective interventions that adapt to individual needs. The objective is to provide continuous, personalised guidance and follow-up that supports behavioural change and long-term wellbeing. The solution is implemented through a digital platform featuring a virtual coaching system that delivers tailored interventions based on individual profiles, preferences, and behavioural patterns. Personalisation is achieved through data-driven models that analyse user interactions and contextual information to recommend goals, activities, and social engagement opportunities. The system integrates mobile interfaces, social networking features, and health-related data sources. The project demonstrates improved user engagement, more effective behaviour change support, and scalable delivery of personalised wellbeing services, contributing to better quality of life and reduced long-term pressure on health and care systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Sorting of Municipal Waste as an Enabler of the Circular Economy
source_description: Municipal waste management systems face persistent challenges in increasing recycling rates, improving material purity, and reducing the volume of waste sent to landfill. Manual sorting processes are labour-intensive, costly, and expose workers to health and safety risks, while also limiting the efficiency of material recovery. The “ZRR for municipal waste” research project addresses these challenges by modernising waste sorting operations to better support circular economy objectives. Stakeholders include municipal authorities, waste management operators, workers, and recycling industries seeking higher-quality secondary raw materials. The objective is to increase recovery rates, capture valuable materials from rejected waste streams, and improve working conditions within treatment plants. The solution introduces robotic sorting systems equipped with advanced perception and decision-making capabilities, integrated into existing waste treatment facilities. These systems analyse waste streams in real time to identify and separate materials with high precision, complementing or replacing manual sorting. Operational data is used to optimise performance under real plant conditions. Results from pilot deployments, including tests in Barcelona, show higher recycling yields, improved purity of recovered materials, and reduced landfill disposal. The initiative delivers environmental benefits, operational efficiency gains, and safer working environments, demonstrating the potential for scalable, technology-enabled circular waste management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Prevention of Diabetic Foot Syndrome
source_description: Diabetic Foot Syndrome represents a major public health concern, frequently leading to hospitalisation and lower-limb amputation if not detected at an early stage. Many patients lack accessible tools for continuous monitoring of foot health outside clinical settings, resulting in delayed intervention and increased healthcare costs. Team FAIDEN from Leiden University proposed a user-friendly software solution to support at-home monitoring of early warning signs associated with diabetic complications. The objective is to empower patients to detect anomalies promptly and seek timely medical advice, thereby reducing severe outcomes. The proposed system uses machine learning models trained on clinical image datasets to identify visual indicators of inflammation, ulcers or tissue deterioration. Through image capture via smartphone or dedicated devices, computer vision algorithms analyse patterns and classify risk levels. The application provides automated feedback and may connect to healthcare providers for further assessment. The project is currently at the concept and development stage, presented within innovation and regional collaboration frameworks. Its potential impact includes earlier detection, reduced hospital admissions, lower amputation rates and improved patient autonomy, contributing to cost savings and improved quality of life.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smart enforcement: automated detection and handling of prohibited transit in Vojkovice
source_description: The municipality of Vojkovice has experienced increased safety risks and infrastructure damage due to heavy trucks using roads where transit is prohibited. Manual enforcement mechanisms proved insufficient, limiting the municipality’s ability to monitor violations and impose penalties effectively. The objective of the project is to strengthen traffic law enforcement, protect infrastructure and improve quality of life for residents by introducing automated monitoring and sanctioning mechanisms. The system employs camera-based monitoring infrastructure combined with automated number plate recognition technology to detect unauthorised transit in real time. Image processing algorithms extract vehicle identifiers, while rule-based validation systems compare detected vehicles against authorised transit databases. Integration with municipal enforcement systems enables automated generation of violation records and supports administrative follow-up procedures. The project has been implemented as a smart enforcement solution within the municipality. It improves detection accuracy, accelerates penalisation procedures, enhances road safety and reduces infrastructure damage, while optimising resource allocation within local law enforcement services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: AOC Consorci Administració Oberta de Catalunya
title: La Paula i la Rita - the chatbot assistants in the authentication processes in Catalunya
source_description: Catalonia's Open Administration Consortium (AOC) receives over 91,000 annual support requests, with citizens struggling to navigate complex e-government procedures for digital identification and certificate management. The AOC deployed La Paula (January 2021) and La Rita (April 2021) as AI-powered chatbot assistants supporting the VALid identification service and idCAT Certificate respectively, developed in partnership with 1MillionBot. The chatbots use natural language processing to interpret citizen queries and provide instant responses 24/7, achieving over 95% accuracy rate. In 2022, Paula supported 62,588 people with 127,454 messages whilst Rita assisted 43,520 people through 100,606 messages. The AOC has pioneered algorithmic transparency in Spain, publishing detailed documentation of chatbot operation, governance, and limitations. In May 2024, the AOC upgraded to generative AI chatbots, serving 11,575 monthly users with 88% success rate and 90% cost savings per query.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Process Mining pilot for the support service and case management of the Diputació de Girona
source_description: Public sector support and case management services often appear straightforward but can hide significant operational complexity that affects efficiency, response times, and resource allocation. At the Diputació de Girona, the user support service managed by the AOC faced challenges in understanding process variability and identifying improvement opportunities based on traditional reporting methods. The objective of this pilot was to gain a clear, evidence-based view of how support processes actually function in practice and to identify optimisation scenarios that could improve service delivery. Stakeholders include support staff, service managers, and public sector users relying on timely and effective assistance. The solution applies process mining techniques to system event logs generated by support and records management platforms. By reconstructing real process flows from operational data, the approach reveals hidden process variants, bottlenecks, and rework loops. The pilot uncovered more than 3,400 distinct process variants within workflows previously assumed to be linear. Simulation capabilities allow decision-makers to test “what-if” scenarios, such as changing escalation paths between support levels. The results indicate potential savings of up to 16,000 processing hours per year, alongside improved transparency and data-driven decision-making. The pilot demonstrates how process intelligence can significantly enhance efficiency, service quality, and organisational learning in public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: AOC Consorci Administració Oberta de Catalunya
title: Automatic classification of citizens' issues or solecituds
source_description: Public administrations receive large volumes of citizen requests through digital channels, often submitted as generic applications that require manual review and routing. This leads to delays, inconsistent handling, and increased administrative workload. The AOC initiative addresses the need to streamline the intake and management of citizen submissions received via platforms such as EACAT and e-TRAM. Stakeholders include civil servants responsible for case handling, administrative managers, and citizens expecting timely responses. The objective is to improve efficiency and consistency by automatically classifying incoming requests and directing them to the appropriate services. The solution implements predictive classification models trained on historical application data to analyse the content and metadata of submissions. Incoming requests are automatically categorised based on learned patterns, enabling faster routing and prioritisation. The system integrates with existing document and case management platforms, supporting human oversight and continuous improvement. The pilot demonstrates reduced manual effort, faster response times, and more consistent case handling. It also improves scalability as request volumes grow, while freeing staff to focus on higher-value tasks. Overall, the initiative enhances administrative efficiency and user experience, supporting more responsive and effective digital public services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Lithuanian solution for systematised forecast of the regional labour market demand
source_description: Regional authorities often lack timely, evidence-based insights into how labour market demand evolves, making it difficult to plan vocational education, reskilling programmes and economic development policies. In Lithuania, the Panevėžys Development Agency initiated this pilot to address fragmentation of labour market data and the absence of long-term, region-specific forecasts. Stakeholders include regional development agencies, vocational training providers, educational institutions, employers and job seekers. The objective is to provide a comprehensive and forward-looking view of labour market dynamics to better align skills supply with future demand. The solution automatically collects and aggregates publicly available data sources related to employment, education, demographics and economic activity. Advanced forecasting models are applied to identify trends, skill shortages and emerging occupations over extended time horizons. The system integrates these outputs into a regional labour market model that supports scenario analysis and policy planning. The pilot was co-created with Neurotechnology, a Lithuanian technology company acting as a startup partner. The impact includes improved strategic planning for vocational guidance, more targeted training and retraining services, and better-informed regional economic policies. Qualitatively, the solution reduces manual analytical effort, improves forecast accuracy and provides a scalable decision-support tool that can be replicated in other regions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Lithuania Solution for greening the city of Vilnius using satellite data and AI
source_description: Urban greenery plays a critical role in environmental quality and citizens’ wellbeing, yet monitoring vegetation health across an entire city is resource-intensive and often relies on manual inspections. The City of Vilnius launched this pilot to improve oversight of urban green areas and enable early identification of issues such as drought stress, lack of maintenance or illegal felling. Stakeholders include municipal environmental departments, urban planners, maintenance contractors and citizens. The objective is to reduce administrative burden while improving the accuracy and timeliness of greenery management decisions. The prototype continuously monitors the city’s green infrastructure using a combination of radar and optical satellite imagery. Analytical algorithms process time-series data to detect changes in vegetation condition, identify problem areas and flag anomalies requiring intervention. Outputs are visualised through a monitoring interface that supports planning of watering, mowing, replacement and enforcement activities. The pilot significantly reduces the need for on-site inspections, improves detection of illegal or unauthorised actions, and enables proactive maintenance. It delivers qualitative gains in efficiency, environmental protection and decision-making quality, while providing a scalable model for data-driven urban environmental management that can be extended to other cities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Lithuania Innovative solution for the assessment of the impact and damage of hydrometeorological phenomena
source_description: Extreme weather events and hazardous natural phenomena pose increasing risks to populations, infrastructure and economic activity, yet information about their impact is often fragmented across agencies and data sources. This Lithuanian pilot was initiated to strengthen national capabilities in monitoring, forecasting and impact assessment of hydrometeorological events. Stakeholders include public authorities, emergency services, infrastructure operators, businesses and citizens. The objective is to improve situational awareness and deliver more accurate and timely alerts to support preparedness and response. The solution integrates data from multiple sources, including meteorological observations, environmental sensors and historical records, into a unified processing pipeline. Predictive and analytical models are applied to monitor conditions, forecast hazardous events and assess potential impacts and damages across sectors. The system supports the generation of targeted alerts and risk assessments tailored to specific regions and user groups. The pilot improves the performance of climate monitoring and forecasting, enhances coordination between institutions, and supports more effective risk communication. Qualitative impacts include faster response times, better-informed decision-making and increased resilience of communities and economic actors. The approach is designed to scale nationally and to evolve with additional data sources and use cases.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Servizz.Gov Chatbox in Malta
source_description: Citizens often need quick answers to routine questions about public services, but traditional customer-service models in government can be costly to scale and may deliver inconsistent response times across ministries. In Malta, the Servizz.Gov chatbot was introduced to improve front-line digital interaction and create a shared support layer that could serve multiple ministries more efficiently. The objective is to provide more immediate access to information, achieve economies of scale through horizontal collaboration, and gradually develop a more capable citizen chatbot integrated with wider government services. The implementation uses a chatbot architecture based initially on a rule-based mechanism and FAQ content, with machine-learning elements added incrementally as user intents are captured and used to refine the model through iteration and feedback. At a conceptual level, the solution combines a central knowledge base, conversational handling in Maltese and English, and a training loop that improves responses over time. The longer-term design also envisages integration with third-party systems so that the chatbot can move beyond information provision towards more connected service support. The impact includes reduced waiting time for routine enquiries, broader 24/7 digital access, and more consistent handling of common questions. It also improves scalability across government and creates operational value by consolidating support functions into a shared conversational channel.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI tool to spot undeclared swimming pools in France
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Property-tax compliance is difficult to enforce comprehensively when local authorities depend on declarations that may omit features affecting taxable value, such as swimming pools and other built structures. In France, this use case was developed to help the tax administration identify undeclared swimming pools more efficiently and strengthen property-tax enforcement using large-scale image analysis. The objective is to detect non-declared taxable features, increase the accuracy of property records, and improve revenue collection without relying solely on manual inspection. The implementation uses a computer-vision system developed with Capgemini, working with aerial photographs and comparing detected features against real-estate and tax databases. At a conceptual level, the system scans images for pool-like visual patterns, links identified locations to property records, and flags cases where a relevant address appears not to have declared a pool. This creates a targeted workflow for further tax compliance action. Reported results show that 20,356 previously undeclared residential swimming pools were identified, generating about EUR 10 million in additional tax revenue in the earlier reported phase, while later reporting noted wider fiscal gains and plans to extend checks to features such as annexes and verandas. The impact includes stronger compliance detection, more efficient tax control, and improved scalability in property-record verification.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: VeRa 1.0, the artificial intelligence that tracks tax evaders
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Italy loses over €99 billion annually to tax evasion, with €30 billion from VAT alone, whilst traditional enforcement methods struggled to identify non-compliant taxpayers among millions of returns. The Agenzia delle Entrate developed VeRa (Verifica dei Rapporti finanziari), an AI-powered algorithm that cross-references taxpayer filings with data from the Financial Relations Archive, property registries, bank accounts, and electronic payments to identify compliance risks. In 2022, VeRa flagged one million high-risk cases and helped prevent over €6.8 billion in fraud. The system assigns risk scores enabling targeted audits rather than random checks, whilst EU-funded projects through Sogei introduce network analysis, machine learning, and data visualisation for complex evasion schemes. In 2023, the agency recovered €18.1 billion, increasing to projected €19.6 billion by 2025. A complementary AI chatbot launched in 2023 analyses VAT returns in real-time, flagging irregularities for immediate investigation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications (MKM)
title: "Donate a Speech"": Estonia crowdsources speech data for the preservation of the Estonian language"
source_description: Estonia identified the limited availability of high-quality speech datasets as a barrier to the development of advanced language technologies in a small-language context. To preserve the Estonian language and enhance digital public services, the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications and the State Information System Agency launched the “Donate a Speech” campaign. The objective is to create an open, large-scale spoken language corpus to support the development of speech-based digital services across the public and private sectors. Citizens voluntarily contribute voice recordings, which are anonymised and compiled into a national speech database. The dataset supports the training of machine learning models for speech recognition, text-to-speech and real-time subtitling applications. The infrastructure integrates data collection platforms, secure storage systems and research access frameworks. The initiative has been implemented and successfully collected thousands of hours of speech data. It strengthens Estonia’s digital sovereignty, enhances accessibility of public services, supports innovation in language technologies and improves inclusivity through better speech-enabled services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Applying AI to increase quality in the patent grant process at the European Patent Office
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Patent examination at the European Patent Office involves assessing millions of applications against complex technical and legal criteria, with AI-related inventions presenting particular challenges due to rapidly evolving technology and novel patentability questions. The EPO has implemented AI and machine learning tools to enhance patent examination quality, assist examiners with prior art searches, and improve consistency in assessing technical character and inventive step for computer-implemented inventions. The 2024 Guidelines for Examination introduced specific provisions for AI inventions, requiring disclosure of training datasets when necessary to reproduce claimed technical effects and establishing standards for plausibility of AI-related claims. These updates followed decisions from the Boards of Appeal (including T 0161/18) addressing sufficiency of disclosure for machine learning inventions. The system supports examiners whilst maintaining human decision-making authority, processing applications across all 39 member states of the European Patent Organisation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Advanced Technology for National Topographic Map Updating - Increasing spatial data accuracy with AI in Finland
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Maintaining accurate and up-to-date national topographic maps is essential for land management, infrastructure planning, environmental monitoring, and public safety. Traditional map updating methods are time-consuming and struggle to keep pace with rapid changes in the built and natural environment. In Finland, the National Land Survey sought to improve the accuracy and timeliness of spatial data while reducing manual effort. The objective of the ATMU project was to enhance object detection and change recognition for buildings, roads, and watercourses at national scale. Stakeholders include mapping authorities, planners, and public agencies relying on high-quality geospatial data. The solution applies advanced image analysis techniques to aerial and satellite imagery, using deep neural models trained for object detection and change recognition tasks. Different model architectures are applied to specific features, supported by transfer and multitask learning approaches. By the end of the project, building detection achieved an accuracy of 97.9%, and 96% of building and road changes were correctly identified. The project delivers significant improvements in data accuracy, update frequency, and operational efficiency, providing a scalable foundation for modern, data-driven national mapping services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Mapping mangroves with Serverless and Deep Learning
source_description: Global mangrove mapping relied on infrequently updated datasets that could not capture the dynamic changes affecting these critical coastal ecosystems, limiting understanding of carbon sequestration, biodiversity, and natural coastal protection. The UK Hydrographic Office (UKHO) developed the ADMIRALTY Global Mangrove Data Set using deep learning applied to European Space Agency Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, creating the world's highest resolution, most up-to-date global view of mangrove forests. The neural network was trained on over 7,000 coastal images and achieves geo-generalisability across diverse global locations through collaboration between UKHO's Data Science, Data Engineering, and Remote Sensing teams. The system automatically updates every six months, processing new cloud-free satellite imagery to detect mangrove extent changes. This serverless architecture enables scalable analysis supporting marine navigation, coastal sustainability planning, and climate change research on these vital carbon sinks that sequester 3-5 times more carbon than inland tropical forests.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SensusQ: transforming information into knowledge with the help of automation, integration, and interoperability
source_description: Military intelligence operations struggle with data overload from multiple sources including UAVs, cyber events, open-source intelligence, and human reports, requiring rapid integration and analysis to support tactical decision-making. SensusQ, an Estonian DefenceTech startup founded by combat veterans Marko Kaseleht and Villiko Nurmoja, developed an AI-powered intelligence management platform that fuses data from diverse sensors and sources into a unified operational picture. The system has been deployed by NATO forces and Ukraine, where it has demonstrated 200% improvement in response times and significant increases in data accuracy. In 2024, SensusQ secured €3.8M funding from US-based New North Ventures and in 2025 contributed to the British Army's Project ASGARD digital targeting initiative. The platform supports both the Estonian Defence League and allied nations, featuring NATO-standard military symbols, cross-data search, and standardised reporting whilst maintaining on-premise deployment to ensure sensitive data remains under client control.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: The AI algorithm that blew up Italy’s school system
source_description: Italy's education system faced the annual challenge of assigning approximately 100,000 teachers to schools across diverse regions, a complex optimization problem that had historically relied on manual processes prone to errors and delays. The Ministry of Education implemented an algorithmic system to automatically assign teachers to schools based on preferences, qualifications, and regional needs, processing massive datasets to generate placements within compressed timeframes. However, the 2020 deployment generated significant controversy when thousands of teachers received assignments to schools far from their preferences or in regions they had not selected, with some relocated hundreds of kilometres from their homes. The algorithm's logic and decision criteria remained opaque, preventing affected teachers from understanding or effectively challenging their placements. The case became a prominent example in debates about algorithmic accountability in public administration, highlighting tensions between efficiency gains and transparency requirements in automated government decision-making.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Signals - Detection of statistically significant clusters in reported infectious diseases
source_description: Germany's disease surveillance system required methods to identify unusual patterns in reported infections that might indicate emerging outbreaks, requiring analysis of large volumes of routine surveillance data against expected baselines. The Robert Koch Institute (RKI) developed the Signals system using statistical algorithms to automatically detect statistically significant changes in reported disease incidence that warrant epidemiological investigation. The system processes data from Germany's mandatory notification system, comparing current case counts against historical patterns whilst adjusting for seasonal variations and reporting delays. When anomalies are detected, automated alerts trigger specialist review to determine whether observed increases represent genuine outbreaks requiring public health response. The platform has operated since 2015, providing early warning capabilities that complement traditional epidemiological surveillance methods and supporting Germany's capacity to detect and respond to infectious disease threats.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI to spot counterfeit products at customs
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Customs authorities face growing challenges in detecting counterfeit goods within increasing volumes of international trade. Manual inspection processes are resource-intensive and may not consistently identify sophisticated counterfeits, undermining trademark protection and fair competition. The German Federal Information Technology Centre (ITZBund), advising the Central Office for Commercial Legal Protection and the General Directorate of Customs, developed an AI-supported solution to enhance counterfeit detection. The objective is to improve efficiency and accuracy in identifying infringing goods while supporting customs officers in decision-making. The system uses image recognition algorithms trained on extensive datasets of authentic and counterfeit product images. Visual data captured during inspections are processed through convolutional neural networks that classify brand attributes and estimate the probability of counterfeiting. The system continuously updates its training dataset to improve performance. Integration with customs databases enables officers to access risk assessments in real time, while final decisions remain under human authority. The solution has been implemented within customs advisory frameworks. It increases detection accuracy, accelerates inspections, reduces manual workload and strengthens protection of intellectual property rights.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot LinA: the chatbot that answers general inquiries in the field of motor vehicle tax and customs law
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Germany's customs authority receives high volumes of citizen inquiries about import duties, customs procedures, and international trade regulations, creating significant workload for staff and variable response times for users. The Federal Customs Administration (Zoll) deployed LinA, an AI-powered chatbot that answers general inquiries about customs matters through natural language interaction available 24/7 on the authority's website. The system handles routine questions about duty calculations, prohibited goods, travel allowances, and customs procedures, freeing human agents to address complex cases requiring specialist expertise. LinA is part of Germany's broader Bundesbots initiative developing standardised chatbot infrastructure for federal agencies, sharing technological approaches and ensuring consistent user experience across government services. The platform demonstrates how conversational AI can improve public service accessibility whilst managing increasing demand for digital interaction channels with government authorities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Assessment of money laundering activities through AI
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The German Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) is responsible for analysing suspicious transaction reports to detect and prevent money laundering and terrorist financing. The increasing volume and complexity of financial data make manual analysis inefficient and time-consuming. The objective of this use case is to enhance risk analysis capabilities and improve the efficiency of processing suspicious activity reports. The solution automates parts of the analytical workflow by applying machine learning techniques to identify patterns, correlations, and anomalies within large datasets of financial transactions and reports. The system continuously incorporates new data, enabling iterative re-evaluation of cases and improving detection accuracy over time. It integrates with existing FIU systems to support analysts in prioritising high-risk cases. As an implemented solution, it contributes to faster processing times, improved risk assessment, and more effective allocation of investigative resources, strengthening the overall capacity to combat financial crime.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot ViOlA for the homepage of the german Federal Central Tax Office
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Germany's Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) serves millions of citizens seeking employment services, training, and benefits. With 14,000 daily consultations and 95,000 telephone calls, managing routine enquiries whilst ensuring staff availability for complex cases presents a significant operational challenge. The Bundesagentur für Arbeit deployed ViOlA (Virtual Online Assistant), an AI-powered chatbot on its website to handle common enquiries about job searches, unemployment benefits, vocational training, and family allowances. The chatbot uses natural language processing to understand user questions and provide relevant information or direct users to appropriate resources. ViOlA operates alongside other digital services including video consultations (Mein Videotermin) that connect over 1,000 locations. The agency's digital transformation runs on a containerised infrastructure with approximately 600 services and 24,000 containers managed through Rancher Prime and Kubernetes, migrated at the end of 2021. The chatbot reduces pressure on telephone services and local offices by addressing frequently asked questions automatically, allowing the agency's 100,000 employees across 156 employment agencies and 302 job centres to focus on personalised advice and complex benefit determinations. The approach supports the agency's mission to remain close to customers whilst managing increasing service demands.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: X-PIDER - an electonic investigative tool in the field of e-commerce used by the German tax authorities
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Tax authorities face growing challenges detecting undeclared economic activity as commerce increasingly moves online. Traditional audit methods cannot efficiently monitor the vast volume of internet commercial activity, creating opportunities for tax evasion through e-commerce platforms and social media. The German Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern) deployed X-PIDER, an AI-powered web crawling and scraping system to automatically identify taxable business activity online. The system operates as an internet crawler connected to a knowledge management component, systematically following links across websites, e-commerce platforms, and social media to detect indicators of commercial activity. X-PIDER can identify internet pages suggesting business transactions and collects taxpayer-related data for cross-referencing with tax records. The system can be deployed anywhere on the internet and autonomously navigates web content to build comprehensive profiles of online commercial presence. X-PIDER supports the regional tax authorities by providing centralised intelligence on potential tax non-compliance. The system complements other AI initiatives in German tax administration including the Steuerchatbot virtual assistant (extended nationally and to English and French in 2024), nudging tools that adapt communication based on taxpayer risk profiles, and automated verification systems for processing tax returns. These tools collectively strengthen enforcement whilst reducing manual investigative workload.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Environmental monitoring with AI at the German Environment Agency
source_description: Environmental authorities face growing challenges in analysing large volumes of heterogeneous data across climate, air quality, energy and resource use, often stored in fragmented and hard-to-access systems. The German Environment Agency (UBA) established its AI Application Lab to improve the operational use of complex environmental data and support evidence-based environmental policy. Stakeholders include UBA departments, federal and regional authorities, researchers and policy makers. The objective is to enable cross-disciplinary and cross-scale analysis of environmental data while ensuring that digital solutions themselves are energy- and resource-efficient. The Lab develops and evaluates data-driven applications that integrate diverse datasets such as environmental measurements, administrative records and scientific data. Advanced analytical pipelines and modelling approaches are used to structure, process and visualise complex information, making it accessible across domains. Particular emphasis is placed on sustainable system design, including efficient computing architectures and responsible data practices. The initiative improves analytical depth, reduces manual effort in data preparation, and enhances the usability of environmental data for decision-making. Qualitatively, it strengthens institutional capacity, improves transparency and supports scalable, reproducible analysis across environmental policy areas.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA)
title: AI warns german businesses that the documents uploaded to apply for import tax exemptions might be wrong
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: German businesses, in the case of an application to limit the Renewable Energy Sources (EEG) surcharge as part of the special equalization regulation, must submit all relevant documents before the material deadline. If this deadline is missed, the electricity-intensive companies face the irremediable rejection of the application and thus the payment of the full EEG surcharge. In order to minimize this risk for companies, BAFA has fundamentally modernized the application process this year: With the help of artificial intelligence, the uploaded application documents are automatically searched for errors. If it is determined with a certain probability that the wrong documents may have been uploaded, the application portal issues a warning message.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Institute for Geosciences and Natural Resources (BGR)
title: Artificial intelligence helps predict groundwater levels
source_description: Climate change and increasing water demand are placing growing pressure on groundwater resources, making reliable prediction of groundwater levels critical for sustainable water management. Public authorities and planners require accurate forecasts to support drinking water supply, agricultural irrigation, infrastructure protection, and land-use planning. The Federal Institute for Geosciences and Natural Resources and the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology address this need through a joint initiative focused on nationwide groundwater level prediction. Stakeholders include water authorities, municipalities, farmers, and infrastructure operators. The objective is to improve decision-making by providing timely and reliable groundwater forecasts that support risk assessment and adaptation strategies. The solution uses artificial neural network models trained on historical groundwater measurements, meteorological data, and hydrological variables. These models capture complex, non-linear relationships influencing groundwater behaviour and generate predictive insights at regional and national scales. The results support more accurate identification of drought-prone areas, zones at risk of subsidence, and regions vulnerable to high groundwater levels. The initiative enhances preparedness, supports sustainable resource management, and enables evidence-based adaptation to climate impacts, delivering significant long-term environmental and socio-economic benefits.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Institute for Geosciences and Natural Resources (BGR)
title: ITERATOR – Automated Detection of Pores in Rocks
source_description: Understanding the physical properties of rocks is essential for applications such as geothermal energy, fluid storage, and geological disposal, where porosity plays a decisive role. Traditionally, analysing pore frequency, size, shape, and distribution from microscopic images has been a time-consuming and manual task, limiting consistency and scalability. The ITERATOR project addresses this challenge by supporting geoscientists in the systematic analysis of rock microstructures. Stakeholders include geological research institutions and applied geoscience bodies that require reliable parameters to assess heat flow, fluid flow, and mechanical behaviour of rocks. The objective is to improve the accuracy, reproducibility, and efficiency of porosity analysis while enabling deeper insights into the relationships between mineral phases, stress regimes, and pore orientation. The solution applies advanced image processing techniques to scanning electron microscopy images to semi-automatically detect and characterise pores. Algorithms identify pore boundaries and compute quantitative descriptors, including size distribution and shape metrics, which are then linked to geological and petrophysical models. The results significantly reduce manual effort and increase analytical consistency. The project enables more detailed and data-driven interpretation of rock properties, supporting improved modelling, better parameter estimation, and more robust decision-making in geoscientific applications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Institute for Geosciences and Natural Resources (BGR)
title: MACRO – Cross-Scale Regionalisation of Hydrogeological Information
source_description: Hydrogeological assessments often rely on data collected at different spatial scales, making it difficult to derive coherent regional models that support water management and planning. Local measurements provide high accuracy but limited coverage, while regional datasets lack detail and consistency. The MACRO project addresses this gap by developing methods to integrate and regionalise hydrogeological information across scales. Stakeholders include geological surveys, water authorities, and planners who require harmonised, spatially consistent groundwater information for sustainable resource management. The objective is to establish a methodological foundation that allows reliable upscaling of hydrogeological parameters while preserving local characteristics. The project develops and tests data-driven modelling approaches using selected hydrogeological use cases. Diverse datasets, such as geological maps, monitoring data, and environmental variables, are combined to generate regionally consistent representations of subsurface properties. These methods are designed to support cross-scale learning and validation, ensuring robustness across different spatial resolutions. The project delivers improved regional groundwater models, reduced uncertainty in parameter estimation, and enhanced transferability of local knowledge to larger areas. This contributes to more informed decision-making, better water resource planning, and a scalable framework for nationwide hydrogeological assessments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Ministry of Economics and Climate Protection (BMWi)
title: EnMAP - Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program
source_description: Traditional satellite imagery captures only a limited portion of the electromagnetic spectrum, restricting scientists' ability to detect subtle environmental changes in vegetation health, water quality, soil composition, and mineral deposits essential for climate monitoring and resource management. EnMAP (Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program) is Germany's first hyperspectral satellite mission, launched in April 2022 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9. The satellite carries a dual-spectrometer instrument capturing 230 spectral bands from 420 to 2450 nanometres at 30-metre ground resolution, enabling detection of biochemical and geochemical signatures invisible to conventional sensors. Operating in sun-synchronous orbit at 653 kilometres altitude, EnMAP records up to 5,000 kilometres of imagery daily with 4-day revisit capability. The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) leads scientific coordination whilst DLR manages operations. In 2024, the SpectralEarth dataset was released, comprising 538,974 image patches for training AI foundation models in hyperspectral analysis. EnMAP provides unprecedented environmental monitoring capability for agriculture, forestry, water management, and geology applications. The mission supports Copernicus services and contributes to climate protection initiatives by enabling precise characterisation of ecosystem changes. Data is freely available to the global scientific community through DLR's ground segment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Office of Consumer Protection and Food Safety (BVL)
title: G@ZIELT: Safe shopping on the internet
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Consumers in Germany are increasingly purchasing food and cosmetics online, with a rising trend in online purchases of various items including kitchen utensils, toys, clothing, and tobacco products. The Federal Office of Consumer Protection and Food Safety (BVL) hosts a central unit called G@ZIELT, jointly managed by federal states, to regulate internet trade in products covered by the Food and Feed Code and tobacco. The G@ZIELT unit searches the internet to identify risky food offers, misleading labels, and unregistered businesses, reporting findings to appropriate authorities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Automated image recognition for determining the type of wood
source_description: Ensuring the legal origin of timber products is a key requirement under the European Timber Trade Regulation, which obliges market participants to accurately document the wood species used in traded goods. Manual identification of wood species is labour-intensive, requires specialist expertise, and is difficult to apply at scale for inspections and compliance checks. This use case addresses the need for efficient and reliable verification methods that support regulatory enforcement. Stakeholders include regulatory authorities, inspection bodies, and timber traders responsible for due diligence. The objective is to enable large-scale verification of declared wood species and reduce the risk of illegal timber entering the market. The solution involves the development of automated image recognition systems that analyse macroscopic and microscopic wood images. By learning distinguishing visual patterns across species, the system supports consistent classification and comparison against declared information. Integrated into inspection workflows, it enables rapid screening of products and supports expert decision-making. The results include faster and more scalable compliance checks, reduced dependence on scarce specialist resources, and improved detection of mislabelled timber. The initiative strengthens enforcement of timber regulations, supports sustainable forestry, and enhances transparency in the wood supply chain.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Monitoring biological diversity in agricultural landscapes with remote sensing
source_description: Maintaining and enhancing biodiversity in agricultural landscapes is a central objective of agri-environment-climate measures under the EU Common Agricultural Policy. Policymakers and environmental agencies require consistent, large-scale monitoring tools to assess habitat quality, land-use intensity, and landscape structure over time. Traditional field surveys are accurate but costly and limited in spatial coverage. This project addresses the need for a nationwide, spatially explicit monitoring approach that captures biodiversity-relevant habitat features across agricultural landscapes. Stakeholders include agricultural authorities, environmental agencies, and policymakers responsible for evaluating and designing biodiversity measures. The objective is to establish a robust indicator framework that reflects landscape and field-level characteristics relevant to different taxonomic groups. The solution uses Earth observation data from the Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellites within the Copernicus programme to model habitat features and land-use intensity at large scales. Spatial indicators are derived to describe landscape structure, elements, and management intensity in cropland and grassland areas. The results provide consistent, repeatable monitoring of biodiversity-related patterns at national level. The project supports evidence-based policy evaluation, improved targeting of agri-environment measures, and long-term tracking of biodiversity trends.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Language skills in the digital age
source_description: Public administrations operating in international contexts require fast and reliable translation capabilities, yet traditional human-only workflows struggle to keep pace with growing volumes of multilingual content. The Federal Language Office initiated this pilot to modernise language services and support staff working with foreign-language materials. Stakeholders include translators, analysts, defence and diplomatic personnel, and administrative units relying on timely translations. The objective is to improve efficiency while maintaining acceptable quality standards for official use. The pilot applies automated translation systems trained on extensive existing linguistic corpora held by the institution. These systems learn from previously translated documents and continuously improve translation accuracy across relevant language pairs. The solution is integrated into existing translation workflows, allowing human experts to review, correct and refine outputs rather than translating from scratch. The impact includes faster turnaround times, reduced workload for routine translations and better prioritisation of expert human resources. Qualitatively, the project improves operational responsiveness and supports knowledge sharing in multilingual environments, while laying the groundwork for scalable language services across government.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI in numerical weather and climate forecasting
source_description: Numerical weather prediction relies on complex physical models and vast quantities of observational data, including satellite imagery. Processing and integrating this data efficiently remains computationally demanding and may limit forecasting precision, particularly in extreme weather scenarios. The German Weather Service (DWD), in collaboration with Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, developed an AI-supported neural network approach to enhance the processing of satellite imagery within forecasting workflows. The objective is to improve predictive accuracy and optimise the integration of observational data into numerical models. The system uses deep neural networks trained on historical meteorological datasets to extract relevant atmospheric patterns from satellite images and translate them into parameters usable by forecasting models. The AI component operates alongside traditional physics-based simulations, providing complementary inputs that refine model outputs. The approach has been implemented within operational research environments at DWD. It contributes to more accurate short-term forecasts, improved detection of extreme weather events and enhanced computational efficiency, supporting better-informed public warnings and climate resilience planning.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: German Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF)
title: AI-based Integrated identity management for asylum procedures, improving plausability, data quality and security aspects
source_description: Asylum procedures require accurate registration and verification of personal identity under challenging conditions, often involving missing documents, language barriers, and high case volumes. Manual processes increase the risk of data inconsistencies, duplicate records, and security vulnerabilities. This use case supports the Federal Office responsible for asylum procedures by improving the quality, plausibility, and security of identity data. Stakeholders include caseworkers, asylum authorities, and applicants whose cases depend on accurate and fair identity assessment. The objective is to streamline registration processes while strengthening data integrity and preventing fraud. The solution integrates multiple automated support tools into a single identity management system. These include automated transcription of names from non-Latin scripts, dialect analysis to support origin verification, biometric image checks to prevent duplicate files, and extraction of relevant information from mobile devices when documents are unavailable. The system supports caseworkers with structured, evidence-based inputs while maintaining oversight and control. The results include improved data quality, reduced duplication, enhanced security, and more efficient case handling. This leads to faster, fairer asylum procedures and increased trust in administrative processes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot for the 2021 Federal Elections
source_description: Elections require well-informed citizens who understand voting procedures, the electoral system, and key democratic principles. During the 2021 Federal Elections, the Federal Agency for Civic Education sought to improve access to reliable information and support voter engagement, particularly among digitally active audiences. Traditional information channels can be difficult to navigate or overwhelming, especially for first-time voters. The objective of this use case was to provide accessible, structured, and neutral information about the election process and related political topics. The solution involved deploying an interactive chatbot that delivered curated content on voting procedures, electoral system structure, and practical considerations before election day. Information was organised into thematic dialogues, complemented by quizzes that allowed users to test their knowledge. The chatbot was accessible through digital channels commonly used by citizens, enabling on-demand interaction. The initiative improved accessibility to civic information, encouraged active learning, and supported informed participation in the electoral process.
