Stakeholders include pathologists, oncologists, and patients whose treatment decisions depend on reliable tumour grading. The objective is to improve accuracy and consistency in Ki-67 index calculation. The solution develops a digital image analysis system that automatically identifies tumour cells and calculates the Ki-67 index based on large cell populations in histological slides. The system is trained and validated on representative datasets and designed for integration into clinical workflows. The impact includes improved grading accuracy, reduced observer variability, and lower manual workload. This supports better treatment stratification, more reliable prognostic assessment, and improved quality of care for patients with neuroendocrine tumours.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MIM - Machine learning in the Mammography programme
source_description: Breast cancer screening programmes generate very large volumes of mammograms, the majority of which show no signs of disease, yet all images must be carefully reviewed by specialists. This creates significant workload pressure and limits the capacity of screening services. The MIM project addresses the need to improve efficiency and effectiveness in mammography screening while maintaining high diagnostic quality. Stakeholders include radiologists, screening programme operators, and women participating in national screening initiatives. The objective is to support early detection of breast cancer by enabling more efficient triage of screening images and allowing clinicians to focus attention on higher-risk cases. The solution develops deep learning models trained on large datasets combining mammograms, screening metadata, and confirmed breast cancer diagnoses. By learning complex visual patterns associated with disease and normal findings, the system can identify mammograms that are highly likely to be free of cancer. These predictions can be used to prioritise or streamline review processes within screening workflows. The expected impact includes reduced reading workload, improved use of specialist expertise, and increased screening capacity. Ultimately, the project supports more sustainable screening services while maintaining early detection and patient safety.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Naturinngrep i inngrepsfri natur
source_description: The Norwegian Environment Agency is responsible for maintaining a national map of intervention-free nature, defined as areas located at least one kilometre from the nearest technical infrastructure or human intervention. Monitoring these areas is challenging due to Norway’s vast territory and the need to detect new roads or construction linked to energy and forestry developments. To support systematic surveillance, the Norwegian Computing Center developed an automated method to identify construction and forest roads using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery with 10-metre spatial resolution. The approach applies a deep convolutional neural network based on the U-Net architecture, trained on labelled examples from wind power development sites and known road datasets. The model performs pixel-level segmentation to distinguish road structures from surrounding terrain. Testing in Åfjord municipality successfully identified all wind power development areas, several of which reduced intervention-free zones. Additional training enabled detection of an illegally constructed road in Melhus. The solution improves monitoring efficiency, enables early identification of encroachments and strengthens evidence-based environmental governance while reducing reliance on manual inspection.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot Frida
source_description: NAV introduced Chatbot Frida to improve responsiveness to citizen enquiries and reduce pressure on call centres and service desks. The objective was to provide continuous digital assistance for frequently asked questions related to welfare benefits, employment services and administrative procedures. The chatbot, delivered by boost.ai, is integrated into NAV’s digital service platform and website. It uses natural language processing models trained on historical enquiry data and curated question–answer pairs developed by subject matter experts. The system classifies user intent, retrieves relevant information from knowledge bases and guides users through structured dialogue flows. Escalation mechanisms redirect complex cases to human advisers when required. Frida operates continuously, handling large volumes of routine enquiries simultaneously and standardising responses across regions. The deployment has reduced waiting times, improved accessibility outside office hours and enabled staff to focus on complex cases requiring individual assessment. The system contributes to service efficiency and consistent communication while maintaining oversight through supervised content management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: RE-SIKTET- Conversation and documentation quality in medical telephone assessment assisted by artificial intelligence
source_description: Emergency medical call centres play a critical role in patient safety, yet telephone assessments are complex, time-pressured, and highly dependent on operator experience. Important questions may be missed, documentation quality can vary, and subtle indicators of serious conditions may be overlooked. The RE-SIKTET project addresses these challenges by supporting operators during live medical calls. Stakeholders include emergency call centre staff, healthcare services, and patients relying on accurate triage. The objective is to improve conversation quality, documentation, and clinical assessment without disrupting the natural flow of dialogue. The solution provides an interactive web interface that dynamically suggests relevant questions based on the conversation context, predicted severity, and known medical patterns. Selected questions and responses are automatically documented, creating structured and standardised records. Over time, the system generates large, high-quality datasets describing medical assessment interviews. The project evaluates the effect of this support on call quality and documentation. The impact includes more consistent assessments, reduced risk of misinterpretation, improved documentation, and better decision support for operators. It also creates a strong foundation for further research into communication, triage, and patient safety.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CONWIND: Forskning på smarte driftskontrollteknologier for havvindparker
source_description: Offshore wind energy has significant potential but faces operational challenges that limit efficiency and profitability. Larger turbines reduce costs per unit of energy, yet they also create complex wake effects and turbulent wind fields that increase mechanical stress and reduce energy output. The CONWIND project addresses the need for smarter operational control of offshore wind farms. Stakeholders include energy producers, turbine operators, and grid operators seeking to maximise output and reduce maintenance costs. The objective is to improve wind farm performance through more accurate prediction and control of wind conditions under uncertainty. The solution develops advanced control algorithms that combine wind field modelling, sensor data, and predictive methods to optimise turbine operation across the farm. These control strategies account for wake interactions and uncertainty in environmental conditions. Even modest improvements in control performance can yield significant gains at scale. The project demonstrates that a control system increasing profitability by just over 2% would have major economic impact. CONWIND contributes to lower operating costs, higher energy production, and increased competitiveness of offshore wind, supporting the transition to renewable energy.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Research grant for case management AI
source_description: The Research Council of Norway (RCN) processes large volumes of grant applications, requiring efficient classification and routing to appropriate expert panels. Manual handling is time-consuming and risks inconsistencies, particularly as interdisciplinary research grows. To address this, RCN explored digital support tools to optimise case management while keeping human oversight central. Stakeholders include case officers, expert evaluators, applicants and research institutions. The objective was to reduce administrative workload and improve consistency in thematic classification. The solution applies thematic modelling to analyse submitted proposals and predict characteristics such as academic disciplines, research topics and sector relevance. These predicted tags are presented to case officers, who review and decide on final classifications. The system integrates with existing grant management workflows and supports, rather than replaces, human judgement. Early results indicate improved efficiency, faster processing times and more consistent tagging across applications. The pilot demonstrates how decision support tools can enhance public sector workflows while preserving accountability and professional control.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AdaptAl - Adaptive control of aluminium production
source_description: Aluminium production involves complex, tightly coupled processes that are sensitive to raw material quality, chemical variations, and operational disturbances. Without adaptive control, these variations can exceed tolerance limits, leading to increased costs, waste, and quality issues. The AdaptAl project addresses this challenge by extending digital process optimisation into real-time adaptive control. Stakeholders include aluminium producers, industrial operators, and downstream manufacturing sectors such as automotive and furniture. The objective is to stabilise and optimise production across the aluminium value chain under varying conditions. The solution builds on Hydro’s PRO3 digital twin, which simulates and optimises aluminium production processes. AdaptAl integrates sensor data, virtual models, and optimisation software to enable adaptive control that continuously adjusts process parameters in response to observed deviations. The system is demonstrated in extrusion and forming processes across multiple industrial markets. The impact includes improved process stability, reduced production costs, higher product quality, and increased flexibility. AdaptAl strengthens industrial competitiveness and demonstrates how digital twins and adaptive control can deliver measurable value in energy-intensive manufacturing.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Norsk Hydro's AI tool to detect hackers
source_description: Large industrial operators face significant risks from cyberattacks targeting operational technology and production infrastructure, as demonstrated by the 2019 ransomware attack against Norsk Hydro. As a partly state-owned aluminium producer operating complex, globally distributed industrial systems, Hydro needed a way to strengthen cyber resilience beyond traditional perimeter security. The objective of this use case is to continuously identify vulnerabilities and early warning signs of malicious activity across industrial control systems, reducing the likelihood of large-scale operational disruption. The solution monitors industrial equipment and network behaviour to detect deviations from normal operating patterns over time. It applies machine learning–based anomaly detection techniques trained on historical operational data to identify subtle changes that may indicate cyber intrusion or system misuse. The tool integrates with Hydro’s existing industrial monitoring and security infrastructure, enabling continuous assessment without interrupting production processes. The pilot improved Hydro’s ability to detect security weaknesses earlier and prioritise mitigation actions, strengthening situational awareness across plants. Qualitatively, it reduced reliance on reactive incident response and improved confidence in industrial cybersecurity governance. The project demonstrates the business value of predictive security monitoring in critical infrastructure, particularly for large industrial actors with high availability requirements.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Unsupervised learning to detect customs declarations
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Norwegian customs authorities faced analytical challenges because foreign operators in customs declarations were recorded as free-text entries, resulting in inconsistent spellings and fragmented data that limited statistical analysis and risk assessment. To improve data quality and support enforcement activities, the data analytics department developed an unsupervised clustering solution to group similar operator names automatically. The system constructs similarity networks based on textual features and string distance measures, then applies cluster analysis and cluster-splitting techniques to identify likely matches without pre-labelled training data. By grouping variant spellings and related entities, the tool enhances data harmonisation and supports downstream analytical tasks, including risk profiling and trade pattern analysis. The approach reduces manual cleaning efforts, improves accuracy in identifying economic actors and strengthens the analytical basis for customs controls. The solution increases scalability in processing large declaration datasets and enhances operational insight while preserving human oversight in enforcement decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Automatisert saksbehandling med arkivmessige hensyn for kunstig intelligens
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The Norwegian Maritime Authority seeks to modernise certificate issuance and case processing through automation while ensuring proper archival compliance and long-term document preservation. Manual case handling can be resource-intensive and prone to inconsistencies in documentation management. The objective is to automate administrative workflows while maintaining legally compliant record-keeping practices. Stakeholders include maritime authorities, certification applicants, the National Archives and the Directorate of Digitisation. The new solution integrates automated decision rules into certificate issuance processes and embeds metadata capture, documentation logging and archival structuring within the workflow. Automated systems collect, process and store data while ensuring traceability and accessibility in accordance with public sector information management standards. The project is being developed within a regulatory sandbox and organisational transformation programme. It is currently in development and phased implementation, with testing focused on ensuring archival integrity and lawful automation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate
title: NVE Copernicus 2
source_description: Norway faces significant risks from floods and avalanches, requiring timely monitoring of snow and water conditions. The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE), in collaboration with Norsk Regnesentral, aims to enhance emergency warning systems by improving environmental data analysis. The objective is to strengthen early warning capabilities and disaster preparedness. The project develops algorithms that process satellite imagery from the Copernicus programme alongside hydrological and meteorological data. Machine learning techniques extract indicators related to snow cover, water levels and terrain conditions, supporting predictive modelling for hazard warnings. The system integrates with NVE’s emergency alert infrastructure to provide decision support to authorities. The initiative has been implemented within NVE’s operational forecasting and monitoring framework. It enhances forecasting accuracy, improves response times and strengthens resilience against natural hazards.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-Mind
source_description: Dementia places a growing burden on healthcare systems, and early identification of individuals at risk remains a critical unmet need. The AI-Mind project addresses this challenge by focusing on patients with mild cognitive impairment, a group in which approximately half may progress to dementia. Stakeholders include clinical researchers, neurologists, patients, healthcare providers, and academic institutions coordinated by Oslo Metropolitan University. The objective is to enable earlier and more reliable risk stratification, supporting timely intervention and improved care planning. The project centres on the analysis of electrophysiological brain signals collected through EEG examinations, which can reveal disturbances in brain networks associated with early synaptic dysfunction. The AI-Mind Connector processes EEG data to detect network-level patterns indicative of elevated dementia risk, integrating clinical, demographic, and neurophysiological information into a unified assessment framework. The system is designed to support clinicians rather than replace diagnostic judgement. Funded with approximately EUR 14 million and subject to European ethical review, the project remains in the research and validation phase. Expected impacts include improved diagnostic accuracy, better targeting of preventive measures, and reduced long-term healthcare costs through earlier intervention.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
source_description: The National Archives of Norway sought to enhance access to digitised historical documents by automating transcription and metadata extraction processes. Large volumes of scanned archival material required efficient processing to enable searchability and identification of sensitive content. The initiative combined advanced optical character recognition with systematic preprocessing of scanned files to improve text recognition accuracy. Machine-trained recognition models were applied to detect structured metadata elements such as letterheads, sender and recipient names, dates and document identifiers. Additional classification models were trained to categorise concepts including locations, individuals and organisations, and to flag case files potentially containing sensitive information based on patterns learned from annotated examples. The integration of OCR outputs with archival management systems improved indexing, retrieval and compliance with access restrictions. The project enhanced processing speed, reduced manual cataloguing effort and expanded digital accessibility of archival collections, supporting research and administrative transparency.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI to detect incorrect health reimbursement payments
source_description: Public health reimbursement systems must balance timely payments with robust controls to prevent incorrect or fraudulent claims. In Norway, Helfo initiated a collaborative innovation project to improve the accuracy of health reimbursement payments and ensure responsible use of public funds. Stakeholders include Helfo, healthcare providers, researchers from Skatteforsk at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences, the Norwegian Institute of Public Health, and the University of Agder. The objective is to detect erroneous claims earlier, reduce manual audits, and simplify compliance for legitimate providers. The project develops data-driven control systems that analyse large volumes of reimbursement claims, historical payment data, and provider behaviour patterns. These systems generate risk indicators that support pre-payment checks and post-payment reviews, while remaining integrated with existing reimbursement workflows. Emphasis is placed on uncovering blind spots in current controls and improving reporting efficiency. The initiative is still under development, with pilots used to test models and operational integration. Anticipated benefits include reduced incorrect payments, more efficient use of inspection resources, and increased trust among healthcare providers by focusing controls where risks are highest.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SSmart On-Line health assessment of cable terminations
source_description: Failures in high-voltage cable terminations pose a significant risk to electricity supply security, particularly in transmission networks. The SmartACT project addresses this issue by developing a continuous, non-intrusive monitoring system for 420 kV oil-filled cable terminations, which are among the most failure-prone components. Stakeholders include the Norwegian transmission system operator Statnett, industrial partners, and research institutions such as SINTEF and NTNU. The objective is to enable early detection of degradation and prevent costly supply interruptions. The project develops long-life sensors installed inside cable terminations to continuously measure temperature, humidity, pressure, and partial discharges. Sensor data is analysed through a digital assessment framework that combines physical modelling with data-driven evaluation methods. The monitoring system is designed to integrate with grid operation and maintenance systems, enabling condition-based maintenance strategies. SmartACT remains in the research and testing phase under the ENERGIX programme. Expected impacts include improved grid reliability, reduced unplanned outages, lower maintenance costs, and enhanced decision-making for critical energy infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: NewbornTime
source_description: Accurate documentation of events during newborn resuscitation and early care is essential for clinical quality, training, and patient safety, yet manual recording is often incomplete or imprecise. The NewbornTime project aims to generate an objective and detailed timeline of events surrounding newborn care immediately after birth. Stakeholders include clinicians, neonatal researchers, hospitals, and healthcare quality organisations. The objective is to improve clinical documentation, support performance analysis, and enhance learning in neonatal care. The project combines infrared thermal video and optical video recordings captured in delivery rooms and resuscitation areas. Using advanced modelling techniques, the system estimates the precise time of birth from thermal signals and recognises key clinical activities from video streams. These events are automatically assembled into a structured timeline that can be reviewed by clinicians and researchers. The system is designed to integrate with hospital workflows while respecting strict data protection and ethical requirements. NewbornTime remains in the research phase, with validation studies ongoing. Potential impacts include more accurate clinical records, improved training and audit capabilities, and better insights into time-critical newborn interventions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Automated case management of family immigration with a professional background
source_description: Norway’s Directorate of Immigration (UDI) faced growing backlogs in citizenship and family immigration applications, driven by rising volumes and fully manual case handling. Processing times regularly exceeded one year, placing strain on applicants, caseworkers and administrative resources. The objective of this use case was to streamline case management by automating routine assessments, while preserving legal certainty and human oversight. The system focuses on applications from individuals with professional backgrounds where documentation and eligibility criteria are relatively standardised. The solution uses rule-based automation combined with data-driven classification models to pre-process applications, extract relevant information and assess whether cases meet predefined conditions for simplified handling. Structured data from application forms and supporting documents is analysed and routed accordingly, while complex or ambiguous cases are flagged for manual review. The system integrates with UDI’s existing case management platforms and national registers. The impact has been a substantial reduction in average processing time for eligible cases, freeing case officers to focus on more complex applications. Administrative efficiency improved, backlogs decreased and applicants benefited from faster, more predictable outcomes, demonstrating how automation can enhance public service delivery at scale.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Ada-bot helps process applications for family reunification
source_description: The Norwegian Directorate of Immigration introduced the automated system “Ada” to improve efficiency in processing family reunification applications, which involve high case volumes and legally structured eligibility criteria. The objective was to streamline document collection and support consistent application of statutory rules. Ada processes application data, verifies submitted documentation and applies rule-based logic derived from immigration legislation and administrative guidelines. The system cross-checks information against internal registries and predefined criteria, identifying complete cases suitable for automated decision pathways while routing complex or ambiguous cases to human caseworkers. By standardising routine assessments and data validation, Ada reduces manual workload and processing times. Authorities reported that certain cases can be handled up to five times faster compared with traditional processing. The implementation enhances consistency, shortens waiting periods for applicants and allows staff to focus on legally complex cases requiring discretionary judgement, while maintaining legal accountability and audit trails.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: KartAi - Automate and streamline case management in construction cases
source_description: Accurate and up-to-date property and land-use data are essential for urban planning, construction permitting, and public administration. Manual processing of construction cases and maintenance of cadastral and mapping databases is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies. KartAi addresses the need to improve data quality and streamline administrative workflows related to construction and property management. Stakeholders include municipalities, planning authorities, surveyors, and citizens interacting with land administration systems. The objective is to automate and support case management while improving the quality of the property register and the Central Common Map Database. The solution applies machine learning to analyse geospatial data, documents, and historical records to detect inconsistencies, support classification, and assist decision-making in construction cases. Automated analysis supports faster updates to cadastral records and improved alignment between maps and legal property information. The impact includes reduced processing time, higher data accuracy, and more transparent case handling. KartAi contributes to more efficient public administration, better land-use decisions, and improved trust in core spatial data infrastructures.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI in Social Services
source_description: The City of Barcelona’s social services manage a high volume of complex cases involving vulnerable individuals, requiring timely and consistent decision-making by professionals. Social workers must assess diverse situations and determine appropriate interventions, often under time constraints and with varying levels of information. The objective is to support professionals in delivering more consistent and informed service allocation. The solution uses natural language processing and machine learning models trained on a large corpus of historical case records to analyse interview data and suggest relevant interventions and services. The system processes structured and unstructured inputs recorded during consultations and provides recommendations to social workers, who retain full decision-making authority. It is integrated into existing case management workflows as a decision-support tool. The implementation enhances efficiency, supports consistency in case handling, and improves access to relevant resources, while maintaining human oversight and ethical safeguards in sensitive decision-making contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Helsinki chatbot
source_description: The City of Helsinki implemented a 24-hour chatbot service to improve accessibility of municipal information and enhance user experience on its public website. Initially deployed within Sports and Recreation pages, the objective was to provide residents with rapid, tailored answers without requiring manual searches or direct contact with staff. The chatbot operates using structured rule-based dialogue paths and curated question–answer pairs developed by Helsinki City Information specialists and thematic experts. Natural language understanding components interpret user queries and match them to predefined intents, guiding users through conversational flows that provide location details, service descriptions and practical instructions. The system integrates with the city’s content management environment to ensure updated information delivery. The deployment reduced routine enquiries to customer service channels, improved response speed and enabled continuous availability beyond office hours. It supports scalable digital interaction while preserving human oversight in content design and maintenance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia
title: E-vignette: toll road payment controlled by AI
source_description: Slovenia replaced its physical motorway vignette with a fully digital e-vignette system to simplify toll payment and improve enforcement efficiency. Motorists purchase access online using a vehicle registration number and email address, eliminating the need for physical stickers. Compliance is monitored by the Motorway Company of the Republic of Slovenia (DARS), the Financial Administration and the Police through roadside cameras, control points and mobile enforcement vehicles. The system captures vehicle registration numbers and compares them in real time with the central e-vignette database. Automated image recognition and database matching confirm whether a valid vignette has been purchased. If compliance is verified, vehicle data are deleted immediately; if not, records are retained for minor offence proceedings. The digital infrastructure improves enforcement coverage, reduces administrative costs and enhances convenience for drivers, while incorporating data minimisation safeguards. The system enables scalable motorway toll management and streamlined cross-agency cooperation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: City of Amsterdam, Barcelona, Brussels, Eindhoven, Mannheim, Rotterdam and Sofia
title: Algorithmic Transparency Standard
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Public administrations increasingly rely on algorithmic systems, creating a growing need for transparency, accountability and public understanding. Cities lacked a shared, practical framework for explaining how such systems are used, for what purpose, and with what safeguards. The Algorithmic Transparency Standard was developed to address this gap by providing a common structure for documenting algorithmic use across local governments. The initiative involves municipalities, civic technology organisations and researchers, with the objective of enabling meaningful transparency for citizens while supporting internal governance. The standard defines a shared set of information categories, such as system purpose, data sources, decision impacts, oversight mechanisms and risks. These are published in open, machine-readable formats (CSV and Excel), allowing comparison across systems and jurisdictions. The standard can be integrated into existing registers or disclosure portals without requiring new technical infrastructure. Its impact lies in improved comparability, easier public scrutiny and stronger internal documentation practices. Cities using the standard benefit from clearer governance processes and reduced duplication of effort, while citizens gain accessible insight into algorithmic decision-making. The initiative supports trust, accountability and responsible digital transformation in public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BEE Pilot - Building Energy Efficiency
source_description: Buildings play a crucial role in the energy transition, both as major energy consumers and as flexible assets that can support renewable integration. The BEE pilot addresses the challenge of reducing emissions while maintaining comfort for building occupants. Stakeholders include building owners, facility managers, energy providers, and city authorities. The objective is to use buildings as flexible energy resources that shift consumption towards periods of high renewable availability. The solution integrates with existing building management systems to collect data on energy use and indoor conditions, combined with external data such as weather forecasts and grid information. Daily forecasts of grid mix, building usage, and flexibility potential are used to generate optimised control schedules for heating, cooling, ventilation, water heating, and electric vehicle charging. These schedules proactively minimise energy use and maximise renewable consumption while preserving comfort. The pilot demonstrates reduced emissions, improved energy efficiency, and better alignment between buildings and the energy system. BEE shows how intelligent building control can support decarbonisation at city scale while delivering operational and comfort benefits.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Public Eye: AI crowd monitoring system in Amsterdam
source_description: The City of Amsterdam developed Public Eye to support crowd management in busy public spaces such as Arena Boulevard, Marineterrein and Dam Square, where high visitor numbers can create safety risks and congestion. The objective is to provide real-time insight into crowd density to inform operational decisions and increase transparency for residents. Cameras installed at selected locations transmit video streams to municipal servers, where computer vision algorithms analyse images to estimate the number of people present and, in some areas, the occupancy of bicycle parking facilities. The system extracts numerical counts and density indicators without storing or displaying identifiable images. Aggregated data are published on a public platform for citizen access and simultaneously shared with municipal staff to support traffic regulation and event management. By delivering near real-time occupancy data, Public Eye enhances situational awareness, enables proactive crowd control measures and improves public communication. The approach supports scalable deployment across additional sites while embedding data minimisation principles in its technical architecture.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI for poverty detection
source_description: Amsterdam implemented an early intervention system to identify households at risk of financial hardship based on payment arrears reported by health insurers, housing associations, energy suppliers and Waternet. The operational goal is to prevent escalation into problematic debt by initiating timely social support. When a creditor submits a report, the system links it with municipal poverty reduction databases through an automated matching process initiated by authorised staff. The case is then forwarded to a social worker in the relevant district, who must contact the resident within 14 days and complete an initial assessment within 28 days. After this point, the process relies on human case management rather than automated decision-making. Data integration tools support case allocation and tracking, while professionals determine appropriate support measures and agreements with creditors. The system improves early detection of financial vulnerability, strengthens coordination between creditors and social services and promotes preventive intervention, while maintaining human oversight in all substantive decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Autonomous Boats Deployment
source_description: Amsterdam’s dense canal network presents both opportunities and challenges for urban mobility, logistics and environmental monitoring. Traditional boats require human operators, limiting scalability and increasing operational costs. The Roboat project was launched by MIT and the AMS Institute, together with the City of Amsterdam and Waternet, to explore autonomous vessels as a new urban infrastructure layer. The objective is to deploy self-driving boats capable of performing multiple functions, including passenger transport, waste collection and water quality monitoring. Roboats are equipped with sensor suites such as cameras, lidar and GPS, enabling perception, navigation and collision avoidance in complex canal environments. Onboard systems process real-time data to plan routes and coordinate with other vessels, while shore-based platforms monitor fleet operations. The pilots demonstrated safe autonomous navigation, modular vessel design and flexible deployment across use cases. Impacts include reduced labour requirements, improved efficiency in waste collection and new data streams for environmental management. The project highlights the potential of autonomous waterborne transport to complement urban mobility systems, reduce congestion and support sustainable city operations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Using AI to measure accessibility
source_description: Ensuring equal access to public space for people with disabilities requires detailed, up-to-date information on urban accessibility. Historically, such data was fragmented, outdated or manually collected. The City of Amsterdam launched the “Amsterdam for All” initiative to systematically measure accessibility barriers across the city and support evidence-based interventions. Stakeholders include city planners, accessibility experts and residents with mobility impairments. The objective is to identify obstacles such as blocked pavements, missing curb ramps or inaccessible crossings. The project analyses street-level imagery and spatial data to detect urban features relevant to pedestrian accessibility. Predictive models identify the presence and condition of sidewalks, crossings and obstacles, producing city-wide accessibility maps. These outputs integrate into municipal planning tools and dashboards used by city officials. The impact includes improved visibility of accessibility issues, better prioritisation of infrastructure investments and reduced reliance on manual surveys. Qualitatively, the project strengthens inclusive urban design and supports Amsterdam’s commitment to universal accessibility through data-driven decision-making.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Automatically Assessing and Improving the Readability of Municipal Communication
source_description: Low literacy levels present barriers to civic participation, particularly in accessing municipal services such as taxation, voting and social benefits. The City of Amsterdam, through its “Amsterdam for All” initiative, aims to improve the accessibility of public communication by ensuring that official texts are understandable to citizens with varying literacy levels. The objective is to support inclusive public services and reduce administrative exclusion. The project applies natural language processing techniques to analyse municipal texts and measure readability. Algorithms evaluate lexical complexity and syntactic structure, and contextual lexical simplification methods suggest alternative wording for complex terms while preserving meaning. The system integrates into content creation workflows to assist communication officers in drafting clearer documents. The project has been implemented as an operational support tool within the municipality. It improves clarity of communication, enhances citizen access to services and promotes inclusive governance through data-driven language optimisation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI for green roof management
source_description: The City of Amsterdam required reliable data on green roof coverage to support climate adaptation, biodiversity and urban planning policies, as previous mapping methods classified entire roofs as green when only partial vegetation was present, leading to significant overestimation and unreliable statistics. Municipal authorities, environmental planners and property owners needed precise measurements of actual vegetated surface across the city. To address this, a proof of concept was developed using Very High Resolution satellite imagery with a spatial resolution of approximately 30 cm, enabling detailed observation of roof composition. Geospatial image analysis techniques were applied to classify pixels according to material type and vegetation cover, allowing roof areas to be quantified accurately at pixel level. The processed data were integrated into municipal geographic information systems to update spatial datasets and support policy analysis. The approach substantially improves data granularity and reliability compared with previous estimates, enabling better targeting of incentives, monitoring of environmental performance and evidence-based investment in green infrastructure, while offering a scalable method for continuous urban monitoring.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: 3D Point Cloud
source_description: The City of Amsterdam aims to improve urban asset management by maintaining accurate and up-to-date information about public infrastructure such as trees, street lighting, and traffic signs. Traditional data collection methods are labour-intensive and may lack precision or timeliness. The objective is to automate the detection and classification of urban assets to support planning, maintenance, and operational efficiency. The solution uses mobile LiDAR scanners to generate detailed three-dimensional representations of the urban environment in the form of point clouds. Machine learning and computer vision techniques are applied to process these datasets, identifying and classifying objects based on their geometric and spatial characteristics. The system integrates with municipal data platforms to update asset inventories. As an implemented solution, it improves data accuracy, reduces manual surveying efforts, and enables more efficient urban management and planning.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: The Hague Digital Twin
source_description: The Municipality of The Hague is developing a digital twin within the Scheveningen Living Lab to better understand and manage urban dynamics, particularly in high-traffic coastal areas. Urban planners face challenges in monitoring real-time conditions and anticipating congestion, especially during peak periods. The objective is to support data-driven urban management and planning through integrated visualisation and analysis tools. The solution consists of a digital twin platform that aggregates and visualises real-time and static data, including pedestrian and bicycle flows, public transport movements, and infrastructure availability. Advanced analytics are applied to model mobility patterns and support scenario analysis. The system integrates multiple data sources into a unified dashboard accessible to decision-makers. As a pilot initiative, it demonstrates the potential to improve traffic management, optimise infrastructure use, and enhance urban planning, although full-scale deployment has not yet been confirmed.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Twin Technology to Improve Operations
source_description: The Port of Rotterdam initiated the development of a digital twin to enhance operational efficiency and optimise maritime logistics. Port operations involve complex coordination of vessel movements, infrastructure, and environmental conditions, where inefficiencies can lead to delays and increased costs. The objective is to improve planning and utilisation of port resources by providing real-time insights and predictive capabilities. The solution is based on an Internet of Things-enabled cloud platform that collects data from sensors measuring hydrological and meteorological conditions such as water levels, currents, wind, and visibility. Advanced analytics and predictive models are applied to simulate port operations and determine optimal timing for mooring, loading, and departure. The platform integrates data from multiple stakeholders to support coordinated decision-making. As a pilot, it demonstrates potential to reduce waiting times, improve capacity utilisation, and enhance operational reliability, though full deployment status remains unconfirmed.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot for rental apartment search
source_description: The City of Helsinki introduced a rental apartment search chatbot to improve accessibility and efficiency of housing services. Prospective tenants frequently required guidance on eligibility criteria, application procedures and housing availability, placing pressure on customer service channels. The chatbot provides a continuous digital interface integrated into the city’s housing services website. It operates through structured rule-based dialogue paths and curated question–answer pairs defined by housing service experts. Natural language understanding components interpret user queries and map them to predefined intents, enabling tailored responses related to rental applications, waiting lists and housing policies. The system automates responses to common enquiries while escalating complex cases to human advisers when necessary. By providing immediate answers, the chatbot reduces response times, increases service availability outside office hours and improves user experience. It enhances operational efficiency by handling high volumes of routine questions and standardising information delivery across the housing service.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Proof of Business
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The Swedish Companies Registration Office identified inefficiencies in how entrepreneurs, customers and business partners access and share verified company information, as validation often relies on fragmented registers, manual document exchange and repeated checks. The objective was to enable secure, rapid and trustworthy exchange of certified corporate data while reducing administrative burden and strengthening confidence in digital interactions. A proof of concept digital wallet was developed using Distributed Ledger Technology to collect, store and manage verified company credentials issued by the authority. Blockchain infrastructure ensures immutability and traceability of records, while cryptographic mechanisms allow authorised parties to share tamper-evident certificates through secure interfaces. The system demonstrates how verified information can be accessed and exchanged in a controlled, interoperable environment without duplicating data across institutions. The pilot highlights potential reductions in processing time and administrative costs, faster onboarding of business relationships and improved transparency in commercial transactions, supporting scalable digital trust services for both public and private sector stakeholders.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Participa.gov – Digital Public Participation Platform
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Participa.gov was launched under Portugal’s Simplex modernisation programme to provide a unified national platform for participatory processes across public entities. The challenge addressed was fragmented citizen engagement mechanisms and limited transparency in consultation and participatory budgeting initiatives. Developed by the Administrative Modernisation Agency, the platform enables institutions to launch structured participatory processes, define eligibility criteria and manage proposal submission and voting through a standardised interface. Citizens authenticate using secure electronic identification mechanisms, and distributed ledger technology records transactions to ensure auditability and integrity of votes and proposals. Cryptographic safeguards protect data while allowing transparent verification of outcomes. The system supports diverse use cases, including national participatory budgeting, sector-specific consultations and restricted processes for defined groups. A consistent front-end design enhances usability, while configurable back-office tools allow institutional customisation. Participa.gov increases transparency, broadens civic engagement and strengthens trust in digital democratic processes through secure, standardised participation infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Reducing Friction in Trade (RFIT) in the UK
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Importers and exporters trading with the United Kingdom must submit multiple declarations to authorities such as HM Revenue & Customs and the Food Standards Agency, leading to duplication of information, administrative burden and delays at the border. The RFIT project was launched as a proof of concept to explore how supply chain data could be shared directly with public authorities to ensure timeliness, provenance and compliance without repetitive filings. In collaboration with Chainvine’s “Intelligent Wine” application, upstream data from wine producers relevant to customs and Port Health Authorities were captured digitally and recorded on a blockchain-based platform. Distributed ledger mechanisms ensured data integrity, traceability and controlled access for authorised stakeholders through secure system integration. The pilot demonstrated how trusted shared datasets can streamline regulatory processes, reduce the need for discrete declarations and lower the cost of compliance. Anticipated benefits include faster clearance times, improved transparency across the supply chain and enhanced coordination between businesses and authorities, supporting more efficient and reliable cross-border trade.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Harnessing the potential of blockchain technology for due diligence and sustainability in cotton value chains
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: Global cotton value chains are complex and fragmented, making it difficult for governments and companies to ensure traceability, compliance, and sustainability from production to retail. Risks such as forced labour, environmental harm, and lack of transparency undermine due diligence efforts and consumer trust. The UNECE pilot project addresses these challenges by supporting traceability and accountability across the cotton supply chain, involving farmers, processors, manufacturers, brands, regulators, and consumers. The objective is to provide practical tools that enable reliable verification of origin, production practices, and sustainability claims, aligned with international policy and trade frameworks. The solution implements a distributed ledger–based traceability system that records key events and data points along the value chain, from field to shelf. Standardised data models developed under the UN/CEFACT framework ensure interoperability and consistency, while secure digital records enable verifiable information sharing among authorised actors. The pilot improves transparency, supports regulatory compliance, and strengthens due diligence processes. It enables more responsible sourcing, reduces information asymmetries, and enhances trust between stakeholders. Overall, the initiative contributes to more sustainable cotton value chains and provides a scalable reference model for traceability in the garment and footwear sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LBChain - Blockchain sandbox
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The Bank of Lithuania, as central bank and financial market supervisor, seeks to promote innovation in the fintech sector while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and maintaining financial stability. Start-ups and technology firms often face challenges in testing novel financial services within existing supervisory frameworks and accessing regulatory guidance during early development stages. LBChain was established as a technological and regulatory sandbox to provide a controlled environment where innovative solutions can be developed and assessed. The platform is based on blockchain architecture and combines distributed ledger infrastructure with supervisory support, enabling participants to test smart contracts, payment solutions and other ledger-based services under defined conditions. Secure nodes and predefined testing scenarios allow experimentation without full market exposure, while regulators observe performance and compliance aspects. The initiative fosters collaboration between innovators and authorities, accelerates product development cycles and reduces regulatory uncertainty. As a result, it strengthens the competitiveness of the national fintech ecosystem and supports responsible deployment of emerging financial technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Transforming International Remittance for Serbian Diaspora using Blockchain and Digital Identity
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: To reduce remittance costs and increase transparency in cross-border transfers, UNDP Serbia partnered with AID:Tech to pilot a blockchain-based remittance solution targeting the Serbian diaspora. Traditional remittance channels often involve high fees and limited traceability, constraining economic benefits for recipient communities. The system tokenises remittance value into blockchain-based digital assets linked to specific entitlements such as utilities or goods. Transactions are recorded on a distributed ledger, enabling traceability while preserving user privacy through cryptographic mechanisms. Digital identity components authenticate senders and recipients, ensuring that funds or entitlements reach intended beneficiaries. The pilot, launched in 2018 in the City of Niš, covered the full remittance journey from diaspora sender to local service redemption. The solution aimed to lower transaction costs, improve accountability and stimulate local economic activity. By combining distributed ledger infrastructure with digital identity verification, the initiative demonstrated an alternative model for secure, transparent remittance delivery.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain of Frequencies
source_description: The rapid growth of wireless devices and digital services has increased demand for radio spectrum, a finite public resource that must be carefully managed to avoid interference and ensure service quality. During major cultural, political and sporting events, numerous wireless microphones and devices operate simultaneously, creating risks of signal conflicts in Programme Making and Special Events bands. The French National Frequency Agency sought to improve transparency and coordination in frequency allocation within general authorisation bands. A blockchain-based booking platform was developed to register and manage frequency reservations using distributed ledger technology. The system records allocations in an immutable and transparent manner, enabling authorised users to reserve frequencies while preventing double bookings and ensuring traceability. Smart contract functionalities manage permissions and updates across stakeholders involved in event organisation and spectrum management. The solution enhances reliability and coordination, reduces interference risks and improves overall quality of service during high-profile events, supporting more efficient and accountable spectrum governance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DiBiHo - Digital Credentials for Higher Education Institutions
source_description: Higher education institutions face growing demand for secure, interoperable, and internationally recognised academic credentials, as student mobility and digital service delivery increase. Paper-based certificates and fragmented digital solutions create administrative burdens, slow verification, and limit cross-border recognition. The DiBiHo project addresses this challenge by exploring a trusted digital infrastructure for academic credentials that can be used nationally and internationally. Stakeholders include German higher education institutions, students, employers, and credential evaluators. The objective is to define a vendor-independent, interoperable standard for issuing, storing, presenting, and verifying digital academic credentials. The solution investigates distributed infrastructure approaches that allow institutions to issue tamper-resistant credentials while enabling learners to control and share them securely. Common standards and governance principles are defined to ensure long-term interoperability, legal validity, and alignment with European and international frameworks. The project improves efficiency in credential management, reduces verification costs, and enhances trust in academic records. It supports student mobility, lifelong learning, and digital transformation in higher education, while providing a foundation for scalable, future-proof credential ecosystems independent of specific technology providers.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Competency certificates in Small Private Online Courses (SPOCs)
source_description: Universities issuing digital certificates for online courses must ensure authenticity, prevent fraud and enable straightforward verification by employers and other institutions, as conventional digital documents can be copied or altered and often require manual validation. The project aimed to strengthen trust in competency accreditations generated through the OPEN edX Learning Management System and formally issued by the university. A blockchain-based mechanism was implemented to anchor each certificate to a distributed ledger by storing a cryptographic hash of the credential on-chain, creating a tamper-evident and time-stamped record linked to the learner’s achievement. The certificates remain accessible through the LMS, while external stakeholders can verify their validity by comparing the document with the ledger entry, without relying on intermediaries. The solution reduces administrative workload and verification time, enhances transparency and portability of qualifications, and increases confidence in digital credentials across academic and professional contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Intelligent management of Aid to Citizens and companies
source_description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Andalusian administration was required to rapidly distribute large-scale financial aid to citizens and businesses to protect employment and economic stability. The volume and complexity of aid schemes made manual processing inefficient, error-prone, and difficult to scale. This use case addresses the need to accelerate aid delivery while ensuring compliance, transparency, and accountability. Stakeholders include public administrators, beneficiaries, and oversight bodies. The objective is to automate complex administrative workflows to process aid applications quickly and reliably. The solution applies robotic process automation to handle repetitive, rule-based tasks such as data validation, eligibility checks, and application processing. Automated workflows integrate with existing administrative systems, while human oversight is retained for exception handling and decision-making. Since implementation, the system has processed more than 300,000 aid applications, significantly reducing processing times and administrative workload. The initiative improves service delivery, ensures timely support to citizens and companies, and strengthens institutional resilience during crises. It demonstrates how intelligent automation can enhance public sector efficiency, scalability, and responsiveness in high-pressure policy contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Flemish Ministry of Mobility and Public Works (MOW)
title: Monitoring structure health of bridges with InSAR
source_description: Public authorities responsible for bridge management must ensure structural safety while optimising inspection budgets and minimising traffic disruption. Conventional monitoring relies on periodic visual inspections and targeted topographic surveys, which may fail to detect gradual deformations at an early stage. The project explores whether satellite-based interferometric analysis can support daily bridge management by identifying millimetre-level displacements and prioritising on-site investigations. Using Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), phase differences between successive radar satellite images are processed to calculate surface deformation over time. Different satellite data sources and processing techniques are assessed to determine their suitability for bridge monitoring, with algorithms designed to filter noise and automatically flag anomalous displacement patterns. The results are compared with ground-based measurements to validate accuracy and reliability. The approach aims to enable earlier detection of structural issues, more efficient allocation of inspection resources and reduced monitoring costs. By supporting risk-based maintenance planning and continuous remote observation, the solution enhances infrastructure safety, scalability of monitoring operations and evidence-based asset management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Hello Lamp Post
source_description: The Environment Agency is responsible for protecting communities from flood and coastal risks, yet engaging diverse local audiences and providing timely, location-specific safety information has been challenging through traditional communication channels. The objective was to create an accessible, continuous engagement mechanism in high-risk areas in the South West of England and Newcastle, improving public awareness and preparedness. Hello Lamp Post introduced an interactive 24/7 conversational platform accessible via mobile devices, allowing residents to interact with physical infrastructure such as flood defences through text-based messaging. The system uses natural language processing to interpret questions and deliver contextualised information, drawing on curated flood safety guidance and local data. Conversations are geo-referenced to specific assets, ensuring relevance and enabling authorities to analyse recurring concerns. The initiative increased public interaction with flood risk information, improved accessibility outside office hours and generated insights into community awareness gaps. This supports more responsive communication strategies, strengthens trust between authorities and citizens and enhances resilience through scalable, place-based digital engagement.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ViEWS - The Political Violence Early-Warning System
source_description: The Violence Early-Warning System was launched in 2017 by Uppsala University and the Peace Research Institute Oslo to support policymakers and humanitarian actors in anticipating organised political violence. The objective is to provide transparent, evidence-based forecasts of conflict fatalities up to 36 months ahead across Africa and the Middle East. ViEWS integrates historical conflict event data, socioeconomic indicators, political variables and spatial-temporal datasets into statistical forecasting models. Ensemble modelling techniques and machine-learning algorithms generate monthly probabilistic predictions at fine geographic resolution. Results are published through an open online platform, enabling users to explore forecast scenarios and underlying data. The system enhances anticipatory action planning, resource allocation and early intervention strategies. By making methodology and forecasts publicly accessible, ViEWS strengthens transparency and reproducibility in conflict forecasting. Its structured modelling framework supports continuous updates and methodological refinement as new data become available.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Citibeats – Ethical AI for Social Understanding
source_description: Governments and public organisations often struggle to interpret large volumes of unstructured citizen feedback from social media, surveys and open data sources, limiting their ability to detect emerging social concerns and respond proactively. The objective is to transform dispersed textual data into structured insights that inform policy design and service delivery while ensuring ethical data practices. The platform applies natural language processing and machine learning techniques to analyse large-scale text datasets, identifying themes, sentiment patterns and leading indicators of social trends. Algorithms classify content into policy-relevant categories and generate dashboards that visualise geographic and temporal patterns, using anonymised and aggregated data to protect privacy. The system integrates open data streams and institutional datasets to provide near real-time monitoring of public discourse. The solution enables earlier identification of societal risks, evidence-based prioritisation and more inclusive decision-making. By automating large-scale text analysis, it reduces manual workload, enhances analytical capacity and supports scalable, data-driven governance grounded in citizen perspectives.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Empresa Municipal de Transported del Ayuntamiento de Madrid
title: Madrid Mobility 360 (multimodal planner for urban commuting)
source_description: Madrid Mobility 360 was developed to provide residents and visitors with an integrated digital tool for planning journeys across multiple transport modes in the city. Urban commuters often face fragmented information across public transport, carsharing and bicycle services. The application aggregates data from transport operators and mobility providers into a unified platform offering route calculation, real-time updates and integrated payment options. The route planner uses optimisation algorithms to estimate current and projected journey times, incorporating live traffic data and vehicle capacity information for selected bus routes. Users can compare transport options, purchase tickets and view estimated carbon dioxide emissions associated with each trip. The system supports multimodal planning by integrating public transport schedules, shared mobility availability and geolocation services. By centralising mobility information, the app improves travel efficiency, enhances user experience and supports sustainable transport choices. It contributes to smart city mobility management and data-driven urban planning.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Faculty of Medicine, University of Belgrade
title: Transforming Public Healthcare and Education Using AI-powered Mixed Reality Technology
source_description: The Government of Serbia, in collaboration with Microsoft, explored the use of mixed reality technologies to enhance healthcare delivery and medical education. Healthcare systems often face challenges in providing access to specialised expertise, particularly in complex cases requiring multidisciplinary input or remote consultation. The objective of this initiative is to enable remote collaboration among healthcare professionals and improve training opportunities for medical students. The solution combines mixed reality environments with data-driven analytical tools to allow clinicians to visualise patient data and medical scenarios in immersive formats. It supports real-time collaboration, enabling experts to contribute to diagnosis and treatment planning regardless of location. The system also facilitates remote education by simulating clinical scenarios for training purposes. While the initiative demonstrates potential to improve efficiency, reduce the need for physical presence, and enhance learning experiences, no recent evidence confirms large-scale deployment or continued operational use.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: My First Salary - a project to address youth unemployment
source_description: Young graduates often face a difficult transition from education to work, particularly when they lack practical experience and employers are hesitant to recruit first-time entrants during uncertain labour-market conditions. In Serbia, the My First Salary programme was designed to address this gap by helping young people under 30 obtain their first work opportunity while supporting employers in filling roles with subsidised early-career talent. The objective is to reduce youth unemployment, shorten the waiting time for a first job, and make the application and recruitment process far less bureaucratic than conventional state-support schemes. The implementation is built around a fully digital platform that automates application handling, approval, eligibility checks, and candidate-employer matching. At a conceptual level, the system combines digital identity and certificate-based registration, automated verification of company and candidate conditions, and a recommendation algorithm that helps match participants to opportunities. The programme also includes dashboards and visualisation tools to support administration of the scheme. The impact includes a simpler zero-paper process, faster access to support for both employers and young applicants, and more efficient matching between labour demand and available candidates. It also improves scalability and transparency in programme delivery while creating public value through a more accessible route into first employment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: HOPE - Healthy Outdoor Premises for Everyone
source_description: Urban air quality monitoring traditionally relies on a limited number of fixed stations, providing only coarse-grained insights into citizens’ actual exposure to pollution. In the Helsinki region, this limits the ability of individuals and policymakers to understand air quality variations at neighbourhood or street level. The HOPE project addresses this gap by enabling hyper-local air quality monitoring through a dense, participatory sensing network. Stakeholders include citizens, city authorities, researchers, and public health organisations. The objective is to provide accessible, location-specific information on air pollution exposure in daily life. The solution combines data from fixed monitoring stations with crowdsourced measurements collected via portable sensors carried by citizens. These data are aggregated and visualised on digital maps, providing near real-time insights into air quality across the city. The project enhances spatial coverage, raises public awareness, and supports evidence-based urban planning and health interventions. HOPE empowers citizens with actionable information, improves understanding of pollution dynamics, and supports targeted measures to improve urban environmental health and quality of life.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Aeolus – Mid-altitude maritime monitoring platform for security, search & rescue and environmental monitoring
source_description: Maritime authorities require wide-area surveillance to address security threats, coordinate search and rescue operations and monitor environmental risks, yet conventional ship-based sensors have limited range constrained by low elevation. The Aeolus project aims to extend maritime situational awareness by elevating monitoring systems to mid-altitude, thereby expanding coverage without deploying additional vessels. The platform consists of an airborne sensor system operating at approximately 450 metres above a host ship, increasing the observable area by more than eleven times compared with standard configurations. It can be deployed using different lifting mechanisms and remain operational for extended periods. Equipped with optical and radar sensors, the system transmits real-time data to onboard command centres, where information is processed and integrated with existing surveillance systems. The solution enhances detection capabilities for vessels, persons in distress and environmental anomalies, while improving operational efficiency. By increasing coverage and persistence at relatively low cost, the platform strengthens maritime safety, supports faster response times and enables scalable monitoring across diverse missions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Monitoring slavery from space
source_description: Brick kilns across the South Asian “Brick Belt” are associated with high prevalence of forced labour, yet the absence of reliable data on their number and distribution has hindered effective intervention by governments and non-governmental organisations. The project sought to generate an evidence base to estimate the scale of kiln operations and, by proxy, potential exposure to modern slavery. High-resolution satellite imagery was analysed to identify and map kiln structures across regions of Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Nepal. Image recognition techniques and spatial analysis were used to detect characteristic kiln shapes and validate findings against ground-truth information. The resulting geospatial dataset enabled a more credible estimate of kiln numbers and their geographic concentration. By providing transparent, large-scale evidence, the initiative supports targeted inspections, policy prioritisation and resource allocation. It enhances situational awareness for anti-slavery actors and demonstrates how satellite data can improve accountability, scalability of monitoring and informed action against labour exploitation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: R2D3: Active-waiting robot for the disabled people’s waiting room
source_description: The Seine-Saint-Denis Innovation Lab developed the R2D3 robot to improve accessibility and user experience for individuals visiting the Departmental House for Disabled Persons. Waiting times in administrative services can be challenging, particularly for users with diverse needs and varying levels of digital literacy. The objective is to provide an inclusive and engaging way to deliver information and support users during waiting periods. The solution consists of an interactive robot equipped with speech recognition and multilingual capabilities, enabling it to communicate with users in a simple and accessible manner. It delivers information on administrative procedures and services through conversational interaction, using natural language processing and pre-programmed knowledge bases. The system is designed to be user-oriented and adaptable to different user profiles. As a pilot initiative, it demonstrates the potential to reduce the digital divide, improve access to information, and enhance user experience, although no evidence confirms broader deployment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Voice assistant services
source_description: Aylesbury Vale District Council sought to expand digital access to local government information by offering residents an alternative to web-based and telephone enquiries. The objective was to improve convenience and accessibility for routine questions relating to council services, payments and waste management. The council became the first UK local authority to launch an Amazon Alexa skill, enabling residents to obtain information through voice commands. The service integrates structured council data and frequently asked questions into Amazon’s voice interface using predefined intents and dialogue flows. Users can ask about political leadership, council tax payment options, recycling guidance and book assisted waste collections. Requests are processed through Amazon’s voice recognition infrastructure and linked to council information systems via secure APIs. The solution increases out-of-hours access, reduces pressure on contact centres and broadens digital inclusion for users preferring voice interaction. It demonstrates how local authorities can leverage commercial voice platforms to extend service delivery channels efficiently.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Alexa skill - vehicle tax and MOT
source_description: The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency introduced an Alexa skill to simplify access to information about vehicle tax and MOT expiry dates. Vehicle owners often needed quick confirmation of compliance deadlines without navigating government websites. The objective was to provide a convenient, hands-free information channel. Users can ask Alexa when a vehicle’s tax or MOT is due by stating the registration number. The service connects Amazon’s voice recognition system with DVLA databases through secure application interfaces, retrieving real-time status information. Structured query handling ensures that only publicly accessible vehicle compliance data are returned, without disclosing personal details. The implementation reduces friction in accessing regulatory information and encourages timely renewals, supporting road safety and compliance. By leveraging a commercial voice platform, DVLA broadened service accessibility while maintaining existing digital channels. The initiative illustrates integration of public registers with consumer voice technologies for citizen-facing information services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Alexa skill and Google home app - checking state pension age
source_description: The Department for Work and Pensions developed a prototype voice service enabling citizens to check their state pension age through Amazon Alexa and Google Home devices. Many users sought quick clarification of eligibility timelines without navigating detailed guidance pages. The objective was to provide simple, accessible answers via voice interaction. The service uses predefined conversational flows and structured eligibility rules based on date of birth. Users provide relevant information verbally, which is processed through the respective voice assistant platforms and matched against pension age legislation encoded in the application logic. The system returns an estimated pension age without storing personal data beyond the session. By offering voice-based access, DWP aimed to enhance accessibility for users with limited digital literacy or visual impairments. The prototype demonstrated the feasibility of integrating statutory rules into consumer voice platforms while maintaining privacy safeguards and limiting responses to informational guidance rather than personalised entitlement decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Alexa skill - enquiring about tax credits
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: HM Revenue and Customs launched an Alexa skill to support over three million tax credit customers during renewal periods, when contact volumes are typically high. The objective was to provide accessible guidance on renewal deadlines, required information and general eligibility queries. The service integrates structured knowledge content into Amazon’s voice assistant using defined intents and scripted dialogue paths. Users can ask about renewal dates, documentation requirements and payment information.
