The system retrieves up-to-date guidance from HMRC information sources without enabling transactional account access or disclosure of sensitive personal data. By automating responses to common enquiries, the skill reduces call centre demand and improves response times during peak periods. The initiative broadens digital engagement channels while preserving existing secure online and telephone services for account-specific matters. It illustrates the use of voice platforms for scalable dissemination of public information in high-demand administrative processes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Alexa skill - personalised weather report and forecast
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The UK Met Office introduced an Alexa “Flash Briefing” skill to provide personalised weather forecasts and updates through voice interaction. The operational goal was to extend access to official meteorological information beyond traditional broadcast and web channels. Users can request weather updates for selected regions, receiving spoken forecasts tailored to their preferences. The service integrates the Met Office’s forecasting datasets with Amazon’s voice recognition and delivery platform. Structured content feeds and location-based parameters generate region-specific briefings, while forecast data are updated regularly from meteorological models and observation systems. The solution enhances accessibility, enabling hands-free access to authoritative weather information in homes and workplaces. It supports public safety and daily planning by delivering timely updates through widely adopted consumer devices. The deployment demonstrates integration of national forecasting infrastructure with commercial voice ecosystems to expand reach and user convenience.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Big Data Analysis for HR efficiency improvement
source_description: The Ministry of Public Administration sought to improve organisational efficiency, workforce planning and employee satisfaction, but faced fragmented human resources data and limited analytical capacity to extract strategic insights. The pilot project aimed to assess how a big data tool deployed on the Governmental State Cloud Infrastructure could support advanced analysis of HR datasets. The solution integrated personnel records, performance indicators and administrative data into a centralised analytics environment, applying data mining and statistical techniques to identify patterns related to staffing levels, absenteeism and organisational performance. Dashboards and reporting tools enabled managers to explore trends and simulate scenarios for workforce optimisation. By consolidating data sources and automating analysis, the project enhanced evidence-based decision-making in HR management. Anticipated benefits include improved allocation of human resources, increased organisational effectiveness and better-informed strategies to support staff development and satisfaction, while demonstrating the scalability of cloud-based analytics within public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Kora - virtual assistant
source_description: The Municipality of Heidenheim introduced Kora, a virtual assistant designed to provide round-the-clock responses to common citizen enquiries. The objective was to improve accessibility to municipal information while reducing administrative workload. Kora operates as a self-learning chatbot integrated into the municipal website, handling approximately 70 enquiries per day with a reported success rate of 99 per cent at launch. The system uses natural language processing to interpret user questions and match them to a structured knowledge base of predefined answers. Machine-learning components refine intent recognition over time based on interaction patterns and supervised updates. Initial high-demand topics included weather, local events and coronavirus-related guidance. The chatbot standardises responses, shortens waiting times and ensures consistent information delivery outside office hours. By automating routine enquiries, the municipality can allocate staff resources to more complex cases requiring individual attention, enhancing service efficiency and digital engagement.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot Munich
source_description: The IT-Department of the municipality of Munich is developing a chatbot for Munich which is supposed to complete the current services like the common emergency number 115, the service portal and mobile apps.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Steuerchatbot
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Tax administrations receive large numbers of routine questions about declarations, deadlines, and procedures, and handling these enquiries manually can consume staff time that could otherwise be used for more complex taxpayer support. In Baden-Württemberg, the Karlsruhe finance administration introduced a tax chatbot to answer simple questions related to tax declarations and make basic guidance available through a digital self-service channel. The objective is to improve accessibility to standard tax information, reduce waiting times for routine enquiries, and offer citizens a more convenient entry point into tax-related guidance. The implementation uses a conversational chatbot provided through the Baden-Württemberg tax administration’s digital service environment. At a conceptual level, the solution combines a question-and-answer interface with a structured knowledge base on tax topics, enabling users to ask common questions and receive immediate responses without having to contact the tax office directly. The chatbot is positioned as a front-line support tool for straightforward matters rather than for complex or case-specific advisory work. The impact includes quicker access to tax information, reduced pressure on telephone and counter services, and a more scalable way to provide standard guidance. It also improves the user experience by making tax support available through a simple digital interface that can handle repetitive enquiries consistently and at any time.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DB Smile - the national railway service chatbot for job seekers
source_description: Deutsche Bahn introduced DB Smile to streamline recruitment processes and support job seekers navigating employment opportunities within the national railway company. The operational challenge was to manage high volumes of candidate enquiries and simplify application procedures. DB Smile functions as an interactive chatbot on the company’s recruitment platform, guiding users through job searches, answering application-related questions and facilitating submission of applications via chat. The system uses natural language processing to interpret queries and match candidates with suitable vacancies based on role preferences and qualifications. Integrated with Deutsche Bahn’s recruitment database, the chatbot provides real-time information on openings and application status. By automating responses to frequently asked questions and enabling conversational job matching, DB Smile accelerates the recruitment journey and reduces administrative burden. The solution improves candidate experience, shortens response times and supports efficient talent acquisition within a large public transport organisation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SEMMI - Avatar
source_description: Deutsche Bahn developed SEMMI Avatar to enhance customer service interactions in stations and other service environments by providing an engaging digital interface capable of handling routine enquiries. The operational objective is to complement human staff, improve accessibility and deliver consistent information across locations with varying infrastructure constraints. SEMMI Avatar is built on the SEMMI Conversational AI platform and combines speech recognition, natural language understanding and animated visual representation to create a multimodal human–machine interface. The system can be deployed on existing or new display hardware, indoors or outdoors, with or without touchscreen functionality, and adapts responsively to different screen sizes and formats. User queries are processed through conversational models that interpret intent and retrieve relevant information from integrated service databases. The avatar delivers responses through synchronised speech and visual cues, creating an interactive experience. The solution improves service availability, reduces waiting times for routine questions and supports scalable deployment across transport hubs and public-facing environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SEMMI - Robot
source_description: Customer-facing organisations often struggle to provide multilingual, consistent and accessible front-office support, particularly in high-traffic environments such as transport hubs or service centres. SEMMI Robot was designed to enhance on-site customer interaction by answering routine enquiries in visitors’ native languages, reducing waiting times and improving service accessibility. Stakeholders include service providers, customer service staff and end users. The robot combines speech recognition, natural language understanding and multilingual conversational models to interpret user queries, retrieve relevant information from integrated knowledge bases and generate context-appropriate responses through speech synthesis and on-screen displays. The system connects to backend information systems, such as timetables or service databases, enabling real-time responses. Early deployments indicate improved user engagement, reduced pressure on frontline staff and enhanced customer experience, particularly for international users. The solution remains in progressive development and deployment phases across selected sites, with no confirmed large-scale standardisation across all potential service locations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SEMMI - Hotline
source_description: High call volumes and repetitive enquiries place significant strain on customer service centres, leading to long waiting times and rising staffing costs. SEMMI Hotline was conceived as an advanced interactive voice response solution capable of handling routine enquiries autonomously while escalating complex cases to human agents. Stakeholders include contact centre operators, service agents and callers. The system uses automatic speech recognition, intent classification models and dialogue management frameworks to conduct natural conversations, access integrated customer databases and provide real-time responses. Cloud-based telephony integration allows rapid scaling to handle simultaneous calls without proportional increases in staffing. Reported benefits include reduced agent workload, shorter waiting times and improved scalability during peak demand. The solution continues to evolve, with ongoing enhancements to conversational capabilities; no definitive information indicates full replacement of traditional call centre models at scale.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Urban Cockpit - a digital twin of Bad Hersfeld
source_description: The municipality of Bad Hersfeld developed the Urban Cockpit as a publicly accessible digital twin to increase transparency and improve urban management. The objective was to aggregate heterogeneous municipal data into a single visual platform supporting informed decision-making and citizen engagement. The system integrates open-source datasets and sensor data into a geospatial dashboard that visualises real-time and static information. Data layers include parking occupancy, waste bin fill levels and locations of electric vehicle charging stations. Geographic information systems and data integration tools harmonise inputs from different municipal departments, enabling dynamic visualisation on an interactive map. The platform allows residents to monitor service availability and urban conditions, while municipal staff use the same data to support operational planning. By centralising urban indicators, the Urban Cockpit enhances situational awareness, promotes transparency and supports data-driven governance. The digital twin approach enables scalable expansion to additional datasets and smart city applications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Traffic flux representation with AI in Lisbon
source_description: Lisbon City Council partnered with the National Civil Engineering Laboratory and Instituto Superior Técnico to improve integrated traffic management in a densely populated urban environment. The operational challenge was to collect and interpret diverse mobility and contextual data to support coordinated transport planning and congestion mitigation. The initiative deploys data analytics systems that gather information from traffic sensors, mobility services and contextual urban datasets. Machine-learning models classify traffic patterns and estimate flow dynamics across the road network, generating predictive and descriptive indicators for decision-makers. Integrated dashboards visualise congestion levels and support scenario analysis for traffic regulation measures. The system enhances coordination between agencies and enables evidence-based planning of mobility interventions. By transforming raw mobility data into actionable insights, Lisbon strengthens its capacity to manage traffic flux proactively, optimise infrastructure use and improve travel conditions for residents and visitors.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Baggage handling at the Copenhagen Airport
source_description: Copenhagen Airport introduced data-driven optimisation in 2016 to improve baggage handling efficiency and passenger experience. Managing baggage flows requires precise coordination of staff and conveyor systems to minimise delays and queue times. The airport implemented predictive analytics models that analyse operational data, flight schedules and historical handling patterns to forecast where staff deployment would most effectively empty aircraft and load baggage onto conveyor belts. Optimisation algorithms recommend resource allocation to reduce bottlenecks and improve turnaround times. The system integrates with airport operational management platforms, providing decision support to supervisors. By anticipating workload peaks and adjusting staffing dynamically, the solution shortens waiting times, enhances punctuality and improves passenger satisfaction. The initiative demonstrates how advanced analytics can optimise complex logistics environments, increasing operational efficiency while maintaining safety and reliability in airport ground handling processes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Cluny Abbey using AR and 3D recordings to visualise "what has today disappeared"""
source_description: The town of Cluny implemented a digital heritage initiative to enhance visitor engagement by reconstructing historical environments that are no longer physically present. Cultural heritage sites often face challenges in conveying their original scale and significance due to the loss or deterioration of structures. The objective is to provide visitors with an immersive understanding of the abbey’s historical context. The solution uses augmented reality and three-dimensional modelling to recreate the abbey and its surroundings, based on historical documents, architectural plans, and visual records. Visitors can access digital reconstructions through AR interfaces installed on-site, enabling them to visualise past structures in their original locations. The system integrates a comprehensive database of 2D and 3D assets for both public engagement and scientific use. As an implemented solution, it enhances cultural interpretation, improves visitor experience, and supports research and preservation efforts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Fietsbarometer - barometer for cycleways safety
source_description: The Province of Antwerp developed the Fietsbarometer as a web-based participatory platform to assess and improve cycling safety, particularly on home-to-school routes. The objective was to gather detailed, location-specific insights from adolescents regarding perceived and observed safety conditions in school neighbourhoods. Participants digitally map their daily cycling routes and evaluate factors such as infrastructure quality, traffic intensity and hazardous points. The platform aggregates geolocated inputs into spatial datasets, which are visualised through interactive mapping tools. Data analytics functions identify recurring safety concerns and prioritise areas requiring intervention. Municipal planners use these insights to inform infrastructure improvements and traffic management measures. By combining citizen-generated data with geographic information systems, the Fietsbarometer strengthens evidence-based policy-making and youth engagement in mobility planning. The approach enhances transparency and supports targeted investment in safer cycling environments across Flemish municipalities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Jelbi - the mobility app for Berlin's public and sharing services
source_description: Jelbi was launched by Berlin’s public transport authority BVG to integrate public transport and shared mobility services into a single digital platform. Urban travellers often face fragmented booking and payment systems across transport providers. Jelbi aggregates buses, trains, carsharing, bike sharing and e-scooter services within one application, enabling route planning, booking and payment through a unified interface. The platform integrates real-time transport data, availability feeds from mobility partners and secure payment processing systems. Route optimisation algorithms propose multimodal journeys tailored to user preferences and current conditions. Physical Jelbi stations across Berlin provide co-located access to shared vehicles, reinforcing the digital–physical integration. The app enhances user convenience, encourages multimodal travel and supports sustainable urban mobility by reducing reliance on private car ownership. By centralising mobility services, Jelbi strengthens cooperation between public and private providers and contributes to Berlin’s smart city transport strategy.

title: NOMAD - the travel-app to travel anywhere in the Nordics
source_description: The Nordic Open Mobility and Digitalisation initiative aims to enable seamless cross-border travel across Nordic countries by promoting interoperable Mobility as a Service solutions. Travellers often encounter fragmented booking systems and limited integration between national transport providers. NOMAD seeks to establish a market-enabler framework combining technological standards and business practices that support MaaS roaming. The system architecture allows users to plan, book and manage multimodal journeys across borders through a single interface. Interoperability protocols connect transport operators, payment systems and journey planning services, facilitating integrated ticketing and administration of international trips. Data exchange standards ensure compatibility between participating platforms while respecting national regulatory requirements. By fostering cross-border cooperation and digital integration, NOMAD enhances user convenience, supports sustainable mobility choices and strengthens regional transport connectivity. The initiative contributes to harmonising smart mobility ecosystems across the Nordic region.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Explore.Porto - discover and explore the city through a digital platform
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The Municipality of Porto developed Explore.Porto to provide visitors and residents with an integrated digital tool for navigating the city and accessing up-to-date information on attractions and mobility options. Urban tourists often face fragmented sources of information covering points of interest, transport routes and local services. The objective was to centralise these datasets into a single web-based and mobile application offering intuitive and real-time guidance. The platform aggregates geolocated information from municipal databases and authorised partners who can create and update points of interest on an interactive map. Route optimisation functions analyse available mobility options, suggesting the most efficient paths between selected locations and highlighting nearby attractions. The system integrates tourism content, transport data and spatial analytics within a unified interface, enabling personalised exploration of the city. By consolidating dispersed information streams, Explore.Porto enhances user experience, supports sustainable mobility choices and strengthens digital engagement with the city’s cultural and commercial ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: RePAIR – Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Cultural Heritage Reconstruction
source_description: Archaeological artefacts are often discovered in thousands of fragments, making physical reconstruction a painstaking and time-consuming task that requires scarce expert skills. Many damaged artworks remain in storage for decades due to the effort required to restore them. The RePAIR project addresses this challenge by supporting archaeologists and conservators in reconstructing fragmented cultural heritage. Stakeholders include museums, researchers, conservation experts, and the public. The objective is to dramatically reduce the time and effort needed to restore large, shattered artefacts while preserving scientific and cultural integrity. The solution develops an intelligent robotic system capable of digitally analysing fragments, identifying matching pieces, and physically assembling artefacts autonomously. Advanced pattern recognition and shape-matching techniques guide robotic manipulation, enabling precise reconstruction. The system is tested on complex frescoes from the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Pompeii. RePAIR accelerates restoration timelines, reduces manual labour, and enables the recovery of artefacts previously considered too complex to reconstruct. It opens new possibilities for preserving and showcasing cultural heritage through scalable, technology-enabled conservation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot - German Federal Employment Agency
source_description: The Federal Employment Agency introduced a chatbot to improve accessibility to information on employment services and social benefits. Citizens frequently seek guidance on unemployment benefits, short-time allowance, child supplement, training opportunities and related administrative procedures, creating high enquiry volumes. The chatbot provides a digital self-service channel available at all times through the Agency’s website. It uses natural language processing to interpret user questions and match them with curated responses drawn from official guidance content. Structured dialogue flows guide users to relevant pages, forms and contact points. The system automates responses to routine enquiries while redirecting complex or case-specific matters to human advisers. By standardising information delivery and reducing response times, the chatbot alleviates pressure on call centres and improves user convenience. The deployment supports scalable digital service provision while maintaining human oversight for personalised assistance and legal determinations.

title: Chatbot Guido
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The State of North Rhine-Westphalia implemented Chatbot Guido to simplify access to information regarding online business registration procedures. Entrepreneurs and business owners often require clear guidance on administrative steps, documentation requirements and digital submission processes. The objective was to provide immediate, structured answers through a conversational interface integrated into the state’s business service portal. Guido operates using predefined question–answer pairs and natural language processing components that classify user intent and deliver relevant guidance. The chatbot directs users to appropriate online forms, explains procedural steps and clarifies regulatory requirements. By automating responses to frequently asked questions, the system reduces administrative burden on service desks and improves accessibility for businesses seeking to register or modify operations. The solution enhances efficiency in public service delivery and supports digitalisation of business administration processes across the state.

organization: Integration Office of the State Government of Schleswig-Holstein
title: Digitale Assistenz Ina
source_description: The state of Schleswig-Holstein introduced the digital assistant Ina to provide information related to the Integration Office, particularly on matters concerning disability and workplace inclusion. Citizens and employers often require guidance on rights, benefits and administrative procedures, leading to frequent general enquiries. Ina offers a conversational interface embedded in the state administration website, delivering responses based on curated knowledge content and structured dialogue paths. Natural language processing components interpret user input and map questions to predefined topics such as disability support, financial assistance and legal frameworks. The system provides general information and directs users to relevant forms or contact points, while complex or individual cases remain handled by human staff. By offering continuous digital assistance, Ina improves accessibility, reduces waiting times and supports consistent information dissemination. The initiative contributes to inclusive digital public services while preserving professional oversight for case-specific decisions.

title: TWIN4ROAD@Essen: AI-based analysis and forecast
source_description: Managing Germany’s extensive road network requires continuous assessment of pavement condition and infrastructure assets, yet the volume and complexity of data make manual evaluation inefficient and costly. The City of Essen launched TWIN4ROAD to build a comprehensive digital representation of its road infrastructure to support maintenance planning and investment decisions. Data are collected using ground penetrating radar, mobile laser scanning, 3D measurements and high-resolution imagery to create a detailed inventory of road surfaces and subsurface structures. Advanced data analytics and machine learning models process these datasets to assess current damage, identify structural weaknesses and forecast potential pothole development. The resulting digital twin integrates condition data with spatial information systems, enabling automated evaluations and scenario analyses. The approach improves accuracy and timeliness of maintenance planning, reduces inspection costs and supports preventive interventions. By providing a reusable infrastructure inventory, the system also benefits other municipal services operating in public road space, enhancing cross-departmental coordination and long-term asset management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: KI4Forst - Monitoring the Forest with Satellite Data and AI
source_description: The Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geoinformation aims to improve forest monitoring and management by leveraging satellite data. Traditional methods for assessing forest conditions are resource-intensive and may not provide timely or comprehensive insights into environmental changes such as drought damage or pest infestations. The objective is to enable automated, large-scale monitoring of forest areas and their condition. The solution involves developing an automated processing chain that applies deep learning techniques to satellite imagery. Image classification models, based on artificial neural networks, are trained to detect forest areas and distinguish between different forest types, such as deciduous and coniferous. The system also identifies changes in vegetation health and potential damage. Outputs are integrated into geospatial information systems for visualisation and decision support.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot Govii
source_description: The City of Flensburg piloted Chatbot Govii in 2021 to streamline access to municipal administrative services and contact information. Residents often encounter difficulty identifying the correct department or procedure for specific requests. Govii provides a conversational interface on the city’s website, enabling users to ask questions in natural language and receive structured guidance. The system relies on predefined knowledge bases and intent recognition models to classify enquiries and retrieve relevant service descriptions, contact details and application links. By automating responses to routine queries, the chatbot reduces the need for direct phone or in-person enquiries and improves navigation of municipal services. The deployment enhances service efficiency, shortens response times and supports digital-first interaction with the administration. It also allows municipal staff to focus on complex cases requiring personalised attention.

organization: Immigration Service, Patent and Registration Office and the Tax Administration
title: Starting up smoothly: chatbot service (Virtual Agent Network) for foreign entrepreneurs in Finland
source_description: Starting a business as a foreign entrepreneur can require interaction with multiple agencies covering immigration, registration, patents, and tax, and this fragmentation often creates confusion, duplicated effort, and avoidable delays. In Finland, the “Starting up Smoothly” initiative was designed to reduce these barriers by connecting the conversational services of the Immigration Service, the Patent and Registration Office, and the Tax Administration into a more seamless user journey. The objective was to break down agency silos and give entrepreneurs a more coherent route through immigration, business-registration, and taxation questions. The implementation linked three virtual agents—Kamu, PatRek, and VeroBot—through a shared conversational network, using natural language understanding to detect when a user’s question fell outside one bot’s scope and hand over the conversation within the same chat window to the most relevant agency bot. However, Finnish official material from the start of the project described the inter-agency cooperation as a trial ending in June 2019, and Migri later announced that Kamu itself was discontinued after 31 October 2024, even though PRH still operates its Trade Register chatbot. The impact of the original project was to demonstrate smoother inter-agency digital support, but its current status is best described as partly absorbed into successor services rather than still running unchanged.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: 120 Words per Minute - a Training App for Basal Automated Reading
source_description: Primary schools face a persistent literacy challenge, as a substantial share of pupils do not reach fluent reading speed by the end of primary education and often struggle to recover later. In Schleswig-Holstein, the “120 Words per Minute” project was conceived to support the “Lesen macht stark” programme by converting a printed diagnostic and training approach into a more flexible app-based tool for schools. The objective is to improve reading fluency, make diagnosis and support easier to use in everyday teaching, and enable children to practise independently or in pairs while giving teachers a more continuous way to monitor progress. The implementation centres on an app that digitises the phases of the existing reading-support programme and uses speech-to-text methods to automate the level check that children would otherwise complete manually. Public descriptions of the project present it as a digital education solution intended to support classroom use from the earliest training stages and to simplify the practical application of the methodology in school settings. The expected impact includes improved reading fluency, more practical use of diagnostic support at school level, and a more scalable method for early literacy intervention, especially for children at risk of falling behind.

organization: Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geo-Information
title: KI4GeoSeDa – AI-Based Georeferencing of Specialist Data Pools for Semantic Data Integration
source_description: The Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geoinformation, in collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, aims to improve the integration of heterogeneous spatial datasets used in public administration. Many specialised databases contain location references in unstructured textual form, making it difficult to integrate them into standardised geospatial systems. The objective is to enable automated georeferencing and semantic integration of such data. The solution uses natural language processing and machine learning techniques to analyse address data and linguistic spatial references, converting them into precise geospatial coordinates. These outputs are then integrated into existing spatial data infrastructures, enabling unified access and analysis. The system supports semantic enrichment and interoperability across datasets. As a pilot project, its focused on algorithm design and validation includes with expected benefits including improved data integration, enhanced decision-making, and more efficient use of geospatial information.

title: AI-Supported unmanned aeriasl vehicles (UAVs) for Ecological Agriculture and Forestry
source_description: This project explores the use of unmanned aerial vehicles to support ecological agriculture and forestry management. Monitoring weeds, crop health, and forest conditions typically requires significant manual effort and may lack precision at scale. The objective is to enable automated and efficient environmental monitoring and intervention. The solution involves adapting an existing AI-based weed detection system to operate on low-power embedded hardware mounted on drones. Machine learning models process visual data captured by onboard sensors to identify weeds and assess vegetation conditions in real time. The project also investigates the transferability of these models to forestry applications. Integration with drone platforms allows flexible and targeted data collection across large areas. As a research and development initiative, the system is still being tested and validated, with expected benefits including reduced labour requirements, improved precision, and more sustainable land management practices
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Support the integration of job seekers with artificial intelligence
source_description: The University of Applied Sciences Kiel, in collaboration with Jobcenter Kiel and the Institute for Labour Market and Vocational Research, is developing tools to improve the integration of job seekers into the labour market. Employment services often face challenges in matching individuals with suitable job opportunities and training pathways, particularly when dealing with diverse profiles and labour market dynamics. The objective is to enhance counselling services through data-driven recommendations. The solution uses machine learning techniques, including self-organising maps and reinforcement learning, to analyse anonymised data and cluster job seekers based on skills, experience, and labour market conditions. These clusters are used to generate personalised recommendations for employment, retraining, and further education opportunities. The system is designed to complement the expertise of job centre staff and support decision-making processes. The project aims to improve matching efficiency and service effectiveness, although no evidence confirms full operational deployment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Autonomous Fawn Tracking System - AROS
source_description: Farmers and wildlife-protection volunteers have only a short time to locate hidden fawns in fields before mowing begins, and manual searches with thermal drones can still be labour-intensive, weather-sensitive, and dependent on multiple people. AROS was designed in Schleswig-Holstein to address this by automating more of the detection and localisation process so that fawns can be found and rescued more efficiently. The objective is to protect wildlife, reduce dependence on scarce human resources, and enable more reliable pre-harvest scanning of fields across different conditions. The implementation combines autonomous drone flight, thermal and visual sensing, computer-vision models based on convolutional neural networks, and geolocation functions that send the detected animal’s GPS position and aerial view to the farmer and hunter for intervention. Technical reporting describes an autonomous fawn-tracking system with high positioning accuracy, while project material presents the solution as a collaboration between nAIture and public actors in Schleswig-Holstein. The expected impact is faster rescue, better field coverage, and a more scalable wildlife-protection workflow during mowing season.

organization: Ministry of Social Affairs, Youth, Family, Senior Citizens, Integration and Equality of Schleswig-Holstein
title: “Demenzwegweiser-SH” (Schleswig-Holstein Guide to Dementia)
source_description: Demenzwegweiser-SH was created to centralise and maintain up-to-date information on dementia-related services across Schleswig-Holstein. Individuals and families often struggle to identify regional counselling centres, specialist doctors, care options and support services. The platform functions as a searchable database providing structured information on medical, social and legal aspects of dementia, including nursing care insurance, legal guardianship and non-pharmacological therapies. Automated data processing techniques support continuous updating and categorisation of entries, ensuring that regional service information remains current. Information extraction and classification tools organise content into thematic categories and geographic locations. By consolidating dispersed information into a single digital guide, the platform enhances accessibility for patients, caregivers and professionals. It improves transparency of available support networks and facilitates informed decision-making regarding care pathways.

title: MASIRI – Multi-Agent Simulation for Integrated Energy and Mobility Systems
source_description: The integration of energy and mobility systems, such as vehicle-to-grid solutions, depends not only on technical optimisation but also on human behaviour and decision-making. Traditional system models often neglect how users’ experiences, preferences, and habits influence energy and mobility usage. The MASIRI project addresses this gap by exploring how behavioural insights can improve the design and regulation of integrated energy and mobility systems. Stakeholders include researchers, system designers, policymakers, and energy providers. The objective is to understand and simulate interactions between human behaviour and intelligent energy systems to optimise resource use. The solution develops a multi-agent simulation framework in which intelligent agents represent energy users with psychologically informed behaviour models. These agents interact within simulated vehicle-to-grid environments, allowing analysis of how different incentives, regulations, and system designs influence outcomes. The project improves understanding of behavioural dynamics, supports more realistic system modelling, and informs better policy and infrastructure design. MASIRI contributes to more efficient, user-centred, and resilient energy and mobility systems that align technical optimisation with real-world human behaviour.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Licence to practice
source_description: The issuance and verification of professional licences for graduates in regulated professions, such as engineering or medicine, is often a manual and time-consuming process, particularly in cross-border contexts. In Cyprus and Greece, where many students study abroad, delays, administrative burden, and risks of fraud undermine efficiency and trust. The objective of this use case is to streamline the issuance, sharing, and verification of professional credentials across borders. The solution leverages the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) to enable secure, verifiable digital credentials. Academic and professional authorities issue licences in a digital format that can be shared and validated across jurisdictions using distributed ledger technology. The system ensures authenticity, integrity, and traceability of credentials while reducing reliance on paper-based processes. As a pilot initiative involving stakeholders such as GUnet, the Cypriot Deputy Ministry, and ETEK, it demonstrates potential to reduce processing times, administrative costs, and fraud risks, while improving cross-border mobility and trust in professional qualifications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Helsinki Map Service
source_description: The Helsinki Map Service is a browser-based geospatial platform providing comprehensive mapping and real-time urban data to residents, businesses and visitors. The operational objective is to centralise spatial information about city infrastructure, services and environmental conditions into an accessible digital interface. The system integrates geographic information systems with datasets covering traffic conditions, public transport, real estate, buildings, outdoor lighting, cycling and walking routes and municipal services. Real-time feeds update traffic and mobility layers, while thematic map tools allow users to visualise specific categories of interest. The platform supports interactive exploration, search functions and layered data visualisation through a web-based map viewer. By consolidating diverse geospatial datasets, the service enhances transparency, supports urban planning and enables residents to make informed mobility and property decisions. The initiative strengthens Helsinki’s data-driven governance and open data ecosystem.

title: Talbotti - Helsinki's financial management service chatbot
source_description: The City of Helsinki introduced Talbotti as a digital contact channel for its financial management services to improve accessibility and reduce pressure on traditional customer service channels. Residents and city employees frequently require guidance on invoicing, payments and financial procedures, often outside standard office hours. Talbotti provides round-the-clock responses to common enquiries and, during opening hours, allows seamless transfer to a live chat with a customer adviser. The chatbot uses natural language processing to interpret questions and retrieve information from curated knowledge bases and financial service databases. It offers self-service guidance, up-to-date information and direct links to relevant webpages, streamlining access to forms and instructions. Interaction data are analysed to refine responses and improve intent recognition over time. By automating routine queries, Talbotti shortens response times, enhances user experience and enables staff to focus on complex cases requiring individual assessment. The solution strengthens service continuity and operational efficiency within municipal financial administration.

title: Sotebotti hester

Citizens often seek guidance on maternity clinics, child health services and other social and health-related provisions. The chatbot provides a digital interface available at all times, delivering structured information and directing users to relevant services. Hester operates using predefined dialogue paths and natural language understanding components that classify user intent and retrieve content from official service databases. It guides users through service descriptions, contact information and procedural steps, while complex or sensitive matters remain handled by professionals. By automating responses to frequently asked questions, the system reduces call volumes and enhances accessibility outside office hours. The solution supports consistent information delivery and facilitates navigation of health and social care services, contributing to improved user experience and more efficient allocation of administrative resources.

title: Dutch cycling intelligence
source_description: The Dutch Cycling Intelligence programme developed the Digital Twin “Atlas of the Accessible City” to provide data-driven insights into urban accessibility and cycling infrastructure. Coordinated by Logistics Community Brabant in collaboration with academic partners and Argaleo, the initiative addresses the need for integrated analysis of mobility bottlenecks and opportunities in urban environments. The Atlas aggregates publicly available datasets and, where applicable, private data sources into a three-dimensional geospatial visualisation platform. Geographic information systems and data analytics tools map traffic flows, cycling routes and accessibility indicators, enabling stakeholders to identify congestion points and infrastructural gaps at a glance. The digital twin translates policy questions into measurable spatial insights, supporting planning decisions and infrastructure investment. By centralising and visualising complex datasets, the system enhances collaboration between public authorities and research institutions, strengthens evidence-based mobility policy and improves strategic planning for accessible and sustainable urban transport networks.

title: Atlas Cyclable Utrecht
source_description: Commissioned by the Province of Utrecht, Atlas Fietsbaar Utrecht was developed within a digital twin framework to assess cycling accessibility, particularly in relation to educational institutions. Policymakers required detailed insights into route quality, infrastructure performance and optimal locations for bicycle tunnels. The platform integrates publicly available transport data with advanced bicycle usage analyses into a centralised dashboard. Geospatial modelling and traffic data processing tools visualise cycling flows, detect bottlenecks such as traffic light delays and evaluate accessibility scenarios. The dashboard enables users to explore route efficiency and identify priority areas for infrastructure development. By translating mobility data into actionable policy insights, the Atlas supports targeted investment in cycling infrastructure and promotes sustainable transport. The system enhances transparency and decision-making efficiency by offering user-friendly access to consolidated, data-driven indicators relevant to regional planning and educational accessibility strategies.

title: Atlas Multimodal Brabant – Digital Twin for Freight Corridors (Netherlands)
source_description: Atlas Multimodal Brabant was developed by Argaleo for Logistics Community Brabant to support coordination of multimodal freight transport corridors. Transport operators require clear visibility of shared routes, transhipment terminals and environmental performance indicators to optimise logistics planning. The digital twin aggregates data on transport corridors, terminal locations and CO₂ reduction targets into an interactive geospatial platform. Users can identify accessible terminals from their location, evaluate route options and contact operators directly through integrated communication functions. Data integration and visual analytics tools provide insights into corridor usage and sustainability performance, enabling evidence-based decisions on modal shifts and collaborative transport solutions. By centralising freight information and environmental metrics, the Atlas enhances transparency, supports emission reduction goals and improves efficiency in regional logistics networks. The platform strengthens cooperation between public authorities, academic institutions and private transport actors within Brabant’s multimodal strategy.

title: Crowd management dashboard in 's-Hertogenbosch
source_description: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the municipality of ’s-Hertogenbosch implemented a digital dashboard to manage pedestrian flows safely during reopening phases. The operational objective was to monitor visitor density and movement patterns in real time to prevent overcrowding. Developed by Argaleo, the dashboard integrates pedestrian sensor data and historical mobility datasets into a unified visual interface. Data analytics tools process current flow information and analyse trends, answering questions such as peak entry times and predominant directions of movement. The system provides municipal staff with situational awareness to support timely crowd control measures and communication strategies. By combining real-time monitoring with historical analysis, the dashboard enables data-driven decisions that balance public health considerations with economic activity. The initiative enhances urban resilience and supports safe city centre management through digital twin technologies and mobility analytics.

title: Outdoor Mobility Digital Twin at TU Delft
source_description: The Technical University of Delft developed a digital twin of its campus environment to analyse and manage pedestrian and cyclist flows during the COVID-19 pandemic. Managing crowd density in public spaces became critical to ensure safety and compliance with health measures. The objective is to provide real-time insights into mobility patterns and support data-driven decision-making for crowd management. The solution integrates data from sensors that convert visual inputs into privacy-preserving representations, combined with external data sources such as public transport locations and infrastructure status. These data are visualised in a three-dimensional digital twin dashboard, using heat maps to indicate crowd density and movement patterns. Advanced analytics are applied to identify congestion and support scenario analysis. As a pilot, the system demonstrates the potential to improve situational awareness, enhance safety, and optimise space utilisation, although no evidence confirms long-term operational deployment.

title: Chatbot - Municipality of Senigallia
source_description: Municipal administrations often receive a high volume of general enquiries from citizens, many of which concern routine information that can be handled more efficiently through digital self-service than through direct staff intervention. In Senigallia, this use case centres on a chatbot introduced on the municipality’s official website to respond to general citizen enquiries and provide a more accessible first point of contact. The objective is to improve responsiveness, make common information easier to obtain, and reduce the burden on municipal staff dealing with repetitive requests. The implementation uses a website-based conversational interface embedded in the municipality’s digital environment. At a conceptual level, the chatbot serves as a front-end guidance tool that interprets user questions and returns prepared answers or directions to the relevant information, helping citizens navigate services without needing to identify the correct office in advance. The solution is intended for general enquiries rather than personalised case handling, making it suitable for high-volume, low-complexity interactions. The impact includes faster access to municipal information, improved user convenience, and a more efficient allocation of staff effort. It also supports the wider digitalisation of citizen services by creating a scalable channel for routine communication and by improving the municipality’s ability to handle enquiries outside traditional contact methods. The official municipal site confirms the broader digital service context in which this type of web-based support is delivered.

source_description: The University of Helsinki implemented Hubot to support student advisory services and improve access to information regarding applications and studies. title: Blockchain to increase security in foreign aid disbursement in Demnark
source_description: Aid disbursement in fragile or corruption-prone environments raises a longstanding public-administration challenge: how to ensure that funds reach the intended beneficiaries securely, transparently, and with reduced leakage. The Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs explored this issue in a Danida report that considered whether blockchain and cryptocurrency-based approaches could improve traceability and integrity in development assistance. The objective was to test whether distributed-ledger models might reduce corruption risks, strengthen beneficiary access to funds, and modernise aid-delivery mechanisms. At a conceptual level, the proposed implementation would use blockchain-based transaction records and digital-payment mechanisms to track disbursements and potentially route aid more directly to end recipients. The case is therefore framed as an innovation concept for development cooperation rather than a conventional administrative service. The expected impact lies in stronger transparency, improved traceability of transfers, and greater confidence that funds can reach intended beneficiaries safely, while also contributing to wider debate on how emerging financial technologies might support more accountable aid delivery.

organization: Publications Office of the European Union
title: Chatbot Publio - EU Publication Office
source_description: Publio is the virtual assistant of the Publications Office of the European Union, designed to help users navigate extensive digital repositories of EU documents and institutional information. Researchers, professionals and citizens often require support in locating specific publications, organisations or officials within complex databases. Publio provides a multilingual conversational interface available in English, French and Spanish. The assistant uses natural language processing to interpret user queries and match them with indexed content across the Publications Office website. It retrieves document references, organisational details and relevant links, guiding users through search results without requiring advanced search skills. By facilitating structured interaction with large document repositories, Publio improves discoverability, reduces search time and enhances accessibility to EU information resources. The solution supports transparency and public access to official documentation through scalable digital assistance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI for analysing investigative data in Austria
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Austrian authorities implemented advanced analytics tools to process and analyse large volumes of investigative data in complex cases involving fraud and financial crime. Investigators face challenges in extracting relevant information from heterogeneous datasets, including documents, communication records and transactional data. The solution applies machine-learning techniques for classification, metadata extraction and relationship detection across structured and unstructured data sources. Natural language processing and pattern recognition models identify semantic correlations, trace information origins and map communication flows. Visual analytics components generate network graphs and fraud pattern visualisations without requiring custom coding for each case. The system integrates into investigative workflows, supporting analysts in identifying hidden links and prioritising lines of enquiry. By automating data processing and pattern detection, the solution accelerates investigations, improves analytical depth and enhances evidence-based decision-making while maintaining human oversight in prosecutorial actions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Court of Ravenna - digital signature
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: Courts increasingly need secure, traceable ways to authenticate documents and preserve confidence in judicial records as procedures become more digital. In Ravenna, this project was described as an enhancement to the court’s existing IT system through the addition of a digital-signature solution and data storage on a private or consortium permissioned blockchain. The objective is to improve the integrity, authenticity, and traceability of judicial documents while fitting within an existing court information environment rather than replacing it. The implementation, as described in European public-sector blockchain case documentation, combines digital-signature workflows with permissioned distributed-ledger storage so that document events and validation information can be recorded in a controlled blockchain environment. At a conceptual level, the solution is aimed at strengthening evidential trust and process reliability in a judicial setting where records must remain tamper-evident and attributable. The anticipated impact is stronger document security, better traceability, and a more robust digital workflow for judicial administration, especially where authenticity and auditability are essential to procedural trust.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Lawyers' blockchain-based register in Malta
source_description: Malta sought to modernise the management of lawyers’ warrants by replacing fragmented and paper-based records with a transparent, reliable and accessible digital register. Previously, verifying whether a lawyer was duly authorised required consultation of administrative records that were not fully interoperable or publicly searchable, limiting transparency for citizens and institutions. The pilot project aimed to create the first electronic register of lawyers in Malta, enabling government, legal professionals and the public to access consistent and up-to-date warrant information. A blockchain-based architecture was implemented to store and synchronise records in an immutable and decentralised ledger. The system was initially developed as a private blockchain to ensure controlled participation, with a design allowing future migration to a public blockchain for non-personal data such as names and warrant status. Cryptographic mechanisms ensure data integrity and traceability of updates, while authorised entities can validate entries in real time. The initiative enhances trust in legal services, reduces administrative verification time and strengthens transparency, providing a scalable digital infrastructure for professional registers.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DigiAkkoord - blockchain-based approval processes for government activities
source_description: Government approval workflows often involve many actors, documents, and hand-offs, making it difficult to ensure transparency, trust, and efficient coordination across the full chain of transactions and authorisations. DigiAkkoord was presented as a project using a permissioned blockchain to support workflow, transaction, and document approval processes in government. The objective is to increase trust, improve traceability, and streamline approval procedures where multiple parties need a shared record of validated process steps. The implementation, as described in European public-sector blockchain material, uses a permissioned distributed ledger to record approval events and workflow progression in a controlled environment suitable for public administration. At a conceptual level, the approach seeks to create a shared, tamper-evident process layer across approvals, rather than relying only on fragmented back-office records. The expected impact is greater transparency, stronger process integrity, and better efficiency in document approval and inter-organisational workflow handling, particularly where several public actors need a common, trusted view of procedural progress.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Known Traveller Digital Identity Pilot Project (KTDI)
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: International travel requires repeated identity checks across airlines, airports, border agencies, and other actors, and this fragmented process can create friction, redundancy, and security inefficiencies. KTDI was developed to explore whether a trusted, decentralised digital identity could simplify this end-to-end journey by allowing traveller data to be shared and reused in a more secure and interoperable way. The objective was to test a traveller-centric identity model that could support smoother airport passage, reduce repeated manual checks, and improve trust between public and private travel actors. The implementation combined decentralised identity concepts with technologies such as biometrics, blockchain, mobile devices, and cryptography. In the pilot model, travellers would upload information in advance, and the system would use biometric recognition, including facial-image matching, to support functions such as automated check-in and airport gate passage. The impact of the project lies in demonstrating a possible future travel architecture and informing best practices for digital identity in cross-border mobility, with potential benefits in speed, convenience, interoperability, and more efficient use of identity data across the travel ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital receipt processing at the Swedish Tax Agency
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The Swedish Tax Agency identified inefficiencies in accounting, auditing and taxation processes linked to paper-based and fragmented receipt management, which increases administrative burden for businesses and limits real-time oversight. The project aimed to explore digital solutions capable of streamlining receipt handling and improving data reliability for tax purposes. Following an initial phase examining blockchain-inspired approaches to accounting and auditing, the second phase focused on end-to-end digital receipt processing for companies. The solution tested distributed ledger concepts and secure data-sharing mechanisms to record transaction data in a tamper-resistant format, enabling authorised stakeholders to access verified information directly. Digital receipts are standardised, stored electronically and linked to accounting systems, reducing manual input and reconciliation tasks. The approach supports automated validation and traceability of transactions, facilitating more efficient audits and compliance checks. Expected benefits include reduced administrative costs for businesses, improved accuracy of tax reporting and enhanced transparency in financial flows, contributing to a more efficient and trustworthy taxation ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chatbot Skatti - Swedish Tax Agency
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The Swedish Tax Agency introduced Chatbot Skatti to provide accessible guidance on tax-related matters through its official website. Citizens frequently seek clarification on filing procedures, deadlines, deductions and digital services, creating recurring enquiries. Skatti offers a conversational interface available around the clock, delivering responses to general questions based on curated tax guidance content. The system employs natural language processing to interpret user input and match it with predefined intents and information sources. It directs users to relevant forms, explanatory pages and digital services while refraining from handling personalised account data. By automating answers to routine enquiries, Skatti reduces call centre workload, improves response times and enhances user convenience. The chatbot supports consistent dissemination of tax information and contributes to the Agency’s broader digital service strategy.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FAKE-ID - Video analysis using AI to detect false and manipulated identities
source_description: The rapid spread of manipulated video content poses growing risks to trust, security, and democratic processes, as falsified or synthetic identities can be used for fraud, disinformation, and impersonation. Public authorities, media organisations, and digital platforms require reliable methods to detect such content at scale. The FAKE-ID project addresses this challenge by supporting the identification of falsified and manipulated identities in video material. Stakeholders include security agencies, technology providers, and institutions responsible for safeguarding digital integrity. The objective is to improve the detection of deep-fake videos and manipulated identity representations to strengthen trust in digital media. The solution develops advanced video analysis methods that examine visual and temporal inconsistencies in facial movements, expressions, and image artefacts. Trained models analyse video streams to identify signs of synthetic manipulation under varying recording conditions. The project establishes robust evaluation frameworks and datasets to ensure reliability. The impact includes improved detection accuracy of manipulated videos, reduced risk of identity fraud, and enhanced resilience against disinformation. FAKE-ID contributes to safer digital environments and supports the development of trustworthy media verification technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Fraunhofer Institute for Computer Graphics Research IGD
title: Environmental monitoring of sea trouts with AI
source_description: Monitoring fish populations such as sea trout is essential for environmental conservation and fisheries management, but traditional counting methods based on manual observation are labour-intensive and prone to error. The objective of this use case is to automate the monitoring process and improve accuracy in species identification and counting. The solution uses underwater cameras to capture video sequences, which are analysed using deep learning models trained to distinguish sea trout from other objects such as leaves or different fish species. The system processes visual data to detect and count individuals in real time or through batch analysis. This approach enables scalable and consistent monitoring across different locations. The system demonstrates potential to improve efficiency and data quality in environmental monitoring.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Differentiation of ship types on satellite radar images
source_description: Monitoring maritime activities over large ocean areas is critical for environmental protection, security, and enforcement against illegal activities such as unregulated fishing. Traditional methods rely on manual interpretation of satellite imagery, which is time-consuming and limited in scalability. The objective is to automate the detection and classification of vessels using remote sensing data. The solution applies deep learning techniques to satellite radar images, enabling the identification and differentiation of ship types based on their radar signatures. These models are trained on labelled datasets and integrated into earth observation systems used by authorities and organisations. The system supports applications such as maritime surveillance, environmental monitoring, and enforcement. The project demonstrates potential to improve detection accuracy and operational efficiency, although full deployment details remain limited.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel (GEOMAR)
title: CONMAR - studying contaminated sites with underwater drones
source_description: The CONMAR project addresses the environmental and safety challenges posed by marine munitions and contaminated sites in coastal and offshore areas. These hazards are difficult to monitor due to limited accessibility and fragmented data across institutions. The objective is to improve understanding, monitoring, and management of such sites through integrated data and advanced technologies. The solution combines underwater drones with data integration and analysis tools to collect and process information on contaminated areas. Machine learning techniques are applied to analyse sensor and imaging data, supporting detection and assessment of hazards. The project also integrates existing datasets from research organisations, government agencies, and industry to create a comprehensive knowledge base. As a research and development initiative, the project is ongoing, with expected outcomes including improved environmental monitoring, informed policy decisions, and enhanced remediation strategies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Peter L. Reichertz Institute for Medical Informatics
title: MoCaB - Reliable mobile support for caring relatives
source_description: Caring relatives often face complex daily coordination tasks, emotional strain and limited access to tailored nursing knowledge while supporting family members in need of care. The MoCaB project aims to develop a mobile assistance system that helps organise care routines, provides situation-specific guidance and promotes carers’ physical and mental wellbeing. A knowledge-based infrastructure, known as the MoCaB world, underpins the system and enables a mobile software agent to deliver context-aware support. Sensors capture relevant data from everyday activities to recognise situations and trigger appropriate recommendations, while maintaining an overview of the condition of the person receiving care. Intelligent algorithms process contextual information to provide timely prompts, educational resources and links to support services. Data protection and privacy safeguards are integrated into the architecture to ensure secure handling of sensitive health information. The solution seeks to reduce stress, improve care quality and strengthen carers’ resilience, offering scalable digital support that complements existing health and social care services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Data4UrbanMobility - Development of application-driven tools for mobility information
source_description: Urban mobility planning increasingly depends on integrating diverse data sources to understand traffic dynamics, user behaviour, and emerging mobility services. Cities often lack tools that translate large volumes of heterogeneous mobility data into actionable insights for planning and operations. Data4UrbanMobility addresses this gap by developing application-driven tools that support data-informed mobility decisions. Stakeholders include urban administrations, mobility service providers, and citizens. The objective is to enable evidence-based planning, development, and operation of innovative mobility services. The solution integrates regional and historical mobility data from multiple sources and applies data extraction, integration, and analytical methods to create event-based views of mobility systems. Predictive models generate forecasts of traffic behaviour and system development, while tailored analytics tools support specific use cases. All components are brought together in a unified platform. The project improves situational awareness, supports proactive planning, and enables more efficient mobility services. It contributes to better-coordinated transport systems, improved user experience, and data-driven urban mobility governance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Julius Kühn Institute Federal Research Institute for Cultivated Plants (JKI)
title: AI^2 - (Aphid identification through artificial intelligence)
source_description: The AI² project focuses on improving the monitoring of harmful insects in agriculture, where timely detection is critical to prevent crop damage and ensure food security. Traditional methods of analysing insect trap data are labour-intensive and slow, limiting the ability to respond quickly to emerging threats. The objective is to automate identification and counting of insect species in monitoring systems. The solution uses machine learning and deep learning techniques to analyse images from airborne insect traps, identifying and classifying species such as aphids. Neural networks are trained on labelled datasets to recognise visual patterns and quantify insect populations. The system enables rapid and standardised analysis across multiple locations. As an ongoing development project, it demonstrates potential to significantly reduce processing time, improve consistency of results, and support early detection and management of invasive pests.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence GmbH (DFKI)
title: AI-TEST-FIELD – Semantic Environment Perception for Intelligent Sensor Systems
source_description: Safe operation of autonomous and assisted systems requires reliable perception of complex and changing environments. Current sensor systems often struggle to deliver consistent and certifiable outputs under varying conditions, limiting deployment in safety-critical contexts. AI-TEST-FIELD addresses this challenge by developing the foundations for robust, trustworthy sensor systems. Stakeholders include industrial developers, certification bodies, and operators of automated systems. The objective is to enable sensor technologies that provide stable and interpretable guidance for action across diverse environmental scenarios. The solution focuses on semantic environment perception using learning-based approaches that fuse data from multiple sensor modalities. Models are trained and tested in controlled environments to ensure robustness and consistency of outputs. Emphasis is placed on reproducibility, validation, and suitability for certification. The project delivers reference architectures, datasets, and testing methodologies. The impact includes increased reliability of intelligent sensor systems, improved safety assurance, and accelerated industrial adoption. AI-TEST-FIELD supports the deployment of trustworthy perception technologies in domains such as automated transport and industrial automation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Julius Kühn Institute Federal Research Institute for Cultivated Plants (JKI)
title: BETTER-WEEDS - AI to recognise weed species
source_description: Farmers must balance effective weed control to protect crop yields with growing societal and regulatory expectations for environmentally sustainable practices and biodiversity preservation. Conventional blanket herbicide application can harm beneficial plant species and increase ecological pressure. The BETTER-WEEDS project aims to develop cost-effective and time-efficient tools to record weed species and densities at field level, enabling differentiated management strategies. High-resolution field imagery and sensor data are analysed using machine learning-based image recognition models trained to distinguish between competitive and non-competitive weed species. The system generates area-specific maps indicating species distribution, density and ecological traits, which are then used to design tailored management plans. By identifying competitively weak or rare species with ecosystem benefits, the approach supports selective interventions rather than uniform treatment. The solution enhances operational efficiency, reduces input costs and promotes biodiversity-friendly farming practices. It contributes to improved sustainability and ecological performance while maintaining agricultural productivity through data-driven, site-specific decision support.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: FZI Research Center for Computer Science
title: BoniKI - plant-specific assessment by autonomous systems
source_description: Assessing plant health, growth, and pest infestation is essential for sustainable agriculture, yet manual inspection is labour-intensive, costly, and dependent on expert judgement. Sampling-based methods provide limited resolution and may miss early signs of stress or disease. The BoniKI project addresses this challenge by enabling automated, plant-level assessment at scale. Stakeholders include farmers, agronomists, and agricultural service providers. The objective is to increase efficiency, transparency, and sustainability in crop monitoring and decision-making. The solution uses unmanned aerial systems to capture high-resolution imagery of agricultural fields. Data processing pipelines separate crops from weeds and background elements, followed by automated assessment of plant condition using trained analytical models. The system derives relevant scoring parameters and generates actionable insights for field management. The project aims to deliver an integrated, user-friendly solution for routine agricultural use. The impact includes reduced monitoring costs, earlier detection of stress or infestation, and more targeted interventions. BoniKI supports precision agriculture and contributes to more resource-efficient and resilient farming practices.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Julius Kühn Institute Federal Research Institute for Cultivated Plants (JKI)
title: DynAWI - Predict extreme weather situations reliably and region-specific
source_description: Extreme weather events increasingly threaten agricultural productivity, yet timely and region-specific assessment tools are often lacking. Farmers and public authorities need reliable indicators to anticipate yield impacts and support risk management decisions. DynAWI addresses this need by developing a process chain for monitoring and analysing extreme weather conditions in agriculture. Stakeholders include agricultural agencies, researchers, and private sector users of environmental data. The objective is to provide scalable, regionally differentiated indicators that link weather extremes to crop yield outcomes. The solution integrates geospatial datasets within a scalable data infrastructure and applies analytical models to derive dynamic agricultural weather indicators. These indicators capture the intensity, duration, and spatial extent of extreme conditions relevant to crop development. Outputs are made available through standardised interfaces for integration into national and European data spaces. The project improves early warning capabilities, supports impact assessment, and enhances planning under climate uncertainty. DynAWI contributes to more resilient agricultural systems and informed adaptation strategies in the face of climate change.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FreshRegio – making the quality of fruit and vegetables measurable
source_description: Quality assessment of fruit and vegetables is critical for regional agriculture and efficient food supply chains, yet traditional inspection methods are often subjective, labour-intensive, and limited in predictive power. FreshRegio addresses this challenge by enabling objective, data-driven evaluation of product quality and shelf life. Stakeholders include farmers, distributors, retailers, and consumers. The objective is to strengthen regional food systems by improving transparency and reducing waste. The solution combines near-infrared sensor technology with analytical models to assess internal quality attributes of produce non-destructively. Measurements are processed to predict freshness and remaining shelf life, supporting informed decisions along the supply chain. The system simplifies quality control processes and enables consistent evaluation across batches. The impact includes reduced food waste, improved product differentiation, and stronger trust between producers and buyers.
