Qualitative results suggest increased empathy, improved self-reflection and potential reductions in repeat offending, supporting future scaling of immersive interventions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Karlskrona generates digital twin to show the city's present and future in three dimensions
source_description: Municipal planning increasingly requires integrated spatial analysis and effective citizen engagement to manage complex urban environments. In Karlskrona, fragmented datasets limited the ability to simulate future development scenarios. The objective of this project is to create a comprehensive digital representation of the city to support planning, infrastructure management and public engagement. The implementation combines aerial imagery, building plans, drone data, IoT inputs and departmental datasets into a three-dimensional digital twin. The model supports internal analysis, such as infrastructure planning, and immersive engagement through AR and VR events for residents. Expected impacts include more informed decision-making, improved coordination across departments and enhanced transparency. Qualitative outcomes include stronger public participation, better scenario testing and streamlined municipal processes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Skanderborg Municipality uses virtual reality to help people with anxiety
source_description: People with anxiety often struggle to engage with traditional therapeutic approaches due to fear of real-world exposure. In Skanderborg, social and employment services explored new welfare technologies to support gradual treatment. The objective of this pilot is to provide a safe, controlled environment for exposure-based therapy. The implementation uses virtual reality to recreate social situations that users can experience progressively, guided by professionals. The approach allows customisation to individual needs and integration into existing care pathways. Expected impacts include improved treatment engagement, reduced anxiety symptoms and enhanced therapeutic outcomes. Qualitative benefits include increased confidence, better coping strategies and a scalable model for mental health support.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Municipality of Skövde provides funds to purchase driving simulators to improve training and reduce emissions
source_description: Vocational education programmes in transport, construction and heavy vehicle operation require extensive practical driving hours, which can limit student access, increase fuel consumption and generate avoidable emissions. In Skövde, vocational teachers identified capacity constraints and environmental impacts linked to traditional vehicle-based instruction. Stakeholders include the municipality, vocational schools, teachers and students in vehicle transport and construction programmes. The objective is to expand access to practical training while reducing environmental footprint and operational costs. The solution involves the deployment of eight advanced driving simulators that replicate vehicle, truck and machinery operation scenarios through immersive software environments. Simulation platforms integrate realistic physics engines, scenario-based training modules and performance analytics dashboards to track learner progress. These systems complement, rather than fully replace, on-road instruction and are embedded within the existing curriculum. Expected impacts include increased training capacity, reduced fuel use and emissions, lower wear-and-tear costs on vehicles and improved safety through risk-free scenario practice.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: City of Helsinki evaluates sensory room and virtual reality therapy at Kustaankartano Senior Centre
source_description: Older adults with memory disorders often experience anxiety, stress, and reduced quality of life, placing pressure on care staff and increasing reliance on medication. The City of Helsinki sought innovative, non-pharmacological approaches to improve wellbeing in residential care settings. This pilot, developed at the Kustaankartano Senior Centre, addresses the need for calming, engaging therapeutic environments for residents with cognitive impairment. Stakeholders include residents, care staff, healthcare providers, and city authorities. The objective is to reduce stress, improve mood, and support care delivery through immersive and sensory-based interventions. The solution combines a sensory room featuring natural elements with interactive digital installations and virtual reality experiences. Residents can engage with calming nature simulations or creative activities that stimulate senses and memories. These interventions are integrated into daily care routines and tailored to individual needs. The pilot demonstrates reduced stress levels among residents, lower staff workload, and decreased use of antidepressant medication. It improves quality of life, supports staff efficiency, and provides evidence for scalable, technology-enabled therapies in elder care.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Greater London Authority places city planning into virtual reality with Square Mile VR project
source_description: Urban planning in London involves balancing growth, density and heritage across multiple boroughs, while ensuring transparency and public trust in decision-making. The Greater London Authority (GLA), borough planning departments, developers and citizens require clear ways to understand how new developments affect their surroundings. The objective of this use case is to improve planning decisions, pre-application discussions and public consultations by providing accurate, city-wide visual context for proposed developments. The implementation relies on a highly detailed three-dimensional digital model of London, covering the full 1,619 km² of the capital with accuracy down to 15 cm. The platform integrates geospatial data, building information and planning datasets, allowing users to visualise massing, height, density and sightlines in an interactive environment, including immersive virtual reality. It integrates with planning workflows used by boroughs and developers. The results include faster and more informed planning decisions, improved quality of submissions and clearer communication with citizens. Over 80% of London boroughs use the platform, reporting improved transparency, reduced planning friction and better understanding of impacts, delivering time and cost savings while increasing confidence in the city’s long-term development strategy.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Trafford Council mixes virtual reality with online engagement for Urmston Active Neighbourhood
source_description: Trafford Council started with a pre-COVID listening session that generated more than 3,400 comments on walking and cycling plans for Urmston. Residents now use the council's virtual room to find data, suggested solutions, and maps in a format similar to the in-person session. Project leaders conduct webchats with up to 20 participants in each session for additional feedback. Engaged residents can help those without computers understand the planning process as project ambassadors.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Fingal County Council, IE shows Balbriggan residents the future with a 3D Virtual Reality plan
source_description: Urban regeneration projects often struggle with public engagement, as long-term plans can be difficult for residents to visualise. Fingal County Council addressed this challenge in Balbriggan by creating a 3D virtual reality experience showcasing six years of planned development. Stakeholders include local residents, planners and county operations staff. The objective is to improve transparency, community involvement and understanding of how regeneration initiatives will affect daily life. The VR environment presents planned infrastructure such as smart public furniture, maker spaces, micro-mobility hubs and harbour upgrades. Users explore the town’s future layout using VR headsets maintained at the Our Balbriggan Hub, with staff available to answer questions. The system integrates urban planning data and architectural models into an immersive experience. The impact has been improved public understanding, more informed feedback and stronger community buy-in. The project demonstrates how immersive technologies can enhance participatory planning, reduce consultation barriers and support smarter, citizen-centred urban development.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Fingal County Council and Cork county council
title: Fingal County Council and Cork county council partnered with AVIVA Driving School to launch "Your Life - Your Choice"" VR"
source_description: Fingal County Council and Cork County Council partnered with AVIVA Driving School to deliver the “Your Life – Your Choice” virtual reality road safety experience targeting young drivers aged 16 to 25. Road accidents involving distraction and speeding remain a significant public safety concern among this age group. The programme uses immersive virtual reality headsets to simulate a car journey from the passenger’s perspective, culminating in a realistic traffic accident scenario. The simulation reconstructs contributory factors such as mobile phone distraction and excessive speed, alongside the serious consequences of collisions. Interactive audiovisual elements create an experiential learning environment designed to influence attitudes and risk perception. By placing participants in a controlled yet immersive scenario, the initiative aims to strengthen awareness of dangerous driving behaviours. The programme supports preventive education efforts and enhances engagement compared with traditional classroom-based road safety campaigns.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Pothole ROBOT hits the roads in Hertfordshire
source_description: Local highway authorities face persistent challenges from potholes, which damage vehicles, increase accident risk and generate high maintenance costs through labour-intensive repair processes. Hertfordshire County Council sought a solution to improve repair speed, consistency and worker safety while minimising disruption to road users. The objective of this use case is to modernise road maintenance by automating pothole detection and repair. The implementation deploys a robotic system equipped with sensors, cameras and automated repair mechanisms capable of identifying surface depressions, assessing their size and filling them without manual intervention. The system combines computer vision, depth measurement and automated material application, integrating with maintenance planning processes to log repairs and prioritise intervention areas. The reported impact shows that repairs can be completed up to 70% faster than traditional methods, with fewer road closures and reduced exposure of workers to live traffic. Qualitative outcomes include improved road condition reliability, lower operational costs over time, enhanced worker safety and increased public satisfaction with road maintenance services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Suma Gestión Tributaria. Diputación de Alicante
title: Chatbot alicante
source_description: Municipal administrations routinely handle large volumes of repetitive citizen enquiries related to local services, opening hours and administrative procedures, which places pressure on staff and slows response times. The City of Alicante aimed to improve accessibility to information while optimising internal resources. The objective of this use case is to provide fast, consistent answers to general enquiries through digital channels. The implementation introduces a conversational interface embedded in the municipal website, connected to curated knowledge bases containing validated service information. The system retrieves relevant answers and directs users to appropriate online resources or offices when needed, integrating with existing content management systems. The impact includes reduced call centre workload, improved response times and increased availability of information outside office hours. Qualitative benefits include enhanced citizen experience, greater service consistency and more efficient allocation of municipal staff to complex cases.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Suma Gestión Tributaria. Diputación de Alicante
title: Office in the metaverse through mobile phone
source_description: Accessing municipal services can be difficult for citizens facing mobility constraints, limited opening hours or low familiarity with traditional digital portals. Alicante sought to explore new interaction models that improve accessibility and engagement. The objective of this use case is to provide an immersive, user-friendly digital environment for interacting with public services. The implementation delivers a virtual office accessible via mobile devices, where citizens create avatars and navigate a three-dimensional municipal space to consult services and obtain guidance. The environment integrates service information, interaction tools and navigation support within a simulated public office setting. The impact includes improved accessibility, increased citizen engagement and a more inclusive service channel. Qualitative results suggest higher user interest, improved understanding of available services and a novel complement to traditional e-government platforms.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Suma Gestión Tributaria. Diputación de Alicante
title: Innovation in Local Government: digital transformation and GeoAI for Data Management.
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Local governments often face revenue losses due to incomplete or inconsistent property data spread across multiple administrative databases. Alicante sought to improve tax fairness and revenue collection. The objective of this use case is to identify buildings that are not correctly registered for taxation. The implementation integrates geospatial analysis with data-sharing across cadastral, planning and utility databases. By cross-referencing spatial footprints with administrative records, discrepancies are detected and flagged for review. The impact includes increased tax revenue, improved data accuracy and more efficient enforcement processes. Qualitative benefits include fairer taxation, improved inter-agency cooperation and stronger financial sustainability for local government.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI within the Flanders Investment and Trade organisation
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Flanders Investment and Trade (FIT), the regional trade promotion organisation, manages numerous ‘trade cases’ submitted by Flemish companies seeking information on foreign markets, regulations, partners or opportunities. Previously, case handling relied on Microsoft Dynamics for customer relationship management and SharePoint for document storage, requiring manual searches through past files and reports. To improve efficiency and knowledge reuse, FIT implemented a natural language processing solution designed to partially automate responses to routine enquiries. Trained on a large dataset of historical trade questions and answers, the model functions as a semantic search engine that interprets the full context of incoming questions rather than matching isolated keywords. The system retrieves relevant prior answers and presents suggestions directly within the CRM interface through an additional tab. Staff review and adapt these suggestions before responding. The solution reduces search time, accelerates handling of frequently asked questions and strengthens organisational knowledge management while maintaining human oversight for complex or strategic cases.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Public Service Policy ans Support (FPS BOSA)
title: AI-enable accessibility check tool to make EU-compliant federal websites
source_description: Following the EU Web Accessibility Directive requiring public sector websites to meet accessibility standards, Belgium’s Federal Public Service Policy and Support (BOSA) sought to improve consistency and reduce manual errors in compliance assessments. Traditional accessibility checks relied heavily on human evaluation, which could be time-consuming and inconsistent. BOSA integrated an AI-driven open-source module into its accessibility checking tool to automate detection of common accessibility issues. The system analyses website code and content, identifying potential non-compliance with accessibility guidelines such as missing alternative text, improper structure or contrast issues. Automated classification algorithms flag problematic elements and generate structured reports for public organisations. The tool is available for use by federal agencies to support continuous monitoring and corrective action. By combining automated scanning with human review, the solution increases efficiency, standardises evaluation processes and supports EU-compliant digital services across federal institutions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: The Flemish public employment service reinvents orientation tests with AI
source_description: VDAB, the Flemish public employment service, modernised its career orientation testing system to provide more personalised guidance for job seekers. Traditional standardised tests offered limited adaptability to individual profiles and labour market trends. In collaboration with Radix, VDAB developed Orient 2.0, a digital orientation tool incorporating machine-learning techniques to tailor assessments dynamically. The system analyses user responses and behavioural patterns to predict professional interests and suggest relevant career paths. Models are trained on historical test data and employment outcomes, enabling adaptive question sequencing and personalised feedback. The tool integrates into VDAB’s digital platform, supporting counsellors in advising job seekers while preserving professional oversight. By delivering customised assessments at scale, Orient 2.0 enhances user engagement, improves relevance of career recommendations and increases efficiency in employment guidance services. The approach strengthens data-driven labour market orientation while maintaining human involvement in final counselling decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Brussels Airport Company – Check-in Forecasting Project (Belgium)
source_description: As part of its Airport Operations Plan, Brussels Airport Company sought to optimise workforce allocation by forecasting passenger arrivals at check-in counters in 30-minute intervals. Fluctuating passenger flows can create congestion or underutilised staff capacity. In collaboration with Radix, predictive models were developed using historical passenger survey data and flight characteristics. Machine-learning algorithms analyse variables such as flight type, destination and traveller behaviour patterns to estimate arrival volumes at specific times. Forecast outputs are integrated into operational dashboards used by airport managers, who share insights with partners to align staffing levels. By anticipating peak loads more accurately, the system improves passenger experience, reduces queues and enhances cost efficiency. The data-driven approach supports coordinated planning across stakeholders and strengthens real-time operational decision-making within the airport environment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Brussels Airport Company – Passenger Reduced Mobility (PRM) Forecasting (Belgium)
source_description: Brussels Airport Company aimed to improve planning for assistance services provided to passengers with reduced mobility (PRMs), a resource-intensive yet essential service. Daily fluctuations in PRM numbers require accurate staffing forecasts to maintain service quality without incurring excessive costs. As part of the Airport Operations Plan, predictive analytics models were developed to estimate PRM demand based on flight data, historical assistance records and seasonal trends. Machine-learning techniques generate forecasts that inform workforce scheduling and coordination among service partners. Outputs are integrated into operational dashboards, enabling proactive capacity planning. By improving demand prediction, the airport enhances service reliability for PRMs, reduces waiting times and optimises staff allocation. The initiative balances inclusivity and operational efficiency, ensuring high-quality assistance while maintaining financial sustainability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Brussels Airport Company – Baggage Forecasting Project (Belgium)
source_description: To prevent bottlenecks in baggage handling, Brussels Airport Company implemented predictive analytics to forecast the number of bags per flight, with particular focus on time-critical transfer baggage. With an average of 17,150 departing bags daily in January 2023, including 5,796 transfer bags, accurate forecasting is essential for smooth operations. Machine-learning models analyse historical baggage volumes, flight schedules and transfer patterns to estimate expected bag counts at granular intervals. The forecasts support allocation of staff and conveyor resources within the baggage handling system. Integrated into operational dashboards, the predictions enable airport managers to anticipate peak loads and mitigate delays. The approach improves processing efficiency, reduces congestion risks and enhances overall airport performance. By leveraging data-driven forecasting, the airport strengthens coordination among operational partners and supports a reliable passenger experience.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-Based Public Sentiment Analysis – Statistics Flanders (Belgium)
source_description: Statistics Flanders explored the use of publicly available social media data to complement official statistics with timely insights into public sentiment. The objective was to assess societal reactions to major events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine. In collaboration with a technology partner, the agency developed an AI-powered dashboard analysing up to 50,000 Flemish tweets per month. Natural language processing and sentiment analysis models classify posts by topic and emotional tone, generating aggregate indicators displayed in interactive visualisations. The system enables trend analysis over time and comparison across themes. While not replacing traditional survey methods, the tool provides experimental, complementary insights into societal perceptions. The pilot enhances methodological innovation, expands data sources and supports evidence-based policy discussions while maintaining transparency regarding data limitations and representativeness.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-Powered Speed Measurement – Municipal Police of Prague
source_description: The Municipal Police of Prague operate an automated speed enforcement system to improve road safety and ensure compliance with traffic regulations. The system comprises over 60 devices across the city, including more than 40 section-control installations that calculate average speed between two points using induction loops embedded in the road surface, and around 20 radar-based cameras measuring instantaneous speed. Captured data include vehicle images and licence plate numbers, with automatic number plate recognition applied in designated subsystems. The technology processes speed measurements and generates violation records, producing approximately 300,000 fines annually. While detection and data processing are automated, all sanction decisions are reviewed by a human officer before issuance, ensuring procedural oversight. The system enhances enforcement coverage, increases consistency in speed control and supports deterrence of traffic offences. By combining automated measurement with human validation, Prague strengthens road safety management while maintaining administrative accountability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Algorithm based quality control of presidential candidates
source_description: To ensure compliance with legal requirements for presidential candidacy, Czech authorities apply statistical verification to nomination signatures submitted by candidates. Candidates may qualify either through parliamentary support or by collecting 50,000 voter signatures. In the latter case, the Ministry of Interior conducts a statistical quality control process to verify that signatories are eligible voters. An algorithm randomly selects two batches of 8,500 signatures for detailed validation against population registers. Error rates identified in the samples are extrapolated to estimate the overall validity of submitted signatures. The process resembles statistical quality control methods used in auditing, enabling efficient review of large datasets without checking every entry individually. While the approach accelerates verification and standardises assessment, it has generated debate regarding sampling design and accuracy. In the 2013 election cycle, two candidates were excluded following application of this procedure. The system aims to balance administrative feasibility with electoral integrity safeguards.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Algorithm to detect fraud at the National Tax Authority in Hungary
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Tax administrations face increasing challenges in detecting complex and evolving forms of tax fraud while ensuring compliance with strict data protection and transparency requirements. The Hungarian National Tax Authority (NAV) manages extensive datasets related to declarations, transactions and compliance behaviour, yet traditional analytical approaches limit the ability to uncover hidden patterns at scale. To address this, NAV established a dedicated working group in April 2022 to explore advanced, data-driven approaches to fraud detection within a clearly defined legal and organisational framework. The objective of this use case is to improve the effectiveness of fraud prevention and risk analysis while safeguarding taxpayer rights and data confidentiality. The implementation focuses on developing a semantic data asset methodology that enables structured use of anonymised tax data for advanced analytical research. This includes the design of algorithms for pattern detection, as well as robust validation and testing methodologies to assess reliability and bias. Strong governance mechanisms ensure that data protection rules define the operational boundaries of the work. The expected impact includes improved identification of fraudulent behaviour, more targeted inspections and better allocation of investigative resources. Qualitative outcomes include enhanced analytical capacity, stronger evidence-based decision-making and a scalable methodological foundation for future tax compliance initiatives.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain-enhanced INPS disability card
source_description: People with disabilities often face repeated verification processes when accessing services, while authorities must ensure eligibility, prevent fraud and protect personal data. INPS aimed to strengthen the European Disability Card system. The objective of this use case is to improve reliability, transparency and accessibility of disability certification. The implementation supports the physical card with a secure distributed digital infrastructure that records eligibility attributes and access rights in a tamper-resistant manner. Service providers can verify entitlements quickly without accessing unnecessary personal data. The impact includes reduced fraud risk, faster service access and improved user experience. Qualitative benefits include greater trust, better interoperability across services and improved protection of sensitive information.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain-enabled "building bonus"" credits in Italy"
source_description: Italy’s “110% superbonus” policy generated complex administrative flows for managing construction tax credits, creating risks of fraud and inefficiency. The objective of this proof of concept is to improve transparency and traceability of bonus payments to construction firms. The implementation tokenises building credits on a distributed ledger, enabling secure tracking of issuance, transfer and redemption. The impact includes improved oversight, reduced fraud risk and more efficient credit circulation. Qualitative outcomes include stronger confidence in public incentive schemes and improved administrative control.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Welfare ticket - a blockchian-based platform for the gig economy environment
source_description: Labour platforms and gig workers often operate outside traditional social security frameworks, creating gaps in insurance coverage and administrative complexity for short-term or task-based work. In Italy, a concept known as the “Welfare Ticket” was developed to address these challenges by enabling temporary, portable social security coverage for gig economy workers. Stakeholders included employers, platform workers, and social security institutions, with the objective of simplifying compliance while ensuring that workers remained insured during the execution of specific tasks. The proposed solution centred on a shared digital register where employers could issue a time-bound social security ticket linked to a specific job. The platform design relied on distributed ledger technology to record the issuance, validity period, and redemption of welfare tickets in an immutable and auditable manner. Each transaction would be visible to authorised parties, reducing disputes and administrative reconciliation. Although the concept was developed through an enterprise design thinking process and documented by INPS, it did not progress to operational deployment. Nevertheless, the initiative provided a structured blueprint for how decentralised registers could support more flexible labour markets, influencing later discussions on portable benefits and digital welfare infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain-based virtual large-scale storage for photovoltaics system operators
source_description: As feed-in tariffs are phased out, photovoltaic system operators face declining revenues, while consumers seek affordable green electricity. Traditional energy markets offer limited support for local energy exchange and self-consumption. The BloGPV project addresses this challenge by enabling local trading of solar electricity among neighbours through a virtual storage concept. Stakeholders include PV system operators, electricity consumers, and local energy communities. The objective is to maintain the economic viability of solar installations and strengthen local renewable energy use. The solution creates a distributed virtual storage network that connects producers and consumers, allowing surplus electricity to be traded locally. Automated transaction mechanisms record energy exchanges and settlements within the network, ensuring transparency and reliability. By coordinating production and consumption, the system reduces reliance on centralised grids and supports local balancing. The impact includes improved returns for solar producers, more attractive green electricity for consumers, and increased local self-sufficiency. BloGPV contributes to decentralised energy systems and offers a replicable model for community-based renewable energy trading.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Norway’s central register and Norway's tax authority
title: Norway steps into the metaverse with decentraland tax office
source_description: Public administrations increasingly seek new ways to reach citizens and businesses, particularly younger and digitally native audiences, while improving accessibility to information and services. In Norway, authorities identified emerging digital environments as potential new channels for public engagement. The objective of this use case is to explore whether immersive virtual spaces can complement traditional service channels for providing tax-related information and guidance. The implementation involves establishing a virtual tax office within Decentraland, a decentralised digital platform, through a partnership between Brønnøysund Register Centre, the national tax authority Skatteetaten and external advisors. The virtual office replicates elements of a physical service point, allowing users to access information, attend events and interact with guidance resources in a three-dimensional environment. The pilot focuses on experimentation, user experience and organisational learning rather than transactional services. Expected impacts include insights into citizen engagement in virtual environments, expanded outreach to new user groups and lessons on integrating public services into emerging digital ecosystems. Qualitative benefits include increased visibility of public institutions, innovation capacity building and evidence to inform future digital service strategies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: The City of Helsinki is investigating the benefits of generative artificial intelligence in various work tasks
source_description: Municipal administrations face increasing pressure to deliver high-quality services while managing growing volumes of documents, correspondence and internal coordination tasks. In the City of Helsinki, employees across departments spend significant time on routine knowledge work, limiting their capacity for strategic analysis, collaboration and citizen-facing activities. The objective of this use case is to assess how everyday work processes can be streamlined and supported in a controlled and responsible manner, while maintaining public sector values such as reliability, transparency and staff wellbeing. The implementation consists of a structured experimentation phase within the existing Microsoft 365 work environment, where selected employees test integrated digital assistance functions. These include support for drafting and reviewing documents, summarising lengthy materials, managing email overload and organising information across files and meetings. Usage is monitored to understand task suitability, workflow integration and organisational implications rather than to automate decisions. The expected impact includes reduced administrative workload, time savings in routine tasks and improved consistency in document handling. Qualitative results focus on improved employee experience, better focus on high-value work and evidence-based insights to guide future adoption decisions, ensuring that productivity gains align with ethical, organisational and operational requirements.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (ADM)
title: Traceability Platform for Alcoholic Production Certification
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Producers of high-quality regional spirits face increasing regulatory and market demands for traceability, authenticity, and proof of origin. Certification processes are often fragmented across authorities and perceived as administrative burdens rather than value drivers. This project addresses the need to transform certification into a strategic asset for “Made in Italy” products, starting with Genepì del Piemonte. Stakeholders include producers, certification bodies, public administrations, and consumers. The objective is to ensure transparent tracking of production batches while enhancing product value and consumer trust. The solution implements a platform-based certification system that records production and certification data across the supply chain. Information is securely shared among authorised administrations, creating a one-stop framework for compliance and verification. Batch-level traceability enables producers to demonstrate authenticity and quality to markets and regulators. The impact includes reduced administrative complexity, improved transparency, and stronger brand protection for regional products. The initiative supports innovation in agri-food certification and provides a scalable model for traceability across other protected productions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BLOCKCERTS: Blockchain-based university degrees at Bicocca and Padua University in Italy
source_description: The University of Milan Bicocca, in collaboration with the Cineca inter-university consortium, implemented a blockchain-based certification system to safeguard the authenticity of academic degrees and official documents. Universities face risks of document falsification and administrative burdens in responding to verification requests from employers. The solution issues certified digital diplomas anchored to a blockchain infrastructure, ensuring immutability and verifiable integrity. Cryptographic hashes of degree documents are recorded on the distributed ledger, allowing third parties to validate authenticity without accessing personal data or contacting the issuing institution. The system is based on open standards for blockchain certification, enabling secure, tamper-evident verification through a simple digital check. By digitising credential validation, the initiative reduces administrative workload, accelerates employer verification processes and strengthens trust in academic qualifications. The approach enhances transparency and international portability of degrees while preserving data protection safeguards.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: App ACI Space - blockchain-based notarisation
source_description: The Automobile Club of Italy (ACI), in cooperation with EY, developed the ACI Space application to enable digital certification of vehicle data and lifecycle records. Vehicle ownership history and documentation verification traditionally require manual administrative checks. The app allows users to enter a vehicle registration number and access certified information recorded on a private blockchain platform integrated with Ethereum technology. Cryptographic notarisation ensures that stored records cannot be altered retroactively, providing tamper-evident documentation of key vehicle events. Smart contract components manage validation processes and secure data anchoring. The application enhances transparency in used-car transactions by enabling buyers, sellers and businesses to verify vehicle history quickly through a smartphone interface. By digitising notarisation processes, ACI improves data integrity, reduces fraud risks and streamlines administrative procedures related to vehicle documentation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: "LLMoin"" pilot project to provide insight into Hamburg's medium-term LLM strategy"
source_description: Public administrations face growing demands for efficiency in text-heavy tasks such as summarising documents, drafting responses and conducting research. Hamburg’s local government launched the LLMoin pilot to explore how large language models could support administrative work while meeting strict data protection and organisational requirements. Around 100 employees across departments participate, with the objective of assessing acceptance, usefulness and governance needs. The pilot uses the Luminous language model developed and hosted in Germany by startup Aleph Alpha, with a custom front-end and data processing layer built specifically for Hamburg. The system supports tasks such as text summarisation, drafting and information retrieval, operating within controlled environments. Outputs are reviewed by users, ensuring human responsibility for decisions. Early results show productivity gains for participating staff and valuable insights into training needs, technical integration and ethical considerations. The pilot informs Hamburg’s medium-term strategy for language technologies in government, highlighting both efficiency potential and the importance of sovereign, transparent deployment models in the public sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Dublin City Council accelerates the potential of drones across Ireland
source_description: Local authorities increasingly recognise the potential of unmanned aerial vehicles to support public services, yet fragmented regulation, limited operational experience and lack of shared standards have slowed adoption. Dublin City Council (DCC), through its Smart Dublin programme, launched a coordinated initiative to explore how drones could be safely and effectively used across Ireland for civil defence, emergency response, public safety and environmental monitoring. Stakeholders include local and national government agencies, emergency services, regulators and technology providers. The objective is to build institutional knowledge, test real-world applications and inform policymaking through evidence rather than isolated trials. The programme establishes a cross-agency network to identify priority use cases, assess operational constraints and share best practices observed internationally. Drone deployments are tested in controlled pilots, integrating aerial data collection with existing emergency management and environmental monitoring systems. Outputs include geospatial imagery, situational awareness data and operational insights rather than standalone services. The initiative has accelerated learning across the public sector, reduced duplication of effort and positioned Ireland to adopt drones more strategically. Its impact lies in improved readiness for emergency scenarios, more efficient data collection and a clearer regulatory and governance framework for scaling drone use nationwide.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-powered “Gestore Emendamenti” (GEM) at the Italian Senate
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: The Italian Senate introduced the “Gestore Emendamenti” (GEM) system to manage large volumes of legislative amendments more efficiently. Parliamentary debates often involve numerous amendments with similar wording, creating administrative complexity in scheduling votes. GEM applies text clustering algorithms to group amendments based on semantic similarity, enabling simultaneous discussion and voting where appropriate. Natural language processing techniques analyse amendment text and generate clusters within seconds. Parliamentary staff review, adjust and validate the machine-generated groupings before integration into the legislative workflow, ensuring that final procedural decisions remain under human control. The system reduces manual sorting effort, accelerates legislative processing and enhances organisational efficiency during plenary sessions. By combining automated text analysis with expert oversight, GEM supports transparent and accountable parliamentary procedures while maintaining institutional authority over decision-making.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV)
title: Artificial Intelligence and Mobility - AIAMO
source_description: Fragmented mobility data and limited interoperability between transport services hinder environmentally oriented and multimodal traffic management across cities and regions. The AIAMO project seeks to strengthen data sovereignty in transport by networking mobility services and simplifying access to high-quality data for innovative applications. Coordinated by ITS Germany, the initiative establishes a networked integration zone where mobility data from different providers can be securely shared and processed. Trusted data infrastructures and interoperable interfaces enable the development of advanced analytics and decision-support applications, facilitating research results and market-ready services. The platform supports small and medium-sized enterprises by lowering barriers to entry and enabling scalable deployment of digital mobility solutions. By improving data availability and integration, the project enhances traffic management, supports multimodal planning and fosters innovation ecosystems across cities. The initiative also promotes European cooperation through outreach to national ITS organisations, strengthening cross-border interoperability and sustainable mobility development.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: University of Applied Sciences Energy Technology Center (TZE)
title: Open Mobility Electrical Infrastructure - OMEI
source_description: The expansion of electromobility requires coordinated planning of charging infrastructure, integration of renewable energy, and efficient management of energy flows across regions. Fragmented data and incompatible systems currently limit optimisation of charging networks and energy use. This use case addresses these challenges by developing an open data and service framework to support planning, operation, and optimisation of fast and bidirectional charging infrastructure across Europe. The project involves public authorities, infrastructure operators, energy providers, and mobility stakeholders, with the objective of enabling a decarbonised and economically viable energy supply for electric mobility. The solution is implemented through a digital platform that collects and integrates charging, user, energy, and traffic data from demonstration sites, including fast-charging stations with hybrid energy storage and bidirectional charging capabilities. Advanced analytics and simulation models are used to optimise operating strategies, economic performance, and vehicle-to-home and vehicle-to-grid concepts, while distributed ledger technology is examined for secure and transparent energy trading and billing. The project supports improved infrastructure planning, better utilisation of renewable energy, and scalable data sharing across borders. It contributes to reduced emissions, more efficient charging operations, and a robust foundation for future European mobility and energy data spaces.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: acatech - German Academy of Engineering Sciences
title: National Initiative for AI-based Transformation in the Data Economy - NITD
source_description: Germany seeks to strengthen its position in the European data economy by improving interoperability, governance and trust in data-driven innovation. Fragmented data ecosystems and inconsistent standards can hinder cross-sector collaboration and scalable digital services. Stakeholders include federal ministries, industry partners, research institutions and public interest organisations. The objective is to create technical, organisational and funding foundations that enable marketable and socially beneficial data-driven applications. The initiative develops interoperable data spaces, harmonised quality and testing standards, and a quality and innovation centre to validate and certify applications. It also designs funding mechanisms that complement existing innovation schemes and accelerate implementation. Technical components include shared architectures for secure data exchange, governance frameworks and evaluation methodologies for compliance and performance. Anticipated impacts include improved data sharing across sectors, enhanced trust through transparent standards, accelerated innovation uptake and strengthened competitiveness of European digital ecosystems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, Authority for Transport and Mobility Transition (FHH)
title: Automation of Hamburg's on-demand offering with integration into public transport - AHOI project
source_description: Urban mobility providers face operational and regulatory challenges when integrating on-demand transport services and emerging autonomous vehicle technologies into existing public transport systems. The AHOI project in Hamburg aims to analyse, design and implement operational concepts for a mixed fleet of manually driven and autonomous vehicles within an on-demand service model. A dedicated control centre is developed to coordinate fleet management, dispatching and data integration, ensuring accessibility across the entire travel chain. The project progresses through three phases: operation of a manually driven on-demand fleet with passengers; testing integration of autonomous vehicles under technical supervision without passengers; and deployment of a mixed fleet with passengers and integrated data ecosystems. Advanced fleet management algorithms and data analytics support routing, demand forecasting and system optimisation. The initiative evaluates user behaviour, accessibility impacts and regulatory implications, generating evidence for large-scale deployment. Expected outcomes include improved service efficiency, enhanced user experience and a scalable framework for integrating automated mobility into public transport networks.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Establishment of a U-Space real laboratory in Hamburg - U-Space real laboratory
source_description: The increasing use of drones for commercial and public services requires their safe and equitable integration into controlled airspace alongside traditional aviation. To support implementation of the European U-space regulatory framework, Hamburg established a real-world laboratory to test operational, technical and procedural arrangements for unmanned aircraft systems. The project brought together aviation authorities, drone operators, air navigation service providers and technology developers to simulate and demonstrate coordinated airspace management in a controlled environment. Digital traffic management systems, communication interfaces and identification services were deployed to enable real-time data exchange between airspace users and supervisory entities. Operational scenarios tested flight authorisation, tracking, conflict detection and emergency procedures under realistic conditions. The laboratory also enabled participation of third parties, fostering interoperability and stakeholder collaboration. The initiative demonstrated practical pathways for compliant drone integration, reduced regulatory uncertainty and provided a replicable model for other German and European regions. It strengthens safety, transparency and scalability in the emerging low-altitude drone ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Trustworthiness platform for AI solutions and data rooms - TrustKI
source_description: Manufacturing companies increasingly rely on data-driven solutions and shared data spaces, yet potential users often lack transparent criteria to assess organisational reliability and the robustness of digital solutions. The TrustKI project aims to establish a platform that enables structured evaluation and documentation of trustworthiness in manufacturing organisations, their data rooms and related digital applications. The platform develops a trust index and reputation system based on defined assessment criteria, incorporating technical, organisational and governance indicators agreed upon with industry stakeholders. Companies can document compliance, security standards and quality assurance measures within a cooperative, sector-specific framework. Data are aggregated into a transparent scoring mechanism accessible to users and partners, facilitating informed decisions. By providing a structured and comparable basis for evaluating digital offerings, the initiative reduces uncertainty, promotes responsible deployment of advanced technologies and supports broader adoption of trusted industrial data ecosystems. It enhances transparency, strengthens collaboration and contributes to a competitive and reliable digital manufacturing landscape.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Alpine mobility data room Inntal - ALMODA
source_description: Mountain regions face complex mobility challenges due to terrain, weather variability, cross-border traffic, and safety requirements. Local communities in the Alpine Inntal region require accurate, real-time information to support safe, efficient, and sustainable mobility. This use case addresses these needs by establishing a cross-border data space that supports real-time communication, navigation, and surveillance services for mobility users and authorities. The project involves regional administrations, mobility service providers, and infrastructure operators, with the objective of enabling Mobility 4.0 through a shared and trusted digital situation picture. The solution is implemented through a multimodal data platform that aggregates high-precision digital elevation models, static and dynamic geographic protection zones, navigation and communication data, and high-resolution local weather information. Data is authenticated, validated, and combined using advanced analytical methods to create real-time situational awareness, which is then distributed securely to users and systems across borders. The platform supports multiple mobility use cases tailored to local needs, including safety, routing, and traffic management. The project improves reliability and safety of mobility in complex Alpine environments, enhances cross-border coordination, and enables scalable data-driven services. It delivers clear value by supporting informed decision-making, reducing risk, and laying the groundwork for integrated, resilient mobility services in sensitive regions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Fraunhofer Institute for Material Flow and Logistics IML
title: Digital test field Air Cargo - DTAC
source_description: Air freight transport involves numerous actors, including airlines, freight forwarders, ground handlers and customs authorities, whose fragmented information systems limit efficiency and transparency across the logistics chain. The Digital Test Field Air Cargo (DTAC) aims to enhance performance by increasing networking and digitalisation of air cargo processes in a neutral, cross-site environment. Stakeholders collaborate to improve data exchange standards and interoperability across the transport chain. The project develops shared digital platforms and interfaces to enable real-time information flow, while testing automation of dispatching, handling and transport operations. Advanced analytics and predictive models are applied to optimise capacity utilisation, forecast demand and streamline workflows. Solutions are piloted under operational conditions to validate scalability and integration with existing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include reduced processing times, improved coordination among actors and more reliable cargo flows. The initiative strengthens competitiveness of the air freight sector by enabling data-driven optimisation, increased transparency and higher overall system efficiency.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Kombiverkehr German Society for Combined Freight Transport mbH & Co. KG
title: AI and discrete loading optimization models to increase utilization in KV - KiBa
source_description: Combined transport terminals must assign loading units to wagon sets efficiently, yet placement decisions often need to be made before complete information on incoming shipments is available. This creates operational uncertainty and can reduce utilisation of rail capacity. The KiBa project addresses this assignment problem by developing IT-based optimisation methods that generate rapid and efficient loading proposals under dynamic conditions. Discrete mathematical optimisation models are combined with machine learning techniques to calculate optimal placement of loading units on available wagons, considering route, weight and temporal constraints. The system processes partial and evolving data, updating recommendations as new information becomes available. By integrating predictive algorithms into terminal management systems, the solution supports near real-time decision-making. The approach improves wagon utilisation, reduces empty capacity and enhances planning reliability in combined transport operations. It contributes to more efficient rail logistics, lower operational costs and increased competitiveness of intermodal freight transport.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Networked LiDAR bus for safe autonomous use in shared spaces - LiDARshared
source_description: Urban authorities require detailed and up-to-date traffic data to manage complex shared spaces safely, particularly in dense city centres where interactions between vehicles, cyclists and pedestrians are frequent. The LiDARshared project equips public buses with high-performance LiDAR sensors to collect comprehensive three-dimensional traffic data during regular operations. In cooperation with stakeholders in Kiel, sensor-equipped buses capture detailed information on traffic flows, road geometry and movement patterns along main arteries and busy intersections. The collected data are processed using advanced spatial analytics to identify congestion points, risk zones and behavioural patterns. Results can inform adjustments to traffic light phases, speed limits, one-way regulations and targeted safety interventions for vulnerable road users. By leveraging existing public transport fleets as mobile sensing platforms, the project enables cost-efficient, large-scale data acquisition. The initiative supports smarter traffic management, enhances road safety and provides a scalable data foundation for future autonomous mobility applications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Erfurt University of Applied Sciences, Faculty of Economics, Logistics, Transport
title: Feasibility study for the harmonisation of truck parking space occupancy through networked model-predictive control systems based on V2X technologies - PAHA
source_description: Overcrowding at truck rest areas along heavily used federal highways leads to safety risks, inefficient parking searches and uneven utilisation of available capacity. Despite infrastructure investments, demand peaks in the evening and at night continue to strain facilities. The PAHA project examined how predictive and networked control systems could harmonise occupancy across rest areas. Based on reference scenarios and interface analyses, a forecasting model was developed to predict time- and location-specific occupancy rates using available traffic and infrastructure data. Model-predictive control approaches generate recommendations for optimal rest areas tailored to individual vehicles, incorporating static and dynamic variables such as current occupancy and travel time. The concept integrates Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication to transmit guidance directly to drivers. Requirements for upgrading existing large-scale occupancy detection systems were identified to enable integration of forecasting and control functions. The approach promises improved utilisation of parking capacity, reduced congestion and enhanced safety and efficiency in long-distance freight transport.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smart Urban Logistics through Electrification Collaboration and Automation - SULEICA
source_description: Urban freight transport contributes to congestion, emissions and reduced quality of life, prompting cities to seek cleaner and more efficient logistics models. The SULEICA project aimed to design, implement and validate an emission-free and traffic-reducing urban logistics concept that integrates electrification and automation while actively involving citizens. Pilot operations were conducted using partially automated, electrically powered logistics vehicles capable of communicating and interacting with pedestrians and other road users. A key outcome was the development and road approval of the modular “Ducktrain” vehicle, designed for flexible goods transport in urban areas. The system was integrated into existing transport infrastructure, and operational data were analysed to refine vehicle design and coordination mechanisms. Acceptance studies assessed public perception and identified factors influencing user confidence, such as train length and infrastructure use. The project demonstrated potential improvements in traffic flow and ecological performance for logistics operators. Results include a roadmap for future vehicle registration under increasing automation levels and a foundation for scaling emission-free, cooperative urban logistics solutions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: State of Berlin, represented by the Senate Department for the Environment, Transport and Climate Protection
title: Autonomous shuttles & Co in the digital test field for city traffic - Shuttles &Co
source_description: Urban authorities face challenges in integrating highly automated vehicles into complex city traffic while ensuring safety, interoperability and public acceptance. The Shuttles &Co project established a digital test field in Berlin to trial automated fleet vehicles under real traffic conditions and evaluate requirements for future regular operation. Tests revealed technological limits but generated valuable operational insights, particularly regarding perception, localisation and prediction in dense environments. Cooperative methods based on Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication enabled data exchange between vehicles and infrastructure, improving situational awareness and road safety. Enhanced traffic control and information services were demonstrated to public stakeholders, supported by newly integrated data and exchange platforms. The project also advanced automated recognition and updating of map objects, contributing to the self-updating digital map managed by the Berlin administration. Outcomes include improved cooperative traffic management methods, strengthened data interoperability and practical knowledge to support safe deployment of automated fleets in urban environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI and M2M -based optimization of safety and comfort for people with mobility restrictions in non-motorized individual transport in the ERFURTS location
source_description: People with mobility restrictions often encounter safety risks and accessibility barriers at signalised intersections and public transport stops, particularly where pedestrian flows intersect with motorised traffic. The project aimed to enhance safety and comfort for vulnerable road users by improving infrastructure responsiveness and information exchange. Sensor systems and machine-to-machine communication technologies were deployed to automatically detect individuals requiring assistance at traffic light-controlled junctions and transition points to public transport. Intelligent control mechanisms dynamically adjusted traffic signal phases and transmitted relevant information to approaching vehicles and public transport operators. Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) interfaces were designed to enable future communication with automated vehicles. Data-driven algorithms supported real-time decision-making while respecting privacy requirements. The initiative contributes to inclusive mobility by reducing conflict situations and waiting times, improving perceived safety and facilitating smoother transfers between transport modes. It advances the development of a connected and automated transport ecosystem that better accommodates diverse user needs.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smart control center for automated transport robots and buses in the city of Lauenburg/Elbe - TaBuLa-LOGplus
source_description: Integrating passenger and goods transport through automated systems requires coordinated fleet management and reliable operational oversight. The TaBuLa-LOGplus project aimed to implement a prototypical control centre to enable efficient combined transport services in Lauenburg/Elbe. Building on previous test tracks and self-developed transport robots, the project connected autonomous logistics units with a conventional scheduled bus service. The control centre used advanced coordination algorithms to optimise routing, scheduling and resource allocation across passenger and freight flows. Increased automation levels in the transport robots were achieved through technical enhancements in navigation and system integration. Real-time data exchange enabled synchronisation between vehicles and infrastructure, supporting seamless multimodal operations. The demonstrator showed how centralised supervision can improve utilisation rates and operational reliability. The project provides a blueprint for scalable urban and regional mobility systems that integrate automated freight and passenger services, enhancing efficiency and sustainability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Shuttle model region Upper Franconia II - SMO-II
source_description: Public transport providers in rural and semi-rural regions face growing pressure to offer flexible, reliable, and cost-efficient mobility services despite low passenger density and challenging operating conditions. In Upper Franconia, authorities and operators sought to modernise shuttle services by reducing dependence on onboard staff, improving passenger assistance, and enabling safe operation even in difficult weather, while complying with national regulations on autonomous driving. This use case focuses on the SMO-II project, involving regional transport authorities, operators, and control centres, with the objective of holistically automating the mobility chain and enabling demand-responsive shuttle services. The solution is implemented through a highly automated transport system that integrates vehicle automation, sensor technology, passenger assistance systems, and remote operations. Shuttles are designed to operate at Level 4 autonomy in defined environments, with real-time monitoring and manoeuvre release managed from an existing control centre. Digital systems cover vehicle interiors, door areas, and passenger support functions, while advanced perception and control technologies enable safe operation without accompanying personnel. The project improves operational efficiency by reducing staffing requirements, increases service availability through on-demand operation, and enhances safety and reliability under varied conditions. It supports scalable deployment of autonomous shuttles in non-urban regions and contributes to more inclusive, sustainable public transport offerings.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: State of Berlin, represented by the Senate Department for the Environment, Mobility, Consumer and Climate Protection
title: AI-based system for connected mobility - KIS'M
source_description: Rapidly growing residential areas in Berlin require affordable and reliable public transport solutions capable of operating safely in mixed traffic environments. The KIS'M project explores driverless on-demand transport integrated into the existing public transport network, aiming to develop robust processes for technical supervision at virtual stops and within vehicles. Automated vehicles are networked with traffic management systems to enhance coordination and safety. Data collected from operations are analysed to generate updated map and traffic information, improving navigation accuracy and situational awareness. Cooperative communication interfaces enable interaction between vehicles and infrastructure, supporting realistic autonomous driving manoeuvres in mixed traffic. The project also evaluates governance, safety and operational frameworks necessary for large-scale deployment. Results will inform a strategic roadmap for introducing driverless vehicles in Berlin. Expected benefits include improved service reliability, enhanced traffic safety and scalable integration of automated mobility into urban public transport systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI -supported data analysis and simulation of rescue services - AI-Rescue
source_description: Rescue services in Germany operate within heterogeneous organisational structures and varying levels of digitalisation, limiting data-driven optimisation of emergency response. The AI-Rescue feasibility study aimed to develop a simulation demonstrator to assess how advanced analytics could support operational decision-making. Real operational data on mission frequency, duration and spatial distribution were collected and used to parameterise a spatially referenced simulation model. The model replicated dispatch and resource allocation decisions using adaptive algorithmic strategies to test alternative deployment scenarios. By modelling dynamic and static influencing factors within the rescue chain, the system enabled evaluation of response times and resource utilisation under different conditions. The approach provides a foundation for evidence-based planning, allowing authorities to identify bottlenecks and optimise station locations or staffing patterns. Anticipated impacts include improved response efficiency, better allocation of emergency resources and strengthened resilience of rescue services through data-driven scenario analysis.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Weather-independent and highly automated ridesharing service in Kelheim (Germany)
source_description: Rural and semi-urban districts such as Kelheim face challenges in providing reliable and affordable public transport, particularly under adverse weather conditions that affect automated vehicle performance. The KelRide project aims to establish a highly automated ride-sharing service integrated into public transport, operating with a mixed fleet of automated and conventional shuttles. A central objective is to develop a robust overall system capable of maintaining reliable operation in rain, snow and other challenging weather scenarios. Sensor fusion techniques, enhanced perception algorithms and resilient control systems are implemented to ensure safe navigation year-round. The service model combines demand-responsive routing with integration into existing transport networks, supported by digital booking and fleet management platforms. Operational trials will assess technical reliability, user acceptance and system efficiency. The project seeks to provide a transferable blueprint for other municipalities, demonstrating scalable, weather-resilient automated mobility services that enhance accessibility and sustainability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Adaptive maps and AI -based infrastructure monitoring - AK-KII
source_description: Highly automated mobility depends on precise and continuously updated digital maps reflecting the condition of road infrastructure. Vehicles can only operate safely and efficiently if they have reliable, location-specific information about road geometry, surface condition and structural integrity. The AK-KII preliminary study aimed to establish an interdisciplinary consortium to advance infrastructure monitoring methods capable of updating high-definition maps in near real time. The project analysed the state of the art in sensor technologies, including camera, radar and LiDAR systems, to determine how infrastructure condition data can be captured and processed. Approaches to sensor data fusion were examined to combine heterogeneous data sources across different road types, with particular attention to bridge condition monitoring and automated documentation of algorithmic decision processes. Evaluation criteria for data relevance and quality were defined to support scalable deployment. The study lays the groundwork for integrating automated infrastructure assessment into adaptive map layers, improving reliability of automated driving systems, enabling faster reflection of infrastructure changes and supporting safer, more sustainable mobility.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI -based cross-type mobility optimization in non-urban regions - KIMoNo
source_description: Regions at the interface between urban and rural areas often suffer from fragmented mobility systems, inefficient logistics, and limited transport alternatives, leading to higher emissions and reduced accessibility. In the Passau district, stakeholders sought to better understand and optimise mobility patterns across different transport modes, taking into account the specific needs of rural populations. This use case addresses these challenges by developing cross-type mobility optimisation strategies that improve sustainability and performance in non-urban regions, involving local authorities, residents, logistics providers, and researchers. The objective is to design mobility solutions that are technically viable, socially accepted, and tailored to local demand. The project is implemented through data-driven analysis of mobility flows across logistics and individual transport, supported by advanced modelling and optimisation techniques. Decentralised infrastructure concepts are evaluated, and digital solutions are developed to coordinate different modes more efficiently. The initiative also establishes the necessary technological infrastructure and actively engages citizens through targeted science communication, public events, and interactive exhibitions to assess acceptance and usability. The project supports more efficient and sustainable mobility patterns, improves alignment between infrastructure and real demand, and strengthens public acceptance of new mobility services, creating long-term value for regional transport planning.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Artificial intelligence in Ingolstadt's transport system - KIVI
source_description: Modern transport systems often lack a complete and up-to-date view of all road users, particularly pedestrians and cyclists, which makes it harder to optimise traffic control and improve safety in mixed urban environments. In Ingolstadt, the KIVI project was developed to address this problem by building a more comprehensive, multimodal picture of traffic conditions across selected network nodes and using that information to support smarter control and warning functions. The objective is to improve traffic efficiency and safety by recognising all relevant road users, forecasting network conditions, and adapting traffic measures more precisely to real demand. The implementation combines local high-definition stationary sensors with mobile sensors from cars, buses, bicycles, and pedestrians equipped with 5G-enabled devices, and fuses these data using data-driven methods into a current digital representation of the traffic situation. At a conceptual level, the system supports network-wide multimodal forecasting, demand-based green-time allocation for different road users, a traffic-light phase assistant, and warning functions that recognise behaviour and intent and provide visual or acoustic alerts in dangerous situations. The impact includes better situational awareness, more balanced traffic control, and stronger protection for vulnerable road users. It also supports smarter urban mobility management by improving scalability, responsiveness, and the quality of data available for operational traffic decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Fraunhofer Institute for Material Flow and Logistics IML, Dortmund
title: Silicon Economy Logistics Ecosystem - SELE
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: Fragmented digital systems and limited interoperability hinder efficiency and innovation in logistics and supply chain management. The SELE project sought to establish an open-source infrastructure and shared technical components to support a platform-based logistics ecosystem. The objective was to facilitate cross-company collaboration, digitisation and automation of supply chain processes through interoperable digital services. The initiative developed modular software components and open standards that enable secure data exchange and integration across logistics actors. Advanced analytics and intelligent optimisation algorithms were implemented to enhance planning, coordination and resource allocation, while new communication technologies were integrated to strengthen connectivity across platforms. The ecosystem approach promotes reusable services and common digital building blocks, enabling companies to develop and deploy innovative applications more rapidly. By improving interoperability and reducing duplication of effort, the project enhances operational efficiency, transparency and resilience within supply chains. It supports scalable digital transformation of the logistics sector and contributes to more sustainable and competitive transport systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Institute of Shipping Economics and Logistics (ISL)
title: Intelligent information technologies for process optimization and automation in inland ports - Binntelligent
source_description: Inland waterways offer underutilised capacity for freight transport, yet coordination gaps within multimodal logistics chains limit the performance of inland ports. The Binntelligent project aimed to strengthen inland port operations by improving data-driven coordination among transport stakeholders. Intelligent information technologies were designed and tested to collect, process and share decision-relevant data across shipping companies, port operators and logistics providers. Real-world operational data were used to develop predictive models for arrival times, handling processes and resource allocation. Data integration mechanisms enabled improved forecasting of transport flows and alignment with road and rail networks. The system supports adaptive planning and real-time optimisation of port processes, enhancing transparency and collaboration. By increasing predictability and reducing idle times, the solution improves utilisation of inland waterway capacity and strengthens integration within the broader freight transport system. The project contributes to more efficient, reliable and sustainable multimodal logistics operations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Autonomously working machines in road construction 4.0 - ROBOT road construction 4.0
source_description: Road construction projects often face labour shortages, safety risks and inconsistent quality control during asphalt paving. The ROBOT road construction 4.0 project aimed to enable construction machines to operate autonomously and in a networked manner, reducing reliance on additional operating personnel while ensuring continuous quality assurance. A detailed 3D digital model of the road served as the basis for automated paving operations. Modern sensor systems and connected IT architectures were integrated into machinery to enable precise positioning, material control and real-time monitoring of paving parameters. Data-driven control systems continuously compared execution with design specifications to maintain consistent quality. Networked coordination between machines improved workflow synchronisation and reduced operational interruptions. The approach enhances occupational safety by limiting manual intervention, improves asphalt durability through precise application and minimises traffic disruption during works. The project demonstrates how automation and digital modelling can increase efficiency, quality and safety in infrastructure construction.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smartmail - intelligent handling of mails
source_description: Municipal administrations handle large volumes of physical and digital correspondence, and inefficient mail distribution and journaling processes can lead to delays, lack of transparency, and increased administrative costs. In Norddjurs Municipality, improving internal mail handling was identified as a way to accelerate case processing for citizens while ensuring accountability within municipal workflows.
