This use case addresses these challenges by optimising postal and journaling processes across municipalities, involving administrative staff, caseworkers, and citizens, with the objective of reducing processing times and improving transparency. The solution is implemented through an intelligent mail-handling system that automatically classifies incoming letters and emails, identifies the correct recipient or department, and journals documents immediately within municipal case management systems. The system integrates with existing digital infrastructure and supports both physical and electronic correspondence. Following successful implementation, the solution was scaled to ten municipalities. The approach significantly reduces manual handling, shortens case processing times, and lowers the risk of misrouting or delays. It improves transparency by ensuring timely registration of correspondence and delivers clear efficiency gains for municipalities, while enhancing service quality and responsiveness for citizens.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Decision support for handling municipal document access cases
source_description: Municipalities face increasing demand for access to public documents, requiring significant administrative effort to review, redact, and process requests in compliance with legal requirements such as data protection regulations. Manual handling of these cases is time-consuming and may lead to inconsistencies. The objective is to improve efficiency, quality, and consistency in processing document access requests. The solution uses natural language processing models to analyse large volumes of text, identify relevant documents, and detect information that requires anonymisation. These models support case handlers by automating parts of the review process and enabling more efficient file searches. The system is designed to integrate with existing administrative workflows and ensure compliance with data protection requirements. As a pilot project in Sønderborg Municipality, it demonstrates potential to reduce processing time and administrative burden while improving service quality.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: GovTech Midtjylland, Favrskov, Syddjurs and Aarhus Municipality
title: Optimised building use with artificial intelligence
source_description: Many municipal primary schools are ageing buildings with high energy consumption and low space utilisation outside teaching hours, creating inefficiencies and avoidable CO₂ emissions. The project aimed to optimise room allocation and building use to reduce energy demand while maintaining service quality. Building data and Internet of Things sensors were used to monitor occupancy patterns and environmental conditions. Intelligent algorithms analysed usage data to recommend consolidation of activities into fewer rooms during low-demand periods, such as afternoons and weekends. The solution was based on existing technology platforms and datasets from the “Smarte Kvadratmeter” initiative and developed as open source to facilitate wider adoption. Recommendations generated by the system supported targeted heating, lighting and maintenance strategies. The approach enables municipalities to lower operational costs, reduce emissions and improve utilisation of public assets. By providing actionable insights for facility management, the project supports scalable and data-driven optimisation of public building portfolios.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: An effective and holistic employment effort through the artificial intelligence technology Process Mining
source_description: The use case addresses inefficiencies and fragmentation in public employment services, where multiple stakeholders—including job centres, administrative units, and case workers—operate across disconnected systems, limiting coordinated and citizen-centric support. The objective is to enable a more flexible and holistic employment pathway by improving transparency, identifying bottlenecks, and supporting informed decision-making across organisational boundaries. The solution applies process mining and predictive monitoring techniques to existing log data from case management and financial systems, reconstructing end-to-end citizen journeys and mapping workflows, actors, and interventions. Machine learning models analyse historical data to identify patterns in successful outcomes and predict the most effective interventions for different citizen groups, with integration into existing IT systems for continuous analysis and visualisation. The impact includes enhanced process transparency, improved coordination, and more targeted interventions, leading to increased efficiency and better employment outcomes. Additional benefits include reduced administrative burden, improved scalability, and more consistent, data-driven decision-making.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Aalborg Municipality, Syddjurs Municipality, Aalborg University
title: Increased continuity in elderly care using artificial intelligence
source_description: Elderly citizens often experience fragmented home care services involving multiple caregivers, which can reduce perceived safety and continuity of care. The project aimed to enhance transparency and improve the citizen experience by increasing continuity in the staff assigned to each individual. Building on the existing Greenforce planning solution, the system was adapted to incorporate additional parameters such as actual time spent per visit and limits on the number of different caregivers assigned. Algorithmic optimisation generated visit schedules balancing continuity, working hours and operational constraints. A feedback loop enabled continuous retraining based on user input and operational outcomes. The solution was implemented in Aalborg and Syddjurs municipalities, allowing comparison across organisational structures and urban–rural contexts. Results indicate improved planning transparency, more consistent caregiver assignments and potential reductions in travel time between visits. The initiative strengthens quality of care, supports greener routing and provides a scalable model for data-driven workforce planning in elderly services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Artificial intelligence to support the visitation of rehabilitation courses (AIR Project)
source_description: Municipal case workers in Denmark faced increasing pressure to assess citizens’ suitability for rehabilitation programmes consistently and efficiently. The AIR pilot in Aalborg aimed to support decision-making while maintaining professional judgement. Stakeholders included municipalities, case workers, healthcare providers, and citizens.Between 2018 and 2021, statistical and predictive models analysed historical rehabilitation data to estimate eligibility, risk of dropout, and expected outcomes. Outputs were presented as decision support within existing case management systems. The pilot improved consistency and efficiency in assessments, supported better allocation of rehabilitation resources, and freed staff time, while keeping humans in control of final decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Aarhus University Hospital, Aarhus Municipality,MedTech Innovation Consortium,Regional Hospital Horsens and Skanderborg Municipality
title: Artificial intelligence for the prevention of malnutrition and hospitalization of the elderly
source_description: Malnutrition among older citizens is a major risk factor for prolonged hospital stays, readmissions and increased mortality, yet early identification in community settings remains challenging. The project aimed to prevent emergency hospitalisations by identifying individuals at risk of malnutrition so that timely interventions could be initiated. Health and care data were analysed using predictive modelling techniques to detect patterns associated with nutritional risk. Risk scores were generated to support care professionals in prioritising preventive measures, such as dietary support or follow-up assessments. The system was designed to integrate with existing municipal health records, ensuring that insights could inform routine care processes. By enabling earlier intervention, the solution seeks to improve treatment outcomes, enhance self-reliance and increase quality of life for elderly citizens. Anticipated impacts include reduced hospital admissions, lower long-term care costs and more proactive, data-driven management of elderly health services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: CAMES Rigshospitalet, DTU Compute, Region Zealand, Southern Denmark and North Jutland
title: Better diagnostics of pregnant women using artificial intelligence
source_description: Early identification of complications during pregnancy is essential to initiate preventive measures and improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. However, variability in ultrasound image quality can affect diagnostic accuracy and limit the ability to predict adverse developments. This project aimed to enhance the quality and consistency of prenatal ultrasound examinations by supporting clinical staff, including midwives, nurses and doctors, during scanning procedures. Building on a validated prototype capable of assessing completed ultrasound recordings, the solution was further developed into a real-time decision-support tool. Advanced image analysis algorithms evaluate scan quality during the examination, providing immediate feedback to ensure that images meet predefined clinical standards. The system integrates with existing ultrasound equipment and clinical workflows, enabling seamless adoption without disrupting routine practice. By improving image quality at the point of care, the tool increases diagnostic reliability and supports earlier detection of potential complications. Expected impacts include more accurate risk assessment, improved patient safety and more efficient use of clinical resources, contributing to higher overall standards in prenatal care.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: TeleCare Nord/Region Nordjylland, North Jutland, Aalborg University, TeleCare Nord
title: Artificial intelligence for predicting exacerbations in multidisease with easy-to-understand explanation of complex results
source_description: The project focuses on improving care for citizens with multiple chronic conditions, where disease progression is complex and difficult to monitor, often leading to unanticipated exacerbations and hospitalisations. Healthcare professionals require better tools to anticipate deterioration and communicate risks clearly to support timely intervention and patient trust. The objective is to enhance clinical decision-making and patient outcomes through early detection and understandable risk assessment. The solution combines clinical data on chronic diseases with contextual information, such as epidemiological trends, using predictive modelling techniques to forecast potential exacerbations. Explainability methods are incorporated to translate complex model outputs into clear, interpretable insights for clinicians and patients, ensuring transparency and ethical use. The system is conceptually integrated into clinical workflows to support decision-making without disrupting existing practices. The impact includes earlier interventions, reduced hospital admissions, and improved patient outcomes. It also enhances trust and usability through transparent communication, while supporting more efficient resource allocation and improved quality of care.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Region Zealand, Capital Region of Denmark
title: Artificial intelligence to support the visitation of referrals from general practice
source_description: The use case addressed inefficiencies and inconsistencies in the handling of patient referrals from general practitioners to hospitals, where large volumes of referrals require manual processing, classification, and routing across multiple stages. This creates delays, variability in decisions, and administrative burden for clinical staff. The objective is to improve consistency, efficiency, and patient rights by optimising the referral handling process. The solution uses natural language processing and classification models to analyse referral content and automatically assign cases to the appropriate medical specialty and local department. For selected specialties, the system further associates referrals with predefined patient pathways. It is integrated conceptually with hospital information systems to support seamless workflow automation and human oversight. The impact includes faster processing times, improved consistency in decision-making, and reduced administrative workload. This leads to better patient experience, more efficient use of clinical resources, and enhanced operational scalability within hospital systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Artificial intelligence for treatment support for eye patients
source_description: Ophthalmology departments faced growing demand to assess patients with age-related macular degeneration (AMD), a leading cause of blindness in Denmark. The pilot aimed to support treatment decisions and optimise specialist time. Stakeholders included patients, clinicians, and hospital administrators. From 2017 to 2019, decision-support algorithms analysed clinical imaging and patient data to classify patients requiring treatment, observation, or discharge. The system integrated into hospital workflows with a focus on transparency. The pilot enabled greater delegation of routine assessments, reduced pressure on ophthalmologists, and improved efficiency while maintaining trust and clinical oversight.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Capital Region of Denmark (Bispebjerg Hospital and Rigshospitalet) DTU and Region Zealand
title: WARD-HOME – Safe discharge from hospital
source_description: WARD-HOME focuses on enabling safe early discharge of patients by addressing the risk of undetected deterioration once patients return home. Healthcare providers require continuous monitoring solutions to ensure patient safety while reducing hospital stays and associated costs. The objective is to support rehabilitation at home through timely detection of health deterioration and rapid clinical response. The solution builds on a wireless monitoring system that continuously collects vital parameters such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate. These data are analysed using predictive algorithms to assess patient condition in real time and trigger alerts when intervention is needed. The system integrates conceptually with clinical monitoring platforms, enabling healthcare professionals to oversee patients remotely. The impact includes reduced hospital length of stay, improved patient safety, and enhanced quality of care. It also supports healthcare system efficiency by optimising resource utilisation, increasing scalability of remote care, and improving patient experience through home-based recovery.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: From A to B: Generalizing the mathematics of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to biological neural networks (BNNs)
source_description: Understanding why and when neural network models learn effectively remains a fundamental scientific challenge with implications for both artificial intelligence and neuroscience. This project seeks to develop advanced mathematical tools to analyse learning processes in Bayesian Neural Networks as statistical models and to explore parallels with biological neural systems. The research builds on a novel interpretation of local parameter updates in Bayesian Neural Networks as a derivative-free optimisation method, challenging the assumption that such approaches are inherently slow. Using nonparametric and high-dimensional statistical theory, the project investigates the convergence properties and generalisation performance of these models. By establishing rigorous mathematical guarantees, it aims to clarify the statistical mechanisms underlying efficient learning. Insights gained could inform the design of more data-efficient training methods and contribute to the development of neuromorphic computing architectures inspired by biological networks. The project has the potential to open new directions in mathematical statistics while strengthening the conceptual bridge between computational models and brain function.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Practical, Learning-Based Tools for Finding and Fixing Bugs
source_description: Software defects cause system failures, security vulnerabilities and financial losses, yet traditional static analysis and rule-based tools often miss complex or context-dependent errors. This project aims to translate advanced research on learning-based bug detection into practical tools for everyday software development. Building on techniques developed in the LearnBugs ERC project, the initiative develops intelligent models capable of analysing source code to detect anomalous patterns and suggest corrective changes. Deep learning architectures are trained on large code repositories to recognise bug signatures and generate candidate fixes that align with programming context and style. The proposed tools are designed for integration into common development environments, providing automated feedback during coding. By combining detection and repair functionalities, the system seeks to reduce debugging time and improve software reliability. Anticipated impacts include increased developer productivity, reduced maintenance costs and enhanced security of digital systems, with potential for commercial deployment in the software tools market.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Avifauna in archaeoecological networks
source_description: Human–bird interactions have shaped ecosystems and cultural practices throughout history, yet their complexity remains insufficiently understood. The AviArch project investigates avifauna within past socio-ecological systems, focusing on key transitions such as the shift to agriculture in Southwest Asia and urbanisation in Bronze Age Crete. Researchers employ zooarchaeology, palaeoproteomics and advanced computational analysis to identify bird species and reconstruct their ecological and cultural roles. Large, heterogeneous datasets are integrated using network analysis and multispecies theoretical frameworks to model relationships between humans, birds and environments. Analytical models process morphological, ecological and behavioural data to trace biodiversity patterns and assess how environmental change influenced interspecies dynamics. By generating unprecedented insights into long-term human–avian interactions, the project enhances understanding of adaptability and resilience in past societies. Outcomes contribute to contemporary biodiversity conservation strategies and foster interdisciplinary dialogue between archaeology, ecology and data science.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-enabled healthcare services during cross-border medical emergencies and regular patient services
source_description: Healthcare systems face increasing strain when managing medical emergencies across borders and ensuring continuity of care for mobile populations, while also improving routine patient services. Differences in systems, data availability, and coordination can hinder timely and effective treatment. This use case addresses these challenges through the ESCORT project, which brings together healthcare providers, emergency services, patients, and research organisations across multiple European countries. The objective is to improve patient treatment, experience, and system resilience in both emergency and regular care scenarios, including cross-border situations. The project is implemented through the integration of connected medical devices, wearable technologies, and advanced data analytics to support pre-clinical, clinical, and post-clinical care. Digital services are co-designed with stakeholders and validated in real-life scenarios across six countries, building on prior European research initiatives. The system supports real-time data exchange, decision support, and coordination between providers in emergency medicine and routine care. The project enhances the quality and continuity of care, improves response times in emergencies, and strengthens cross-border cooperation. It delivers scalable digital health services that increase resilience of healthcare systems and improve outcomes and experience for patients across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CLARITY - Causative Link between respirAtory syncytial viRus and chronic lung diseases: Identifying Targets for therapY
source_description: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infections in early life are associated with increased risk of chronic respiratory conditions, including asthma, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. The CLARITY project aims to identify genetic risk factors and molecular pathways linking RSV infection to long-term lung disease. Using national cohort data from Estonia and Spain, the project integrates genomic, clinical and epidemiological datasets to examine virus–host interactions. Advanced computational models analyse cellular networks disrupted by RSV, identifying key pathways associated with inflammatory responses and asthma development. Predictive modelling supports stratification of individuals according to genetic susceptibility and disease risk. The project also screens for drug-like compounds capable of reversing virus-induced molecular alterations. By elucidating causal mechanisms and identifying therapeutic targets, CLARITY seeks to inform personalised prevention strategies and improve treatment options. The findings may extend to other non-communicable diseases triggered by viral infections, enhancing translational impact in respiratory medicine.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: WISDOM - Well-being improvement through the Integration of healthcare and reSearch Data and models with Out border for chronic iMmune-mediated diseases
source_description: Chronic immune-mediated diseases affect around 10 % of Europeans and require coordinated, data-driven approaches to improve outcomes. However, fragmentation of medical and research data limits comprehensive analysis and personalised care strategies. The WISDOM project aims to integrate heterogeneous healthcare and research datasets within secure, interoperable infrastructures to support risk stratification and outcome prediction. Computational models are developed to translate complex biological and clinical information into actionable insights across multiple disease use cases. Privacy-preserving data-sharing frameworks and responsible governance mechanisms ensure secure collaboration across institutions. Advanced predictive algorithms identify patient subgroups and forecast disease progression, supporting personalised treatment decisions. The project also promotes critical assessment and responsible deployment of data-driven models in healthcare settings. By enhancing interoperability and analytical capacity, WISDOM seeks to improve patient well-being, optimise therapeutic strategies and reduce the societal burden of chronic immune-mediated diseases.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ZEBAI - Innovative methodologies for the design of Zero-Emission and cost-effective Buildings enhanced by Artificial Intelligence
source_description: The construction sector faces growing pressure to reduce emissions while maintaining affordability and high indoor environmental quality. ZEBAI aims to develop innovative methodologies for designing zero-emission and cost-effective buildings through a holistic, data-driven approach. The project first establishes an open-access catalogue of well-characterised construction materials, including environmental and performance indicators. Based on this knowledge base, advanced design algorithms generate optimised building configurations that balance energy efficiency, cost, indoor comfort and environmental impact. Simulation models assess lifecycle performance across different climates and usage scenarios, incorporating resilience to climate change. The methodology integrates architectural, engineering and sustainability parameters within a unified optimisation framework. By enabling systematic comparison of design alternatives, the project supports informed decision-making in early planning stages. Expected impacts include reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved resource efficiency and scalable pathways towards sustainable building practices across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FARMWISE - Future Agricultural Resource Management and Water Innovations for a Sustainable Europe
source_description: European agriculture faces mounting pressure to optimise water use, increase productivity and reduce environmental impact under climate variability. FARMWISE aims to support farmers and decision-makers with an advanced decision-support system that enhances resource management and sustainable practices. The project integrates remote sensing data, in-field sensors and agronomic datasets to generate actionable insights on irrigation, soil conditions and crop performance. Machine learning models process satellite imagery and environmental indicators to provide field-level recommendations for water allocation and precision farming interventions. The platform facilitates knowledge sharing and co-creation among farmers, researchers and European organisations, ensuring that solutions are adaptable to regional contexts. Interoperable tools enable integration with existing farm management systems, promoting scalability and uptake. Expected impacts include improved water efficiency, reduced input costs and enhanced resilience to climate change. By combining digital technologies with stakeholder collaboration, FARMWISE strengthens sustainable agricultural productivity and supports evidence-based policymaking.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: EXTRA-BRAIN - Explainable Trustworthy brain-like AI for Data Intensive Applications
source_description: Data-intensive applications increasingly require learning systems that are energy-efficient, adaptable across tasks, and transparent to users, particularly when deployed across edge and cloud environments. Traditional approaches often struggle with high energy consumption, limited generalisation, and lack of explainability, constraining their use in critical or resource-constrained settings. This use case addresses these limitations through the EXTRA-BRAIN project, involving researchers, technology developers, and application partners, with the objective of developing more universal, trustworthy, and efficient learning models inspired by brain function. The project is implemented by designing novel neural network architectures based on principles from computational neuroscience, enabling functional flexibility and improved hardware compatibility. These models are supported by data optimisation pipelines that enhance data quality and reduce annotation effort, alongside explainability frameworks that allow users to understand and trust system outputs. The solutions are tested across diverse use cases along the edge–cloud continuum, addressing different performance and hardware constraints. The project contributes to reduced energy consumption, improved adaptability across tasks, and greater transparency of advanced data-processing systems. It supports wider adoption of trustworthy, efficient learning technologies in demanding real-world applications, delivering long-term value for industry and society.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: IRE - Intelligent Robotic Endoscopes for Improved Healthcare Services
source_description: Colonoscopy is essential for early detection of colorectal cancer, yet procedural variability and navigation complexity can affect diagnostic success and patient safety. The IRE project seeks to develop intelligent robotic endoscopes that enhance precision, autonomy and clinical outcomes. The system combines robotic control architectures with learning mechanisms derived from human operator data and large datasets of real-life colonoscopies. Biomechanical modelling and digital twin simulations replicate anatomical variability, enabling safe testing and refinement of navigation strategies. Sensory feedback systems and soft robotic components improve manoeuvrability and reduce patient discomfort. Machine learning algorithms support adaptive path planning and obstacle avoidance within complex anatomical structures. Integration with clinician input ensures usability and clinical relevance. The solution aims to increase lesion detection rates, standardise procedure quality and reduce complications. By enhancing autonomy and adaptability in endoscopic navigation, IRE contributes to improved cancer screening effectiveness and more efficient healthcare delivery.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Twi Ellas Astiki Mi Kerdoskopiki Etaireia
title: ARISE - Advanced AI and RobotIcS for autonomous task pErformance
source_description: Labour shortages and hazardous conditions in sectors such as renewable energy and agriculture create demand for adaptable robotic systems capable of performing complex tasks autonomously. ARISE aims to advance automation through reconfigurable robotic manipulators integrating perception, control and learning capabilities. Pneumatic-based manipulators with soft end-effectors are combined with advanced localisation, mapping and semantic perception modules to enable precise interaction with dynamic environments. Hierarchical imitation learning and knowledge representation frameworks allow robots to acquire task strategies from human demonstrations and adapt to new scenarios. An edge-computing framework facilitates deployment of machine learning and computer vision models in real operational settings. The system is validated in solar farm installation and maintenance tasks, as well as hydroponic transplanting and harvesting operations. By improving flexibility, safety and efficiency, ARISE enhances competitiveness in key industries and supports scalable automation solutions tailored to complex real-world environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Language Planning Department of the Government of Iceland
title: How Iceland is using GPT-4 to preserve its language
source_description: Small language communities face risks of digital marginalisation when advanced language technologies are predominantly trained on high-resource languages. Iceland sought to ensure that its national language remains represented and usable in emerging digital services. Stakeholders include the Government of Iceland, language experts, technology providers and citizens. The objective is to enhance the performance of large language models in Icelandic and establish resources that support long-term linguistic preservation. The collaboration involved adapting and evaluating GPT-4 using curated Icelandic language data, linguistic expertise and targeted testing to improve comprehension and generation quality. Techniques include fine-tuning, evaluation benchmarking and iterative feedback loops to strengthen performance in low-resource language contexts. Expected impacts include improved access to digital services in Icelandic, strengthened cultural preservation, and a replicable framework for supporting other low-resource languages in advanced language technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Better Reykjavik
source_description: Cities need practical ways to involve residents in shaping local priorities, yet traditional consultation methods often struggle to attract broad participation or turn large volumes of public input into useful policy signals. Better Reykjavik was created as a collaborative platform between the Citizens Foundation, Reykjavik City, and residents to crowdsource ideas, support debate, and strengthen trust and policy development through digital participation. The objective is to give citizens a more direct role in agenda setting, participatory budgeting, and policy discussion, while helping the city process and improve the quality of contributions at scale. The implementation combines an online participation platform with artificial intelligence and machine learning features used to surface relevant information, improve user experience, and support the quality of proposals submitted by participants. The platform also includes structured debate functions, multimedia submissions, and proposal-assistance mechanisms designed to guide users in framing stronger ideas. At a conceptual level, the system integrates crowdsourcing, participation workflows, and intelligent support features to make large-scale civic input more manageable and useful. The impact includes broader citizen engagement, improved quality of submissions, and stronger support for transparent and collaborative urban governance. It also demonstrates how digital participation platforms can scale public input while making it easier for both users and public authorities to navigate complex civic conversations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Generative AI Transformation Project with Derby City Council and ICS.AI
source_description: Municipal councils face increasing demand to deliver responsive, high-quality customer services while managing budget constraints and rising case complexity. Derby City Council needed to modernise how residents interact with services, reduce pressure on frontline staff, and improve resolution of more nuanced enquiries across departments. This use case addresses these challenges through a long-term transformation of customer service operations, involving the Council, residents, and the technology partner ICS.AI, with the objective of streamlining service delivery, improving accessibility, and enabling staff to focus on higher-value tasks. The solution is implemented through generative language technologies embedded into existing digital assistants, Darcie and Ali, which are extended to function as conversational copilots across customer service workflows. These systems are trained on council service data, policies, and historical interactions to support natural, context-aware dialogue, case triage, and guided resolution, while integrating with customer relationship management and back-office systems. The initiative improves service consistency, reduces handling times, and enables more complex interactions to be resolved digitally. Over the four-year, £7 million programme launched in 2024, the Council expects improved citizen experience, greater operational efficiency, and scalable digital capability that delivers long-term value for public service transformation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Elements of AI - free online course designed by the Icelandic government
source_description: Building broad public understanding of artificial intelligence requires educational offers that are accessible to non-specialists, especially if governments want citizens and workers to engage confidently with technological change. The Elements of AI initiative addresses this challenge by providing a free online course aimed at a wide audience, explaining what artificial intelligence is, what it can and cannot do, and how people can begin to understand or develop related methods. The objective is to expand AI literacy across society and lower the barriers to entry for learners without advanced mathematics or programming backgrounds. The implementation consists of a series of online courses created by MinnaLearn and the University of Helsinki and delivered through digital learning platforms designed for self-paced participation. At a conceptual level, the programme combines structured educational content, practical examples, and accessible explanations so that learners from varied backgrounds can engage with core concepts. The material is presented as open, reusable digital education rather than as a specialist technical qualification. The impact includes broader public access to foundational AI knowledge, improved digital skills awareness, and greater readiness among learners to understand the implications of AI in work and society. It also creates scalable educational value by offering a freely available course model that can reach large and diverse audiences across countries and sectors.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Auditing a City of Vienna AI solution under IEEE CertifAIEd
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Public service providers increasingly deploy automated systems that must align with ethical, legal, and societal values. The City of Vienna sought to ensure that its digital services adhere to principles of transparency, accountability, and human-centric design. This pilot addresses the challenge of systematically assessing automated systems used by a large municipal service provider, Wiener Stadtwerke. Stakeholders include public authorities, service users, regulators, and technology developers. The objective is to validate that deployed systems meet recognised standards for responsible and trustworthy use. The solution applies the IEEE CertifAIEd assessment process to a concrete application, evaluating governance, risk management, transparency, and impact on users. Independent auditors analyse documentation, development processes, and operational practices against established criteria. The impact includes increased organisational awareness of ethical and governance requirements, strengthened trust in public digital services, and international recognition of Vienna’s digital humanism strategy. The pilot provides a reference for other cities seeking structured assurance of responsible technology deployment in public services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: British Standards Institution: EU AI Act Readiness Assessment and Algorithmic Auditing
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Organisations deploying advanced algorithmic systems face growing regulatory requirements under the EU AI Act, necessitating robust compliance, testing and documentation processes. Many lack structured methodologies to assess fairness, robustness and transparency. Stakeholders include technology providers, regulated organisations, auditors and regulators. The objective is to provide structured readiness assessments and algorithmic auditing services aligned with emerging European standards. The approach combines technical testing tools with conformity assessment frameworks. Automated evaluation platforms measure compliance against technical standards through fairness testing, bias detection, robustness analysis and performance validation. Detailed reporting tools generate evidence to support governance and certification processes, and assessments are designed to integrate with organisational risk management systems. Expected impacts include improved regulatory preparedness, reduced compliance uncertainty, enhanced trust in algorithmic systems and clearer accountability mechanisms across sectors deploying high-risk applications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Z-Inspection – Assessment for Responsible Artificial Intelligence
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Governments adopting automated systems face complex ethical, legal, and social considerations that cannot be addressed through technical evaluation alone. The Z-Inspection pilot in the Province of Fryslân addresses the need for holistic assessment methods that support responsible adoption across public administrations. Stakeholders include policymakers, civil servants, citizens, and interdisciplinary experts. The objective is to identify risks, ethical dilemmas, and governance gaps early in the lifecycle of automated systems and to build institutional capacity for responsible use. The solution applies the Z-Inspection methodology, bringing together experts from multiple disciplines to analyse the purpose, design, data use, and societal impact of a concrete system. Structured discussions explore conflicts of interest, accountability, and alignment with public values. The outcomes are documented as lessons learned and shared across government. The impact includes improved understanding of responsible deployment practices, increased digital awareness, and a practical framework for assessing future systems. The pilot supports more confident, transparent, and trustworthy use of advanced technologies in the public sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Anotherblock
source_description: Music rights are traditionally difficult for creators to monetise directly, with complex royalty chains and intermediaries that can reduce transparency for both artists and fans. Anotherblock addresses this by enabling artists and rights-holders to sell defined portions of track-level rights to their community, creating a clearer route for participation and investment in streaming royalties while maintaining a legally enforceable relationship between parties. Stakeholders include creators, collectors, platforms handling royalty reporting, and regulators seeking clarity on how tokenised intellectual property rights should be structured and supervised, with the objective of making rights transfers simpler, auditable, and fairer. The service is implemented by issuing music ownership tokens on Ethereum using the ERC-721 standard, where each token carries a unique identifier and encodes an ownership percentage for a specific song, alongside associated artwork and a linked real-world legal contract defining royalty terms and ownership guarantees. Transactions and ownership history are recorded on-chain, while off-chain legal documentation and royalty flows are aligned to token holdings through platform governance and reporting integrations. The approach can reduce friction and costs in rights distribution, improve transparency of ownership, and create new, engagement-driven revenue options for artists; participation in the European Blockchain Sandbox is used to test compliance pathways and surface regulatory needs for legal certainty in tokenised IP structures.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Dedit.io – Blockchain-Based Notarisation and Custodial Wallet Platform
source_description: Organisations and individuals increasingly rely on digital documents for contractual, legal, and administrative processes, yet traditional notarisation, signing, and document management remain fragmented, slow, and costly. Ensuring legal validity, integrity, and long-term trust in digital documents is a persistent challenge, particularly in cross-border contexts. Dedit.io addresses this need by providing a unified platform for secure document notarisation, signing, storage, and sharing. Stakeholders include legal professionals, businesses, public authorities, and end users requiring trusted digital transactions. The objective is to streamline document workflows while ensuring high levels of legal certainty and regulatory compliance. The solution provides a distributed notarisation and validation service supporting multiple protocols and development environments, combined with a custodial wallet for managing digital assets and documents. Advanced electronic signatures are integrated, with ongoing development towards stronger digital identity and signature authentication mechanisms. The platform is designed for interoperability and scalability, allowing adaptation to diverse legal and market requirements. The impact includes faster document processing, reduced administrative overhead, and improved trust in digital transactions. Participation in the European Blockchain Sandbox supports regulatory alignment and positions Dedit.io as a scalable, compliant solution for end-to-end digital document management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Chunk Works – Universal Security Layer for Distributed Data Protection
source_description: As organisations increasingly operate across hybrid and decentralised infrastructures, ensuring data security, availability, and resilience has become more complex. Conventional storage systems face risks from cyberattacks, data loss, and emerging threats such as quantum computing. Chunk Works addresses this challenge by providing a universal security layer that combines strong encryption with resilient data storage. Stakeholders include enterprises, public bodies, and service providers handling sensitive data across cloud, on-premise, and edge environments. The objective is to ensure privacy, integrity, and continuous availability of data without compromising performance or deployment flexibility. The solution breaks data into encrypted fragments using erasure coding, adds redundancy, and distributes these fragments across multiple locations using distributed ledger technology. Post-quantum hybrid encryption protects data against future cryptographic threats, while autonomous recovery mechanisms reconstruct data even if parts are lost or unavailable. The impact includes increased resilience to failures and attacks, reduced risk of data loss, and future-proof security. Chunk Works delivers a scalable, infrastructure-agnostic solution that strengthens trust in digital data management and supports secure operations in increasingly decentralised environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Coinfirm – Blockchain Analytics and Investigations for Regulatory Compliance
source_description: The growth of crypto-assets and decentralised finance has created new challenges for combating money laundering, terrorist financing, and financial crime. Regulators and financial institutions require sophisticated tools to understand complex transaction flows and assess risk in blockchain ecosystems. Coinfirm addresses this need by providing advanced analytics and investigation capabilities for digital assets. Stakeholders include banks, virtual asset service providers, payment providers, financial intelligence units, regulators, and decentralised platforms. The objective is to support compliance with anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing requirements while enabling responsible innovation. The solution aggregates on-chain, off-chain, and shared intelligence data to build detailed models of asset flows and address behaviour. Advanced risk analytics evaluate transaction patterns, identify high-risk entities, and enable real-time monitoring of address clusters. These insights support source-of-funds analysis, transaction screening, and regulatory reporting. The impact includes improved detection of illicit activity, stronger compliance capabilities, and increased transparency in crypto markets. Coinfirm supports safer adoption of digital assets and contributes to the integrity and stability of the evolving financial ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Eonpass: stopping counterfeit goods
source_description: Counterfeit goods entering the European Union pose risks to consumer safety, brand integrity, and public revenues, while placing significant strain on customs authorities. Eonpass emerged as a proposed solution following a competition organised by the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO), aiming to improve the detection of fraudulent goods at borders. Stakeholders included EUIPO, customs authorities, logistics providers, and private-sector partners such as EY and Jet Air Service. The objective was to create a shared, trusted mechanism for verifying the authenticity of goods across complex international supply chains. The proposed system used distributed ledger technology to record product identifiers, shipment data, and verification events, enabling customs officials to cross-check goods against tamper-resistant records at the point of entry. Open standards were emphasised to allow interoperability between manufacturers, freight operators, and enforcement agencies. While Eonpass was recognised as the strongest conceptual model in the EUIPO competition, public sources indicate that it remained at proof-of-concept level and was not rolled out as an operational customs system. Nonetheless, the project demonstrated how shared digital ledgers could enhance transparency and trust in border processes, informing later policy and technical discussions on anti-counterfeiting measures.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Hydropower for bitcoin mining
source_description: Small hydropower plants often struggle with economic viability during periods of low energy demand, leading to underutilised infrastructure. In northern Italy, municipalities sought alternative revenue models. The objective of this initiative is to improve the economic sustainability of hydropower plants by coupling energy production with high-performance computing demand. The implementation involves colocating data centres at hydropower facilities, where computing capacity is sold to external operators. This model avoids direct municipal involvement in digital asset markets while monetising surplus capacity. Expected impacts include improved financial sustainability of renewable infrastructure and reduced waste. Qualitative outcomes include regional innovation, repurposing of abandoned assets and alignment between renewable energy and digital infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Bitcoin and Tether as Legal Tender in Lugano
source_description: Seeking to position itself as a European hub for digital finance, the City of Lugano announced a partnership with Tether to promote the use of cryptocurrencies for everyday transactions. The initiative aimed to allow residents and businesses to use Bitcoin, Tether, and a local token (LVGA Points) for taxes, public services, and retail payments. Stakeholders included the city administration, local businesses, residents, and technology providers. The objective was to stimulate innovation, attract investment, and modernise payment infrastructure. The initiative relied on blockchain-based payment rails and digital wallets to enable peer-to-peer and merchant transactions without traditional intermediaries. While the announcement framed cryptocurrencies as “de facto legal tender,” subsequent reporting indicates a more limited implementation focused on voluntary acceptance, pilot use cases, and municipal payments rather than universal adoption across all businesses. The initiative increased Lugano’s international visibility and led to selective uptake among merchants, but it did not replicate the mandatory legal tender model seen elsewhere. As such, it represents a partial implementation that illustrates both the opportunities and practical constraints of integrating crypto-assets into local economies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Central Bank of Norway CBDC Sandbox
source_description: Norges Bank established a central bank digital currency (CBDC) sandbox to test technical solutions for potential issuance of digital central bank money. The objective is to evaluate infrastructure for minting, transferring and destroying digital tokens in a controlled experimental environment. The sandbox is built on Ethereum-based technology and includes smart contracts implementing ERC-20 token standards. Access is restricted to authorised participants, with credential-based controls. A custom front-end interface allows interaction with the test network, while monitoring tools such as BlockScout and Grafana provide transaction tracking and performance analytics. The environment enables simulation of issuance, distribution and redemption scenarios without public deployment. By releasing open-source code, the central bank promotes transparency and technical experimentation while assessing feasibility, scalability and security considerations. The sandbox supports evidence-based evaluation of digital currency infrastructure before any policy decision on formal implementation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Product Passport solution for the Circular Economy
source_description: Upcoming EU regulations require manufacturers to provide transparent, verifiable information on product origin, composition and environmental impact, creating significant compliance and data management challenges across supply chains. Compellio, a Luxembourg-based startup, developed a Digital Product Passport (DPP) solution to support circular economy objectives and regulatory readiness under the Ecodesign and Battery Regulations. Stakeholders include manufacturers, regulators, consumers and third-party auditors. The objective is to create a trusted, interoperable mechanism for tracking product lifecycle data while ensuring data integrity and regulatory compliance. The solution uses blockchain-based infrastructure to anchor verified product data and Product Circularity Data Sheets (PCDS) in line with the emerging ISO 59040 standard. Third-party verified data is recorded to ensure traceability and immutability, while off-chain systems manage detailed product information and updates. The platform integrates with enterprise systems and supports selective data disclosure. Selected for the EU Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox, the pilot demonstrates compliance-by-design, improved trust across supply chains and reduced reporting friction. It positions DPPs as a scalable tool for transparency, enabling businesses to meet regulatory demands while supporting greener consumer choices and circular value chains.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Bonds on a Public Blockchain – European Investment Bank
source_description: Traditional bond issuance processes involve multiple intermediaries, manual reconciliation steps and settlement delays, which can increase operational complexity and cost. Capital market participants seek more transparent and efficient issuance mechanisms. Stakeholders include the European Investment Bank, underwriting banks, central banks and investors. The objective is to demonstrate the feasibility of issuing and settling bonds using distributed ledger technology. The solution records bond registration and settlement transactions on a public blockchain platform, enabling tokenised bond representation and near real-time transaction visibility. In collaboration with Banque de France, central bank digital currency was used to represent payment flows on-chain. Smart contract functionalities automate key lifecycle events, and interoperability with existing financial systems is maintained. Anticipated impacts include reduced intermediary reliance, faster settlement, enhanced transparency of ownership and trading flows, and lower fixed operational costs, contributing to the digitalisation of capital markets.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Survcoin
source_description: Urban mobility is a major contributor to carbon emissions, particularly commuting by private car, and local authorities are seeking practical ways to influence behaviour while supporting employee wellbeing. In Differdange, the municipality aimed to reduce emissions generated by daily commuting among its approximately 800 employees and encourage healthier, more sustainable travel choices. This use case addresses these objectives by incentivising the use of soft mobility options such as walking, cycling, and public transport, involving municipal employees and local stakeholders. The solution is implemented through a digital reward system based on an alternative local currency, Survcoin, which is issued to participating employees according to their verified reduction in CO₂ emissions. Mobility data is collected to calculate individual contributions, and rewards are credited in Survcoins that can be used within the local ecosystem. The initiative increases awareness of travel-related emissions, encourages behavioural change, and promotes active mobility. It delivers measurable environmental benefits through reduced car usage, supports employee health and wellbeing, and strengthens local engagement, while providing the city with a scalable and transparent mechanism to link climate goals to everyday mobility choices.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI for Emergency information system
source_description: Emergency departments face increasing pressure due to high patient volumes, time-critical decision-making, and limited medical staff, raising the risk of delayed or missed diagnoses. This project proposal aimed to explore a new emergency information system to support faster and more accurate triage and intervention. Stakeholders included hospitals, emergency responders, healthcare professionals, and regional authorities. The objective was to improve the overall rescue process by enhancing early assessment of patients’ conditions before or during emergency intake. The proposed system would analyse facial expressions and vocal characteristics captured during emergency interactions, combining these signals with contextual information to identify potential indicators of distress or medical urgency. Conceptually, the system would integrate real-time data capture with analytical models and clinical workflows, providing decision-support signals to medical staff rather than automated diagnoses. Despite its inclusion in Interreg Europe’s project ideas, the initiative remained at the exploratory and proposal stage, with no evidence of operational deployment. Nonetheless, it highlighted emerging directions in emergency care innovation and contributed to policy-level discussions on the responsible use of advanced analytics in high-risk healthcare settings.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ARTIMATION Project: Building trust in air traffic management AI
source_description: The ARTIMATION project, funded under the SESAR Joint Undertaking, addresses the challenge of transparency in artificial intelligence systems used in air traffic management (ATM). Increasing reliance on automation and predictive models in ATM requires high levels of trust, safety and regulatory compliance. ARTIMATION developed explainable AI techniques to make the outputs of neural networks and deep learning models more interpretable for human operators. The project integrates explainability algorithms that highlight relevant input factors and provide traceable reasoning for system recommendations within ATM decision-support tools. By embedding transparency mechanisms into existing AI applications, the solution enables controllers and system managers to understand and validate automated outputs. The approach strengthens operational trust, supports regulatory acceptance and facilitates responsible deployment of AI in safety-critical environments. ARTIMATION contributes to modernising Europe’s ATM infrastructure while ensuring that human oversight remains central to operational decision-making.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI Anonymisator for Estonian public sector
source_description: Estonian public authorities process large volumes of personal data in appeals, case files and administrative documents, creating risks related to privacy protection and GDPR compliance. To mitigate these risks, an AI-based anonymisation application was developed in 2022 to automatically identify and transform personal data within textual documents. The tool uses named entity recognition models, trained on corpora developed by the University of Tartu, to detect entities such as personal names, identification codes and locations. Detected entities can be replaced with alternative values from the same category, enabling anonymisation or pseudonymisation depending on user requirements. The application can be integrated into existing information systems and used across institutions handling sensitive data. Clients may further train the models with institution-specific datasets to improve accuracy in specialised contexts. By automating personal data masking, the solution reduces manual workload, lowers the risk of data breaches and strengthens compliance with data protection regulations while supporting secure training and document handling processes in the public sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Automatic real-time subtitles
source_description: To enhance accessibility of live broadcasts for people who are hard of hearing, Estonia introduced automatic real-time subtitles generated through speech recognition technology. Traditional subtitling requires manual editing and preparation, limiting its use for live events. The autosubtitles system produces captions instantly during broadcasts without human editing, relying on machine speech-to-text models developed within the Quick Writer solution at Tallinn University of Technology. The system processes live audio streams, converts speech into text and displays captions with a short delay of a few seconds. Performance depends on speech clarity, background noise and speaking speed. Users can activate subtitles via their television remote control when supported by their service provider. By automating caption generation, the initiative increases inclusion, improves access to public information and reduces production costs associated with manual subtitling. Although minor inaccuracies may occur, the system significantly expands real-time accessibility across national broadcasting services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Bureaucrat on eID website
source_description: Citizens interacting with public authorities often need to consult multiple institutions, each with its own website and processes, leading to fragmented experiences and repeated enquiries. Estonia addressed this challenge by creating a unified conversational access layer across government websites. This use case involves the Information System Authority, multiple public institutions, and citizens, with the objective of providing a single, intuitive way to access public information. The Bureaucrat operates as an interoperable network of chatbots deployed across authority websites, enabling colloquial, natural communication through a shared chat interface. The system routes queries to the relevant institution and retrieves accurate information from official sources, while maintaining a consistent user experience. Integration across agencies reduces duplication and improves coherence of responses. The solution enhances accessibility of public services, reduces navigation complexity for users, and improves efficiency for institutions by sharing a common conversational infrastructure. It delivers scalable digital government interaction and strengthens trust in public service delivery.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
title: Prototype of the entrepreneur's early warning service
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Small and medium-sized enterprises often encounter financial distress too late to take corrective action, leading to insolvency risks with wider economic consequences. Estonia developed a prototype early warning service to help entrepreneurs identify potential liquidity and solvency issues at an early stage. Stakeholders include business owners, public authorities and economic policymakers. The objective is preventive support rather than enforcement, enabling informed decision-making before financial difficulties escalate. The prototype continuously monitors publicly available and submitted financial data, comparing company performance against sector-specific benchmarks and economic principles. When deviations from typical patterns are detected, additional analyses assess trends related to cash flow, obligations and sustainability. If risks persist, the system generates an informational alert to the company. The service is advisory only and carries no legal consequences. The prototype demonstrated feasibility and value as a preventive economic tool, supporting business resilience and reducing the likelihood of sudden failures. Its impact lies in empowering entrepreneurs, improving economic stability and enabling public authorities to offer support earlier, while maintaining a non-intrusive, trust-based approach.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Bureaucrat of the Environment Agency
source_description: The Estonian Environment Agency implemented a “Bureaucrat” chatbot on its website to streamline citizen enquiries and provide accessible digital interaction with public services. Residents often require guidance on environmental regulations, permits and public information, generating recurring questions. The Bureaucrat operates as part of an interoperable network of chatbots deployed across Estonian public authorities, enabling conversational access to services through a unified interface. The system uses natural language processing to interpret user queries and retrieve information from institutional databases and knowledge repositories. It provides structured responses and directs users to relevant services, while complex cases remain handled by staff. Integration within the wider Bureaucrat ecosystem allows cross-institutional information exchange and consistent user experience. The chatbot enhances accessibility, reduces administrative workload and supports Estonia’s digital governance strategy by enabling colloquial, user-friendly access to public information services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Remote snow monitoring
source_description: Estonian meteorological services introduced machine vision techniques to automate measurement of snow cover at weather stations. Manual snow depth measurement is labour-intensive and may limit data frequency and coverage. The remote monitoring system uses camera-based image capture combined with computer vision algorithms to detect and quantify snow depth from visual markers. Image analysis models interpret changes in visible reference scales and surface conditions, converting them into structured meteorological data. The automated measurements are integrated into forecasting databases and contribute to development of improved predictive models. By replacing manual readings with continuous digital observation, the system reduces operational costs, increases measurement consistency and enhances temporal resolution of snow data. The approach supports more accurate weather forecasting and climate monitoring while improving efficiency in environmental data collection.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GAP: preparation of Estonian language tests easy and the assessment automatic.
source_description: The Estonian Institute developed GAP to simplify preparation and evaluation of Estonian language tests. Teachers previously needed to manually design gap-fill exercises and assess responses, which was time-consuming and inconsistent. GAP uses natural language processing to analyse selected texts and automatically generate gap exercises based on specified criteria such as word type, grammatical form and difficulty level. The system identifies appropriate lexical items, removes them to create gaps and produces structured test versions for learners. Automated assessment tools evaluate responses according to predefined linguistic rules. By enabling rapid creation of customised exercises, GAP reduces preparation time and supports differentiated learning. The tool enhances consistency in assessment and facilitates scalable language testing aligned with curriculum requirements. It strengthens digital support for language education while preserving teacher oversight in final evaluation and pedagogical decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Machine translation customer support communication window on the website of Tartu University Hospital
source_description: Healthcare providers increasingly serve diverse populations with varying language needs, making effective communication essential for safety and patient satisfaction. Tartu University Hospital sought to improve accessibility of its online customer support for non-Estonian speakers. This use case involves the hospital, patients, and support staff, with the objective of enabling multilingual communication through digital channels. The solution is implemented as an online customer support window combining live chat, email submission, FAQs, and machine translation powered by Askly. Incoming messages are translated in real time, allowing staff to respond in their own language while patients communicate in theirs. The system integrates with existing support workflows and hospital information systems. The solution improves inclusivity, reduces misunderstandings, and enhances response efficiency. It delivers better patient experience, supports equitable access to healthcare information, and enables scalable multilingual support without proportionally increasing staffing costs.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
title: Politsei.ee large-language model LLM trained on data
source_description: Citizens often struggle to find accurate and relevant information on public authority websites, particularly when content is complex or legalistic. The Estonian Police and Border Guard Board tested a pilot to improve information retrieval on politsei.ee by developing a tailored language model trained on official legal texts. Stakeholders include citizens, public service users and government web administrators. The objective was to assess whether customised language models could improve searchability and user interaction in Estonian-language public services. The pilot trained a model on State Gazette data and tested it within the Azure OpenAI environment, using a ChatGPT 3.5-based architecture. The system was evaluated on its ability to answer questions and retrieve relevant information. Results showed that performance in Estonian lagged behind English, highlighting language resource gaps and training data limitations. Despite mixed results, the pilot provided valuable insights into localisation challenges, infrastructure needs and language equity in digital public services, informing future investments in Estonian-language models.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: RaRa Bureaucrat
source_description: The National Library of Estonia implemented a Bureaucrat chatbot on its website to improve access to library services and information. Users frequently require assistance with catalogue searches, opening hours, digital collections and service procedures. As part of Estonia’s interoperable Bureaucrat network, the chatbot provides conversational interaction through a web-based chat interface. Natural language processing components interpret user questions and retrieve relevant information from library databases and curated knowledge sources. The system delivers structured responses and directs users to appropriate resources, while complex research queries remain managed by library staff. Integration with the broader Bureaucrat ecosystem ensures consistent functionality across public institutions. The deployment enhances user experience, increases service availability outside office hours and reduces routine enquiry workload. By enabling accessible digital interaction, RaRa Bureaucrat supports the Library’s modernisation and public engagement objectives.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: HIF EE: Information-based decision support
source_description: Healthcare professionals frequently encounter complex cases where symptoms do not clearly indicate a single diagnosis, requiring consultation of multiple information sources during limited consultation times. Fragmented access to guidelines and drug databases can delay decision-making. Stakeholders include physicians, nurses, healthcare institutions and patients. The objective is to provide integrated, real-time decision support during clinical encounters. The system aggregates international and domestic treatment guidelines, drug interaction databases, adverse reaction registries and pregnancy and lactation information into a unified search interface. Natural language search and structured query mechanisms enable rapid retrieval of evidence-based recommendations. Integration with clinical workflows ensures accessibility during patient visits. Expected impacts include reduced time spent searching for information, improved diagnostic accuracy, safer prescribing through interaction checks and enhanced patient-centred care by freeing time for direct consultation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Computer Vision for monitoring the condition of streets and the city environment
source_description: Municipalities require timely information on the condition of streets, waste containers and public infrastructure to maintain cleanliness and service quality. Manual inspections are costly and infrequent. This pilot addressed the problem by developing a visual monitoring system for overflowing waste containers, with potential extension to other urban anomalies. Stakeholders include city service departments and residents. The objective was to improve responsiveness and optimise maintenance operations. A computer vision model based on fine-tuned ResNet-32 architecture was trained on a dataset of 300 images of waste containers collected from streets and online sources. The system detects overflowing containers and visual anomalies, with results displayed on a city map via a React-based frontend using Leaflet. Although limited in scale, the pilot demonstrated improved situational awareness, faster intervention by city services and better user experience for residents. It highlighted scalability potential to potholes, signage and broader urban monitoring, offering a cost-effective approach to smarter city maintenance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Europe Language Tools - eSummary
source_description: Public administrations and organisations handle large volumes of documents, making it time-consuming to identify relevant information quickly. The European Commission developed eSummary to support faster understanding of documents across languages. This use case involves EU institutions, public administrations, and professionals, with the objective of improving efficiency in document analysis. The service is implemented as an online summarisation tool that processes common office and PDF formats and produces concise summaries highlighting key points. By connecting to the EU’s eTranslation service, it supports all EU languages and additional ones. The system applies advanced text analysis techniques to identify salient information and generate structured summaries returned as Word documents. The solution reduces reading time, supports quicker decision-making, and improves accessibility of information across language barriers. It delivers productivity gains, supports multilingual workflows, and provides scalable value for document-intensive public sector environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Europe Language Tools - eBriefing
source_description: eBriefing is an AI-based drafting service developed within the European Commission’s language technology ecosystem to assist in preparing official briefings. EU staff frequently need structured briefing documents summarising complex materials in a standard institutional format. The service allows users to upload documents in docx, txt or text-based PDF format and generates a draft briefing structured with elements such as summary, line-to-take and defensive points. The system leverages advanced generative language models and operates in conjunction with eTranslation, enabling submission and output in multiple EU languages. Prompt engineering ensures alignment with institutional conventions, while outputs require human review for accuracy and style before official use. By automating first-draft preparation, eBriefing reduces drafting time, enhances productivity and supports multilingual document workflows. The tool facilitates consistent formatting and accelerates preparation of policy briefings while maintaining human responsibility for validation and final approval.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Europe Language Tools - Speech Transcription
source_description: The eTranslation Speech Transcription service was developed to provide EU institutions and public administrations with an accessible tool for converting audio and video content into written text. Public bodies frequently need transcripts of meetings, speeches and multimedia material for documentation, accessibility and multilingual workflows. The web-based interface allows users to upload sound or video files and receive an automated transcription without specialised software. The system currently relies on customised Microsoft Azure speech-to-text engines, configured to support institutional terminology and multilingual requirements, with plans to integrate alternative engines over time. Uploaded files are processed through secure cloud-based speech recognition models that convert spoken language into structured text output. The service accelerates documentation processes, improves accessibility for hearing-impaired users and supports translation and archiving activities. By automating transcription tasks, the tool reduces manual workload and shortens turnaround times while enabling scalable processing of multilingual audiovisual material across EU institutions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Europe Language Tools - Social Media Translator, Anonymization support, Classification
source_description: The eTranslation Social Media Translator enables EU institutions to publish multilingual social media content efficiently while maintaining consistency and reach. Communication teams often need to disseminate short messages across multiple EU languages under tight deadlines. Through a web interface, users compose a message in one language and automatically generate translations using eTranslation’s “General Text” engines, optimised for short-form content. The system accounts for character limits and allows direct posting via linked social media accounts, with an indication that the message was machine translated. Complementary services include anonymisation and document classification. The anonymisation tool replaces or obscures identifiable information using entity recognition and obfuscation techniques derived from the MAPA project, while the classification service assigns Eurovoc descriptors using the JEX tool and returns structured metadata in JSON format. Together, these tools enhance multilingual communication, protect personal data and streamline content management within EU digital workflows.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Europe Language Tools - Named-entity recognition
source_description: The eTranslation Named-Entity Recognition (NER) service provides EU institutions with automated extraction of key entities from documents in common formats. Administrations handling multilingual documentation require efficient methods to identify references to persons, organisations and locations. The web interface processes uploaded text-based documents and applies entity recognition models to detect and tag named entities. Results are returned in structured XML format, enabling integration with downstream systems. Complementary anonymisation and classification modules support replacement or masking of personal data and assignment of Eurovoc descriptors using the JEX taxonomy tool. The anonymisation component builds on the MAPA project and allows either entity substitution or visual obfuscation. The services operate on text-based files; scanned PDFs without embedded text are not processed due to lack of standalone OCR functionality. By automating metadata extraction and tagging, the tool enhances document management, improves searchability and supports GDPR-compliant handling of official texts across EU administrations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0
