organization: Municipalities of Santarcangelo di Romagna, Riccione and Cattolica
title: Acquedotto 4.0, Hera invests in artificial intelligence
source_description: Water utilities face significant challenges in maintaining ageing distribution networks, where undetected leaks can lead to water loss, infrastructure damage, and costly, disruptive repairs. Hera Group sought to improve monitoring of water networks in several municipalities in Emilia-Romagna while minimising the need for invasive inspections and roadworks. This use case addresses these challenges by enabling early detection of leaks and targeted maintenance, involving the utility operator, municipalities, and residents. The Acquedotto 4.0 pilot is implemented by combining low-cost acoustic sensors with data-driven analysis of water flow sounds to identify patterns associated with leaks. Sensors are deployed across the network to continuously capture data, which is analysed to detect anomalies and localise potential failures. The system integrates with existing maintenance and asset management processes to support timely interventions. The project improves reliability of water supply, reduces non-revenue water, and lowers repair costs by avoiding unnecessary excavation. It also limits traffic disruption and environmental impact, demonstrating how digital monitoring can enhance resilience and efficiency of critical urban infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Carboni Zero: minimizing the carbon footprint of the food sector
source_description: Food supply chains face increasing pressure to quantify and reduce carbon emissions, yet fragmented tools and lack of trust hinder consistent measurement and reporting. The Carboni Zero project in Catalonia addresses this gap by creating an integrated system to quantify and certify emissions across food production processes. Stakeholders include agri-food companies, technology providers, researchers and local authorities. The objective is transparency with confidentiality, enabling optimisation without exposing sensitive production details. The solution uses blockchain infrastructure to create a shared standard for emissions data while ensuring immutability and traceability. Zero-knowledge proof techniques allow verification of total emissions without disclosing underlying proprietary data. The platform is designed by the Centre Blockchain de Catalunya (CBCat), with participation from food companies Bonpreu, Noel and Llet Nostra, technology partner SEIDOR, and academic expertise from UVic. The pilot supports process optimisation, trusted certification and regulatory readiness, demonstrating how secure digital infrastructures can align sustainability goals with business confidentiality and scalability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: reWatt: renewable energy standard
source_description: Energy self-consumption has grown rapidly in Spain, yet regulatory and market structures have limited the ability of households and communities to exchange surplus renewable energy efficiently. The reWatt Peers project, developed by the Centre Blockchain de Catalunya (CBCat) with the support of Badalona City Council, addresses this gap by enabling the economic exchange of surplus self-consumed energy at both individual and collective levels. Stakeholders include energy prosumers, consumers, energy marketers and local authorities. The objective is to foster local renewable energy communities, increase participation in clean energy generation and improve the economic viability of self-consumption within the framework of Spanish regulation (RD 244/2019). The platform uses distributed ledger technology to record energy surplus transactions in a peer-to-peer format, removing the need for central intermediaries in surplus management. Smart contracts manage allocation and settlement of exchanged energy between participants of the same energy marketer, while metering data provides the basis for accurate accounting. The pilot demonstrates increased transparency, trust and efficiency in surplus energy sharing. Qualitatively, it encourages collaboration, local energy resilience and citizen engagement in the energy transition, while laying the groundwork for scalable community-based renewable energy markets.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain-Based Gaia-X Data Infrastructure
source_description: European organisations face growing challenges in sharing and monetising data across borders while preserving data sovereignty, intellectual property protection and compliance with EU values. Pontus-X, developed by startup deltaDAO AG, addresses these challenges by providing a federated Web3 ecosystem aligned with Gaia-X principles. Stakeholders include companies, research organisations and public bodies across sectors such as mobility, aerospace, healthcare and manufacturing. The objective is to enable trusted, sovereign data and service exchange within the European digital single market. Pontus-X combines a distributed ledger–based transaction and logging layer with smart contracts for sovereign data exchange, NFT-based metadata catalogues and identity services built on self-sovereign identity and verifiable credentials. Privacy-preserving techniques such as Compute-to-Data allow analytics without exposing raw data. The platform integrates regulated digital payments through the EUROe stablecoin for real-time settlement. Selected for the EU Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox, Pontus-X demonstrates scalable, interoperable data marketplaces that reduce legal and technical friction. Its impact includes improved trust in cross-organisational collaboration, new data monetisation opportunities and stronger alignment with European data strategy objectives, supporting competitiveness and innovation while safeguarding sovereignty.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Vidameco for edge data integrity and standardization
source_description: Industries such as maritime transport generate large volumes of operational data, yet lack of standardisation and data integrity undermines trust, efficiency and regulatory compliance. The Vidameco research project addresses this problem by providing a unified approach to standardised data collection and tamper-proofing at the edge. Stakeholders include vessel operators, certification bodies, regulators and service providers. The objective is to reduce redundancy, prevent manipulation and simplify compliance with regulations such as the EU’s Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) framework. Vidameco combines onboard hardware with a microservices-based software architecture to collect, structure and validate data at source. Blockchain technology anchors data fingerprints and stakeholder actions, ensuring traceability and immutability across the value chain. Smart contracts automate repetitive verification and reporting processes, while identity binding reduces errors and fraud. Selected for the European Blockchain Sandbox, the pilot demonstrates reduced administrative burden, faster verification cycles and improved trust in certified data. Its impact extends beyond shipping, offering a reusable model for data integrity and standardisation in other sectors, accelerating digitalisation while maintaining regulatory confidence.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Equilibrium Group: Tokenizing real-world assets
source_description: Financial markets and corporate structures are increasingly exploring digital representations of real-world assets, but face legal, regulatory, and operational uncertainty, particularly in the European context. Equilibrium Group aims to enable compliant tokenisation of assets such as fiat currency and shares of unlisted companies, while ensuring interoperability, transparency, and regulatory alignment. This use case involves financial institutions, regulators, and market participants, with the objective of creating efficient, legally robust digital asset infrastructures. The solution is implemented through distributed ledger systems that represent real-world assets as digital tokens, including EUROe, a fully regulated electronic money instrument issued under EU law. Tokenisation frameworks are designed to support payments, asset registries, and future marketplaces, while integrating identity and compliance mechanisms such as advanced digital identity and zero-knowledge proof-based verification. Participation in the European Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox allows regulatory questions around issuance, trading, and rights to be explored in a controlled environment. The initiative delivers efficiency gains through faster issuance and settlement, improved interoperability, and reduced operational costs, while contributing to regulatory clarity and laying the foundation for scalable, compliant digital asset markets in Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Eviden battery passport
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: The transition to electric mobility requires transparent lifecycle information on batteries to support sustainability, safety, repairability and recycling, as mandated by upcoming EU Battery Regulations. Eviden’s Battery Passport initiative addresses this need by providing a shared digital infrastructure for battery data across the automotive ecosystem. Stakeholders include vehicle manufacturers, battery producers, repair centres, recyclers and regulators. The objective is to uniquely identify batteries, enable controlled data sharing and ensure compliance without exposing commercially sensitive information. Each battery is represented by a unique digital passport, with production, performance and usage data securely linked over time. Blockchain technology ensures integrity, traceability and decentralised governance of records, while cloud-based services allow participants to manage their own data. The platform supports selective access rights, enabling downstream actors to retrieve only relevant information. Participation in the European Blockchain Sandbox validates the regulatory relevance of the approach. The pilot enhances transparency, supports circular economy practices and reduces information asymmetries across the value chain, creating long-term value through improved sustainability reporting, compliance readiness and operational efficiency.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Open Customs Blockchain
source_description: International trade and customs processes remain burdened by paper-based documentation, fragmented data exchange and limited transparency, resulting in delays, higher costs and unnecessary inspections. The Open Customs Blockchain initiative, led by the Open Logistics Foundation with major logistics companies and research partners, aims to modernise customs data exchange across borders. Stakeholders include logistics providers, customs authorities, IT vendors and exporters/importers. The objective is to streamline customs procedures, improve traceability and accelerate cross-border trade. The solution stores customs-relevant information, such as invoice data and export accompanying documents, in a tamper-proof distributed ledger accessible to authorised parties throughout the supply chain. By ensuring consistent data provenance and reusability, the platform reduces duplication and errors. Integration with existing logistics systems enables incremental adoption. Selected for the European Blockchain Sandbox, the pilot demonstrates potential reductions in transit times, fewer physical inspections and improved trust between public and private actors. The project supports more sustainable, efficient international trade by replacing manual processes with verifiable digital workflows.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Privacy Layer for Digital Pound
source_description: Public trust in a potential UK digital pound depends heavily on assurances around privacy, fraud prevention and proportional oversight. To address these concerns, the Bank of England is collaborating with startup Nuggets to explore a privacy and identity layer for a future central bank digital currency. Stakeholders include central banks, payment providers, consumers and regulators. The objective is to design a system that prevents transaction tracking and correlation by default, while still supporting lawful controls against fraud and money laundering. The proposed architecture uses decentralised identity and privacy-enhancing technologies to separate user identity from transaction data. Cryptographic techniques enable selective disclosure, ensuring that personal data is not centrally stored or routinely accessible. The privacy layer is designed to integrate with potential digital pound core infrastructure rather than replace existing payment systems. Although exploratory, the pilot informs the Bank of England’s ongoing consultation and design choices ahead of any issuance decision post-2025. Its impact lies in demonstrating that strong privacy, regulatory compliance and usability can coexist, shaping public confidence and policy discussions around sovereign digital money.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CAMINS Academic credentials
source_description: Catalan public universities face growing demand to issue short, modular learning credentials that are easily verifiable across institutions and borders, while giving students greater control over their academic data. The CAMINS initiative brings together five public universities in Catalonia, coordinated by Rovira i Virgili University, with additional universities and shared service bodies acting as observers. The objective is to create a common, decentralised system for issuing, managing and verifying academic microcredentials that is interoperable at European level and aligned with emerging EU standards. The solution is implemented on the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI), enabling credentials to be issued as verifiable digital records anchored to a distributed ledger. Universities exchange student data securely through a shared blockchain platform developed by Seidor and Validated ID, which also provides digital identity, electronic signatures and verifiable credentials. Students receive credentials in a personal digital wallet linked to a recognised digital identity, allowing selective sharing with employers or other institutions. The pilot improves trust, reduces administrative overhead and enables cross-border recognition of learning achievements. It strengthens student data sovereignty while laying the foundation for scalable, EU-wide academic credential ecosystems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Historical heritage protection
source_description: Córdoba City Council manages extensive historical and artistic heritage assets that are vulnerable to theft, forgery, and loss of provenance information. Existing tools did not allow rapid verification of ownership, location, and authenticity. This use case involves the municipality, museums, cultural authorities, and citizens, with the objective of certifying and protecting heritage assets. The solution is implemented through a digital certification system where heritage records are stored on a blockchain-based platform, combined with physical tags incorporating geolocation and motion sensors. Each asset is digitally registered with provenance, authorship, and condition data, enabling real-time monitoring of up to 2,000 items. The system improves traceability, prevents fraud, and supports rapid alerts in case of theft or unauthorised movement. It enhances protection of cultural heritage, supports data-driven asset management, and delivers long-term value through improved security, transparency, and preservation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Tokenised participatory loans to finance SMEs
source_description: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) often face limited access to flexible financing instruments, while investors encounter high operational costs and fragmented processes when supporting SME growth. To address this challenge, the Spanish stock market operator BME tested a pilot for issuing participatory loans to SMEs using tokenisation. The objective was to improve efficiency, transparency and legal certainty across the lifecycle of SME financing instruments, while exploring the regulatory boundaries of distributed ledger–based markets. The pilot uses Ethereum-based tokenisation to represent participatory loans as digital assets, with smart contracts governing issuance, distribution, settlement and registration. Blockchain records ensure immutability and auditability of transactions, while automated processes reduce manual reconciliation and settlement delays. Although secondary trading was restricted under existing regulation, the pilot anticipated future frameworks such as the EU DLT Pilot Regime and updates to Spanish securities law. The results demonstrate operational efficiencies across issuance and administration, reduced processing times and lower costs for market participants. The initiative positions tokenised financing as a viable complement to traditional SME funding channels, supporting innovation in European capital markets while informing future regulatory developments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CircularTrust, waste management system
source_description: Waste management processes involve multiple actors, including public administrations, local entities, sorting plants and recycling facilities, often resulting in fragmented information flows and limited traceability. Lack of transparency can increase costs and hinder environmental performance monitoring. Stakeholders include recyclers, waste operators, public authorities and environmental organisations. The objective is to enhance transparency, efficiency and trust in the recycling value chain. The system uses blockchain technology to immutably record transactions related to waste collection, sorting and transfer. Smart contracts automate data validation and, where applicable, financial settlements. Real-time monitoring dashboards provide visibility across more than 90 sorting plants and over 70 recycling facilities, processing thousands of monthly transactions. Expected impacts include improved traceability, reduced administrative overhead, enhanced regulatory oversight, lower transaction costs and strengthened confidence among ecosystem participants, contributing to more sustainable waste management practices.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Globallogic (Nuggets) - European cross-border payments
source_description: Cross-border payments within Europe remain costly and complex due to fragmented identity verification processes, compliance checks and intermediaries. This use case, led by startup Nuggets (part of GlobalLogic), aims to simplify and secure European cross-border payments by combining decentralised identity with distributed ledger infrastructure. Stakeholders include individuals, businesses, payment providers and public authorities operating across EU jurisdictions. The objective is to enable faster, more transparent and compliant remittances while reducing friction in customer onboarding and regulatory checks. The solution uses Self-Sovereign Decentralised Identity (SSDID), allowing users to verify themselves once and reuse trusted credentials across payment services. Blockchain infrastructure supports transaction recording and validation, ensuring traceability and integrity without centralised data silos. Verifiable credentials are used to demonstrate compliance attributes, such as identity or eligibility, without exposing unnecessary personal data. Selected for the European Blockchain Sandbox, the pilot enables structured dialogue with regulators on identity, payments and compliance. The initiative shows potential to reduce transaction costs, improve user experience and enhance trust in cross-border payments, while aligning with European data protection and digital identity principles.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Internet Native Organizations
source_description: Decentralised organisations face legal uncertainty in Europe, limiting their ability to operate transparently and engage with public and private institutions. The Internet Native Organization (INO) initiative, led by non-profit startup INO MTÜ in Estonia, seeks to establish a compliant governance framework for decentralised, code-driven organisations. Stakeholders include digital communities, regulators, developers and public administrations interested in new organisational models. The objective is to enable decentralised governance structures that combine legal recognition, accountability and community participation. INO provides a governance architecture where organisational rules are embedded in code and aligned with national legal systems, particularly Estonia’s advanced e-governance environment. Distributed ledger technology is used to record governance actions, membership decisions and organisational changes in a transparent and auditable manner. Smart contracts formalise decision-making processes, while compliance-focused updates ensure alignment with evolving regulation. Selected for the European Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox, INO supports regulatory experimentation around DAOs. Its impact lies in increasing trust, legal clarity and adoption of decentralised governance models, contributing to Europe’s leadership in digital organisational innovation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: unBlock, the web3 Smartcity SuperApp
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Residents and visitors typically navigate multiple disconnected channels to discover services, buy tickets, make bookings, and pay local businesses, which increases friction and limits adoption of digital public services. Murcia’s unBlock aims to provide a single mobile entry point for day-to-day city interactions—such as purchasing event tickets, reserving restaurants or hotels, and paying in participating local commerce—while supporting more seamless authentication for digital access. Stakeholders include the City Council, local businesses and cultural venues, citizens and tourists, and European partners working on digital identity interoperability, with the objective of reducing complexity and improving uptake of city services through one consistent experience. The solution is delivered as a mobile “superapp” connected to participating service providers and payment flows, designed to align with European digital identity initiatives (including wallet-based authentication) and selected for dialogue within the European Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox to explore governance, compliance, and interoperability questions. Conceptually, the platform combines secure user onboarding, a service catalogue, and transaction orchestration, with distributed-ledger components used where auditability or verifiable credentials add value (for example, ticketing integrity and traceable vouchers), while core service fulfilment remains integrated with existing provider systems. The expected benefits include faster access to city services, improved user experience through one-click bookings and ticket display, stronger trust in digital transactions, and a scalable model that can be extended to new municipal services and merchants as adoption grows.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: EU’s Digital Identity Wallet
task: Authentication of self-sovereign Digital ID services
source_description: European citizens and businesses face fragmented digital identity systems that hinder access to cross-border public and private services. The EU Digital Identity Wallet initiative addresses this by creating a unified digital identity solution recognised across Member States. Stakeholders include citizens, businesses, banks, public authorities and service providers across the EU and associated countries. The objective is to enable secure, interoperable and user-controlled digital identity for everyday transactions, from healthcare and education to finance and transport. The EUDI Wallet allows users to store and present identity attributes and credentials securely, using distributed ledger technology to support trust and interoperability between national systems. Biometric verification and cryptographic mechanisms ensure secure authentication, while selective disclosure enables privacy-preserving data sharing. The pilot phase involves more than 250 organisations across 25 Member States and partner countries, testing real-life use cases. The initiative improves user experience, reduces duplication in identity verification and lowers costs for service providers. It represents a foundational step towards a trusted European digital identity ecosystem aligned with EU regulation and values.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Tokenised securities with payments through stablecoins
source_description: Capital market transactions remain operationally complex, with fragmented settlement processes and delayed payment cycles. This pilot, involving startups 2Tokens and Assetblocks alongside ABN AMRO and Rabobank, explores tokenised securities combined with settlement through euro-denominated stablecoins. Stakeholders include banks, investors, issuers and regulators. The objective is to test how distributed ledger–based securities and programmable money can streamline issuance, trading and settlement while remaining compliant with EU financial regulation. The solution tokenises securities as regulated digital financial instruments and uses stablecoins or tokenised bank deposits for payment. Both hosted and non-hosted wallets are supported, enabling flexible access models. Smart contracts coordinate delivery-versus-payment processes, reducing counterparty risk and settlement delays. Selected for the European Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox, the pilot facilitates structured regulatory dialogue on custody, settlement finality and investor protection. The initiative demonstrates efficiency gains, faster settlement and reduced operational risk, while informing future frameworks for digital capital markets in Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Circularity solution for Digital Product Passports
source_description: Manufacturers face increasing regulatory and market pressure to demonstrate product sustainability, traceability and circularity. Startup Twinu addresses this challenge by providing a blockchain-based solution for Digital Product Passports that supports upcoming EU regulation. Stakeholders include manufacturers, consumers, recyclers and regulators. The objective is to enable transparent lifecycle tracking of physical products while improving repairability, reuse and recycling. Twinu assigns each product a digital twin recorded on a blockchain, capturing key lifecycle events from production to end-of-life. This digital passport enables secure data sharing, customer engagement and circular business models without centralised control. The solution aligns with EU proposals for Digital Product Passports and was recognised as “Most Sustainable Solution” by Deutsche Telekom and T-Mobile. Selected for the European Blockchain Sandbox, the pilot demonstrates how distributed ledgers can operationalise circular economy principles. The impact includes improved transparency, stronger customer trust and actionable sustainability insights, supporting both regulatory compliance and long-term environmental value creation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Public Administrations Interoperability
source_description: The Public Administrations Interoperability project leverages the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) to enable secure cross-border exchange of verifiable attestations among regional and local governments. Citizens moving between jurisdictions often face administrative friction due to fragmented recognition of official attributes. The project develops a presentation and verification platform based on the EU Self-Sovereign Identity trust model. Governments issue verifiable credentials anchored on EBSI, while citizens retain control of their digital attestations through digital wallets. Distributed ledger technology ensures integrity and trust in credential verification without centralised intermediaries. The system supports mutual recognition agreements among participating authorities, enhancing administrative cooperation and service continuity. By embedding citizens as active holders of credentials, the initiative strengthens interoperability, reduces administrative burden and supports seamless public service access across regions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: University of Extremadura and Western University of Arad
title: Educational Identification in Europe
source_description: The Educational Identification in Europe project aims to create a cross-border architecture for student identification using verifiable educational credentials. Students studying or moving across EU countries face challenges in presenting and validating academic status. The initiative combines digital wallets, verifiable credentials and blockchain infrastructure within the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure to enable secure issuance, storage and presentation of student IDs. Universities issue credentials in a machine-readable format, which students control and present when required. Verification occurs through decentralised blockchain-based validation mechanisms, ensuring integrity and authenticity without exposing unnecessary personal data. The project involves universities and IT providers from Spain, Romania and Ireland. By enabling portable and secure student identification, the initiative supports seamless cross-border learning, reduces administrative overhead and strengthens trust in digital academic credentials across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Universities of Strasbourg, Deusto, Politehnica University of Timisoara and Lideea
title: Cross-border cross-university micro-credentials in Europe
source_description: A European consortium of universities, IT providers and research organisations is developing a blockchain-based platform to issue and verify micro-credentials across borders. Traditional education systems often struggle to recognise short courses and modular achievements, limiting learner mobility. The project uses eDiplomas formatted as verifiable credentials and anchored on the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure. Learners receive micro-credentials stored in digital wallets, allowing them to present standalone or bundled achievements to institutions and employers. Distributed ledger validation ensures authenticity and cross-border trust without centralised verification requests. The platform facilitates issuance, recognition and acceptance of digital certificates among participating universities in France, Spain and Romania. By enhancing portability and transparency of skills recognition, the initiative supports lifelong learning and European mobility. It strengthens the credibility of micro-credentials and promotes harmonised digital certification standards across higher education systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Greek Ministry of Education, the Greek University Network (GUNet), and the University of Lausanne
title: Formal Accreditation and Recognition
source_description: The Formal Accreditation and Recognition project brings together universities and public authorities from Spain, Switzerland and Greece to modernise cross-institution degree recognition. Students applying to programmes in other countries often encounter administrative delays and verification challenges. The initiative uses Web3 technologies and the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure to issue and verify eDiplomas and transcripts as verifiable credentials. Digital wallets enable students to present academic records securely, while decentralised verification ensures authenticity without repeated institutional checks. The platform integrates accreditation authorities and university networks to streamline recognition processes. By reducing data protection risks and simplifying cross-border applications, the project enhances mobility within European higher education. It promotes secure, interoperable credential exchange and supports next-generation decentralised public services in academic administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: University of Strasbourg, Chamber of Handicrafts Dresden, RISE, Fraunhofer IFAM and GovPart
title: Vocational Education & Training
source_description: The Vocational Education and Training (VET) project leverages the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) to modernise the issuance and recognition of vocational qualifications across Europe. VET systems are governed by networks of social partners, including employers and trade unions, which often rely on fragmented administrative processes and non-standardised data models. This creates inefficiencies, prolonged verification timelines and reliance on intermediaries for credential validation. The project develops a Web3-based infrastructure enabling the issuance of vocational certificates as verifiable credentials anchored on EBSI. Learners store credentials in digital wallets and present them directly to employers or authorities, who can verify authenticity through decentralised validation mechanisms. Standardised data models enhance interoperability among chambers, councils and institutions. By reducing administrative complexity and strengthening trust in digital verification, the initiative supports cross-border labour mobility and improves transparency in skills recognition. The approach enhances privacy by allowing individuals to control credential sharing while ensuring reliable authentication of vocational qualifications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid, University of Strasbourg
title: Employment credentials
source_description: The Employment Credentials project aims to simplify verification of professional skills and work experience across European labour markets. Current hiring processes often rely on paper certificates, PDFs or self-declared CVs, requiring time-consuming manual verification by employers. The initiative establishes a decentralised system for issuing and validating employment credentials using the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure. Employers or authorised bodies issue verifiable credentials representing professional experience, which individuals store in secure digital wallets. Verification occurs through cryptographic validation on the blockchain, confirming authenticity without contacting previous employers. The system reduces fraud risks, accelerates recruitment processes and strengthens cross-border mobility by providing a trusted framework for recognising qualifications. By enabling direct, tamper-evident authentication of employment history, the project enhances efficiency in human resources management and supports a more transparent European labour market ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Development of in Silico Methodologies to Predict the Toxicity of Proteins in Food and Feed Risk Assessment
source_description: Assessing the safety of novel proteins in food and feed is complex, time-consuming and often reliant on experimental testing. Regulatory authorities seek faster, reliable methods to support risk assessment. The objective of this initiative is to identify computational methodologies capable of predicting protein toxicity and associated mechanisms. The implementation explores sequence-based, structural and machine-learning approaches to identify homology with known toxic proteins and detect molecular signatures linked to toxicity. The work focuses on methodology identification and validation criteria rather than operational deployment. Expected impacts include improved efficiency of risk assessment, reduced reliance on animal testing and stronger scientific consistency. Qualitative benefits include enhanced regulatory decision support and scalable foundations for future safety assessment tools.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AICEBlock
source_description: Organisations deploying algorithmic systems in sensitive domains such as healthcare and public administration face stringent requirements for auditability, traceability and regulatory compliance. Fragmented documentation and limited transparency can undermine trust, particularly in collaborative development contexts involving multiple stakeholders. The objective of AICEBlock is to create a certification platform that enhances trust in algorithmic applications by ensuring verifiability of development and operational processes. The solution leverages blockchain technology to register model metadata, training records, versioning information and decision logs in an immutable ledger. Smart contracts manage certification workflows, while cryptographic mechanisms ensure integrity and traceability of updates across training and production environments. The platform supports compliance with regulatory standards, including data protection requirements, and facilitates the integration of interpretability layers. Expected impacts include strengthened user trust, improved audit readiness, reduced compliance risks and enhanced transparency in high-stakes deployments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Contracting, Projects and Works Service Dept of Regional Government
title: AI and ML for the Galician Public Employment Service
source_description: The Galician Public Employment Service launched a project, funded under REACT-EU within the ESF Operational Programme Galicia 2014–2020, to develop a decision-support system using artificial intelligence and machine learning. The objective is to enhance labour market policy design and operational decision-making through advanced data analytics. The system integrates employment records, service usage data and socioeconomic indicators into a central analytical environment. Machine-learning models generate predictive insights and classification outputs to support case management, programme evaluation and resource allocation. Visualisation tools are embedded within existing service applications to present actionable indicators to staff. The cloud-based infrastructure supports scalable data processing and secure integration with institutional systems. By automating analysis and providing evidence-based recommendations, the solution improves efficiency, strengthens policy responsiveness and enhances service quality for job seekers. The initiative contributes to digital transformation of employment services in Galicia.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SMARTECOMOUNTAINS Project in Andalusia
source_description: The SMARTECOMOUNTAINS project, led by the University of Granada within the LifeWatch ERIC research infrastructure, develops advanced digital tools to study biodiversity and global change in mountain ecosystems. Focusing on the Sierra Nevada as a case study, the project addresses the need for reliable, interoperable and reusable environmental data to support research and policy decisions. The initiative integrates deep learning and data analytics methods to process large-scale ecological datasets, including biodiversity records and ecosystem indicators. A structured Data Management Plan ensures traceability, accessibility and interoperability of collected information. The project also develops technological services facilitating data exchange and analysis among scientists, alongside educational and decision-support tools for policymakers and the public. By combining artificial intelligence with environmental monitoring, SMARTECOMOUNTAINS enhances understanding of climate impacts and ecosystem services in mountainous regions while promoting science-based governance and sustainable development strategies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Flanders Research Institute for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (ILVO)
title: AI4AGRIFOOD platform in Flanders - Precision agriculture and data technology
source_description: Agricultural research institutions increasingly rely on data science and advanced analytics, yet researchers often face barriers in accessing user-friendly tools that accommodate varying levels of technical expertise. Within Flanders, the challenge is to democratise the use of advanced analytics across agrifood research while fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing. Stakeholders include ILVO researchers, innovation managers and technology providers. The objective is to establish a platform that enables both experienced and less technically specialised users to apply machine learning methods in agricultural research contexts. The envisaged solution includes a modular platform with graphical user interfaces, low-code functionalities and integrated machine learning libraries. It supports experiment management, model training and deployment within secure research environments, enabling collaborative workflows. Anticipated impacts include accelerated experimentation, improved research productivity, broader uptake of advanced analytics and strengthened innovation capacity in precision agriculture.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Artificial intelligence in operational forest management planning
source_description: Managing state-owned forests requires balancing economic use, environmental protection, and social value, while operating across large and diverse territories. Metsähallitus needed more precise data to support operational planning and sustainable timber harvesting. This use case involves the Finnish state forestry organisation, planners, and technology providers, with the objective of improving decision-making in forest management. The solution is implemented through advanced data-driven models that generate assortment-level timber yield predictions, which are integrated into operational planning systems. These predictions complement existing forestry data and enable more accurate planning of harvesting, logistics, and conservation activities. The solution improves planning accuracy, supports sustainability goals, and reduces uncertainty in operational decisions. It enhances efficiency, optimises resource use, and delivers long-term value by supporting responsible management of public land and natural resources.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Lille Metropole Smart Sensors
source_description: Lille Métropole partnered with VizioSense to research, prototype and deploy intelligent parking sensors aimed at optimising management of public parking spaces. Urban congestion and inefficient parking allocation create traffic delays and environmental impacts. The project implemented AI-enabled sensors capable of detecting vehicle presence and transmitting real-time occupancy data to central management systems. Machine-learning algorithms enhance detection accuracy and support predictive analytics for space availability. The initiative followed a phased approach combining research and development with prototype acquisition through a framework agreement. Real-time data feeds inform navigation tools, guiding drivers to available spaces and reducing circulation time. By integrating sensor networks with intelligent analytics, the city improves traffic flow, reduces emissions and enhances user experience. The project demonstrates how smart infrastructure and data-driven parking management can support sustainable urban mobility strategies.

title: Imatra Street AI project
source_description: The Street AI Innovation Partnership in Imatra developed a cloud-based platform to enhance street maintenance through real-time data integration and analytics. Municipal authorities require accurate information on traffic volumes, snow cover and road conditions to optimise maintenance activities. The project created a digital environment for data storage, analysis and visualisation, integrating sensor inputs and artificial intelligence models. Real-time dashboards present current street conditions, supporting decision-making and resource allocation. The initiative also tests augmented reality applications and advanced sensor technologies to improve situational awareness. By targeting maintenance activities more precisely, the system reduces operational costs, improves service levels and minimises environmental impact. The platform enhances transparency and efficiency in urban infrastructure management while supporting long-term digital transformation in municipal services.

title: Robotics and artificial intelligence solutions for Helsinki City Central Library
source_description: Helsinki City Central Library (Oodi) implemented robotics and artificial intelligence solutions to improve operational efficiency and user services in a high-traffic public library environment. Managing large volumes of returned materials and maintaining organised collections requires significant staff resources. The project introduced automated robotic systems for sorting and handling books, integrated with intelligent software capable of recognising and categorising items. AI-supported logistics optimise internal workflows and support accurate shelving and inventory management. The system interfaces with the library’s catalogue and circulation databases to ensure real-time updates. By automating repetitive handling tasks, the solution reduces manual workload, shortens processing times and enhances service quality for visitors. The initiative supports innovative public service delivery and demonstrates how robotics can improve efficiency in cultural and educational institutions while preserving human interaction for user-facing services.

title: Central Bohemian Region to test on-demand public transport
source_description: The Central Bohemian Region launched an innovation partnership to design and implement a system optimising public transport service settings, including testing on-demand transport solutions. The region faces challenges in balancing cost efficiency and accessibility, particularly in less densely populated areas where fixed routes may be underused. The objective is to develop a data-driven platform capable of aggregating multi-source datasets, including passenger flows, ticketing data and broader mobility indicators. The selected partner is responsible for building the system in line with minimum technical requirements defined by the contracting authority. The solution will process large-scale datasets to model demand patterns, optimise route planning and support adaptive scheduling. By enabling dynamic configuration of services, the platform aims to improve service coverage, reduce operational inefficiencies and enhance responsiveness to passenger needs. The initiative supports evidence-based mobility planning and contributes to more flexible and sustainable regional transport management.

title: City of Herne road maintance with AI
source_description: Urban road networks require continuous monitoring and timely maintenance to ensure safety and cost efficiency. In Herne, managing a 380 km road network posed challenges in data integration, prioritisation and long-term planning. Stakeholders include municipal authorities, infrastructure managers and contractors. The objective is to enable proactive maintenance through data-driven analysis and integrated infrastructure modelling. The solution applies computer vision and predictive analytics to assess road conditions, integrating collected data into a Building Information Modelling (BIM) environment. Over time, enriched BIM models contribute to a digital twin of the road infrastructure, enabling scenario simulations and lifecycle planning. By analysing deterioration patterns and maintenance histories, the system supports optimised intervention scheduling. Expected impacts include reduced data acquisition costs, improved decision-making accuracy, enhanced road safety and more efficient allocation of maintenance budgets.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: City of Prague AI Traffic Management System
source_description: Urban congestion at major transport hubs leads to delays, increased emissions and reduced public transport reliability. Prague seeks to improve traffic flow while maintaining priority for tram services. Stakeholders include municipal transport authorities, road users and public transport operators. The objective is to implement an adaptive traffic management system capable of responding dynamically to real-time conditions. The system employs multi-agent and adaptive control algorithms that process live video and sensor data to assess vehicle counts, flow intensity and directional patterns. Optimisation models generate real-time signalling plans to coordinate intersections and prioritise public transport. Integration with existing traffic infrastructure ensures operational continuity. Anticipated impacts include smoother traffic flow, reduced congestion-related emissions, enhanced tram punctuality and improved overall transport efficiency.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electricity Transmission Network Planning
source_description: France’s electricity transmission operator RTE initiated an innovation partnership to develop advanced analytical tools supporting long-term grid adaptation strategies. The energy transition introduces complexity in forecasting demand, integrating renewables and maintaining grid stability. The project aims to equip research managers with decision-support tools to formulate hypotheses, interpret modelling results and optimise network planning scenarios. The partnership is structured in three phases: prototype design, operational development and testing, followed by acquisition for broader deployment. The system integrates large-scale network data, simulation outputs and predictive modelling techniques to evaluate infrastructure adaptation strategies. By enhancing analytical capabilities, the solution improves scenario assessment, accelerates research workflows and strengthens evidence-based investment planning. The initiative contributes to preparing the transmission network for decarbonisation and increased electrification while ensuring reliability and cost efficiency in grid development.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI Platform for to support primary healthcare in Regione Puglia
source_description: Primary healthcare providers manage diverse patient needs, often requiring timely diagnostic support and coordinated care pathways. Fragmented information systems can limit efficiency and consistency. Stakeholders include regional health authorities, general practitioners and patients. The objective is to design, implement and manage a comprehensive platform that enhances decision support and service coordination in primary care. The solution integrates clinical data repositories, predictive analytics models and decision-support algorithms within a secure digital infrastructure. Functionalities may include risk stratification, early detection of chronic conditions and workflow optimisation tools embedded in clinical systems. Interoperability standards ensure integration with existing regional health information systems. Expected impacts include improved care continuity, earlier identification of high-risk patients, reduced administrative burden and enhanced quality of primary healthcare delivery.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Virtual assistant on the eportugal portal for information about the Digital Mobile Key (CMD)
source_description: The Portuguese government introduced a virtual assistant on the ePortugal portal to support citizens using the Digital Mobile Key (Chave Móvel Digital). Users frequently require guidance on activation, unlocking, updating personal data and applying digital signatures. The assistant provides conversational support through voice and text interfaces integrated into the national public services portal. Natural language processing interprets user queries and retrieves structured information from official guidance databases. The system offers step-by-step instructions and directs users to relevant digital procedures, while complex identity or security issues are handled through established support channels. By automating responses to common enquiries, the assistant enhances accessibility, reduces service centre workload and promotes adoption of secure digital identity tools. The initiative strengthens digital public service delivery and improves user experience in accessing e-government services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Automated evaluations of applications at NAV
source_description: NAV processes a very large number of benefit applications each year, and manual handling of all cases can lead to delays and inconsistent outcomes. This use case addresses the need to improve efficiency while ensuring decisions comply with legislation. It involves NAV, applicants, and public authorities, with the objective of delivering faster and more consistent benefit decisions. The solution is implemented through automated decision systems that check applications against legal criteria for benefits such as child benefit, unemployment benefit, pensions, and parental benefits. The system verifies eligibility, determines benefit levels and duration, and generates formal decisions without human intervention for eligible cases. Integrated with NAV’s case management systems, it ensures transparency and traceability. The solution significantly reduces processing times, frees staff to focus on complex cases, and improves service quality for citizens. It delivers scalable efficiency gains, legal consistency, and sustainable public administration value.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: New AI-Powered Cameras Spot Distracted Drivers in the UK
source_description: Road safety authorities in the United Kingdom face persistent risks from distracted driving and seatbelt non-compliance, contributing to preventable accidents and injuries. To strengthen enforcement, new roadside camera systems have been deployed to detect motorists using handheld mobile phones or failing to wear seatbelts. High-resolution cameras capture images of passing vehicles, which are processed using computer vision algorithms trained to identify prohibited behaviours. Suspected violations are reviewed by police officers before penalties are issued, ensuring human oversight in enforcement decisions. The system integrates with existing traffic monitoring infrastructure and supports evidence-based processing of offences. Drivers face fines of up to £500 for seatbelt violations and up to £1,000 with six penalty points for mobile phone use while driving. The technology enhances detection accuracy and enforcement efficiency, acting as a deterrent and contributing to improved compliance, reduced accident risk and safer road environments.

title: AI camera system catches litter louts in Loughborough
source_description: Littering in public spaces imposes environmental, financial and social costs on local authorities and communities. In Loughborough, an intelligent camera system was deployed on Warwick Way to deter and detect individuals discarding waste from vehicles. The system operates alongside automatic number plate recognition infrastructure, capturing footage of passing traffic and applying computer vision techniques to identify littering incidents. Detected cases are verified and linked to vehicle registration data for enforcement action. During the trial period, 28 fines of £150 were issued, and a 37 % reduction in litter was recorded in the monitored area. The initiative demonstrates how targeted technological interventions can modify behaviour and improve environmental outcomes. By combining automated detection with established enforcement mechanisms, the project enhances operational efficiency and supports cleaner urban spaces, while providing measurable evidence of impact to inform future deployment decisions.

title: NHS AI test spots tiny cancers missed by doctors
source_description: Early detection of breast cancer significantly improves treatment outcomes, yet subtle abnormalities in mammograms can be difficult to identify consistently. The NHS piloted a diagnostic support tool alongside clinicians to assess its effectiveness in analysing breast screening images. The system processed mammograms from over 10,000 women, the majority of whom were cancer-free, and was evaluated in parallel with standard clinical assessment. Advanced image analysis models examined patterns and anomalies within scans to flag potential cases requiring further review. The tool successfully identified all women diagnosed with cancer and additionally detected 11 cases that had not been initially recognised by human readers. Results indicate potential to enhance sensitivity in screening programmes while supporting clinician decision-making. The technology may reduce missed diagnoses, improve early intervention rates and increase overall efficiency of breast cancer screening services through augmented image analysis.

title: French police test AI-powered security cameras ahead of Olympics
source_description: Large-scale public events such as the Olympic Games require robust security arrangements capable of detecting risks in real time while managing dense crowds. France introduced legislation permitting a temporary trial of intelligent video surveillance to identify predefined abnormal events during major gatherings. The system was tested at a large concert, analysing live video feeds using pattern recognition algorithms trained to detect eight categories of incidents, including crowd surges, abandoned objects, fires and the presence of weapons. Alerts are transmitted to security personnel for assessment and response, maintaining human oversight in operational decisions. An evaluation committee monitors the deployment to safeguard civil liberties during the trial period. The initiative aims to enhance situational awareness, accelerate response times and improve crowd safety management during high-profile events. By integrating automated event detection with existing security frameworks, the system supports proactive risk mitigation while operating within a regulated governance structure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Dublin City Council and OpenAI Announce Partnership to Show the Potential of AI to Support Europe’s Tourism Industry
source_description: Tourism authorities aim to enhance visitor experiences by providing personalised, engaging recommendations that go beyond static guides. Dublin sought to demonstrate how advanced language technologies could support tailored travel planning. Stakeholders include the city council, tourism agencies, technology partners and visitors. The objective is to develop a proof of concept itinerary planner capable of generating bespoke daily travel plans. The solution leverages a large language model to interpret user preferences and generate contextualised recommendations, drawing on curated cultural, historical and event data. Prompt engineering and content filtering mechanisms ensure relevance and safety, while integration with tourism information databases enriches outputs. Expected impacts include more personalised visitor experiences, increased engagement with local attractions and demonstration of innovative digital tourism services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: OrQA - Organ Quality Assessment - the technology scans images of organs to look at suitability for kidney and liver transplant
source_description: Organ transplantation depends on rapid and accurate assessment of donor organs, yet decisions about suitability are complex and time-sensitive, and clinicians must often judge quality under conditions of uncertainty. OrQA was developed to support this process by helping specialists assess whether organs are suitable for kidney and liver transplantation through faster and more consistent image-based evaluation. The objective is to improve transplant decision-making, make better use of donated organs, and increase the number of patients who can benefit from successful transplants. The implementation uses an image-analysis approach that scans pictures of organs and applies algorithmic assessment techniques to identify features associated with transplant suitability. Developed by the University of Bradford and Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, the tool is designed to assist clinicians rather than replace human judgement. At a conceptual level, the system uses large image sets to build an assessment model that can support transplant teams with an additional evidence layer during organ evaluation. Reported expectations for the technology suggest that it could help increase the number of kidney and liver transplants carried out in the UK each year. The impact includes the potential for quicker and more reliable assessment, better use of scarce donor organs, and improved outcomes for patients awaiting transplant, alongside operational gains in a highly specialised clinical pathway.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ChatGPT-powered GOV.UK chatbot on trial
source_description: Citizens accessing GOV.UK often need to navigate large volumes of content to find relevant information about public services, benefits and regulations. To improve accessibility and user experience, the Government Digital Service conducted public trials of a conversational chatbot designed to provide direct, human-like responses to user queries. The objective was to assess feasibility, usefulness and risks before any wider deployment. The prototype uses large language model technology to retrieve and summarise information from existing GOV.UK content, generating responses grounded in official sources. The system was tested with members of the public, and feedback mechanisms were embedded to evaluate answer quality, clarity and reliability. Survey results indicated that around 65 % of participants were satisfied overall and 70 % found the responses useful, while issues of accuracy and consistency were identified. The trial adopted a cautious, iterative approach with human oversight and evaluation. Findings support further experimentation while highlighting the need for robust safeguards, quality assurance and governance to ensure trustworthy digital public services.

title: Barcelona tests with a digital twin if it is a 15-minute city
source_description: Urban policymakers seek to ensure that residents can access essential services within a 15-minute walk or cycle, yet measuring such accessibility across complex city environments is challenging. Barcelona tested a digital twin platform to assess whether it meets the criteria of the 15-minute city model. The web-based tool integrates geospatial data on public facilities, transport networks and population distribution into a dynamic urban simulation environment. Accessibility algorithms calculate travel times to schools, healthcare, green spaces and other amenities under different mobility scenarios. The platform enables planners to visualise service gaps and simulate the impact of infrastructure changes in a three-dimensional environment. By combining spatial analytics and interactive modelling, the system supports evidence-based urban planning decisions. The initiative enhances transparency in policy evaluation, enables targeted interventions to reduce inequality in service provision and strengthens long-term strategies for sustainable, liveable neighbourhoods.

title: UrbanistAI, a generative AI platform for participatory planning and co-design: Helsinki use case
source_description: Engaging citizens and local entrepreneurs in urban planning processes can be resource-intensive and limited by traditional consultation formats. The City of Helsinki piloted a participatory approach using a generative design platform to broaden stakeholder involvement in shaping neighbourhood development. During moderated workshops, participants explored alternative visions for specific urban areas and expressed preferences regarding functions and land use. The platform uses generative image models to produce multiple visual scenarios based on user inputs, enabling rapid visualisation of design concepts. City officials and consultants facilitated discussions, ensuring that outputs aligned with planning constraints and policy objectives. The interactive format encouraged dialogue and collective refinement of ideas. The initiative demonstrates how digital co-design tools can enhance inclusivity, stimulate creative thinking and provide structured feedback for planners. By accelerating scenario generation and visual communication, the platform supports more transparent and responsive urban development processes.

title: City of Bologna digital twin
source_description: The City of Bologna is addressing complex urban challenges related to sustainable mobility, energy efficiency, and climate change mitigation, which require coordinated planning across multiple policy domains. City planners, utilities, transport authorities, and citizens all need reliable evidence to support long-term infrastructure investments and behavioural change. The objective of the digital twin initiative is to provide an integrated decision-support environment that allows the city to analyse current conditions and simulate future scenarios before implementing policies or investments. The solution is implemented through a digital replica of the city that integrates data from sensors, administrative systems, and qualitative social data. In mobility, the model combines traffic counts, environmental sensors, and citizen feedback to assess the impact of cycling lanes and tram infrastructure. In the energy domain, it simulates building energy performance to evaluate renovation strategies, incentives, and urban plans aimed at achieving net-zero targets. The digital twin enables scenario testing and cross-sector analysis within a shared platform. As a result, Bologna can design more coherent policies, reduce planning risks, and prioritise investments with higher sustainability impact. The initiative improves transparency, supports data-driven governance, and strengthens the city’s capacity to plan resilient and climate-neutral urban development.

organization: Amsterdam Institute for Advanced Metropolitan Solutions (AMS)
title: Roboat - an autonomous fleet for Amsterdam
source_description: Amsterdam’s canal network presents opportunities for innovative transport and urban services, yet managing congestion, waste collection and logistics in dense waterways is complex. The Roboat project, a collaboration between MIT and the Amsterdam Institute for Advanced Metropolitan Solutions, aims to develop a fleet of autonomous boats capable of performing multiple urban functions. The vessels are equipped with sensors, localisation systems and autonomous navigation software to operate safely within busy canal environments. Modular designs allow reconfiguration for tasks such as passenger transport, goods delivery or waste collection. Fleet coordination algorithms optimise routing and docking operations, while data exchange systems integrate with city infrastructure. Prototypes are tested under real conditions to validate safety and operational efficiency. The initiative explores scalable water-based mobility solutions that reduce road congestion and emissions, contributing to more flexible and sustainable urban transport systems.

title: Digital twin of the City of Pilsen
source_description: The City of Pilsen is advancing its Smart City strategy across mobility, environment, security and public participation, requiring integrated tools to support data-driven decision-making. To enhance understanding of urban dynamics, the city is developing a digital twin that interrelates transport patterns and noise pollution within a three-dimensional environment. The platform aggregates traffic data, environmental measurements and spatial information into a unified simulation model. Analytical modules assess correlations between mobility flows and acoustic impact, enabling scenario testing for infrastructure changes or traffic management interventions. Visualisation tools allow planners to explore outcomes in a realistic 3D context, improving stakeholder communication. By linking environmental and transport indicators, the digital twin supports more holistic urban policy evaluation. Expected benefits include improved mobility planning, reduced noise exposure and enhanced quality of life, while providing a scalable framework for integrating additional smart city datasets over time.

title: Albania to speed up EU accession using ChatGPT
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Aligning national legislation with the European Union acquis requires the translation, interpretation, and integration of very large volumes of legal and regulatory material, making accession an administratively demanding and time-intensive process. In Albania, the government presented this use case as a way to accelerate that work by using ChatGPT to translate EU legal measures and assist with incorporating them into Albanian legal structures. The objective is to reduce the manual burden associated with legal translation and alignment, shorten paperwork timelines, and support faster progress towards EU accession. The implementation uses a large language model to process legal text, support translation into Albanian, and assist with the comparison and integration of EU provisions into the domestic legislative framework. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as a language and legal-text processing assistant for officials dealing with approximation of legislation, rather than as an autonomous decision-maker. The expected impact includes faster handling of large legal-text volumes, reduced administrative effort, and improved capacity to manage a complex accession workload. It also illustrates how generative language technology can be used in public administration to support large-scale legal harmonisation and strategic policy objectives.

title: SOCIAbLE - Social Cognitive Interventions following Adverse early Life Experiences
source_description: Individuals who have experienced childhood trauma often face persistent cognitive and social difficulties that affect mental health and daily functioning. The SOCIAbLE project aims to develop and evaluate a novel psychosocial intervention designed to address these challenges. Researchers are creating a virtual reality-based therapeutic programme that targets social cognition, emotional processing and interpersonal skills. The intervention immerses participants in controlled virtual environments where they can practise social interactions and coping strategies under guided supervision. Data collected during sessions inform adaptive adjustments to therapeutic scenarios, supporting personalised progression. Feasibility studies assess usability, acceptability and preliminary clinical benefits to inform future large-scale trials. By combining immersive technology with evidence-based psychological approaches, the project seeks to enhance resilience and social functioning in individuals affected by early adverse experiences, contributing to improved long-term mental health outcomes.

title: PERCEIVE - Perceptive Enhanced Realities of Colored collEctions through AI and Virtual Experiences
source_description: Cultural heritage institutions face growing interest in digitally preserving and presenting ancient artefacts while addressing gaps in historical understanding, particularly around the original appearance of classical sculptures. Many Greek and Roman statues were originally painted, but their polychromy has been lost over time, limiting public understanding and scholarly interpretation. This use case addresses these challenges by enabling accurate study, reconstruction, and exhibition of coloured cultural heritage, involving researchers, museums, educators, and creative industries. The PERCEIVE project is implemented through advanced image analysis, digital reconstruction techniques, and immersive visualisation technologies that analyse traces of pigment and material data to recreate original colours. These reconstructions are rendered through extended reality and hybrid exhibition formats, supported by a service-based digital architecture and dedicated design toolkits for education and creative reuse. The project improves the accuracy and accessibility of cultural heritage interpretation, enriches visitor experience through immersive storytelling, and supports new educational and creative applications. It delivers lasting value by combining scientific research with engaging digital experiences, strengthening preservation, knowledge transfer, and public appreciation of Europe’s cultural heritage.

title: TIMELAPSE - A VR application for speeding up time passage during chemotherapy
source_description: Chemotherapy treatments often involve long, stressful sessions that can negatively affect patients’ psychological well-being. The TIMELAPSE project aims to prototype and validate a virtual reality application designed to alter subjective time perception, making treatment sessions feel shorter and less burdensome. Developed by a multidisciplinary consortium including research, clinical and industrial partners, the application immerses patients in carefully designed virtual environments that modulate attention and emotional engagement. Cognitive science principles guide the design of interactive experiences intended to influence perceived duration. Clinical testing in oncology settings evaluates feasibility, patient acceptance and effects on well-being indicators. Data collected during trials support iterative refinement of the application. By improving patient experience without altering medical procedures, the solution has potential to enhance quality of care, reduce anxiety and support broader adoption of digital therapeutic tools in clinical environments.

organization: Università degli Studi di Roma La Spaienza
title: BRAINmade - Against prostheses abandonment: immersive and low-cost platform for the rehabilitation of upper-limb amputees
source_description: Upper-limb prosthesis abandonment rates can reach 44 %, often due to limited functionality, discomfort and insufficient rehabilitation support. BRAINmade seeks to reduce abandonment by improving motor training and user adaptation through an accessible rehabilitation platform. The project develops immersive virtual reality scenarios controlled by electromyographic (EMG) signals generated by residual limb muscles. Customised, low-cost EMG sensors capture muscle activity and translate it into movements within virtual training environments, enabling patients to practise control strategies even with non-anthropomorphic prostheses. A structured four-week motor training programme reinforces neuromuscular coordination and embodiment of the device. The system integrates hardware and software components designed for affordability and scalability in clinical settings. Early results indicate improved motor performance and user engagement. By enhancing functional outcomes and confidence, the platform aims to lower prosthesis rejection rates, improve quality of life for amputees and modernise rehabilitation practices through cost-effective, technology-enabled training.

title: KATSIM - Cataract Simulator Diagnostics Device Development Using Computational Holographic Displays
source_description: Cataract surgery outcomes depend heavily on selecting the most suitable intraocular lens, yet predicting postoperative visual perception remains challenging. The KATSIM project aims to develop a diagnostic device that simulates how patients will see after surgery, supporting personalised clinical decisions. The system uses computational holography to recreate realistic visual distortions associated with different cataract conditions and lens options. Advanced optical modelling and image processing algorithms generate holographic projections that replicate patient-specific vision scenarios. Clinicians can visualise and compare expected outcomes before intervention, improving lens selection accuracy. The project brings together expertise in computational holography, ophthalmology and vision science to validate the technology in clinical environments. By enabling more precise preoperative assessment, the device has potential to improve patient satisfaction, reduce revision procedures and optimise surgical planning. The innovation enhances shared decision-making between clinicians and patients and supports more predictable, outcome-oriented cataract treatment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-OBSERVER - Enhancing Earth Observation capabilities of the Eratosthenes Centre of Excellence on Disaster Risk Reduction through Artificial Intelligence
source_description: Effective disaster risk reduction relies on timely and accurate Earth observation data, yet integrating large-scale satellite and environmental datasets into operational decision-making remains complex. AI-OBSERVER aims to strengthen the Earth observation capabilities of the ERATOSTHENES Centre of Excellence in Cyprus by advancing analytical methods for multi-hazard monitoring and assessment. The project combines satellite imagery, geospatial datasets and environmental indicators with advanced machine learning models to improve detection and prediction of natural hazards. Through collaboration with leading research institutions, the initiative enhances technical expertise, research management capacity and innovation potential. Computational tools are developed to automate hazard mapping, risk modelling and impact assessment workflows. Capacity-building activities upgrade infrastructure and support knowledge transfer in disaster risk applications. Expected outcomes include improved scientific excellence, faster hazard assessment and stronger regional resilience. The project positions the centre as a leader in integrating advanced analytics with Earth observation for environmental risk management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: RadioVal - International Clinical Validation of Radiomics Artificial Intelligence for Breast Cancer Treatment Planning
source_description: Radiomics has the potential to support more personalised cancer treatment, but its clinical adoption is limited by the lack of large-scale validation, consistency across centres, and evidence of real-world usability. In breast cancer care, clinicians need reliable tools to predict how patients will respond to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in order to avoid unnecessary treatment and optimise outcomes. The RadioVal project addresses this challenge by bringing together hospitals, clinicians, researchers, and technology developers across eight clinical sites in Europe and beyond, with the objective of validating radiomics-based decision support in routine breast cancer treatment planning. The project implements advanced radiomics pipelines that extract quantitative features from medical imaging data, combined with machine learning models trained to predict treatment response. These tools are evaluated using harmonised imaging datasets and clinical data, and assessed across multiple dimensions, including technical robustness, algorithmic fairness, clinical usability, and acceptance by healthcare professionals, with integration into existing clinical workflows. The project strengthens confidence in data-driven imaging tools, supports more precise treatment decisions, and aims to reduce over-treatment while improving patient outcomes. By providing robust clinical validation and usability evidence, RadioVal contributes to increased trust, scalability, and responsible adoption of advanced imaging analytics in oncology.
source_license: CC BY 4.0
