organization: Ministry of Digital Governance and Ministry of Interior
title: MitosLOD: Exporting Linked Open Data from the Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services
source_description: MitosLOD enhances the Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services by making information on public services easier to search, retrieve and understand. The operational issue is that administrative service catalogues can be difficult for citizens, businesses and public officials to navigate when information is structured around formal terminology rather than the way users naturally express their needs. The project therefore aims to improve access to the MITOS registry through more intuitive, accurate and multilingual search functions. Its implementation combines Linked Open Data, semantic technologies, natural language processing and artificial intelligence techniques to interpret the meaning and intent behind user queries. Instead of relying only on keyword matching, the semantic search engine analyses relationships between public-service descriptions and translates natural-language questions into structured, machine-readable formats. This allows the system to return more relevant results and support multilingual access to registry content. Conceptually, the solution links public-service metadata, semantic relationships, NLP query interpretation and structured retrieval over the registry. The expected impact is a better user experience, more effective discovery of administrative services and improved reuse of public-sector information. By transforming registry data into semantically searchable content, MitosLOD supports transparency, accessibility and more efficient interaction with public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: E-peitharxika - an integrated information system to monitor the forms of disciplinary proceedings and disciplinary cases
source_description: The Greek public sector needed a more consistent and transparent way to manage disciplinary proceedings across a very large and fragmented administrative landscape. Before the introduction of a unified system, monitoring disciplinary cases across thousands of public bodies was difficult, limiting oversight, comparability and timely access to evidence for decision-making. E-peitharxika was developed to address this governance problem by creating a single point of supervision for the full lifecycle of disciplinary cases, from investigation and hearings to appeals and enforcement. The stakeholders include public bodies, disciplinary authorities, employees, policymakers and the wider public, with the objective of improving accountability, standardising oversight and strengthening trust in disciplinary justice. The solution is implemented as an integrated digital platform covering more than 2,000 public bodies and approximately 520,000 employees. At a conceptual level, the system consolidates case data, supports real-time statistical reporting, interoperates with national human-resources registries and exposes reusable datasets through a REST API, all on a secure, high-availability infrastructure using Azure G-Cloud services and ISO-aligned controls for security, quality and accessibility. The impact includes stronger transparency, more efficient supervision and better evidence for policymaking, supported by public access to statistical data. More broadly, the platform creates value by improving institutional integrity, enabling uniform and systematic oversight, and modernising a sensitive area of public administration through interoperable digital governance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Alliance for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC)
source_description: Europe’s language-technology landscape is fragmented by market size, linguistic diversity, and unequal access to high-quality data and infrastructure, which makes it difficult to build competitive large language models and related tools across all European languages. ALT-EDIC addresses this challenge by creating a common European infrastructure for language technologies, with a particular focus on strengthening the foundations for large language models while preserving linguistic diversity and cultural richness. The objective is to improve Europe’s competitiveness, expand the availability of European language data, and support interoperable language-technology capacity across participating states. The implementation uses the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium model, allowing member states to pool funding and resources in a coordinated structure. Official ALT-EDIC and related language-data-space materials describe activities including linguistic-data production and curation, evaluation and normalisation support, adaptation of models to user needs, and advice to the wider ecosystem. The impact includes stronger shared infrastructure, more reusable multilingual resources, and better conditions for developing European language technologies at scale. It also creates long-term strategic value by supporting common standards, reducing fragmentation, and reinforcing Europe’s capacity to develop language AI aligned with its regulatory, linguistic, and public-interest goals.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate
title: GPT-NL - A language model for the Dutch language and culture
source_description: Many widely used language models are developed outside the Netherlands and may not adequately reflect Dutch language use, legal requirements, or national priorities around privacy, cultural context, and technological independence. GPT-NL was launched to address this strategic gap by creating an open Dutch language model designed to strengthen national capability in AI, data science, and data spaces while supporting compliance with European rules. The objective is to improve strategic autonomy, foster domestic expertise, and provide a trustworthy foundation for language applications built around Dutch language and culture. The implementation centres on the development of an open large language model funded by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy through RVO, with EUR 13.5 million allocated to the project after the “Facility for a sovereign Dutch language model” proposal was awarded in October 2023. At a conceptual level, the initiative focuses on building and governing a Dutch-language model in line with the GDPR and the AI Regulation, with an explicit aim of avoiding training sources that infringe privacy or intellectual-property rights. The impact is expected to include a stronger national knowledge base, improved access to compliant Dutch-language AI infrastructure, and greater capacity for public and private organisations to build applications suited to local linguistic and regulatory needs, creating long-term value through sovereign digital capability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: INSAIT – Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology
title: BgGPT - A bulgarian LLM
source_description: Many widely used language technologies provide limited support for smaller European languages, constraining digital inclusion and technological sovereignty. In Bulgaria, public institutions, businesses and citizens lack high-quality language models tailored to national linguistic and cultural contexts. The objective of BgGPT is to develop state-of-the-art generative language models designed specifically for the Bulgarian language and its users. The implementation involves training a series of open and freely available language models using curated Bulgarian-language datasets, supported by advanced computational infrastructure. The models are designed to serve a broad range of applications, including public administration, education, research and business services. Emphasis is placed on openness, transparency and alignment with European values. As the project is still in development, evaluation focuses on linguistic quality, robustness and applicability across use cases. Expected impacts include improved access to language technologies for Bulgarian speakers, strengthened national research capacity and reduced dependency on foreign-language-centric solutions. Qualitative benefits include enhanced digital inclusion, support for public sector innovation and a reusable foundation for Bulgarian-language digital services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GenAI chatbot on the EU-FarmBook platform
source_description: Farmers, foresters, advisers, researchers, and policymakers often need practical knowledge quickly, but relevant materials are frequently spread across projects, languages, and institutions, making them hard to find and apply. EU-FarmBook addresses this challenge by building an open online platform to support knowledge exchange across the European agricultural and forestry innovation ecosystem. The objective is to make research-based and practice-oriented resources easier to discover and use, while improving knowledge transfer between actors at regional, national, and European levels. The implementation includes an AI-powered conversational assistant developed with support from TNO, designed to help users retrieve relevant information interactively from the platform. At a conceptual level, the chatbot uses generative AI to respond to users in a conversational way while grounding its answers in the platform’s own database of contributions, tools, guides, and other materials. Recent project communications state that the AI technology is European and that the responses are based on content held within EU-FarmBook itself, supporting controlled and domain-relevant retrieval. The impact includes easier access to specialised information for users with different backgrounds, improved usability of a large cross-European knowledge platform, and more efficient dissemination of project results and practice-based insight. It also supports scalability by turning a growing repository into a more navigable and interactive service for rural communities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CitiVERSE - LDT CitiVERSE EDIC
source_description: Cities across Europe are developing digital twins to support planning and public-service innovation, but these systems often remain local, fragmented, and difficult to connect into a broader European capability. The LDT CitiVERSE EDIC initiative was created to link existing local digital twins and form the foundation of a broader European CitiVERSE, enabling more coordinated development of data-driven and simulation-based tools for urban policy and citizen interaction. The objective is to strengthen cooperation between participating countries, improve the use of digital twins in smart-city policy, and support new forms of simulation and engagement around issues such as traffic, congestion, air quality, and decarbonisation. The implementation uses the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium model to establish a shared governance and infrastructure framework for networked local digital twins. At a conceptual level, the initiative connects data, analytics, simulation, and generative AI applications so that cities can model real-time or future urban conditions and also explore virtual-reality tools that help citizens understand proposed urban changes more easily. The Commission notes that Croatia, Estonia, France, Latvia, Portugal, Slovenia, and Spain initially called for the EDIC to be established. The impact lies in stronger interoperability between local digital twins, greater capacity for collaborative urban innovation, and more scalable smart-city services across Europe, creating both public-sector efficiency gains and better-informed citizen participation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GPT-SW3 - The first large-scale generative language model for the Swedish language
source_description: Swedish organisations increasingly need language technologies that reflect local linguistic realities and can be developed within a national ecosystem rather than relying entirely on foreign models. GPT-SW3 was created to address this need by providing a large-scale generative language model for the Nordic languages, with a primary focus on Swedish, through collaboration between AI Sweden, RISE, and WASP WARA Media & Language. The objective is to give organisations in Sweden access to a strong domestic foundation for language applications, while also strengthening the country’s applied AI capability across public, private, and academic sectors. The implementation uses a large-scale generative model based on the same broad technical principles as contemporary transformer-based language models, trained to support Nordic-language generation and downstream applications. At a conceptual level, the project combines national collaboration, technical development, and ecosystem building through AI Sweden, which brings together more than 120 partners and is funded by both the Swedish government and public- and private-sector participants. The impact includes a stronger Swedish-language AI infrastructure, new possibilities for organisations to build local language applications, and improved strategic capability in a domain often dominated by global providers. It also creates long-term value by supporting innovation in Swedish and Nordic language technology through a shared national platform.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Kungsbacka municipality, Tjörn municipality, Gothenburg city, Region Skåne, Region Halland, and Västra Götaland Region
title: Svea - A shared digital assistant for the public sector
source_description: Public-sector organisations handle large volumes of text-based work every day, from drafting and revising documents to summarising material, classifying content, and supporting administrative processes, yet these tasks consume significant staff time and are difficult for single organisations to automate alone. In Sweden, the Svea initiative was created as a joint effort between authorities, municipalities, regions, and industry, coordinated by AI Sweden, to develop shared capability rather than fragmented local solutions. The objective is to support public employees in routine text tasks, free time for more interpersonal and creative work, and establish the conditions for national cooperation on shared AI solutions in the public sector. The implementation is organised in phases, beginning with data generation, change management, use-case identification, and prototype development, and continuing with large-scale testing and evaluation. Svea itself is a web-based chat assistant built on open-source, model-agnostic architecture running on Swedish infrastructure; it can already answer organisation-specific questions, summarise documents, extract information, and rewrite text in easy-to-read Swedish. AI Sweden states that participating organisations collectively spent 2,500 hours annotating training data for the assistant. The impact includes stronger reuse of data and effort across institutions, improved scalability of AI adoption, and better productivity in text-heavy public work, while helping organisations prepare for labour shortages and rising service demand.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LightOn's Paradigm platform - Generative AI at the Île-de-France Regional Council
source_description: Public sector agents often struggle to navigate complex internal documentation and information systems, leading to inefficiencies and increased workload for IT support teams. Stakeholders include regional council staff, digital transformation teams and technology providers. The objective is to provide instant, reliable access to technical documentation and internal knowledge resources. The solution deploys a generative AI-powered assistant built on large language model technology, trained and fine-tuned on the Region’s internal documentation corpus. Natural language queries are processed to retrieve and synthesise relevant information, delivering precise responses within existing digital work environments. The platform integrates with knowledge bases and information systems managed by the Digital Transformation Hub. Expected impacts include reduced time spent searching for documentation, lower support demand on IT teams, improved operational efficiency and enhanced digital maturity within public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SOLARIS - Democratic responses to the challenges of deepfakes and infodemics
source_description: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are generative AI models capable of reproducing realistic images, videos and voice outputs. Because they have the potential to create highly realistic content, they can also pose a threat to democracies through the creation and circulation of deepfakes, which spread false information and undermine trust. In this context, the EU-funded SOLARIS project will focus on the challenges and opportunities posed by GANs in the context of democracy. It will study how deepfakes circulate and are trusted by users, thus threatening democratic processes. It will also develop regulatory guidelines about GANs and generative AI for the promotion of democratic engagement. The project will involve three use cases to simulate the circulation of threatening content, and co-create value-based GANs content to enhance digital citizenship.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: TrustLLM - Democratise trustworthy and efficient LLM technology for Europe
source_description: TrustLLM is a Horizon Europe project designed to develop open, trustworthy and sustainable large language models for European languages, with an initial focus on Germanic languages and underrepresented linguistic communities. The strategic problem is that Europe needs language-model infrastructure that is transparent, reliable, energy-conscious and less dependent on closed non-European systems. Coordinated by Linköping University, the project brings together partners across Europe with expertise in natural language processing, high-performance computing, trustworthy AI, model evaluation and downstream deployment. The implementation will develop large language models trained on substantial multilingual European text resources, while addressing reliability, bias, hallucination, sustainability and accessibility. Conceptually, the project combines large-scale model training, exascale computing, trustworthiness research, open model development and ecosystem-building for modular and extensible European LLMs. The expected impact is stronger European capacity in language technologies, improved human-machine interaction across applications, wider access to open models and better support for industry, public services and research. TrustLLM is explicitly positioned as a response to the need for reliable generative models and mitigation of risks such as hallucinations and bias.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Alma Mater Studiorum – University of Bologna ALMA-AI
title: GENAI4LEX-B
source_description: GENAI4LEX-B was developed to support parliamentary work in Italy by using generative AI for the preparation of legislative initiative acts. The institutional problem is that parliamentarians and parliamentary staff must navigate complex regulatory sources, amendments, policy objectives and legislative drafting requirements under time and information constraints. The project won the “Supporting the preparation of initiative acts” area in a call promoted by the Italian Chamber of Deputies, which selected three winning projects from 28 proposals. Its three prototypes are designed to help users explore regulatory sources, simplify and summarise amendments, and measure the alignment between bills and the policies they intend to pursue. The implementation combines generative AI, legal informatics, regulatory-source analysis, summarisation and legislative-support functions. The consortium is coordinated by Alma Mater Studiorum – University of Bologna / ALMA-AI and includes CNR-Igsg with Aptus.AI, Luiss Guido Carli University with Asimov AI, the University of Turin and the University of Verona. The expected impact is more efficient legislative preparation, improved access to regulatory context, clearer amendment analysis and stronger evidence on whether proposed bills match policy goals. Its value depends on careful human oversight and constitutional safeguards in parliamentary processes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: F13, the LLM used by the State of Baden-Württemberg in collaboration with Aleph Alpha
source_description: Baden-Württemberg introduced F13 to support employees of the state administration in drafting, summarising and processing textual information more efficiently. The administrative challenge is that civil servants work with large volumes of documents, cabinet templates, notes and research material, which can slow workflows and reduce time available for substantive policy or service tasks. F13 is designed to relieve staff by providing text assistance functions tailored to administrative routines. The system was developed primarily by the Heidelberg-based company Aleph Alpha and presented by the Innovation Lab Baden-Württemberg, InnoLab_bw. Its implementation uses generative language-model technology to support several functions: a summary tool with selectable compression levels for pasted texts, a Cabinet Template Note function that converts uploaded cabinet templates into summarised note templates, a research assistant for preparing large volumes of information, and the “Vermerkomat”, which creates comprehensive flow text. At a conceptual level, F13 combines large language models, document processing, summarisation, text generation and workflow-oriented user interfaces within the state administration network. The expected impact is faster preparation of administrative documents, reduced repetitive writing work, improved handling of information-intensive tasks and more consistent support for employees. Since 2024, all staff with access to the state administration network can use F13, indicating a move beyond experimentation into full administrative deployment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ALEIA digital assistant - Generative AI at the Île-de-France Regional Council
source_description: The ALEIA digital assistant responds to the difficulty citizens face when trying to identify the regional aid schemes for which they may be eligible. Île-de-France has around 350 aid schemes, and this breadth of provision can make access confusing for residents, associations or other potential beneficiaries. The Regional Council therefore sought a tool that could guide users through the available support landscape and provide clear answers based on the region’s own documentation. Developed by the start-up Aleia, the solution combines a search engine and a conversational agent. It uses the French Mistral language model to formulate responses grounded in the region’s corpus of documents, while data are hosted in France and answers are continuously improved. The system is also designed to recognise when a user asks about support that falls outside the region’s responsibilities and to respond negatively rather than providing irrelevant guidance. Conceptually, the assistant combines document retrieval, generative language modelling, conversational interaction, controlled knowledge sources and French-hosted data infrastructure. The expected impact is simpler access to regional support, reduced user confusion, more efficient routing towards relevant schemes and less pressure on administrative staff handling repetitive eligibility questions. By linking conversational access with an official documentary corpus, the system can improve transparency and make regional aid more navigable.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Open Spanish LLM model in collaboration with IBM
source_description: The Spanish Government and IBM collaboration aims to develop open-source foundation models in Spanish and Spain’s co-official languages, including Catalan, Basque, Galician and Valencian. The strategic challenge is that Spanish and Iberian-language communities require generative AI systems that reflect their linguistic diversity, cultural context and public-interest requirements, rather than relying mainly on models optimised for English. The initiative was launched through a Memorandum of Understanding discussed in April 2024 between the Spanish Government and IBM. The implementation draws on IBM’s open-source AI framework and AI stack, with an emphasis on ethical, sustainable and community-driven model development. Conceptually, the project combines large and small language models, open-source development, AI supercomputing, multilingual training and community contribution mechanisms. The expected impact is stronger national and international Spanish-language AI capacity, improved access to generative AI tools for nearly 500 million Spanish speakers, and better support for co-official languages in digital services and innovation. The collaboration also aims to advance responsible generative AI technologies in Spain and support practical deployment in public and private contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: OpenGPT-X project to create a LLM "Made in Germany"""
source_description: OpenGPT-X was launched to strengthen Europe’s capacity in generative-language technologies by developing a large language model ecosystem rooted in German and European research, industrial capability and trusted data environments. The broader challenge is that advanced generative models are increasingly important for business applications and digital transformation, yet strategic dependence on non-European solutions may limit sovereignty, transparency and local innovation capacity. This use case therefore brings together partners from industry, research and media across the generative AI value chain, with the objective of advancing cutting-edge research while driving practical adoption in the German economy. The solution is implemented as a collaborative Gaia-X-related project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action, with total funding of around EUR 14 million and a project timeline spanning January 2022 to March 2025. At a conceptual level, the initiative develops large language model capabilities, supporting infrastructure and practical application pathways that connect foundational research with real business use cases. This includes work across model development, data spaces and deployment-oriented innovation within a trusted digital ecosystem. The expected impact is stronger domestic capability in generative-language technologies, greater readiness for enterprise adoption and improved alignment between research and market application. More broadly, OpenGPT-X supports technological sovereignty, boosts innovation capacity and creates long-term value by establishing a European foundation for advanced language-model development and use.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Development of GenAI-based tool for education by gov.uk - "Building a proof of concept for Generative AI feedback and resource generation in education contexts"""
source_description: Teachers face substantial workload pressures linked to marking, feedback preparation and the creation of classroom resources, yet these tasks are central to maintaining teaching quality and supporting pupil progress. The National Institute of Teaching and the Department for Education explored this use case as part of a wider effort to transform teachers’ day-to-day work by reducing routine burdens while supporting stronger educational outcomes. The stakeholders include teachers, pupils and education-system leaders, with the objective of helping teachers evaluate work more efficiently, provide useful formative feedback and generate relevant learning activities aligned with the National Curriculum. The solution is implemented as a proof-of-concept tool based on large language models. At a conceptual level, the system uses generative-language capabilities to analyse pupil work against curriculum expectations, draft feedback for formative use and create supporting activities or resources for follow-up teaching. These functions are integrated as exploratory support for professional practice rather than as a replacement for teacher judgement. The expected impact is reduced time spent on repetitive instructional tasks, quicker preparation of feedback and stronger support for lesson adaptation to learner needs. More broadly, the project improves workflow efficiency, enhances the usability of digital tools in education and creates value by testing how generative systems can support teachers in practical, curriculum-linked classroom contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Developing a Generative AI platform for construction cost management
source_description: The BIM-GAIcost project develops a generative AI platform to improve productivity and accuracy in construction cost planning. The operational problem is that cost overruns are widespread in construction, while early cost planning often requires time-consuming manual work, fragmented data and limited certainty. Leeds Beckett University’s Futures of Systems, People and Projects laboratory received a £1.18 million Innovate UK grant to develop the platform after a successful feasibility study. The project upgrades the earlier costplan.ai prototype by integrating Building Information Modelling with generative AI and large language models trained on cost data. Conceptually, the platform will generate construction cost-estimation documents, automate BIM-related cost outputs, provide early cost advice and include accuracy indications to help predict and avoid overruns during planning. The expected impact is a major productivity gain, with the source indicating potential improvement of up to 85% by reducing the time required to prepare initial cost plans. The wider consortium includes The Property Box Group, London South Bank University, Birmingham City University, Leeds Beckett University, Milan Consulting, Ardeo and Kier Group.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Amsterdam: Generating sustainable materials with Generative AI
source_description: The University of Amsterdam’s AI4SMM initiative applies artificial intelligence to the design of sustainable molecules and materials, shifting generative techniques from language to chemistry and materials science. The research challenge is that developing new materials for energy storage, industry, food and plastics can be slow, costly and experimentally intensive, while sustainability transitions require faster discovery of safer and lower-impact alternatives. The initiative is led by Bernd Ensing at the Faculty of Science and connects expertise in computer science, chemistry, ecology, physics and biology. The implementation uses machine-learning and generative approaches to model molecules and materials, replacing word-based associations with relationships between molecular structures and properties. Initial projects focus on areas such as energy-storage salts, sustainable steel, safe plastic and new plant proteins. Conceptually, the approach combines molecular data, computational chemistry, generative modelling, property prediction and experimental validation to propose promising candidates for further study. The expected impact is faster discovery of sustainable materials, better targeting of laboratory work and stronger integration between AI and sustainability research. By applying generative methods to molecules rather than text, the initiative can support innovation in sectors where material performance and environmental impact are central.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Qra - The first Polish open-source LLM
source_description: Qra was developed to provide a strong Polish-language generative model trained specifically on Polish text, responding to the limited availability of open large language models optimised for Polish. The research and technology problem is that models primarily trained on English or multilingual corpora may underperform in Polish-language understanding, question answering and coherent text generation. Gdańsk University of Technology and the AI Lab at the National Information Processing Institute developed Polish generative neural language models using approximately a terabyte of Polish-language data. The implementation involved training open-source models on Polish text, with the Hugging Face model card noting that published versions were based on Llama 2 checkpoints and further trained on a cleaned, filtered and deduplicated Polish corpus of about 90 billion tokens. The models were trained using infrastructure from the PG TASK Computing Centre with 21 Nvidia A100 cards. The expected impact is improved Polish-language AI capacity, broader reuse by researchers and developers, and reduced reliance on foreign-language models for Polish applications. Because the models are open-source, users can download and adapt them to specific domains or tasks, including question answering and text generation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: POLITEHNICA Bucharest, the University of Bucharest and the Institute of Logic and Data Science
title: OpenLLM-Ro - The first LLM in Romanian language
source_description: OpenLLM-Ro was developed to address the limited availability of large language models specifically trained for Romanian, a gap that can constrain the quality of digital services, research tools and language technologies for Romanian-speaking users. The initiative brings together academic actors seeking to strengthen national language-technology capacity and provide an open model that can be further refined for different applications. The main stakeholders include POLITEHNICA Bucharest, the University of Bucharest, the Institute of Logic and Data Science, researchers working pro bono, developers, public or private organisations that may reuse the model, and Romanian-speaking end users. Starting in the second half of 2023, the research team worked on developing and training the model, with POLITEHNICA Bucharest also providing the computing power needed for training. The implementation involves large-language-model development, corpus preparation, training infrastructure, model evaluation and ongoing fine-tuning. Conceptually, the project creates a foundational Romanian-language model that can support downstream tasks such as text generation, summarisation, question answering, classification or conversational interfaces. Its expected impact is to reduce dependence on models optimised primarily for larger languages, improve Romanian-language processing quality, and support innovation in education, administration, business and research. The model’s online availability and continued fine-tuning indicate an evolving resource for the Romanian digital ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GenAI-based chatbot to help the public access services on official websites
source_description: Ireland’s GenAI chatbot initiative was designed to test how generative AI could help members of the public find information on government supports and services through official digital channels. The administrative problem is that citizens and businesses often need to navigate multiple public websites, schemes and eligibility pages, which can create friction and increase demand for direct assistance. The initial project aimed to deliver a “chat agent” able to provide information on business supports offered by the Government, with pilot funding from Microsoft and delivery in collaboration with the Office of the Government Chief Information Officer. Conceptually, the service uses generative AI to interpret user questions, retrieve relevant official content and provide conversational answers, while requiring safeguards around accuracy, transparency, human oversight and data protection. The expected impact is easier access to public information, reduced search burden for users, and better scalability for high-volume enquiries. A related public-facing Irish implementation is now visible through AskCI, an AI-powered chatbot on Citizens Information that uses generative AI to answer questions based on citizensinformation.ie content and was developed with the OGCIO.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FinGPT-3 - The open Finnish LLM
source_description: FinGPT-3 was created to expand the availability of generative language models for Finnish, a language that is less represented than English in many large-scale model ecosystems. The research challenge is to build models that can handle Finnish linguistic structures effectively and support applications in language technology, digital linguistics and natural language processing. The project is led by the TurkuNLP Group at the University of Turku, whose work spans corpus annotation, analysis, machine learning theory and applied language technologies. The National Library of Finland collaborated on the model development, and the project received support from the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101070350. In 2023, the team trained GPT-3-like generative models for Finnish. The implementation involves assembling and processing Finnish-language corpora, training large generative architectures, evaluating linguistic performance and making model outputs available for research or downstream application. Conceptually, FinGPT-3 provides foundational language-model capacity that can support Finnish text generation, summarisation, classification, information extraction and other NLP tasks. The expected impact is stronger technological coverage for Finnish, improved resources for researchers and developers, and reduced dependence on multilingual systems that may underperform for smaller language communities. By combining university expertise, national library resources and EU funding, the project contributes to Europe’s capacity for language-specific AI development.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: NorGPT - The open LLM "Made in Norway"""
source_description: NorGPT forms part of Norway’s effort to develop large language models adapted to Norwegian language needs and national digital capacity. The core problem is that many large language models are optimised for English or broad multilingual use, while Norwegian users, organisations and public institutions need models that understand Norwegian linguistic structures, terminology and cultural context. Developed through NorwAI and NTNU, the initiative supports natural-language interaction so that users can work on language-related tasks through ordinary Norwegian queries rather than artificial syntax. The implementation involves collecting and processing Norwegian-language text resources, training large language models, evaluating performance, and making models available for research and experimental use. Conceptually, NorGPT can support tasks such as text generation, summarisation, translation, question answering and information retrieval. The expected impact is stronger Norwegian-language AI capacity, improved productivity for language-intensive work and reduced reliance on external models not optimised for Norwegian. Current NorwAI material indicates that work on Norwegian LLMs is active, while a recent technical report states that NorwAI models are openly available to Nordic organisations, companies and students for research and experimental use.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ‘Democratic Engagement through a Public Chatbot’ (DepuChat) - How GenAI can increase transparency
source_description: DepuChat proposes a public chatbot to make information on the Italian Chamber of Deputies more accessible, usable and transparent for citizens. The democratic problem is that parliamentary information is often technically complex, dispersed across institutional documents and difficult for non-specialist users to interpret. The project, developed by the IDEAS Research Centre at Roma Tre University in collaboration with the Department of Legal Sciences at the University of Florence, aims to bring citizens closer to institutions by allowing them to query information on the Chamber, its bodies and procedures, individual MPs, and political positions expressed by MPs and the Government. The implementation uses generative AI to create a conversational and potentially graphical interface over parliamentary data. Conceptually, the system combines institutional data retrieval, natural-language interaction, summarisation and visual presentation to help users explore parliamentary activity more easily. The expected impact is improved transparency, broader civic access to legislative information and stronger democratic engagement. The project was announced in July 2024 as a winner of the Chamber of Deputies’ call for ideas, so its current form appears to be a selected proposal or prototype rather than a fully operational public service.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministry of Processing and Function Public Interministerial Directorate for Public Transformation (DITP) and the Interministerial Digital Directorate (DINUM),
title: Supporting Civil Servant with Generative AI
source_description: France’s experiment on generative artificial intelligence in public services was launched to assess how such tools could support civil servants in responding to users more efficiently. The administrative problem is that public agents handle large numbers of online opinions, comments and procedural interactions, many of which require clear written replies but can be repetitive and time-consuming. The initiative involved 1,000 volunteer agents equipped with a tool to help draft responses to users during online procedures, while preserving a human-in-the-loop model: agents supervise, modify and approve responses before they are sent. The experiment is led by the Interministerial Directorate for Public Transformation and the Interministerial Digital Directorate, with a solution provided by Allobrain. The system uses generative language technology to propose draft responses based on anonymised data, meaning confidentiality is intended to be preserved. The model supports response writing rather than replacing the public official, and the approach is framed as a way to save time on specific tasks while strengthening human contact between public services and citizens. The planned extension to France services counters would broaden the support to agents assisting users face to face. The expected impact is faster response preparation, reduced administrative burden, improved consistency in written replies and more time for personalised support where human judgement is most valuable.

title: SNCF collect 3x more customer feedback with AI
source_description: Railway operators need timely and detailed customer feedback to understand service quality, detect weak signals and respond to dissatisfaction before it damages trust. SNCF used AlloReview to improve the collection and analysis of passenger feedback across TER services, particularly in the Grand Est region. The operational problem was that traditional satisfaction surveys were not capturing enough qualitative information, while unsolicited passenger experiences were difficult to process at scale. The implementation combines QR codes, phone numbers, business cards and post-journey feedback mechanisms, allowing travellers to leave comments orally or in writing at different moments of the customer journey. AI-supported real-time analysis processes the resulting verbatims, identifies satisfaction levels and topics raised, and supports scenario-based follow-up. At a conceptual level, the system transforms open-ended voice and text feedback into structured customer intelligence, enabling SNCF to re-engage dissatisfied passengers, reward loyal customers and identify improvement opportunities. The expected impact is richer customer listening, faster detection of recurring problems, better segmentation of passenger satisfaction and stronger customer relationship management. The case demonstrates how AI can be used in transport not only for operations or mobility flows, but also for continuous service-quality improvement through large-scale qualitative analysis.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Legislab - monitoring legislative quality with GenAI
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Legislab is designed to support analysis of the Italian legislative system and assist parliamentary offices in monitoring legal quality. The institutional problem is that new legislative proposals must be assessed against a large and continuously evolving corpus of laws, from the Constitution onwards, making it difficult to identify relevant precedents, overlaps, inconsistencies or references. The project, developed by the Politecnico di Milano and the Istituto Einaudi, is intended for the offices of the Chamber of Deputies and combines a database of Italian laws with analytical and generative functions. Its implementation allows users to input a topic or draft title and receive relevant articles and laws that may need to be considered. The system is deliberately constrained to reduce hallucination risks: it relies on existing legal data, objective information and linguistic metrics from scientific literature rather than generating free-form legal text. The expected impact is stronger legislative quality monitoring, faster identification of relevant legal sources and better support for expert legislative drafting, while preserving the role of legal professionals and parliamentarians in writing the law.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT: A Pre-trained Transformer Language Model for Italian Law
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Legal language differs substantially from general Italian because it contains technical terminology, Latin expressions, formulaic constructions and domain-specific references that general-purpose language models may not represent well. ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT addresses this gap by adapting transformer-based natural language processing to the Italian legal domain. The model was introduced by researchers at the Sant’Anna School of Advanced Studies to improve performance on downstream legal NLP tasks where generic Italian BERT models lose accuracy. The implementation starts from an Italian BERT architecture and performs additional pre-training on Italian civil-law corpora. At a conceptual level, the model learns contextual representations from legal texts, making it better suited to tasks such as legal classification, retrieval, information extraction or document analysis. This approach is important because many public-sector legal applications require high sensitivity to legal wording and cannot rely solely on models trained on Wikipedia, news or other general corpora. The expected impact is improved performance in Italian legal AI systems, stronger foundations for legal analytics, and a reusable research resource for courts, public administrations, legal publishers and academic projects. The published paper reports that ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT outperforms the general-purpose Italian BERT in domain-specific tasks, while a public Hugging Face entry indicates the model remains available as an open machine-learning resource.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Athens university of economics and business
title: LEGAL-BERT: The Muppets straight out of Law School
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: LEGAL-BERT was developed to improve the application of transformer-based language models to legal-domain tasks, where general-purpose models may not perform optimally because of specialised vocabulary, reasoning patterns and document structures. The research problem is that BERT had achieved strong results across many natural language processing tasks, but guidance on how to adapt it to specialised domains had not been sufficiently tested for legal materials. The project therefore evaluates different strategies for applying BERT to legal downstream tasks, including using the original model directly, adapting it through additional pre-training on legal corpora and pre-training models from scratch on domain-specific legal data. The implementation also explores a broader hyper-parameter search space for fine-tuning, recognising that standard configurations may not generalise well to law. The resulting LEGAL-BERT family of models is intended to support legal NLP research, computational law and legal technology applications. Conceptually, the project combines domain-specific pre-training, transformer architectures, legal corpora and systematic evaluation across datasets. Its expected impact is improved model performance for legal text classification, retrieval and analysis, as well as more reliable methodological guidance for researchers and developers working in specialised domains. By releasing LEGAL-BERT, the project provides reusable infrastructure for legal AI experimentation and application development.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Predictice - Summaries of Court Decisions
source_description: Predictice uses generative language technology to make legal research more efficient by producing automatic summaries of court decisions. The practical challenge for legal professionals is that judicial documents can be long, technical and time-consuming to read, while some decisions may prove irrelevant only after several minutes of review. Predictice provides access to a large legal corpus of around 26 million documents, including court decisions, and aims to help users assess relevance more quickly. The implementation applies GPT-3 and ChatGPT-style language-model capabilities to the task of document synthesis. Rather than asking the model to produce legal advice, the tool focuses on summarising existing decisions, a use case considered more reliable by the Predictice team than generating autonomous legal answers. Conceptually, the system combines large-scale legal-document retrieval, generative summarisation, natural language processing and user-facing legal search functions. The expected impact is faster review of case law, reduced time spent on irrelevant documents, improved productivity for lawyers and legal researchers, and easier navigation of large legal databases. By providing concise summaries of lengthy decisions, Predictice can support legal professionals in prioritising which documents deserve closer reading. However, because legal interpretation remains sensitive, summaries should be treated as decision-support outputs and checked against the original court text.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Henchman - contract drafing with AI support
source_description: Henchman supports legal professionals in drafting and improving contract clauses by extending the range of available drafting options during contract preparation. The practical challenge in legal work is that lawyers frequently need to adapt existing clauses to specific transactional contexts, client preferences or drafting conventions, while maintaining consistency, precision and speed. The platform is therefore relevant to law firms, in-house legal teams, contract managers and clients relying on efficient document production. Its objective is to make contract drafting more agile by helping users refine language, adjust wording and introduce clause-level variations without starting from scratch. The implementation uses GPT-3.5 to assist with targeted drafting operations, such as changing a clause from singular to plural or adding a new element to an existing provision. Conceptually, the system combines large language model functionality with contract-drafting workflows, allowing users to generate or modify text within a controlled legal-document environment. The expected impact is faster clause adaptation, reduced repetitive editing, improved consistency across contract drafts and greater productivity for legal teams. By supporting incremental drafting rather than replacing legal judgement, the tool can help professionals focus on negotiation strategy, legal risk and client-specific tailoring. Its value depends on appropriate human review, since AI-generated legal text must be checked for accuracy, enforceability and alignment with the intended contractual position.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Robin AI - LLM for supporting Legals
source_description: Robin AI provides legal teams with a platform for accelerating contract review, drafting and editing through large language model functionality. The operational issue is that legal departments and firms often spend substantial time reading long contracts, identifying risks, suggesting amendments and aligning documents with client preferences. This creates pressure on turnaround times, especially where high volumes of contracts must be reviewed consistently. The platform is relevant to lawyers, in-house legal teams, commercial teams, clients and organisations seeking faster approval workflows. Its implementation uses large language models, including Anthropic’s Claude, to analyse contract text, support reading and editing, and suggest real-time changes based on client preferences. At a conceptual level, the system combines natural language processing, generative text functions, contract analytics, preference-based review logic and workflow integration. It can assist users by identifying relevant provisions, proposing edits and supporting the review process before approval. The expected impact is shorter contract-review cycles, more consistent application of drafting standards and reduced manual workload for routine legal-document tasks. The platform also has potential to improve collaboration between legal and business teams by making contract changes easier to understand and process. However, because the information provided acknowledges the possibility of AI errors, human legal supervision remains essential to validate outputs and ensure that proposed revisions are legally and commercially appropriate.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Harvey - LLM for supporting contract analysis
source_description: Harvey is used in the legal sector to support contract analysis, due diligence, research and knowledge work across different practice areas. The business problem it addresses is the high volume and complexity of legal information that lawyers must review, compare and interpret, particularly in transactional matters, investigations or advisory work. Law firms and legal departments need tools that can accelerate document analysis while preserving expert oversight and professional responsibility. Harvey was reportedly rolled out by Allen & Overy and uses GPT-4 to help lawyers generate insights, recommendations and predictions. Its implementation draws on large language model capabilities for natural language understanding, document summarisation, information extraction, legal research support and analytical assistance. Conceptually, the platform can process legal materials, identify relevant issues, support due diligence questions, assist with drafting or research tasks and provide structured outputs for lawyer review. The expected impact is improved efficiency in document-heavy legal work, faster identification of relevant contractual or legal points, reduced time spent on repetitive analysis and stronger support for multi-practice knowledge work. By augmenting lawyers’ ability to navigate complex information, the tool can create business value through faster delivery and more scalable legal services. Nevertheless, its outputs must be reviewed by qualified professionals, because legal interpretation, strategic judgement and client advice cannot be delegated to automated systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: INNOAIR - Green public transport on-demand in the Municipality of Sofia
source_description: Sofia faces persistent air pollution and traffic congestion, particularly in rapidly developing neighbourhoods with limited public transport coverage. The INNOAIR project aimed to improve urban mobility and air quality by piloting greener, on-demand public transport services in the districts of Manastirski Livadi and Buxton. Coordinated by the Municipality of Sofia and managed by the Sofia Development Association, the initiative tested five electric minibuses with a capacity of 20 passengers each during a one-year trial starting in 2023. Advanced routing algorithms were used to determine optimal service routes based on municipal datasets, including registered vehicles, public facilities and demographic information, complemented by data gathered through community engagement and urban walks. While routes remained fixed once defined, departure times operated on a demand-responsive basis. The pilot provided residents with alternatives to private car use, contributing to reduced traffic volumes and lower emissions. The project demonstrated improved accessibility, enhanced user satisfaction and measurable environmental benefits, supporting scalable deployment of intelligent, low-emission mobility services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: A new virtual assistant for the city of Kortrijk
source_description: The City of Kortrijk sought to enhance accessibility to municipal services and streamline citizen interactions as part of a broader regional digitalisation strategy supported by NextGenerationEU funding. Traditional service channels often require in-person visits or complex navigation of online portals. To address this, the city implemented “De Virtuele Assistent”, a digital platform combining transactional chatbot functionality with advanced language processing capabilities. The system enables residents, associations and businesses to obtain information about municipal services, book appointments and request official documents such as certificates and deeds through a single conversational interface. Integrated with existing administrative systems, the assistant supports automated processing of routine requests while escalating complex cases to human staff when necessary. Accessible via smartphone, tablet and desktop devices, the solution enhances inclusivity and service availability. Expected benefits include reduced administrative workload, faster response times and improved user experience, supporting more efficient and citizen-centred digital public services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ‘Fix the Streets’ - AI that leverages citizen-produced data to improve the streets
source_description: Municipal engineering teams need timely, localised information on potholes, damaged signs, and other street defects, yet conventional inspections can miss issues or detect them only after delays. In Vaasa, the Fix the Streets initiative tackled this challenge by drawing directly on geo-located observations submitted by residents, turning citizen-generated reports into a richer operational picture of street conditions. The objective is to improve infrastructure monitoring, support faster and better-targeted maintenance decisions, and strengthen the city’s use of digital tools within its wider twin-transition and innovation agenda. The implementation combined a mobile application with a multi-format knowledge base built over two years from text, image, and video submissions. Working with Crowdsorsa, the Municipal Engineering Department used AI to analyse reported defects and linked the app with Vaasa’s digital signage and mapping systems for more precise localisation and follow-up. At a conceptual level, the solution joins crowdsourced data collection, geospatial mapping, and automated issue analysis in one workflow, while emphasising data minimisation in the handling of citizen input. The impact includes improved visibility of street health, more informed prioritisation of maintenance activity, and stronger evidence for infrastructure decisions. It also demonstrates a scalable model for combining citizen participation with digital monitoring to improve local public services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Satellites for Wilderness Inspection and Forest Threat Tracking (SWIFTT)
source_description: Forest ecosystems face increasing risks from climate change, pests and biodiversity loss, yet monitoring large and remote areas remains resource-intensive. The SWIFTT project aims to provide forest managers with accessible and scientifically robust remote sensing tools to monitor and mitigate forest threats. The consortium integrates satellite imagery with advanced analytical models to detect changes in vegetation health, biodiversity indicators and environmental stress factors. Machine learning techniques process multi-temporal Earth observation data to generate risk maps and predictive assessments for forest management. The platform is designed to be user-friendly and cost-effective, enabling practical uptake by forestry professionals. Field validation and deployment are planned in large forest areas in Germany, France and Latvia to test operational feasibility. Anticipated impacts include improved early detection of forest degradation, enhanced biodiversity conservation and more informed climate mitigation strategies. The project strengthens data-driven forest governance and promotes sustainable ecosystem management across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: The 'Wet Index’ project - an AI tool to predict local floods
source_description: The tool was developed to tackle the increasing risk of flooding due to extreme weather events, which poses challenges for municipalities, landowners, and urban planners in anticipating and mitigating damage. Existing forecasting tools lack sufficient localisation and lead time for effective decision-making. The objective is to provide accurate, localised early warnings to support proactive planning and risk management. The solution uses predictive modelling techniques applied to geospatial and climate data to forecast flood risks at a local level, providing up to 48 hours of advance warning. The system integrates multiple data sources and is developed in collaboration with research institutions, with conceptual integration into municipal planning and emergency response systems. The impact includes improved preparedness, reduced damage from flooding, and enhanced decision-making for urban and rural planning. It also increases reliability and scalability of forecasting capabilities, delivering significant value in risk reduction and public safety.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Policies for Holistic Urban Mobility and Accessibility
source_description: Urban congestion and accessibility barriers disproportionately affect people with disabilities, requiring targeted policy interventions informed by reliable data. The Municipality of Nicosia, within the AI4PublicPolicy initiative, developed a citizen-centric framework to design evidence-based mobility policies. The project focused on improving access to restricted streets during congestion and optimising parking availability for individuals with disabilities. Analytical models processed traffic data, Smart City platform information and inputs from License Plate Recognition cameras to assess access patterns and forecast congestion hotspots. Predictive tools supported dynamic policy adjustments to enhance mobility and parking accessibility. Co-creation workshops with local stakeholders ensured that policy design reflected community needs and practical constraints. The initiative enabled more precise targeting of interventions, reduced travel time for vulnerable users and strengthened inclusive urban planning. By integrating advanced analytics with participatory governance, the project contributes to fairer and more efficient mobility systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: The AI-based LisNav application improves the lives of the visually impaired
source_description: For visually impaired people, moving independently through unfamiliar indoor and outdoor spaces can be difficult, especially where transport, navigation, and points of interest are not presented in accessible ways. LisNav was developed to address this challenge by improving how users perceive and interact with their surroundings, with particular value in navigating public transport environments and urban spaces. The objective is to increase independence, accessibility, and confidence by giving users real-time auditory support tailored to their location and immediate context. The implementation combines intelligent algorithms with real-time audio descriptions, drawing on publicly available datasets and user-contributed information such as local points of interest and transport details. In particular, the system provides information about bus stops and the wider bus-stop network, helping users orient themselves and travel more effectively. At a conceptual level, LisNav links location-aware data, accessibility-focused design, and audio interaction to create an augmented navigation layer for visually impaired users. Developed by 3FINERY, the solution applies AR-related capability in a way that supports practical, everyday mobility rather than generic mapping alone. The impact includes better access to transport information, greater autonomy in unfamiliar surroundings, and an improved user experience in navigating cities. It also offers a scalable digital-assistance model for inclusive mobility services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: RECITAL' Project: Immediate and Long-Term Energy Reduction
source_description: Municipal buildings represent a significant share of urban energy consumption, yet fragmented monitoring systems limit proactive management of inefficiencies. The RECITAL project in Noisy-le-Grand introduced an “energy hypervisor” to centralise and analyse ten years of consumption data across municipal buildings. The system aggregates data from smart meters and IoT sensors installed in each facility, enabling daily tracking of electricity and heating usage. Analytical models detect anomalies and trigger alerts when overconsumption patterns occur, supporting rapid corrective action. Historical data analysis informs long-term renovation and decarbonisation strategies, while real-time monitoring enhances operational efficiency. The integration of sensing infrastructure with advanced analytics allows targeted optimisation of energy use and improved performance benchmarking. Expected outcomes include reduced energy expenditure, lower carbon emissions and improved sustainability planning. The project demonstrates how data-driven building management can accelerate municipal energy transition efforts and support climate neutrality objectives.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CyberKit4SME - Democratizing a Cyber Security Toolkit for SMEs & Mes
source_description: Small and medium-sized enterprises often lack the resources and expertise to implement robust cybersecurity measures, leaving them vulnerable to data breaches and operational disruptions. CyberKit4SME aimed to provide accessible, affordable and easy-to-use tools enabling SMEs and mid-sized enterprises to better monitor, forecast and manage cyber risks. The project developed practical encryption and system isolation solutions tailored to constrained IT environments, ensuring data protection without requiring advanced in-house capabilities. In addition, blockchain-based mechanisms were introduced to facilitate secure sharing of threat intelligence and incident reports between companies and Computer Emergency Response Teams. The toolkit integrates risk awareness modules and monitoring functions within a user-friendly interface designed for non-specialist users. By lowering technical and financial barriers, the initiative enhances cyber resilience across supply chains. Expected impacts include improved threat detection, stronger collaboration with response authorities and reduced vulnerability of smaller enterprises to cyberattacks, contributing to a more secure digital economy.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CITIES2023 - Co-creating resIlient and susTaInable food systEms towardS FOOD2030
context: General economic, commercial and labour affair
source_description: Urban food systems face challenges related to sustainability, traceability and coordination among diverse stakeholders. The CITIES2030 project brought together researchers, entrepreneurs, civil society and municipalities to transform how food is produced, transported, supplied and reused within urban food system ecosystems. A blockchain-based, data-driven management platform was developed to create a digital twin of the urban food system, integrating information across supply chains. The platform enables secure data exchange, transparency of transactions and monitoring of sustainability indicators throughout the lifecycle of food products. Analytical tools process system-wide data to identify inefficiencies and support evidence-based policy interventions. By fostering collaboration and trust among partners, the project promotes citizen-centred and resilient food governance. Expected outcomes include reduced waste, improved traceability and enhanced sustainability performance. The initiative demonstrates how digital twin modelling and distributed ledger technologies can strengthen urban food system coordination and long-term resilience.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: PILLAR Robots - a project to increase the autonomy of AI-based robots
source_description: PILLAR Robots addresses a fundamental operational challenge in robotics: enabling robots to function with greater autonomy across different domains while ensuring that what they learn remains relevant to real deployment contexts. Many autonomous systems can acquire behaviours through training, yet they often struggle to generalise beyond narrow environments or to focus learning on what truly matters for practical applications. This use case therefore involves robotics researchers, developers and application-oriented stakeholders seeking to improve the adaptability and usefulness of autonomous machines in real-world settings. Its objective is to help robots acquire the knowledge and capabilities needed for target applications more efficiently by giving them a stronger internal basis for selecting, prioritising and acting on relevant goals. The solution is implemented by operationalising the concept of “purpose”, drawn from cognitive science, within robotic cognitive architectures. At a conceptual level, the project develops algorithms for purpose acquisition, mechanisms to bias perceptual, motivational and decision systems towards purposeful behaviour, and learning strategies for representations, skills and models that support both deliberative and reactive decision-making. These elements are designed to work together so that learning is not only autonomous but also better aligned with task relevance. The expected impact is increased robot autonomy, stronger domain independence and more effective acquisition of usable skills. More broadly, the project creates value by improving the transferability, reliability and practical utility of autonomous robots in applied settings.
