title: Aquatic Litter Drones
source_description: Monitoring marine and freshwater litter is essential for environmental protection, yet manual surveys are labour-intensive and inconsistent. This use case establishes a service that processes drone imagery to detect and classify floating litter in water bodies and on beaches. Unmanned aerial vehicles conduct surveys at varying altitudes, generating high-resolution images that are uploaded to a digital platform. Two convolutional neural network models analyse the imagery to quantify and categorise observed waste, producing standardised datasets for environmental management. The system integrates image storage, processing and analytics into a unified workflow, enabling scalable monitoring across regions. Field applications in collaboration with international organisations have demonstrated operational feasibility and support for clean-up initiatives. The approach enhances accuracy, comparability and timeliness of litter assessments. By providing actionable data for policymakers and local stakeholders, the solution strengthens environmental monitoring, supports targeted interventions and contributes to marine ecosystem preservation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SignAvatar – AI Speech to SignLangauge Translator at the Belgrade airport
source_description: Hearing-impaired travellers can be excluded from essential transport information when announcements are delivered only through spoken audio or standard text displays that do not fully meet their communication needs. At Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport, this use case was introduced to improve accessibility by translating passenger announcements into sign language and making key travel information easier to understand within the terminal environment. The objective is to reduce communication barriers, improve passenger experience for deaf and hard-of-hearing users, and demonstrate how inclusive announcement systems can be integrated into major transport hubs. The implementation uses SignAvatar’s TransportSign solution, which automatically converts speech and text into sign-language output displayed on screens. During the airport trial, five screens were installed across the terminal, and the same solution has also been adopted at Belgrade’s central railway station. At a conceptual level, the system combines speech and text processing with sign-language generation so that operational messages can be communicated in a more accessible visual form. The impact includes improved accessibility of real-time passenger information, a more inclusive travel environment, and reduced dependence on ad hoc assistance for understanding announcements. It also provides a scalable model for transport operators seeking to make station and airport communications more equitable and user-centred.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Inter-municipal Chatbot MUNI - Aarhus
source_description: Citizens often find municipal websites and self-service systems difficult to navigate, particularly when they are unsure which service they need or how to complete a process such as obtaining a passport, using MitID, or arranging childcare. MUNI was created to improve this interface between citizens and local government by offering a more conversational and accessible route into municipal services across a large inter-municipal collaboration in Denmark. The objective is to supplement or partially replace traditional self-service pathways with more efficient and user-friendly AI-supported interaction, while ensuring that people can still reach a human adviser if the automated route does not resolve their need. The implementation combines chatbot technology with integrations into municipal call-centre and self-service systems, including Puzzel and Selvbetjening.nu, and more recent descriptions present MUNI as an AI-driven chat and voicebot. Public descriptions of the project report collaboration across 36 municipalities, with the potential to expand further, and note that since launch citizens have rated the service highly, averaging 2.43 out of 3. Where the chatbot cannot provide sufficient help, it can offer a callback from a call-centre agent. The impact includes faster access to municipal guidance, better user experience, and stronger scalability of citizen support across participating authorities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Itla View – Crowdsourcing and AI-based digital tool for knowledge management and systems change in public sector
source_description: Itla View is a digital tool to help local services address the fragmentation of information across services supporting children, young people, and families, where stakeholders lack a shared, up-to-date understanding of well-being and service needs. This limits the ability to identify risks early and coordinate preventive actions. The objective is to create a shared situational awareness to support proactive and coordinated service delivery. The solution aggregates observations from field actors with indicator data and contextual information such as local news, applying analytical techniques to identify patterns and relationships across datasets. The system enables visualisation and interpretation of combined insights, supporting decision-making across organisations. It is conceptually integrated into local service ecosystems to facilitate collaboration and data sharing. The impact includes improved early identification of needs, stronger preventive interventions, and enhanced coordination among stakeholders. It also supports more efficient resource allocation, better service outcomes, and long-term system-level improvements in public sector effectiveness.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Humanising Authonomy - Behavioural AI to improve the safety of public transport
source_description: Public transport and freight operators in London face a persistent road safety challenge in complex urban environments, where interactions between buses, heavy vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, and other road users can change rapidly and create significant risk. Within the context of Transport for London’s Freight Lab and the wider ambition to meet Vision Zero by 2041, this use case aims to strengthen vehicle safety standards and reduce deaths and serious injuries by improving how vehicles detect and respond to human behaviour. The stakeholders include transport authorities, fleet operators, drivers, vehicle technology providers, and road users. The implementation uses real-time intent prediction software that analyses live camera feeds to interpret and anticipate the behaviour of pedestrians, passengers, and surrounding vehicles. Behavioural models and computer vision techniques infer likely movement patterns and provide inputs to vehicle decision systems, supporting functions such as automated emergency braking, front and near-side alerts, and rear-view camera monitoring. The solution is designed to integrate with different levels of vehicle autonomy, from driver assistance in conventional vehicles to more automated environments. The expected impact includes faster hazard recognition, improved driver awareness, and more reliable preventive action, contributing to safer streets, better compliance with evolving safety standards, and reduced operational and social costs linked to collisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Generative AI Assistant PARLA for the City of Berlin
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Public administrations and political institutions generate thousands of documents, but finding the right information quickly across parliamentary papers, committee procedures, and written questions can be time-consuming for civil servants, journalists, associations, and citizens alike. In Berlin, PARLA was developed to make this documentary landscape more searchable and intelligible by supporting research across a large corpus of public documents. The objective is to reduce the effort involved in navigating administrative and parliamentary records, improve access to public information, and provide answer suggestions that remain traceable to their documentary sources. The implementation uses AI to search and synthesise information from more than 10,000 public documents, including answers to written parliamentary questions and main committee procedures, and presents results through a question-answer interface. The system generates proposed answers based on the underlying text and cites the documents used, while also warning users that generated responses are not legally binding and should be checked against the linked sources. At a conceptual level, PARLA combines retrieval, synthesis, and source referencing in one research assistant for public documentation. The impact includes quicker information retrieval, improved transparency through traceable sourcing, and better support for daily work in parliament and administration, while also making complex documentary repositories more usable for external stakeholders.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ABILITY - Improving the accessibility of digital images for blind users
source_description: For blind and visually impaired people, digital images often remain difficult to access in a meaningful way, because standard image analysis tools are typically designed around the assumptions and preferences of sighted users. This creates a gap between what current systems can technically describe and what users actually need in order to form an accurate and useful mental representation of visual content. The objective of this use case is to improve accessibility by developing image interpretation tools tailored to the needs, expectations, and sensory strategies of blind and visually impaired users, with these users involved directly as co-designers and evaluators. The implementation combines computer vision, large language models, and visual-assistant language models with extensive user studies, tactile interaction research, and iterative testing. The partners are also developing dedicated hardware, including a tactile tablet and a pin-display device capable of presenting simplified object outlines, zoomed elements, and other selected outputs derived from image analysis. The system concept therefore links multimodal models with tactile interfaces and user-centred evaluation methods. The anticipated results include more relevant and nuanced image descriptions, improved usability and trust, and a more inclusive digital experience. More broadly, the project supports accessible design innovation, stronger user adoption, and better alignment between emerging image technologies and real user needs.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: A2I - Networked hearing system with innovative sensors
source_description: In audiological, occupational health, and cardiological care, clinicians often rely on fragmented observations and periodic assessments, which can limit their ability to identify emerging issues early and respond with appropriately tailored interventions. This is particularly relevant where hearing-related data may also provide insights into wider physiological conditions, yet such information is not routinely captured or connected across care pathways. The purpose of this use case is to create a user-centred socio-technical system that improves prevention, diagnosis, and care processes by using sensor-based data gathered in and around the ear. The implementation combines innovative hearing-related sensors with data analysis methods to process continuous or repeated health signals collected from wearable or ear-based devices. Analytical models are used to detect patterns relevant to audiological status, occupational exposure, and cardiological indicators, while the overall architecture links sensing technologies, health data processing, and evaluation workflows in a conceptually integrated system. The development approach is explicitly user-focused, ensuring that the technical design reflects clinical and practical needs. The expected impact includes earlier identification of health risks, better continuity of care, and more efficient clinical decision-making. Additional value lies in improved service integration, stronger preventive capacity, and the potential to scale monitoring and assessment across multiple healthcare contexts with greater reliability and personalisation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: RenovAlte - Resilient planning and design of renovation projects
source_description: Building renovation projects frequently encounter delays, cost overruns and vulnerability to changing environmental conditions, undermining long-term sustainability objectives. RenovAIte aims to develop resilient planning methodologies for housing renovation and infrastructure maintenance through advanced simulation and data-driven analysis. The project creates a simulation environment capable of modelling renovation scenarios using sensor data and predictive analytics. Adversarial resilience learning techniques are applied to evaluate potential disruptions and optimise project design under uncertain conditions. The system supports decision-makers in selecting renovation strategies that minimise delays and reduce the need for premature re-renovation. Integrated monitoring of streets and buildings enhances situational awareness and long-term asset management. By combining simulation modelling with adaptive optimisation, the project strengthens robustness of renovation planning. Expected benefits include improved project efficiency, enhanced climate resilience and more sustainable use of public and private resources in the built environment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FloReST - Intelligent tools for urban flood resilience
source_description: Increasing frequency of heavy rainfall events has exposed urban areas to significant risks of flash flooding, causing damage to infrastructure and disrupting communities. Municipal authorities require tools to plan emergency drainage routes and improve resilience, but traditional hydraulic modelling approaches are complex, time-intensive, and difficult to scale. The FloReST project, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, aims to enhance urban flood resilience by providing decision-support tools tailored to local conditions. The solution combines hydraulic-numerical modelling with machine learning techniques to simulate and optimise emergency water drainage pathways across urban environments. These models are supported by data from terrain, infrastructure, and environmental sources, enabling scalable analysis of larger catchment areas. The project also includes user-oriented applications designed to support municipalities and infrastructure operators in planning and response. Pilot testing of a smart application with end users took place in 2024. The approach demonstrates improved modelling efficiency and usability, supporting better preparedness and risk mitigation, although full operational deployment remains under evaluation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Albert France Services - GenAI tool to support public servants
source_description: Front-line public-service advisers often need to consult large volumes of guidance and partner documentation in order to answer citizen questions accurately, which can slow down interviews and reduce the time available for direct support. Albert France Services was introduced to assist advisers in the France Services network by giving them quicker access to reliable information tailored to the user situation they are handling. The objective is to support public servants rather than replace them, improve the speed and consistency of responses, and make it easier to navigate the documentation used in day-to-day case support. The implementation forms part of the broader Albert initiative developed by DINUM and Etalab as a sovereign, open, and secure generative AI capability for public administration. In the France Services version, the tool uses a natural-language response engine that draws on documentation from France Services partners and practical fact sheets from servicepublic.fr, returning sourced answers in French through a search-style interface. More broadly, official materials describe Albert as an interministerial inference platform hosted in a secure sovereign environment. The impact includes faster retrieval of dependable information, better support for advisers handling varied citizen needs, and improved operational efficiency in front-line public service. It also creates a reusable model for scaled adoption of generative AI across administrations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GenAI for Legislative Drafting - Ministry of Transports
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Legislative drafting requires civil servants to examine large volumes of legal, policy, and background material, making the process time-consuming and cognitively demanding, particularly when consistency, traceability, and language quality must be maintained throughout. In this context, the Ministry of Transport and Communications sought to improve the efficiency of drafting work while also reinforcing Finland’s strategic autonomy in digital capability. The objective of the use case was to test whether a practical support service could help drafters navigate legislative content more effectively and retrieve relevant information in a structured manner. The implementation consisted of a service demonstrator built by Futurice around Finnish-language large language models, delivered through a chatbot-style interface. At a conceptual level, the solution allowed legislative drafters to query legislation and related materials in natural language, with the model supporting information retrieval, question answering, and synthesis over large text collections. The system design explored how domestic language models could be incorporated into policy workflows while remaining aligned with public sector requirements. The results indicate potential for reducing time spent searching and reviewing documentation, improving accessibility of complex legal material, and supporting more efficient drafting processes. The wider business value includes strengthened experimentation capacity, greater technological sovereignty, and a foundation for more scalable digital support in public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GenAI for Legislative Drafting - Prime Minister's Office
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Analysing statements submitted during consultation rounds is a demanding part of legislative preparation, as officials must review substantial volumes of written feedback, identify recurring themes, and produce coherent summaries under time pressure. This creates an operational challenge in terms of workload, speed, and consistency, especially when consultation material is extensive and diverse in style or content. The purpose of this use case was to assess whether automated support could help the Prime Minister’s Office process consultation responses more efficiently and accelerate the preparation of summary material for legislative work. The implementation tested the Finnish Poro language model in a summarisation setting, with the experiment carried out by Silo Gen AI Oy and funded by Sitra. At a conceptual level, the approach used a Finnish large language model to generate condensed summaries from consultation texts, exploring how language technology could support document analysis in a policy environment. The trial focused on the model’s ability to synthesise large volumes of textual input into usable outputs for expert review. The results showed clear potential for increasing efficiency in the analysis of consultation rounds, even though the summaries produced were not yet of sufficient quality for operational adoption. Even so, the exercise generated valuable learning on model limitations, future capability needs, and opportunities to improve productivity, scalability, and evidence handling in legislative processes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LUMI - the Made-in-Europe chatbot for Heidelberg
source_description: Municipal residents often need simple guidance on everyday administrative matters, yet city websites can be difficult to navigate when users do not know the exact terminology or service path they need. Heidelberg introduced Lumi to create a more natural and convenient way for citizens to interact with the city through a chat-based interface rather than conventional menu navigation. The objective is to support citizens with routine administrative tasks, improve access to public information, and learn from real interactions in order to refine a more tailored digital-assistance service for the city. The implementation uses large language models developed by Heidelberg-based company Aleph Alpha and draws on publicly available information from the city of Heidelberg to generate responses. The city explains that Lumi can already help with issues such as changing address within Heidelberg or finding waste-paper collection times, and that after an internal testing phase it was opened to citizens so the system could learn what residents ask and how they phrase requests. At a conceptual level, the solution combines a public information base with an LLM-powered conversational interface designed for municipal use. The impact includes easier access to city information, a more intuitive user experience, and better scalability of first-line citizen support, while also giving the city a practical way to experiment with European AI capability in public services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GPT-enabled chatbot of the Rhineland-Palatinate Development Agency
source_description: Agencies that run many projects and programmes often hold relevant information across numerous internal and public materials, making it difficult for users to obtain quick, targeted answers about activities, tasks, and ongoing work. The Rhineland-Palatinate Development Agency addressed this issue by experimenting with an AI assistant that responds to questions about the agency’s projects and remit through its website. The objective is to improve access to organisational information, reduce the effort required to search through scattered material, and test how conversational interfaces can support communication about public development activity. The implementation uses a GPT-enabled assistant that has been specially configured with information about the agency’s own activities, rather than relying only on the general background knowledge of the underlying model. At a conceptual level, the system combines a large language model with agency-specific material to generate answers about projects and responsibilities through a web-based conversational interface. The impact includes easier access to relevant information, quicker resolution of routine informational queries, and a more user-friendly digital front door for stakeholders interested in the agency’s work. It also offers a practical model for limited-scope deployment of generative AI in public-sector communication and knowledge access.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ZüriCityGPT
source_description: People seeking information about city administration often face a familiar problem: official websites contain a great deal of useful content, but search and navigation do not always produce direct answers to practical questions. ZüriCityGPT addresses this by offering a conversational layer over publicly available information about Zurich, allowing users to ask questions in natural language and receive concise answers rather than a list of links alone. The objective is to make local administrative information easier to access, reduce friction in finding relevant guidance, and demonstrate how city-related public information can be made more usable through a question-answer interface. The implementation uses a chatbot grounded in content published on the City of Zurich website; public descriptions of the project explain that it can answer questions based on that material and also offers a version linked to the Swiss LLM Apertus. At a conceptual level, the solution combines retrieval over a defined public corpus with generative answering to provide more precise responses about city services and local administration. The impact includes a more accessible user experience, quicker access to relevant local information, and a scalable way to make complex city websites easier to use. Public project information also makes clear that the tool is Zurich-focused but not officially affiliated with the City of Zurich.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DutchCycling - Cycling Lifestyle AI
source_description: Streets in many cities remain dominated by cars, limited greenery, and fragmented cycling infrastructure, making it difficult for residents and planners to imagine what a healthier, more bicycle-friendly street could look like in practice. The DutchCycling Lifestyle AI project addresses this challenge by giving people a simple way to visualise how an existing street might be transformed into a greener and more cycle-oriented environment inspired by Dutch design principles. The objective is to stimulate public imagination, support discussion on liveability and active mobility, and make the Dutch cycling approach more tangible for users anywhere in the world. The implementation combines generative AI with Google Street View imagery and the expertise of Dutch cycling specialists, allowing users to enter an address, select or upload a street view, and generate alternative visualisations of a more sustainable street layout. At a conceptual level, the tool links image-based generation with mobility-design knowledge to create plausible illustrative scenarios rather than detailed engineering plans. Public project material also makes clear that the tool was designed primarily as an inspiration device and that the concept has since been made open source after the original public tool was taken offline. The impact lies in widening public engagement, making policy ideas easier to communicate visually, and providing a scalable digital method for promoting cycling-friendly urban transformation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Delft University of Technology Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management
title: IVORY – ‘AI for Vision Zero in Road Safety’
source_description: Achieving major reductions in road fatalities requires more than isolated technical improvements, as road safety depends on the interaction between vehicles, infrastructure, human behaviour, governance, and public trust. In support of the United Nations target to halve traffic deaths by 2030 and the European Vision Zero strategy to eliminate road fatalities by 2050, this use case aims to build a robust framework for responsible innovation in road safety while developing specialist expertise across sectors. The stakeholders include universities, industrial partners, associated organisations, researchers, and road safety actors from ten countries. The implementation takes the form of an industrial doctoral network bringing together engineering, data science, and ethics of technology to develop new responsible AI applications for road-user assistance and infrastructure safety management. The programme integrates research training, cross-sector collaboration, and applied experimentation, with 13 researchers working on solutions that combine advanced analytical methods, domain knowledge, and governance considerations. Rather than a single product, the system is a coordinated innovation and learning platform designed to connect research outputs with real-world road safety needs. The expected impact includes stronger interdisciplinary capability, improved methods for safer transport systems, and a more scalable pipeline of expertise. It also creates long-term value through knowledge transfer, international collaboration, and more reliable foundations for future road safety innovation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DIPLOMA Project - Electronic, Didactic and Innovative Platform for Learning based On Multimedia Assets
source_description: The e-DIPLOMA project was initiated in response to challenges identified during the rapid transition to online learning caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, including disparities in access to technology, insufficient teacher training, and limitations in existing digital learning environments. The objective is to enhance the quality, inclusiveness, and effectiveness of distance education across Europe by developing a next-generation e-learning platform. The project adopts a co-creation approach involving educators, students, families, and policymakers to ensure that the platform addresses real user needs. The solution integrates multiple advanced technologies, including immersive environments, intelligent tutoring components, interactive content delivery, and conversational interfaces, to create engaging and adaptive learning experiences. It also incorporates analytics to monitor learning progress and personalise content. As an ongoing EU-funded research and innovation project, the platform is under development and validation. Expected impacts include improved learner engagement, accessibility, and pedagogical outcomes, although large-scale deployment results are not yet available.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research ( BMBWF )
title: Eduthek - The learning platform on AI for schools
source_description: Schools need accessible, up-to-date teaching materials on artificial intelligence, yet many teachers and families lack the time or specialist expertise to assemble reliable resources independently. Austria’s Eduthek responds to this by providing a dedicated digital space within the Ministry’s wider learning platform where teachers, pupils, and parents can access curated material on AI in a structured and reusable format. The objective is to improve AI literacy in schools, support teaching on a fast-changing topic, and make high-quality educational resources easier to find and apply across different levels of schooling. The implementation uses the Eduthek platform as a central repository and delivery channel for learning content, with a specific AI focus area that is continuously expanded and updated. The official course page describes the section as an overview of freely available teaching materials for lower and upper secondary education, designed to help schools address both the opportunities and the challenges raised by AI in everyday life and work. At a conceptual level, the solution combines digital curation, thematic organisation, and open access to support classroom use without requiring each school to build its own material base. The impact includes broader access to AI-related teaching resources, more consistent support for educators, and a scalable way to strengthen digital and technological understanding across the school system.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
title: Humphrey - AI tool to streamline public services, eliminate delays through improved data sharing, and reduce costs
source_description: Public services often suffer from fragmented data, repetitive administrative work, and slow internal processes, which can delay service delivery and reduce the time civil servants can spend on higher-value tasks. Humphrey was introduced by the UK government to address these operational bottlenecks across the civil service by improving productivity, reducing reliance on manual document handling, and supporting faster, more consistent decision-support processes. The objective is to modernise government operations, improve internal efficiency, and reduce costs through a shared suite of AI tools rather than isolated pilots in individual departments. The implementation consists of a family of government-built AI tools developed by the Incubator for AI for tasks such as summarisation, consultation analysis, and administrative support, with civil servants interacting through secure digital interfaces. Public government sources show that Humphrey has already been used to review consultation responses and, in 2025, was also trialled with 25 councils to support work in areas such as planning and social care, indicating that it has moved beyond concept stage into active experimentation and deployment. The impact includes faster processing of large document volumes, reduced administrative burden, improved scalability of internal government work, and potential savings in consultancy and operational costs, while also building a reusable AI capability across public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
title: GOV.UK App chatbot
source_description: Citizens often need to interact with multiple government services through separate websites and processes, making routine tasks time-consuming and difficult to navigate. The GOV.UK App was created to simplify this experience by giving people a single mobile entry point to government services, while the associated GOV.UK Chat capability is intended to make complex information easier to access through conversational interaction. The objective is to improve usability, reduce friction in service navigation, and provide faster access to relevant guidance across government. The implementation combines the GOV.UK App with GOV.UK One Login and an AI-powered GOV.UK Chat feature that uses generative AI to answer questions based on GOV.UK guidance. Official UK sources state that GOV.UK Chat was piloted with 10,000 business users, answered almost 24,000 questions, achieved relevant answers in about 90 per cent of cases, and blocked all tested prompt-manipulation attempts; the government’s algorithmic transparency record also confirms it as an active GDS system. The impact includes more accessible digital public services, quicker resolution of routine information needs, and a more scalable way to guide users through government content, while creating a foundation for more personalised and proactive service delivery through the app.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL)
title: AI Applications within INAIL
source_description: A large public insurance and prevention body such as INAIL must manage diverse tasks ranging from workplace-accident prevention and grant administration to customer service, medical evaluation, fraud control, and legal support, all under strong regulatory and public-value constraints. INAIL’s AI programme addresses this challenge by using data-driven tools to improve operational efficiency, prevention capability, and service quality across several functions rather than in a single isolated application. The objective is to create public value by modernising workflows, improving decision support, and embedding stronger governance for current and future AI use. The implementation includes adopted and developing AI systems across areas such as predictive analysis for accident prevention, customer-service enquiries, automation of ISI grant-management processes, medical and expert assessment support, fraud detection, knowledge-base management, legal assistance, and IT costing. Recent INAIL public material on its 2025–2027 prevention strategy and innovation agenda confirms that AI and related digital technologies remain part of its active prevention and transformation work. The impact includes better planning, more targeted prevention, faster handling of routine processes, and more scalable service delivery, while also supporting stronger institutional learning and improved alignment between prevention, operational efficiency, and user experience.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI @ EDGE: advancing traffic management for cooperative connected and automated vehicles
source_description: The AI@EDGE project addresses challenges in managing traffic involving cooperative, connected, and automated vehicles (CCAVs), particularly in complex scenarios such as roundabouts where coordination and safety remain difficult. Inefficient negotiation of such intersections can lead to congestion, increased accident risk, and higher emissions. The objective is to improve traffic flow and safety by leveraging advanced communication and computing infrastructures. The solution combines edge computing and 5G network capabilities with machine learning models to enable real-time decision-making and coordination among vehicles and infrastructure. These models simulate and optimise vehicle interactions, particularly at bottlenecks, by processing data locally at the network edge to reduce latency. The system supports virtual validation environments to test traffic scenarios and control strategies. As an ongoing research project, the approach is being developed and tested, with expected benefits including improved traffic efficiency, reduced accidents, and lower environmental impact, although real-world deployment remains limited.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: crowdHEDGE: Using AI to help governments and local authorities keep citizens safe
source_description: Local authorities need timely information on how public spaces are being used, especially when crowding, footfall, or unsafe proximity may affect public health and safety, yet traditional monitoring methods can be slow, incomplete, or costly to scale. In Turin, crowdHEDGE was piloted to help the city extract actionable insight from drone footage over parks and other public areas so that officials could understand how people were using space and respond more effectively. The objective is to improve situational awareness, support safer management of public areas, and provide public-health and city officials with evidence they can explore by location and time. The implementation uses drone video streams connected to an AI-based image-recognition and analytics system running with edge-computing infrastructure. According to Addfor, the solution processes footage close to the source, calculates metrics such as crowd size, approximate distancing, and foot-traffic levels, and presents results through a graphical interface for geographical and temporal analysis. At a conceptual level, the system combines aerial sensing, computer vision, and edge analytics in a workflow designed to reduce bandwidth demands while preserving operational responsiveness. The impact includes faster and more detailed insight into how public spaces are used, better support for local safety decisions, and a scalable model for using drone-based analytics in urban public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AIxPA - Artificial Intelligence for the Public Administration
source_description: The AIxPA project, led by the Bruno Kessler Foundation in collaboration with the Autonomous Province of Trento, aims to strengthen data-driven decision-making capabilities within public administrations. Public authorities face increasing complexity in managing socio-economic systems, territorial dynamics, and public services, requiring advanced tools for analysis and forecasting. The objective is to develop a general-purpose analytical platform tailored to public sector needs, supporting multiple domains such as mobility, environmental management, and economic development. The solution uses machine learning models, data integration techniques, and simulation tools to analyse large-scale datasets and generate predictive insights. It incorporates digital twin concepts to model complex systems and support scenario analysis. The platform is designed to be reusable and scalable across different public administrations. As an ongoing initiative, the project is currently developing and validating use cases, with expected benefits including improved policy design, more efficient resource allocation, and enhanced analytical capacity within the public sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Visa Application Chatbot for the EU countries
source_description: The European Commission, in collaboration with Member State authorities and eu-LISA, initiated the VisaChat pilot to address challenges faced by visa applicants in accessing clear and consistent information on Schengen visa procedures. Applicants often rely on fragmented or complex sources, increasing administrative burden and the risk of errors in applications. The objective of the use case was to provide a unified, accessible interface to answer frequently asked questions and improve user experience. The solution consists of a chatbot application designed to respond to general visa-related queries using predefined knowledge bases. It employs supervised learning techniques based on curated datasets of standard responses in multiple languages, complemented by machine translation and unsupervised approaches to extend multilingual capabilities. The system is modular and built using open-source technologies, allowing flexible deployment either centrally or through Member State portals. Privacy-by-design principles are incorporated, including explicit restrictions on collecting personal data. As a pilot conducted between 2021 and 2022, the project demonstrated feasibility in improving information access, but no evidence confirms transition to full-scale implementation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
title: Redbox - Bringing Generative AI to the way the Civil Service works
source_description: Civil servants work with large volumes of briefings, letters, speeches, meeting minutes, and other documents, and much of their time can be absorbed by locating key information, summarising content, and drafting routine material. Redbox was created inside the UK government to address this administrative burden by giving officials a secure generative AI tool for document interaction and general workplace tasks. The objective was to improve productivity, reduce time spent on repetitive document handling, and help staff engage more efficiently with complex written material so they could focus more on higher-value work. The implementation, developed by the Incubator for AI, provided a chat-based and document-oriented assistant that could summarise files, answer questions about their contents, and support drafting and exploration of official material, including at OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE level. Public information from i.AI states that Redbox was rolled out to more than 6,000 users and used across over 150,000 chats and 1.3 million messages. At a conceptual level, the tool combined secure access to large language models with document-processing workflows tailored to government use. The impact included faster information handling, lower administrative effort, and valuable learning for future public-sector AI deployment, even though the project was later sunset as comparable enterprise tools became more widely available in government.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministry for Digital Transformation and of Civil Service
title: V-city - A human-centric platform for Urban Digital Twins
source_description: Cities increasingly need better tools to test the likely effects of public policies before implementation, especially when addressing complex issues such as climate change, social inequality, mobility, and sustainable development. Traditional planning methods can struggle to combine diverse datasets, simulate policy alternatives, and communicate likely outcomes clearly to decision-makers and stakeholders. The purpose of this use case is to support evidence-based urban planning through a human-centric digital platform that helps public authorities and ecosystem partners explore, predict, and visualise the consequences of different interventions. The implementation centres on an urban digital twin platform led by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center, combining real city data with simulation layers and visual analytics. At a conceptual level, the platform integrates heterogeneous urban datasets, modelling tools, and visualisation capabilities to represent current conditions and assess the projected impact of policies in a virtual environment. The approach also seeks to strengthen the surrounding public-private ecosystem by advancing capability in an emerging field of public service technology. The impact includes improved foresight, better-informed planning decisions, and clearer communication of policy trade-offs. In addition, the platform supports scalability in urban analysis, increases institutional capacity for innovation, and creates strategic value by positioning participating organisations to lead in the development and application of digital twin technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BlockchainGov - Blockchain for distributed governance
source_description: The BlockchainGov project explores how distributed ledger technologies can support new models of governance in decentralised digital environments. Traditional governance structures often struggle to ensure transparency, accountability, and inclusive participation in digital communities. The objective is to design and evaluate governance frameworks that can operate effectively in blockchain-based ecosystems. The project combines theoretical analysis with empirical research to develop models that integrate technical protocols, social norms, and economic incentive structures. These models incorporate both on-chain and off-chain governance mechanisms, including voting systems, dispute resolution processes, and participatory decision-making approaches. Techniques such as smart contracts and consensus mechanisms are analysed and adapted to support governance functions. The project includes participatory action research, where selected communities test proposed models and provide feedback. As an ongoing research initiative, the project is still developing and validating these frameworks, with expected contributions to improved transparency, inclusiveness, and robustness of decentralised governance systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FutureCloud - Privacy preserving federated machine learning and blockchaining for reduced cyber risks in a world of distributed healthcare
source_description: The FeatureCloud project addresses the challenge of enabling collaborative analysis of sensitive healthcare data across institutions while maintaining strict privacy and security requirements. Centralised data sharing models increase the risk of data breaches and limit cross-border collaboration due to regulatory constraints. The objective is to enable secure, decentralised data analysis for medical research and innovation. The solution is based on federated machine learning, where models are trained locally on institutional datasets and only model updates are shared, combined with blockchain technologies to ensure integrity, traceability, and trust in distributed processes. The platform implements a privacy-by-design architecture that avoids central data storage and minimises data exposure. It provides a software toolkit enabling researchers and healthcare providers to perform joint analyses without exchanging raw data. As an EU-funded research and innovation project, the system is under development and validation, with expected impacts including enhanced cybersecurity, compliance with data protection regulations, and improved capacity for collaborative medical research.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Dublin Region Active Travel Dashboard
source_description: Transport planners and policymakers need robust evidence on how people walk and cycle across a city, but active-travel data are often fragmented across multiple sources and difficult for non-specialists to use in one place. The Dublin Region Active Travel Dashboard was developed to address this by bringing together key walking and cycling indicators for the capital in a single digital environment that supports evidence-informed mobility planning. The objective is to improve access to active-travel intelligence, support more sustainable transport policy, and make it easier for stakeholders to understand patterns in commuting and route usage. The implementation combines open and operational datasets, including Census information, canal cordon counts, bicycle counters, Google trip data, and Strava-related inputs, into a continuously evolving dashboard. Smart Dublin describes it as a one-stop shop for analysing walking and cycling patterns, while later project material notes that it also correlates activity with infrastructure use, health projections, climate impacts, and estimated financial savings. At a conceptual level, the dashboard integrates heterogeneous mobility datasets into a common visual interface for exploration and comparison. The impact includes better visibility of active-travel behaviour, stronger support for policy and investment decisions, and a scalable platform for sustainable urban-mobility analysis across the Dublin region.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Open LLM France and LINAGORA - Open Source LLM model
source_description: European organisations increasingly want language technologies that are transparent, locally governed, and better aligned with national languages and public-sector requirements than many closed commercial models. The OpenLLM France community and LINAGORA developed LUCIE in this context as an open-source French-language large language model intended to serve as a foundation for dialogue generation and understanding tasks. The objective is to strengthen sovereign and ethical AI capability, provide a reusable base model for French-language applications, and support uses such as meeting summarisation, virtual assistants, and document-related productivity tools. The implementation centres on a pre-trained dialogue-oriented language model developed with open and licensed training datasets, community participation, and access to French high-performance computing resources, including the Jean Zay supercomputer. LINAGORA states that the model is designed to reflect the characteristics of spoken interaction and to be fine-tuned for downstream tasks rather than treated as a fully finished product in itself. At a conceptual level, the initiative combines open model development, transparent data governance, and ecosystem collaboration to create a deployable base model for French-language systems. The impact includes greater technological autonomy, better support for French-language digital services, and a scalable open foundation for public and private innovation in language applications.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GPT@JRC: Generative AI Tool to support Science for Policy at JRC
source_description: Within a large scientific and policy-support organisation such as the Joint Research Centre, staff need secure ways to explore emerging language technologies without exposing sensitive information or working outside institutional governance. The challenge is not only to improve everyday productivity, but also to understand where these tools can genuinely strengthen research activity, policy support, and collaboration across teams and expert communities. The objective of this use case is therefore to provide a controlled environment in which staff can test practical applications, identify risks and opportunities, and develop guidance for effective use across research and operational settings. The implementation takes the form of a secure platform that gives staff access to large language models through a governed internal environment. At a conceptual level, the platform supports several layers of use, from routine tasks such as summarisation, translation, drafting, proofreading, classification, and sentiment analysis, to the enhancement of existing tools and the development of specialised assistants for knowledge synthesis and foresight. It is designed to connect experimentation, API-based cooperation, and institutional learning within the wider European Commission ecosystem. The expected impact includes improved efficiency in knowledge work, stronger internal capability in generative technologies, better-informed governance, and greater organisational readiness to scale high-value, policy-relevant applications safely and consistently.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GPT@EC: Generative AI Tool to support EC administrative task
source_description: Across a large public administration, staff regularly handle time-intensive knowledge tasks such as drafting texts, summarising documents, and producing technical material, often under strict compliance and confidentiality requirements. Reliance on external tools can create risks around data handling, security, and alignment with institutional processes, limiting the safe adoption of advanced digital support. The purpose of this use case is to provide European Commission staff with a secure and compliant environment that improves productivity and creativity while allowing internal information to be processed within the Commission context. The implementation is based on a general-purpose internal platform that provides access to several large language models suited to different tasks and sensitivity levels. At a conceptual level, the service supports text generation, summarisation, code development, and other administrative knowledge tasks, while embedding corporate rules, compliance standards, and secure data handling. It also includes access to open-source and sovereign models, enabling flexibility in model choice according to operational needs and governance constraints. The impact is expected to include faster completion of routine administrative work, improved quality and consistency of outputs, and reduced dependence on third-party services for sensitive tasks. More broadly, the platform strengthens institutional control, supports scalable adoption of trusted digital tools, and creates business value through safer and more efficient administrative processes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: NExt ApplicationS of Quantum Computing
source_description: Quantum computing remains immature for many production uses, yet industry and research actors need to explore practical applications early if they are to understand where near-term quantum systems could create value. NEASQC was created in this context to build a bridge between hardware development and end-user application design, bringing together universities and companies from several European countries to investigate quantum-enabled use cases before the technology fully matures. The objective is to identify promising applications, develop a shared practical toolset, and prepare industrial and scientific actors to experiment with near-term quantum computing. The implementation took the form of an EU-funded consortium project running from September 2020 to 30 November 2024, combining research partners and industrial users in a collaborative environment for application exploration and software-tool development. CORDIS confirms that the project is closed and frames it as an effort to connect NISQ-era hardware activity with practical end-user investigation. The impact lies in capability-building rather than a single public-facing service: the project generated shared tools, results, and application knowledge that can help organisations assess future quantum opportunities more realistically and at lower entry cost.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Max Planck Institute for Human Development
title: AI competences for or the Max Planck Institute for Human Development in the institute's basic research
source_description: Interdisciplinary basic research increasingly depends on high-end AI, machine learning, and software-engineering capability, especially where projects attract public attention and require robust, secure, high-quality digital components. The Max Planck Institute for Human Development used this procurement to obtain specialist external capacity that could support its AI-related research agenda flexibly and quickly across a range of demanding projects. The objective was not to launch a single citizen-facing service, but to secure access to elite AI and software expertise for research work requiring strong quality control, resilience, and technical excellence. The implementation took the form of a framework contract for specialised teams with advanced skills in areas such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, pattern recognition, NLP, generative models, embeddings, and image processing, with an emphasis on assembling the right experts through match-making and quality control. Current Max Planck sources confirm that the institute remains active in AI-related research, particularly around human-machine interaction, which supports the view that this procurement was part of an ongoing research-capability strategy. The impact is therefore improved research execution capacity, faster access to scarce specialist skills, and stronger quality assurance for technically advanced projects, rather than a discrete public-sector AI service with a direct end-user interface.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CdE - Pilot Programme for Series Co-Productions Advertising Visuals
source_description: In the audiovisual sector, promotional content for television series and co-productions must be produced for a highly specialised professional audience across a fast-changing media landscape shaped by multiple distribution channels and new digital production methods. This creates pressure to deliver high-quality advertising visuals efficiently, while adapting to evolving expectations in content creation, branding, and campaign management. The objective of this use case is to support the promotion of series co-productions through modernised visual production processes that are better suited to the speed and complexity of today’s audiovisual industry. The implementation centres on the use of generative and algorithmic content creation and management techniques within the production of advertising materials for professional industry events and market-facing communication. At a conceptual level, the approach combines digital content generation workflows with creative production processes to produce promotional visuals tailored to producers, distributors, sales agents, professional organisations, financial partners, and exhibitors. The solution is intended to fit within the wider communications and campaign ecosystem of the programme, supporting repeatable and adaptable creative production. The expected impact includes faster turnaround in visual asset development, improved responsiveness to market opportunities, and more scalable campaign support across events and formats. It also offers potential cost efficiencies, greater creative flexibility, and stronger visibility for supported series within an increasingly competitive international environment.

title: DestinE Digital Twin Engine (DTE) workflow for weather forecasting.
source_description: Weather forecasting increasingly requires methods that can quantify uncertainty, generate realistic scenario ensembles, and improve temporal detail without unsustainable computational cost. Within Destination Earth, this use case addresses that need by applying advanced generative machine-learning methods to weather forecasting workflows so that public authorities and scientific users can work with richer and more realistic probabilistic scenarios. The objective is to improve forecasting quality, support uncertainty analysis, and make AI-enhanced methods reusable across the DestinE ecosystem. The implementation uses deep-learning techniques including variational auto-encoders, generative adversarial networks, normalising flows, and diffusion models, with researchers from MET Norway, Météo-France, and SMHI collaborating on ensemble generation and temporal downscaling for numerical weather-prediction data. Recent ECMWF and DestinE sources confirm that AI remains an active part of the programme and that Destination Earth has been confirmed for a third phase starting in 2026, indicating continuing institutional commitment beyond the original contract notice. The impact includes more realistic ensembles, improved probabilistic forecasting, better integration of AI into weather and climate digital twins, and a more scalable foundation for future operational and research workflows in European weather forecasting.

title: WISP - Road Crossing Management supported by AI - Pilot - Paris
source_description: Urban traffic-light control often relies on static or costly automated regulation systems that do not adapt well to real-time traffic conditions, leading to unnecessary delays, higher emissions, and inefficient use of infrastructure. WISP was developed to address this problem by optimising traffic-light sequencing dynamically, with an initial field deployment at three intersections in the southern suburbs of Paris. The objective is to reduce waiting times, improve flow management, and lower the ecological and budgetary costs associated with conventional automated signal regulation. The implementation combines real-time traffic-data analysis, connected-vehicle data, optimisation algorithms, and a compact hardware module that can be installed in existing signal-control cabinets. The company states that its AI is specialised in reducing driver waiting time through real-time search for the best signal sequence and that the prototypes already showed waiting-time reductions ranging from 10 per cent to 50 per cent depending on the type of junction. At a conceptual level, the system links live digital traffic inputs with adaptive control logic and lightweight roadside hardware to support responsive intersection management. The impact includes faster vehicle movement through junctions, reduced environmental and operating costs, and a scalable model for upgrading traffic control without the expense of wholesale infrastructure replacement.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: A Public Administration Canvas for Ethical AI implementation
source_description: Public administrations often need structured help to assess legal, ethical, organisational, and technical issues before adopting AI, especially under evolving European regulatory requirements. The Canvas for Ethical AI implementation was developed by FBK with the Autonomous Province of Trento to address this gap by giving public bodies a practical instrument for planning AI adoption responsibly. The objective is to help administrations design AI solutions that are compliant, accountable, and ethically robust from the outset rather than treating ethics as a late-stage add-on. The implementation takes the form of a reusable canvas and guidance framework that prompts users to consider issues such as bias, privacy, accountability, and regulatory fit in a structured way. Current public sources from FBK and the project repository indicate that the tool is available, has been published for broader reuse, and is still being further developed and validated based on the Trento experience. The impact includes better governance readiness, stronger alignment with EU requirements, and a more scalable way for public bodies to assess AI projects consistently before deployment, thereby reducing implementation risk and improving trustworthiness in future AI adoption.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Assess your entitlement to 906 aids: OpenFisca, a tool to writing rules as code
source_description: Social and fiscal rules are often complex, difficult to compare, and hard for both citizens and administrations to apply consistently without digital support. OpenFisca addresses this by turning legal and policy rules into executable code that can be reused to simulate entitlements, compare scenarios, and power public-facing services such as benefit calculators. The objective is to create a common, computable representation of rules so that governments, researchers, developers, and civil society can debate, test, and deliver social and fiscal policy more transparently. The implementation uses the open-source OpenFisca framework, which models taxes and benefits through formal variables, entities, and rule logic that can be exposed through APIs and reused in services such as Mes Aides and Aides Jeunes. The current youth-oriented simulator publicly states that it can estimate eligibility for more than 1,060 aids in a few clicks, while beta.gouv.fr describes OpenFisca as a leading practical implementation of the Rules as Code movement used in multiple countries. At a conceptual level, the solution combines legal modelling, microsimulation, and software engineering to produce machine-executable policy logic. The impact includes faster and more transparent eligibility estimation, easier reuse across public services, and a scalable foundation for policy simulation, digital entitlement tools, and evidence-based reform analysis.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LeXFiles and LegalLAMA: Facilitating English Multinational Legal Language Model Development
source_description: Legal analysis depends heavily on precise language, domain-specific terminology, and the ability to interpret concepts consistently across jurisdictions and document types. General-purpose language models often struggle in this context because they are not sufficiently exposed to specialised legal corpora or evaluated against tasks that reflect genuine legal knowledge. The aim of this use case is to strengthen the development and assessment of legal language models by providing resources that better capture the linguistic and conceptual demands of legal work in a multinational setting. The implementation combines two complementary components: LeXFiles, a large multilingual legal corpus for model training, and LegalLAMA, a benchmark designed to probe legal knowledge in pre-trained language models. At a conceptual level, the project examines how pre-training objectives, model size, and training data influence performance, comparing newly trained and existing models on legal language understanding tasks. The approach supports domain-specific model development grounded in structured evaluation rather than generic performance measures alone. The results show that performance depends strongly on both the data used for pre-training and the scale of the model, highlighting the value of specialised legal resources. The broader impact lies in enabling more reliable legal text processing, improving the quality of downstream legal applications, and supporting more robust, scalable development of language technologies for multilingual legal environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI Sweeps new govs in UK
source_description: Public administrations process large volumes of emails, documents, reports, and routine communications, and this creates pressure to improve productivity without increasing administrative burden. In the United Kingdom, this use case reflects the growing adoption of Microsoft’s AI product suite, including Copilot, across central and local government as a tool for summarising emails, generating text, and supporting document creation. The objective is to streamline routine office work, improve efficiency in day-to-day administrative tasks, and help public servants spend less time on repetitive drafting and information-processing activities. The implementation combines large language model capabilities with office-productivity software used in government environments, embedding AI assistance directly into familiar workflows for document drafting, summarisation, and information handling. Public reporting indicates that more than 100 local councils have adopted the tool and that trials have also taken place in a number of central government departments. The impact includes faster handling of written material, reduced administrative effort, and improved scalability of routine office functions across public bodies. It also shows how AI is being integrated into mainstream workplace software as part of a broader transformation in how government staff manage information and produce content.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Tokenized Bond Issuance
source_description: Public bond issuance processes involve multiple intermediaries, complex settlement mechanisms, and high operational costs, limiting efficiency and innovation in capital markets. Germany’s development bank KfW sought to explore how digital issuance models could modernise bond transactions while remaining aligned with regulatory frameworks and central bank infrastructures. This use case involves KfW, the European Central Bank, Boerse Stuttgart Digital, and financial market participants, with the objective of testing secure, efficient digital bond issuance and settlement. The solution is implemented through a blockchain-based digital bond issued under the German Electronic Securities Act, with lifecycle management supported by crypto wallets and digital registers. The bond issuance is integrated into ECB wholesale settlement trials, enabling delivery-versus-payment transactions using central bank money, with settlement executed on distributed ledger infrastructure. The approach improves settlement speed, transparency, and operational efficiency, reduces reliance on intermediaries, and supports regulatory-compliant innovation. It provides valuable learning for large-scale adoption of tokenised securities, enhances market resilience, and contributes to the evolution of more efficient and interoperable European capital markets.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital sovereign bond
source_description: Sovereign debt management relies on trusted, transparent, and efficient market infrastructures, yet traditional issuance and settlement processes remain complex and costly. Slovenia aimed to modernise its government debt operations and position itself at the forefront of financial innovation within the European Union. This use case focuses on the issuance of the EU’s first digital sovereign bond, involving the Slovenian government, international banks, central banks, and market infrastructure providers, with the objective of increasing efficiency and transparency in sovereign bond markets. The solution is implemented through a distributed ledger-based issuance and settlement framework using the Neobonds platform and Canton blockchain, with settlement carried out via the Banque de France’s interoperability system as part of ECB wholesale experiments. The digital bond lifecycle, from issuance to settlement, is managed through programmable infrastructure that integrates with central bank money. The initiative demonstrates faster settlement, improved auditability, and reduced operational complexity. It strengthens trust in digital financial instruments, supports cross-border interoperability, and establishes a foundation for wider adoption of digital sovereign securities across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital bonds
source_description: European public financial institutions are exploring digital securities to improve efficiency, reduce intermediation, and modernise capital market operations. Italy’s Cassa Depositi e Prestiti sought to test a fully digital bond issuance within a new national regulatory framework, while integrating with European central bank settlement infrastructure. This use case involves CDP, the Bank of Italy, commercial banks, and regulators, with the objective of demonstrating compliant issuance and settlement of digital securities without traditional intermediaries. The solution is implemented through the issuance of a €25 million digital bond recorded on a blockchain-based digital register managed by an authorised operator, under Italy’s Fintech Decree. Settlement is executed through integration with the TARGET2 system using blockchain-enabled payment links as part of ECB wholesale DLT experiments. The approach reduces issuance complexity, shortens settlement cycles, and enhances transparency and control over securities management. It delivers operational efficiency, supports regulatory innovation, and provides a scalable model for future digital capital market instruments, strengthening Italy’s and Europe’s position in financial market digitalisation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Federal Bank to Offer Crypto Custody Services
source_description: Institutional investors and corporate clients are increasingly seeking secure and regulated access to digital assets, while banks must adapt their service offerings to remain competitive under evolving EU regulations. Landesbank Baden-Württemberg (LBBW) aims to address this demand by offering professional-grade custody services for cryptoassets. The objective is to provide secure, compliant storage and management of digital assets for institutional clients, leveraging the bank’s existing trust and regulatory expertise. The solution is implemented through a partnership with Bitpanda, integrating institutional custody infrastructure with LBBW’s banking systems. The service includes secure key management, wallet infrastructure, and compliance with German and EU regulatory requirements. It is designed to align with upcoming EU cryptoasset regulations, ensuring legal certainty and operational robustness. The impact is the expansion of LBBW’s service portfolio into a growing asset class, improved client trust through bank-grade custody, and strengthened positioning in digital finance markets. The initiative supports scalability, risk management, and regulatory compliance, delivering long-term business value while enabling clients to participate safely in the digital asset economy.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Tokenization of Real-World Assets (RWAs)
source_description: Raising capital and managing investor relations for instruments such as equity, debt, or revenue-sharing agreements can be slow, costly, and opaque, particularly for smaller issuers and cross-border offerings. Brickken’s platform targets this by enabling organisations to create and manage digitised representations of real-world financial claims and ownership interests, improving transparency and streamlining lifecycle administration for issuers and investors. Stakeholders include issuers, investors, intermediaries, compliance teams, and supervisors concerned with how tokenised instruments fit within EU financial regulation, with the objective of enabling compliant tokenisation at scale and clearer operational processes. The platform provides end-to-end token issuance and management workflows, using distributed ledger technology to represent assets, automate corporate actions where appropriate, and maintain an auditable register of holdings and transfers. It integrates identity, onboarding, and reporting layers so that token operations can align with regulatory obligations (e.g., disclosures, eligibility constraints, and record-keeping), while sandbox participation supports structured dialogue on legal classification and cross-border compliance. Expected impacts include faster issuance and settlement processes, lower administrative overhead, improved transparency for stakeholders, and increased acceptance among institutional clients by validating compliant design choices through regulator engagement in the European Blockchain Sandbox.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Circularise: securing data across the supply chain
source_description: Companies across complex value chains must increasingly share product and sustainability information (including for Digital Product Passports), yet suppliers are often reluctant to disclose sensitive data that could expose intellectual property or competitive advantage. Circularise addresses this by enabling controlled data sharing across supply chains so that downstream partners can verify required attributes without receiving unnecessary proprietary details. Stakeholders include manufacturers, tiered suppliers, brands, auditors, and regulators pushing for traceability and compliance, with the objective of improving trust and verifiability while preserving confidentiality. The solution uses blockchain-based integrity and access controls to anchor claims and selectively disclose information, conceptually combining on-chain proofs with off-chain secure data storage and permissioning so that partners can confirm provenance, certifications, or material characteristics without full data exposure. Data structures can support Digital Product Passport workflows, with cryptographic techniques used to share only what is needed for a given transaction or compliance check. The expected results include reduced friction in compliance reporting, stronger trust between supply-chain actors, improved auditability, and scalable data governance that supports cross-border requirements; participation in the European Blockchain Sandbox is used to clarify legal and regulatory considerations around confidential data sharing, liability, and interoperability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Real Estate Trading
source_description: Real estate investment is often constrained by high transaction costs, limited liquidity, and barriers to participation, while issuers face lengthy capital-raising processes and complex administration of ownership and transfers. DigiShares’ RealEstate.Exchange (RE.X) aims to modernise this by enabling property-related assets to be issued and traded digitally, opening access to a broader range of investors and supporting secondary market liquidity. Stakeholders include real estate companies raising capital, investors seeking fractional exposure, platform operators, custodians, and regulators focused on investor protection and market integrity, with the objective of creating a secure and compliant trading venue for tokenised real estate interests. The platform tokenises real estate assets using distributed ledger technology so that ownership units can be issued, transferred, and tracked with an auditable history, while compliance layers can enforce eligibility rules and reporting requirements. RE.X has been accepted into the European Blockchain Sandbox’s second cohort to engage in structured regulatory dialogue on cross-border legal questions, governance, and operational safeguards. The anticipated impacts include faster issuance and settlement, improved transparency of holdings, reduced administrative burden through automation, and enhanced liquidity through secondary trading—while sandbox participation helps derisk regulatory uncertainty and supports broader institutional adoption.
