title: Smart Burgas - integrated platform for urban data
source_description: Smart Burgas brings together data from smart devices and urban systems to improve the monitoring, transparency and management of the city environment. The municipal challenge is that modern cities generate information across transport, infrastructure, environment, services and public spaces, but this data can remain fragmented if it is not integrated into a common platform. Residents, visitors, municipal departments, city managers and service operators are the principal stakeholders. The platform is designed to help the municipality observe what is happening in the city, facilitate control, improve service organisation and make urban information more visible to the public. Its implementation consists of an integrated monitoring platform that collects and displays data from smart devices and systems operating in Burgas. Conceptually, the solution combines urban sensing, data aggregation, dashboard visualisation, public information tools and service-management support. By enabling residents and guests to observe city conditions more easily, it also contributes to transparency and civic awareness. The expected impact is improved quality of life, better coordination of municipal services, more responsive urban management and stronger evidence for decision-making. For the administration, integrated urban data can help identify problems, monitor performance and allocate resources more effectively. For citizens and visitors, the platform provides a clearer view of local conditions and supports more informed interaction with the city.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smart Public Lighting in City of Sveta Nedelja (Croatia)
source_description: The Sveta Nedelja smart public lighting pilot tested how existing public lighting infrastructure could become a platform for energy management, environmental monitoring and urban sensing. The municipal problem is that public lighting is a major operational asset, but conventional lighting systems offer limited remote control, monitoring or capacity to generate wider city data. The pilot aimed to improve energy efficiency, quality of life, public safety and reduction of light pollution. The implementation, developed with HT Group, connected 80 control and communication modules to existing lighting poles. The solution can operate across several network technologies, including 3G, 4G, 5G and NB-IoT, and is applicable to different types of public lighting. The smart poles enabled remote wireless monitoring and control of lamps, measurement of energy indicators, and additional sensing functions such as temperature, humidity, pressure, UV radiation, air quality, pedestrian passage and traffic noise. Conceptually, the system combines IoT connectivity, smart lighting control, environmental sensing, remote monitoring and city-data collection. The expected impact is reduced energy use, better maintenance insight, improved environmental monitoring and a foundation for broader Smart City services using existing infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: European Regions Network for the Application of Communications Technology (ERNACT)
title: Enaibler - AI for ethical policies and services across European regions
source_description: Public authorities increasingly recognise the strategic importance of advanced digital technologies, yet many regional and local administrations still lack the practical capacity, frameworks and confidence needed to translate this potential into better public policies and services. ENAIBLER addresses that institutional challenge by helping public-sector organisations across Europe strengthen their readiness to adopt advanced tools in an open, transparent and ethically grounded way. The project brings together nine partners from six EU regions, including regional and local authorities, development agencies and a university, all of whom are involved in shaping or supporting policy instruments linked to digital transformation. Its objective is to empower the public sector to unlock the benefits of these technologies while improving the quality, ethics and transparency of the services and policies delivered to citizens. The solution is implemented through interregional cooperation, policy learning and capacity-building activities aimed at supporting organisations in the design and adoption of appropriate approaches. At a conceptual level, the project combines policy exchange, institutional support and shared experimentation to help partners strengthen governance, implementation capability and ethical practice across their territories. The expected impact is better-informed public administrations, stronger regional policy instruments and more responsible deployment of advanced digital services. More broadly, ENAIBLER creates value by improving public-sector capability, supporting trustworthy innovation and helping regions embed more transparent and citizen-oriented approaches to digital transformation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI4Citizens - Supporting ethical and effective AI governance in European cities and regions
source_description: Cities and regions face growing pressure to modernise public services through advanced digital technologies, but adoption can be hindered by uncertainty around governance, ethics, risk management and the practical design of enabling policy mechanisms. AI4Citizens addresses this challenge by helping local and regional governments strengthen their ability to introduce such technologies safely and effectively, while ensuring that implementation serves the public interest. The stakeholders include local and regional policymakers, public-sector organisations and partner institutions engaged in interregional cooperation, with the objective of improving and creating policy mechanisms that support responsible adoption and, in turn, enhance citizens’ wellbeing and regional vitality. The solution is implemented through interregional exchange, co-creation and learning processes focused on good practices, innovative solutions and governance models relevant to public-sector deployment. At a conceptual level, the project draws on key elements of governance frameworks and implementation processes, enabling partners to compare approaches, identify gaps and develop policy improvements suited to their own institutional contexts. This process is designed not merely to share examples, but to drive concrete policy change and better governance arrangements. The expected impact is stronger governance capacity, more robust and ethical policy instruments and improved readiness for adoption at local and regional level. More broadly, AI4Citizens creates value by supporting safer innovation, more coherent public-sector transformation and a more trustworthy relationship between digital progress and citizen benefit.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Innovation Center of the Košice Region (ICKK)
title: AI Sandbox in the Košice Self-Governing Region (KSK) - Xploro application
source_description: The Košice Self-Governing Region’s AI Sandbox provides a controlled environment for testing artificial intelligence solutions within regional public-administration infrastructure, and Xploro was one of the selected applications in its first cycle. The broader operational problem is that public administrations often need to experiment with innovative technologies while managing legal, technical and organisational risks before wider adoption. The sandbox, initiated by the Innovation Center of the Košice Region, gives companies, universities and start-ups a structured route to test solutions for public services and internal processes. Participants undergo benefit analysis, technical evaluation, feasibility assessment and legal compliance review. Xploro specifically addresses tourism and visitor experience by providing an AI-supported guide that recommends places of interest and delivers information in audio or text form. Conceptually, the application combines location-aware guidance, recommendation functions, natural language content delivery and digital tourism support. The expected impact is twofold: for the regional administration, the sandbox strengthens capacity to evaluate AI tools responsibly before deployment; for tourism users, Xploro can simplify travel, enrich visits and improve access to information about sites. The inaugural sandbox attracted more than ten applications, with two selected for testing, indicating a selective and structured experimentation process. The project’s value lies in combining innovation testing with public-sector governance and practical service improvement.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Innovation Center of the Košice Region (ICKK)
title: AI Sandbox in the Košice Self-Governing Region (KSK) - Recruapplication
source_description: Recru was selected for testing within the Košice Self-Governing Region’s AI Sandbox, a controlled and educational framework created to experiment with artificial intelligence solutions in public-administration settings. The institutional challenge is to improve the digitalisation of regional services and internal processes while ensuring that new tools are assessed for benefits, technical feasibility, implementation readiness and legal compliance before broader deployment. The main stakeholders include the Innovation Center of the Košice Region, the regional administration, participating companies, universities, start-ups, HR teams and applicants who may interact with recruitment processes. Recru focuses on human resources, offering a modern recruitment-management solution intended to simplify and accelerate the hiring process. The implementation is designed to support employers across recruitment tasks, enabling them to focus more directly on candidates. Conceptually, the tool may combine candidate management, workflow automation, recruitment analytics, communication support and AI-assisted processing of hiring information, although the specific technical modules are not detailed in the information provided. The expected impact is faster recruitment administration, more structured candidate handling and reduced repetitive workload for employers. Within the sandbox, the broader value is the ability to test such a system safely in a regional public-sector environment. Since more than ten solutions applied and two were selected, Recru’s inclusion indicates that it met the initial benefit, feasibility and compliance screening requirements.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LifeSaver - enhancing medical services
source_description: LifeSaver aims to strengthen Estonia’s emergency medical services by improving resource allocation, service-area design and system-wide preparedness through data-driven and predictive tools. The operational challenge is that emergency medical systems must respond quickly under uncertain and changing demand, while ensuring that ambulances, staff, dispatch arrangements and service areas are organised effectively. The project focuses on modernising life-saving assistance by using predictive analytics, real-time monitoring and transparent system insights to support faster and more effective emergency responses. The implementation includes the LifeSaver Intelligence Platform and a comprehensive review of Estonia’s emergency medical system by international experts. The platform supports analysis of response patterns, demand forecasting, resource optimisation and identification of improvement projects. The LifeSaver programme identified ten potential innovation projects, from which the Estonian government selected five for future implementation. Conceptually, the initiative combines operational EMS data, predictive modelling, service-area analysis, monitoring dashboards and strategic planning for emergency care. The expected impact is better allocation of emergency resources, faster response capability, improved patient outcomes and stronger public-sector innovation capacity. Estonia was the first country to work with International SOS and Airbus Helicopters on the LifeSaver programme.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BrAIn – BRinging Artificial INtelligence towards SMEs
source_description: BrAIn supports SMEs in the Danube Region in understanding, adopting and benefiting from artificial intelligence and Industry 4.0 technologies as part of a transition towards more sustainable and human-centric Industry 5.0 models. The regional problem is that SMEs across the Danube area face uneven digital maturity, labour shortages, cost pressures, industrial transformation and limited internal capacity to adopt advanced technologies. The project therefore focuses on knowledge transfer, skills development and targeted transnational interventions in sectors such as manufacturing, agrofood, healthcare and sustainable energy. The implementation is structured as an Interreg Danube Region project that equips stakeholders and SMEs with AI-related knowledge, supports pilot solutions and builds on previous regional innovation results. Conceptually, the initiative combines capacity building, technology transfer, pilot experimentation, stakeholder networking and sector-specific AI adoption support. The expected impact is improved SME competitiveness, stronger readiness for Industry 5.0, more balanced regional development and better alignment between AI adoption and economic, environmental and social sustainability. By working across the Danube Region, BrAIn addresses the fact that AI capability gaps are not only technological, but also organisational, skills-based and territorial.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: iTranSys - Public Transport Optimisation Powered by AI
source_description: Považská Bystrica adopted iTranSys to improve the planning and operation of public transport in a town of around 40,000 residents. The main operational pressure was the combination of driver shortages and inefficient scheduling, which can increase costs, reduce service reliability and negatively affect passenger satisfaction. The stakeholders include the City of Považská Bystrica, public transport operators, drivers, passengers, municipal planners and residents who rely on local mobility services. The objective is to make route and timetable planning more efficient while maintaining or improving service quality. The implementation uses an AI-powered optimisation tool that automates aspects of public transport planning, including timetable generation and route scheduling. Conceptually, the system can analyse passenger demand, operational constraints, available drivers, route structures and service-frequency requirements to generate more efficient transport plans. By supporting automated scenario analysis and schedule optimisation, it reduces dependence on manual planning and allows the municipality to respond more flexibly to capacity constraints. The reported impact includes significant annual financial savings, improved passenger satisfaction and reduced per capita CO₂ emissions. These results suggest that the tool delivers both operational and environmental value by using resources more efficiently, improving service attractiveness and supporting more sustainable urban mobility.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LUCID – Data intelligence for cities and urban logistics
source_description: LUCID develops a data-driven platform to improve urban logistics by optimising routes, reducing congestion and improving the use of loading and unloading spaces. The operational challenge is that freight and last-mile logistics contribute significantly to urban congestion, emissions and fuel consumption, while cities and operators often lack a shared evidence base for managing delivery flows. The project integrates public city data and private logistics-operator data to provide real-time insights for both city planners and logistics actors. Its implementation uses advanced analytics and machine-learning methods to support route planning, operational decision-making and more efficient allocation of urban logistics infrastructure. Pilot testing is foreseen in Madrid, Las Rozas and Prague, with logistics operators involved to validate the platform in real-world settings. Conceptually, LUCID combines data integration, predictive analytics, route optimisation, loading-space intelligence and city-dashboard functionality. The expected impact is lower delivery costs, reduced environmental footprint, less congestion and better planning capacity for local authorities. By bringing together public and private data, the project supports a more coordinated model of urban logistics management in rapidly growing cities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SmartDriveAI - digitising accident reporting
source_description: SmartDriveAI was developed to modernise accident reporting in public transport by replacing slow, paper-based processes with real-time digital reporting and predictive safety insights. The operational problem is that conventional accident documentation can delay response, fragment evidence and limit authorities’ ability to identify recurring safety patterns. In Graz, the project involved Graz Linien and Mapular, with drivers equipped to submit GPS-tagged reports, photographs and incident details through a multilingual digital interface. The implementation integrates external data such as weather conditions and uses analytics to generate proactive safety alerts and insights for city authorities and operators. Conceptually, the platform combines mobile accident reporting, geodata technologies, real-time data capture, predictive modelling and safety-dashboard functionality. Pilot results reported by Mapular indicate a 90% reduction in reporting time, 100% data integrity during the pilot phase and identification of three key accident patterns. The expected impact is faster reporting, better data quality, improved resource allocation, stronger road-safety analysis and more proactive prevention of recurring incidents. The initiative also demonstrates how public transport operators can use structured operational data to move from reactive accident handling to evidence-based safety management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SAFELY - Road Safety Analytics System
source_description: Municipalities often rely on recorded accidents alone to understand road-safety problems, yet this reactive approach can miss hidden risks and delay intervention until serious incidents have already occurred. SAFELY was developed to help local authorities move from monitoring past crashes to proactively identifying hazardous conditions before further harm occurs. The platform addresses the need for a more complete understanding of road safety by combining multiple data sources rather than relying only on official accident counts. The stakeholders include municipalities, traffic planners, road-safety teams and local communities, with the objective of prioritising interventions more effectively, allocate resources with greater precision and strengthen evidence-based transport planning. The solution is implemented as a data-driven analytics platform that integrates accident records with traffic patterns, road geometry, environmental data and citizen feedback. At a conceptual level, the system uses clustering techniques such as DBSCAN and ST-DBSCAN, together with geospatial visualisation, to reveal risk hotspots and hidden hazards that are not obvious in raw crash statistics. These insights are presented through actionable hazard maps and planning outputs that fit municipal workflows and align with standards such as CADaS, GDPR and the European Interoperability Framework. The impact has been measurable: in Şanlıurfa, interventions supported by SAFELY were associated with an over 80% reduction in reported accidents and a 90% drop in injuries between 2014–2015 and 2020–2021. More broadly, the platform offers a cost-efficient, scalable and credible model for saving lives through proactive road-safety management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ELIAS - European Lighthouse of AI for Sustainability
source_description: ELIAS addresses a strategic challenge facing Europe: how to accelerate advanced technological research and application in ways that contribute directly to sustainability goals while also respecting ethical and societal considerations. Climate change, the energy crisis and related environmental pressures require new forms of collaboration between academia and industry, yet the pathway from research excellence to deployable solutions is often fragmented. This use case therefore brings together researchers, emerging talent, industrial partners and innovation stakeholders with the objective of building a strong European ecosystem for sustainability-oriented technological development. The project seeks not only to advance research, but also to ensure that resulting solutions generate practical value for society and the environment. The solution is implemented through a programme that combines fundamental academic research, industrial application work, talent development and partnership-building across Europe. At a conceptual level, ELIAS creates a collaborative structure in which advanced methods are developed, tested and translated into seven pilot use cases over the project’s duration, while also supporting the broader research community and strengthening links between scientific and commercial actors. This model is intended to foster both technical progress and responsible innovation. The expected impact is stronger European leadership in sustainability-focused research, improved pathways from research to application and a more capable innovation ecosystem. More broadly, ELIAS creates value by aligning scientific excellence, industrial relevance and societal benefit around pressing environmental challenges.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Wrocław University of Science and Technology
title: PLLuM - Polish Large Language Model
source_description: PLLuM, the Polish Large Language Universal Model, was launched to strengthen Poland’s capacity to develop open and responsible language technologies primarily trained on Polish text. The problem it addresses is the limited availability of high-quality, open-access language models designed around the linguistic, cultural and administrative needs of Polish users. The main stakeholders include Wrocław University of Science and Technology, the wider consortium of six Polish institutions, researchers specialising in artificial intelligence and linguistics, public-service providers, developers and citizens, including those at risk of digital exclusion. The project aims to create the first open Polish large language model and a related smart assistant that can support access to public services electronically and in person. The implementation involves large-scale Polish-language model training, dataset preparation, linguistic expertise, evaluation and the development of assistant functionalities aligned with ethical and responsible AI principles. These include attention to data representativeness, transparency and fairness. Conceptually, PLLuM can support natural-language interaction, information retrieval, text generation and user guidance in public-service contexts. Its expected impact is broader access to digital services, improved quality of Polish-language AI applications and reduced dependence on models developed primarily for other languages. By targeting digitally excluded users, the smart assistant also has potential to improve administrative accessibility and inclusion.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AID HCH – Advancing Humanities and Cultural Heritage with Artificial Intelligence
source_description: AID HCH is a Slovenian research initiative designed to advance the use of artificial intelligence in humanities research and cultural-heritage preservation. The strategic problem is that AI has been widely applied in natural sciences, engineering and medicine, but less systematically in humanities and heritage contexts, where digitised sources, archives, objects and conservation data require specialised methods and ethical safeguards. The project aims to establish Slovenia’s first comprehensive data space for humanities and heritage, strengthening cooperation with infrastructures such as E-RIHS, CLARIN and DARIAH. Its implementation combines AI tools, data-space development, digitised cultural and historical sources, predictive conservation methods, heritage storytelling and interdisciplinary frameworks for legal and ethical use. Conceptually, the project creates shared infrastructure and methodologies for analysing cultural-heritage data, supporting research collaboration and improving protection of heritage assets. The expected impact is stronger digital transformation in humanities research, better access to structured heritage data, improved conservation planning and greater international interoperability. The project also has a capacity-building function by connecting universities, libraries, heritage institutions and technical partners around common data and AI standards.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products
title: Enhancing healthcare policy evaluation through AI-driven analytics platform for the National Public Administration
source_description: Bulgaria’s National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products initiated this project to improve how public authorities evaluate the real-world value of innovative and high-cost medicines. The policy challenge is that reimbursement decisions require evidence on clinical effectiveness, patient outcomes and budget impact, yet traditional evaluation processes may not fully exploit large-scale health data. Stakeholders include the National Council, healthcare policymakers, patients, clinicians, pharmaceutical companies, reimbursement authorities and public-finance actors responsible for sustainable spending. The objective is to support more informed decisions on whether and how medicines should be reimbursed, while balancing patient access with cost-effectiveness. The implementation uses artificial intelligence and big-data analytics to assess the real-world effectiveness of medicines after they enter clinical use. Conceptually, the platform can combine reimbursement records, treatment data, patient outcomes, medicine-cost information and analytical models to compare expected and observed performance. This enables decision-makers to identify which therapies deliver measurable value in practice and where public expenditure may need adjustment. The expected impact is stronger evidence for reimbursement policy, more efficient allocation of public funds, improved accountability for high-cost therapies and better patient care. By linking analytics with reimbursement governance, the project supports a more data-driven and outcome-oriented healthcare administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Automatic Detection of Impervious Surfaces
source_description: Recklinghausen developed this software to give municipalities a more precise basis for monitoring sealed surfaces and planning climate-adaptation measures. The environmental problem is that impervious surfaces prevent rainwater infiltration and contribute to urban heat accumulation, increasing risks related to drainage, flooding and heat islands. In Germany, around 45% of settlement and transport areas are sealed, according to the Federal Environmental Agency statistics cited in the source material. Stakeholders include the District of Recklinghausen, participating cities, the Westphalian University of Applied Sciences, land registry and geo-information staff, environment and climate-protection departments and local residents. The implementation uses artificial intelligence, deep learning and computer vision to derive maps of impervious surfaces from aerial images and aggregate the results to different area divisions. The project was carried out over 12 months with funding of just under €100,000 for a research associate at the university’s Department of Electrical Engineering and Applied Natural Sciences. Regular meetings between the university and participating cities defined objectives and monitored progress. The expected impact is more detailed assessment of urban land conditions, improved evidence for drainage control, stronger planning of climate-effective measures and better evaluation of municipal land-management interventions. By automating surface classification, the tool helps local authorities move towards more systematic, data-based environmental and climate planning.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Circular TwAIn- AI Platform for Integrated Sustainable and Circular Manufacturing
source_description: European manufacturers are under growing pressure to reduce waste, improve resilience and make production systems more sustainable across the full product lifecycle, yet industrial data and decision-making often remain fragmented across suppliers, plants and recovery processes. Circular TwAIn addresses this challenge by helping manufacturing organisations move from linear production models towards more circular and interoperable operations. The use case involves industrial partners in both discrete manufacturing and process industries, with the objective of improving sustainability, flexibility and resource efficiency while strengthening Europe’s position in advanced manufacturing. Its approach spans three industrial pilots, each tackling a different circularity challenge: batteries, waste electrical and electronic equipment, and petrochemical production. The solution is implemented through an integrated platform built around interoperable digital twins, trusted data-sharing mechanisms and advanced analytical models applied across the product lifecycle. At a conceptual level, the platform connects operational, recovery and lifecycle data so that sustainability-related decisions can be supported from design through use, reuse and end-of-life processing. In the battery pilot, it supports new circular value-chain nodes; in the WEEE pilot, it improves recovery and reuse pathways; and in the PETRO pilot, it connects digital intelligence with established industrial processes. The expected impact is more efficient circular manufacturing, better reuse and recycling outcomes, stronger resilience and improved industrial coordination. More broadly, the project enhances scalability, supports trustworthy digital transformation and creates value through more sustainable and competitive production systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Fluently - the essence of human-robot interaction
source_description: Modern manufacturing increasingly depends on effective collaboration between people and machines, yet many industrial systems still require specialised knowledge to operate and can place unnecessary cognitive or physical strain on workers. Fluently addresses this challenge by making human-robot collaboration more intuitive, inclusive and productive in real manufacturing settings. The use case involves shop-floor operators, production managers and industrial technology providers, with the objective of enabling workers of different skill levels to interact more naturally with robotic systems while improving operational performance and worker wellbeing. Rather than requiring users to adapt to rigid machine interfaces, the project seeks to make robots more responsive to human communication and easier to integrate into dynamic factory environments. The solution is implemented through an interface that allows robots to interpret speech and gestures, supported by perception, language-processing and interaction models that translate human signals into machine actions. At a conceptual level, the project combines multimodal interaction, collaborative robotics and a dedicated Robo-Gym training environment where human-robot interaction can be developed and tested before deployment. These capabilities are then validated through real-world industrial pilots. The expected impact is smoother human-robot cooperation, lower barriers to use, improved production efficiency and better worker experience. More broadly, Fluently supports safer and more adaptive manufacturing, increases the practical usability of robotic systems and creates value by aligning automation more closely with human capabilities and needs.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Madrid use case
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: In Madrid, last-mile logistics still depends heavily on a conventional, road-based model in which goods move from DHL facilities into the metropolitan centre mainly by truck and van, often through fragmented arrangements involving external operators. This siloed approach contributes to slower deliveries, road congestion and unnecessary environmental impact, especially in dense urban areas where freight and passenger mobility compete for limited space. The Madrid DELPHI use case addresses this problem by integrating passenger and freight transport more strategically and creating a more sustainable logistics model for urban deliveries. The stakeholders include DHL, metro operators, microhub operators, final-mile couriers and city mobility actors, with the objective of improving delivery efficiency while reducing pressure on the road network. The solution is implemented through a multimodal logistics system in which parcels are pre-sorted into roller cages, transferred to dedicated metro depots and moved through the METRO network before reaching microhubs located in selected stations. From there, KOIKI messengers complete the final delivery on foot or by cargo bike, depending on timing requirements and hub location. At a conceptual level, the system combines data-sharing, multimodal coordination and operational planning within a federated mobility framework. The expected impact is quicker deliveries, lower emissions, reduced congestion and better use of urban transport infrastructure. More broadly, the pilot creates a financially and environmentally more sustainable logistics model for Madrid.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Attika Use Case
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: Freight movement in the Athens metropolitan area is heavily affected by congestion on the Attiki Odos ring road, yet road and metro systems currently operate as separate domains with limited real-time coordination. This disconnect reduces flexibility for logistics providers, especially when delivery services need to respond quickly to traffic incidents or peak-period slowdowns by shifting to faster transport options. The Attika DELPHI use case addresses this lack of integration by creating a dynamic multimodal alternative for urban freight movement. The stakeholders include Attikes Diadromes, which operates and maintains the ring road, STASY, which manages Athens’ fixed-track public transport network, and logistics operators seeking more resilient delivery routes. The objective is to enable on-demand rerouting from roadway transport to metro-based logistics when traffic conditions make this advantageous. The solution is implemented through a coordinated mobility framework that links traffic and transport information from the road and metro systems and supports route suggestions based on current conditions. At a conceptual level, the pilot uses real-time data exchange, multimodal routing logic and operational coordination to redirect deliveries to designated metro stations, where goods can be loaded onto specialised metro carriages for onward movement. This model is designed for flexible, on-demand use rather than fixed metro freight schedules. The expected impact is faster and more reliable deliveries, better adaptation to congestion and improved use of existing transport assets. More broadly, the pilot strengthens multimodal resilience and supports more efficient urban freight operations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Cluj-Napoca use case
source_description: Cluj-Napoca has experienced rapid population growth and increasing pressure on its transport system, making it harder for the city to maintain efficient, sustainable and coordinated mobility services. Although the city already offers real-time public-transport information through a user-friendly mobile application, a key challenge remains: limited data sharing and coordination between the various public and private operators serving the city and surrounding communes. The Cluj-Napoca DELPHI use case addresses this fragmentation by aiming to create a more integrated and data-driven mobility ecosystem. The stakeholders include the Public Transport Company, municipal authorities, surrounding localities and other mobility-service providers, with the objective of improving planning, interoperability and user responsiveness across the transport network. The solution is implemented through the development of a centralised IT platform capable of aggregating and standardising data from buses, trams, bike-sharing systems and parking facilities in line with open-data standards. At a conceptual level, this platform combines data integration, monitoring and user feedback to support better coordination between services and a more coherent picture of mobility demand and supply. These insights can then inform network adjustments, service improvement and long-term planning. The expected impact is more efficient public transport, improved accessibility and stronger coordination between modes and operators. More broadly, the pilot supports sustainable urban mobility, better use of infrastructure and a more responsive transport system for a growing city.

title: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Mykonos use case
task: Tracking of goods and assets along the supply chain
source_description: Public spaces are often designed according to planning assumptions that do not fully reflect how people actually move, stop, interact and spend time in the urban environment. As a result, spaces intended to support walking, socialising and everyday wellbeing may underperform because their design does not align with real behaviour or user needs. The Good Public Space for Walking project addresses this gap by helping municipalities assess and improve public spaces through a more human-centred understanding of how they are used in practice. The stakeholders include municipal planners, urban designers and residents, with the objective of making public spaces more functional, welcoming and supportive of healthy daily activities such as walking, sitting and social interaction. The solution is implemented through an interdisciplinary methodology that combines classical spatial analysis with behavioural studies and digitally supported citizen participation. At a conceptual level, the approach compares the intended design of a place with observed and reported patterns of actual use, then generates practical planning recommendations based on these discrepancies. The integration of AI-supported participation tools helps ensure that community voices are captured more systematically and incorporated into the planning process. The expected impact is better-targeted urban interventions, improved usability of public space and stronger alignment between planning decisions and lived experience. More broadly, the project supports healthier, more responsive urban environments and creates value by embedding citizen-centred evidence more directly into local design and policy choices.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: PERKS - AI for industrial operational efficiency
source_description: PERKS, formally “Eliciting and Exploiting Procedural Knowledge in Industry 5.0”, addresses the difficulty industrial organisations face in capturing, managing and reusing procedural knowledge. The operational problem is that know-how related to processes, safety procedures, system configuration and energy-management practices is often tacit, poorly digitalised or difficult for workers to access at the moment of need. The project therefore aims to improve industrial efficiency by developing modular, AI-based tools and methodologies that support the full lifecycle of procedural knowledge, from elicitation and management to access and exploitation. Its implementation combines symbolic and subsymbolic AI, data technologies, knowledge-management methods and worker-centred digital tools. The solutions are tested in three industrial scenarios: a white-goods production plant, computer numerical control machines and a microgrid testbed, each presenting different procedural-knowledge requirements. The expected impact is improved productivity, fewer operational errors, better knowledge transfer, stronger worker safety and more efficient energy-related practices. With an overall budget of €3.55 million, the project contributes to Industry 5.0 by prioritising human-centric, flexible and accepted tools for industrial workers rather than automation alone.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Bronia.AI - acoustic technology
source_description: Bronia.AI is a Bulgarian start-up established in 2024 to develop intelligent acoustic signal-processing technology for complex sound-related applications. The business and technical problem addressed is that many sectors require more advanced tools for managing audio signals, reducing noise, optimising sound quality and extracting usable information from acoustic environments. Stakeholders include Bronia.AI, potential industrial clients, technology partners, sectors using acoustic systems and end users benefiting from improved sound processing. The company’s objective is to build a cutting-edge platform that can transform how sound signals are processed and applied across different business domains. The implementation is centred on AI-powered acoustic technologies, including sound optimisation, noise reduction and advanced signal processing. Conceptually, the platform may combine machine-learning models for audio enhancement, signal separation, pattern recognition, acoustic modelling and real-time processing. Its value lies in addressing situations where conventional audio-processing methods may be insufficient, particularly in complex, noisy or data-rich environments. The expected impact is improved sound quality, more reliable acoustic analysis, new product possibilities and efficiency gains for organisations using audio technologies. As a young company, Bronia.AI’s broader market impact will depend on product maturity, sector adoption and demonstrable performance in real-world settings. Its positioning suggests a focus on innovation in a specialised technological field with potential cross-sector applications.

title: 5G connection for the Ravenna Port for enhahnced digital connectivity
source_description: The Port of Ravenna’s private 5G network is part of a wider digitalisation strategy to make port operations more competitive, secure and sustainable. The operational problem is that ports require low-latency, reliable and secure connectivity to coordinate cargo traffic, intermodal logistics, monitoring systems and future automation across large and complex areas. The planned Mobile Private Network 5G will cover the entire port area and a 15 km canal corridor linking the port to the city, enabling ultra-fast communications and stronger data security. The implementation supports smart-port applications such as intelligent monitoring through cameras and devices, autonomous vehicles, anti-collision systems, drone-based cargo surveillance, augmented reality for maintenance, environmental monitoring and artificial intelligence for managing logistics flows. It is also connected to broader digital tools, including the Port Community System, Rail Management Platform, virtual gates and a future Digital Twin for simulation and planning. The expected impact is optimised cargo traffic, shorter ship waiting times, improved coordination among port stakeholders and a stronger basis for advanced operational planning. In May 2025, the Port Authority awarded the deployment contract to Fastweb and Vodafone, in partnership with Lepida.

organization: RTVE – Radiotelevisión Española (Spanish Radio and Television Corporation)
title: AI-tool to cover local elections
source_description: RTVE developed this use case to solve a persistent media-coverage challenge: local elections in small municipalities generate official results that are highly relevant to residents, yet producing reliable and accessible reporting for every location can be difficult, especially where traditional newsroom resources are limited. The project aimed to ensure that no community would be left without election information, regardless of location, while also improving accessibility for people with visual impairments. The stakeholders include RTVE journalists, audiences in small municipalities and citizens requiring accessible electoral information, with the objective of expanding coverage, improving speed and maintaining trust by basing outputs strictly on official results. The solution is implemented through a tool that automatically drafts written and audio election content using official election data as its sole input source. At a conceptual level, the system combines automated text generation, structured result processing and editorial supervision so that informative, coherent and useful outputs can be produced quickly for municipalities with fewer than 1,000 inhabitants, while remaining extensible to broader electoral coverage. RTVE professionals train and supervise the system to maintain quality and editorial standards. The impact includes wider electoral coverage, faster production and improved information accessibility, especially in smaller localities that might otherwise receive limited attention. More broadly, the tool creates value by supporting public-service media, strengthening democratic information access and reducing the resource barrier to comprehensive local-election reporting.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smart Assistant - Development of a chatbot for the municipalities of the LEADER Region Weinviertel Ost
source_description: Municipalities in the LEADER Region Weinviertel Ost needed a practical way to automate routine online interactions and improve digital service delivery without each authority having to build separate solutions from scratch. Smaller municipalities often face capacity constraints in maintaining responsive online communication, even though residents increasingly expect fast answers on common topics such as building permits and local administrative procedures. The project therefore set out to provide a shared digital assistant for 58 municipalities, with the objective of streamlining routine enquiries, improving access to information and supporting more efficient day-to-day online operations. The stakeholders include municipal administrations, residents and the regional bodies coordinating the initiative, with the aim of creating a reusable and locally relevant support tool across the whole region. The solution is implemented through a chatbot integrated into municipal websites and trained specifically for the needs of Weinviertel Ost. At a conceptual level, the system uses commercially available chatbot software, but its local effectiveness depends on targeted training using information drawn from publicly accessible databases through central interfaces and from a dedicated frequently asked questions database covering municipal competencies. This creates a shared but customisable knowledge base aligned with local administrative needs. The expected impact is faster handling of standard requests, lower administrative effort for routine digital communication and improved service consistency across municipalities. More broadly, the project creates value by giving smaller local authorities a scalable and regionally coordinated way to modernise citizen interaction.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: 3DAI City Mobile Application - AI for Road Maintenance
source_description: MM Spa introduced the 3DAI City mobile application to address a practical infrastructure-management problem: maintaining Milan’s roads more efficiently by identifying defects earlier and improving the quality of maintenance planning. Since taking responsibility for routine road maintenance in July 2023, MM needed a scalable way to monitor a dense and heavily used urban network without relying solely on slower, labour-intensive manual inspections. The stakeholders include MM’s maintenance teams, city infrastructure managers and Milan’s road users, with the objective of reducing emergency repairs, improving visibility of road-surface conditions and making intervention planning more timely and cost-effective. The solution is implemented in collaboration with Univrses AB through a smartphone-based system mounted on MM vehicles’ windscreens. According to MM, the technology entered a nine-month trial in November 2024 and uses moving-vehicle image capture to detect cracks, potholes, other pavement defects and anomalies in vertical road signs, with outputs integrated into MM’s Web-GIS portal. At a conceptual level, the system combines mobile computer vision, georeferenced defect detection and GIS-based asset mapping to create an updated digital view of the city’s road infrastructure. The expected impact is earlier fault detection, fewer emergency interventions and more efficient allocation of maintenance resources. More broadly, the project creates value through lower operational cost, better planning accuracy and a scalable approach to urban road-condition monitoring.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI to accelerate the legislative power of the Parliament of Estonia
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Estonia's parliament, the Riigikogu, partnered with Nortal to enhance legislative efficiency by implementing an AI-driven intelligent search solution. This system utilizes natural language processing to swiftly retrieve relevant information from extensive legislative documents, streamlining tasks such as drafting responses and preparing materials for members of parliament. By automating these processes, the solution reduces manual workload, minimizes errors, and accelerates decision-making within the legislative framework.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Battling pandemics with the help of AI
source_description: The Lower Saxony State Health Office developed Nova to respond to a recurring public-health communication challenge: during major health events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, public enquiries can rise sharply, overloading staff and making it harder to provide quick, consistent answers through traditional channels alone. The organisation needed a way to offer reliable health information around the clock while preserving staff capacity for more complex work. The stakeholders include the health office, its service teams and citizens seeking guidance on diseases and health-related concerns, with the objective of improving access to official information, reducing pressure on employees and strengthening the administration’s ability to communicate under crisis conditions. The solution was implemented with Nortal using its Tark platform to create Nova, a virtual assistant available on the NLGA website. At a conceptual level, the system combines generative capabilities, large language models and a secure, NLGA-controlled knowledge base to interpret questions, understand contextual meaning and deliver rapid answers on topics such as COVID-19, measles and other public-health concerns. This architecture allows the tool to update quickly as information changes while keeping control of source content within the public authority. The impact includes faster access to health information, better service continuity and lower workload for staff. More broadly, Nova creates value by improving crisis communication, increasing scalability in citizen support and demonstrating a secure model for health-related virtual assistance in public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BeReady - AI to enhance Air Raid Warning System
source_description: Estonia’s BeReady initiative strengthens national air-threat detection by involving citizens in the reporting of suspicious aerial activity through a mobile application. The defence and civil-protection challenge is that traditional surveillance systems may benefit from additional distributed observations, especially where rapid reporting and corroboration can support situational awareness. Stakeholders include the Estonian Air Force, citizens using the application, Estonia-based IT companies, national-security authorities and communities relying on timely air-raid warnings. The implementation integrates an AI-powered air-threat identification feature into the BeReady mobile app. Citizens can capture and submit photos of suspicious aerial activities, while the system processes the inputs and consolidates data from multiple users to generate real-time, actionable intelligence for the Air Force. Conceptually, the solution combines mobile crowdsourcing, image analysis, threat classification, data aggregation and operational intelligence workflows. The system was successfully tested during Spring Storm 2024, Estonia’s largest annual joint military exercise. The expected impact is an expansion of surveillance capacity through citizen participation, faster collection of relevant observations and improved support for air-threat assessment. By connecting public reporting with automated analysis, the application can strengthen national security and resilience. Its deployment also requires safeguards to manage false reports, data quality, privacy and the appropriate use of citizen-generated information in defence contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Municipalities of Den Haag, Groningen, Nijmegen, Rotterdam
title: Good Public Space for Walking pilot in multiple dutch Municipalities
source_description: Across many towns and cities, public spaces are designed with certain assumptions about how people will move, stop and interact, yet the way these places are actually used often differs from what planners intended. This creates a practical challenge for municipalities seeking to make streets, squares and other shared environments more walkable, inclusive and supportive of health and wellbeing. The Good Public Space for Walking project, developed by Humankind between 2021 and 2022, addresses this gap by helping local authorities understand where the design of a space does not match real behaviour and by translating that insight into usable planning recommendations. The stakeholders include municipal planners, urban designers and residents, with the objective of creating public spaces that better support walking, sitting and social interaction while responding more directly to community needs. The solution is implemented through an interdisciplinary methodology that combines classical spatial analysis with behavioural studies and digitally supported citizen participation. At a conceptual level, the approach compares the intended function of a place with observed patterns of use, while AI-enabled participation tools help structure and incorporate residents’ views into the assessment process. This produces a richer evidence base for design decisions. The expected impact is more user-centred urban planning, better-targeted improvements and stronger alignment between public-space investment and actual community use. More broadly, the project enhances liveability, supports healthier daily habits and creates value through more responsive and effective urban design.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Bikeability.AI to analise bikeability in Municipality of Dordrecht
source_description: Dordrecht needed a better way to understand how cycle-friendly different neighbourhoods and city areas actually are, and how planned infrastructure changes might improve the quality of cycling conditions. Traditional policy development in this area can be constrained by fragmented evidence, static indicators or limited ability to test the likely impact of interventions before they are delivered. The use case therefore involves the Municipality of Dordrecht and mobility-policy stakeholders, with the objective of generating stronger evidence for cycling policy, improving planning at both district and city level and supporting more informed investment in active mobility. The solution is implemented through Bikeability.ai, described by Horizons as a tool developed by Sobolt with Dordrecht as launching partner. At a conceptual level, the system uses analytical models to compute and visualise bikeability indicators and to simulate the positive effects of proposed infrastructure interventions. Publicly available technical documentation also shows a bikeability package that works with OpenStreetMap data and spatial indicators such as cycling facilities, greenery and road-network characteristics, suggesting a geospatial analytics approach underpinning the policy tool. This allows city teams to move from descriptive observation towards scenario-based planning. The expected impact is clearer policy insight, better prioritisation of cycling interventions and more evidence-based urban mobility planning. More broadly, the project creates value by supporting healthier, more sustainable transport choices through scalable, data-informed assessment of cycling conditions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI for certfied emails management in the Municipality of Cinisello Balsamo
source_description: The Municipality of Cinisello Balsamo introduced this use case to tackle a significant administrative bottleneck: managing large volumes of certified emails, or PEC messages, which require staff to read, classify and sort incoming communications before they can be directed into the correct municipal processes. This manual work is repetitive, time-consuming and poorly suited to high-volume digital administration, yet it remains essential for ensuring timely response and orderly case handling. The stakeholders include municipal employees, administrative managers and citizens interacting with the municipality through certified email, with the objective of improving operational efficiency, reducing routine workload and allowing staff to concentrate on more strategic and rewarding tasks. The solution was implemented in partnership with Make IT through a machine-learning-based platform for PEC management. At a conceptual level, the system automates the reading, classification and routing of certified emails, creating a structured intake workflow that can integrate with municipal operations while preserving attention to security, data protection and ethical considerations. Rather than replacing human oversight altogether, the platform aims to reduce the clerical burden at the front end of the process. The expected impact is faster handling of incoming PEC traffic, reduced manual effort and improved productivity for municipal teams. More broadly, the project creates value by modernising digital administration, supporting better use of staff time and demonstrating how local authorities can apply automation responsibly in document-heavy service environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: UiPath - AI to help farmers get EU funding
source_description: Romania’s Agency for Financing Rural Investments needed to simplify and speed up the process through which farmers access EU funding, a process that traditionally involves collecting multiple documents and authorisations from different public sources. This administrative complexity can create delays, increase processing costs and discourage applicants, particularly where rural beneficiaries have limited time or resources to navigate public procedures. The use case therefore involves AFIR, farmers and the state institutions whose documents are needed for funding applications, with the objective of making access to EU support quicker, less burdensome and more efficient at scale. The solution was implemented by AFIR in collaboration with UiPath through automation tools that retrieve required documents and approvals as part of the application workflow. At a conceptual level, the system combines robotic process automation with AI-enabled enterprise automation to move across institutional systems, collect the necessary records and reduce the amount of manual administrative intervention needed. AFIR stated in March 2024 that the initiative was expected to benefit more than 50,000 stakeholders, including both farmers and state institutions. The expected impact is shorter processing times, lower administrative cost and improved operational efficiency across the funding chain. More broadly, the project creates value by making public funding more accessible, increasing the efficiency of inter-institutional document handling and supporting a more user-friendly model of agricultural-support administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI Supercomputing Platform
source_description: Serbia launched its national AI supercomputing platform in 2021 to address a strategic capability gap: innovative companies, start-ups and research users often need access to high-performance computing in order to develop advanced models and tackle data-intensive tasks, but such infrastructure is costly and difficult to secure independently. The platform was therefore designed as a national resource to strengthen the country’s innovation ecosystem and help build a stronger domestic community around advanced digital technologies. The stakeholders include start-ups, innovative companies, research institutions and public bodies responsible for digital development, with the objective of widening access to computational capacity, accelerating model development and supporting a more competitive national AI ecosystem. The solution is implemented through the National AI Platform located in the State Data Center in Kragujevac, where users can access supercomputing resources and training free of charge through a public call process. At a conceptual level, the platform combines GPU-based high-performance computing, training support and organised user access under Serbia’s national AI strategies for 2020–2025 and 2025–2030. Official information indicates that 38 institutions and 35 start-up companies currently have access, with more than 360 user accounts in total, and the platform has also received international recognition from the OECD. The expected impact is stronger innovation capacity, broader access to advanced computing and faster development of complex models. More broadly, the platform creates value by reducing infrastructure barriers, supporting start-up growth and reinforcing Serbia’s long-term digital competitiveness.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Innovation Center of the School of Electrical Engineering in Belgrade (ICEF)
title: COMtext.SR - An AI model for a small-ish language
source_description: Serbian-language digital resources remain relatively limited in several important professional domains, which creates a barrier to building robust language technologies for sectors such as law, administration, finance and healthcare. Existing public tools and datasets have not adequately covered these areas, leaving both academic and commercial users with fewer resources for high-quality text processing in Serbian, including both ekavica and ijekavica variants. COMtext.SR was developed to address this gap by creating a foundational set of openly available resources and tools for automatic text processing in Serbian. The stakeholders include the academic community, the IT industry and organisations working in domain-specific language environments, with the objective of strengthening the language-technology ecosystem and making advanced Serbian-language processing more broadly usable. The solution is implemented through the coordinated development of datasets, linguistic resources and processing tools released under a licence that permits all uses, including commercial applications. At a conceptual level, the project combines corpus development, language-model building and community contribution across previously under-resourced domains, while also mobilising donated expertise, materials and intellectual property from both academia and industry. The expected impact is improved access to Serbian-language processing tools, stronger support for specialised text analysis and a more capable national language-technology infrastructure. More broadly, COMtext.SR creates value by reducing resource scarcity, supporting innovation in a smaller language market and enabling broader public and commercial use of Serbian-language tools.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Computing Center of the Slovak Academy of Sciences (CC SAS)
title: Devana Supercomputer in Slovakia
source_description: The Slovak Academy of Sciences introduced the Devana supercomputer to strengthen national research capacity and replace older computing infrastructure that was no longer sufficient for increasingly data-intensive scientific and technological work. Researchers in universities and academy institutes require high-performance computing to run advanced simulations, process large datasets and support innovation in fields where conventional infrastructure can become a limiting factor. The use case therefore involves the Computing Center of the Slovak Academy of Sciences, academic researchers, university teams and commercial users, with the objective of expanding access to modern computational resources, improving research capability and supporting innovation across multiple domains. The solution is implemented through Devana, unveiled in May 2023, with a theoretical performance of around 800 teraflops. At a conceptual level, the system combines 140 universal computing nodes with 8 GPU-accelerated nodes, enabling large-scale modelling, scientific analysis and advanced applications in areas such as machine learning. The platform is provided free of charge to scientists and researchers from Slovak universities and institutes of the Slovak Academy of Sciences, while also supporting commercial projects. The impact includes stronger computational capacity, broader access to advanced infrastructure and improved support for complex research workflows. More broadly, Devana creates value by modernising Slovakia’s scientific infrastructure, fostering innovation and enabling more scalable and competitive research and development across academic and applied domains.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Fire Rescue Service of the Czech Republic
title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Czechia
source_description: Emergency call centres must gather critical information quickly, even when callers do not speak the local language fluently, yet language barriers can delay understanding at the very moment when speed and precision matter most. The Czech PSAP pilot addressed this challenge by testing whether language-support technology could improve emergency communication in multilingual and tourism-related situations. The stakeholders included call takers, PSAP managers and technology providers, with the objective of strengthening communication quality, supporting operators in multilingual calls and assessing whether the tool could become a practical aid in real emergency environments. The pilot focused on around 70 test calls in different languages and examined how well the solution handled transcription and translation under operational conditions. The implementation used Cestel’s NatalíA natural-language-processing solution, which combines simultaneous language detection, translation, transcription and text-to-speech services. At a conceptual level, the tool was tested as a support layer alongside standard emergency-call handling, helping operators understand incoming speech and access written representations of the exchange. The results showed encouraging potential, but also highlighted important limits, including uneven performance across languages, difficulties preserving the chronology of fast conversations and problems detecting questions in Czech, where intonation is especially important. The impact of the pilot was therefore primarily evaluative: it confirmed the promise of multilingual support in PSAP settings while also identifying clear requirements for better linguistic accuracy, stronger conversation handling and on-premise deployment to meet data-security expectations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Andalusia
source_description: In a region with tourism, linguistic diversity and time-critical emergency communications, the ability of call centres to understand callers quickly across languages is an important operational concern. The Andalusia PSAP pilot examined whether language-processing technology could reduce friction in emergency interactions and support operators when callers do not communicate clearly in the local language. The stakeholders included emergency call handlers, PSAP leadership and the technology provider, with the objective of improving communication speed, reducing misunderstanding and assessing the usefulness of automated support tools in emergency workflows. The pilot was conducted on a relatively small scale and concentrated on two specific functions that are especially relevant in live calls: transcription and text-to-speech. The implementation used Cestel’s NatalíA solution, which also includes language detection and translation capabilities. At a conceptual level, the system was introduced as a support mechanism alongside normal call-taking processes, helping operators access spoken content in text form and receive automated language assistance where needed. The findings were mixed: transcription and text-to-speech performed well, while translation was criticised for being too literal and insufficiently adapted to emergency terminology. Background noise also caused delays and disrupted the flow of communication. Even so, the pilot demonstrated operational potential and gave clear direction for improvement, particularly around transcription quality and service cohesion. The expected value lies in faster, more accessible multilingual communication, but only once robustness improves sufficiently for demanding emergency-call conditions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Basque Country
source_description: Emergency call centres in multilingual environments must capture vital information accurately even when callers speak quickly, switch language or place calls from noisy settings. The Basque Country PSAP pilot explored whether transcription technology could help improve the effectiveness of emergency communications by supporting operators with faster and clearer access to spoken content. The stakeholders included call takers, PSAP managers and the solution provider, with the objective of understanding the practical value of automated transcription in real emergency-call scenarios and identifying the conditions under which it might become operationally useful. The pilot focused on more than 25 simulated calls in Spanish and evaluated the quality of transcription produced during the exercises. The implementation used Cestel’s NatalíA language-processing solution, with attention centred in this case on the transcription service rather than the full multilingual feature set. At a conceptual level, the tool functioned as a real-time aid, converting speech into written text so that operators could track and review key information more easily during a call. The results showed good punctuation, spelling and speaker separation in many cases, indicating real promise. However, the system struggled with institution names, certain Basque characters and, crucially, the effects of background noise, especially in hands-free conditions. The pilot therefore demonstrated that transcription can add value in PSAP contexts, but also made clear that better accuracy and stronger chronology handling are needed before the solution is suitable for operational deployment.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Ludwigshafen (Germany)
source_description: Ludwigshafen PSAP explored whether advanced language and call-assistance technologies could improve emergency-call handling in situations where operators must work quickly, accurately and sometimes across multiple languages. Emergency communication centres need tools that support understanding without compromising reliability, privacy or operational control, especially when handling sensitive and time-critical calls. The pilot therefore involved call takers, management and the technology provider, with the objective of evaluating whether automated language services and AI-supported call guidance could improve the operator experience and strengthen information capture during emergencies. The trial tested LiveReader’s ALTERNIS solution for simultaneous language detection, translation and transcription, alongside the NOTITIA tool, which proposes questions and extracts call data to support operators. At a conceptual level, the system combined offline, on-premise detection and transcription for security, browser-based translation without data storage, and AI-assisted prompts to help structure calls. The pilot involved 184 participants working on 1,319 simulated cases, providing a substantial testing base. Participants rated the solution positively, with an average score of 4.1 out of 5, and particularly appreciated the interface and the AI-generated hints. However, the beta version was not considered ready for live operational use, especially because of limitations in generative support and insufficient medical knowledge. Even so, the pilot showed clear value in secure, supportive AI tooling for PSAPs and identified a credible path for future operational maturity.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Trento (Italy)
source_description: Emergency call audio is often one of the most difficult speech environments to process reliably, as conversations may include screams, overlapping voices, weak connections and high background noise. The Trento PSAP pilot examined whether automated transcription could still be useful under these demanding conditions and whether it could support future enhancements in emergency-call processing. The stakeholders included call takers, PSAP managers and the technology provider, with the objective of testing the practical value of transcription tools on live emergency calls and understanding how such outputs might support broader operational improvements. The pilot was conducted on approximately 2,500 emergency calls between mid-August and the end of September 2024, and user experience was assessed through several methods, including focus groups. The implementation used Gladia’s transcription tool as a support layer within the call-handling process. At a conceptual level, the technology sought to convert speech into text in real time, creating a basis for later integration with tools capable of summarising calls, suggesting actions or automatically populating CAD systems. In practice, call takers found that transcription quality was not yet sufficient for emergency audio conditions and rated the service poorly. However, the pilot still generated useful insight: it confirmed operational interest in transcription, identified the audio-quality barriers that must be addressed and highlighted downstream opportunities for large-language-model applications. Gladia reported that some issues found during the pilot were corrected in an October 2024 update, suggesting potential for future improvement.

title: Julia: GenerativeAI as a public service
source_description: Julia is the official AI assistant of Roma Capitale: a free, multilingual public service available 24/7 that uses natural language to help citizens, tourists and city users find answers, navigate the city and access digital services. It is the first generative AI developed and governed by a local public authority. Based on certified data from Roma Capitale and qualified partners, it brings information and services together in a single conversational interface. Available on WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger and Webchat, since June it has also been available on the institutional portal, which hosts more than 160,000 pieces of content, around 90 online services and 18 million annual visits. Julia guides users to official services and sources, providing direct links and related documents. The platform is multi-agent: a Super Agent routes requests to specialized agents for city experiences, authenticated services and CRM. The Azure-centric architecture, with the Fastweb Information Agent integrated across cloud environments, ensures scalability, security and seamless integration.
