title: AI.CAN: AI Citizen Science Aqua Network
source_description: Monitoring water quality across a river system is a complex task, particularly when environmental changes can emerge quickly and official measurement points alone may not provide enough spatial or temporal coverage. AI.CAN addresses this challenge by combining citizen participation with scientific monitoring to improve aquatic-ecology data collection and analysis along the Oder River. The stakeholders include citizen initiatives, NGOs, environmental associations, researchers and public-interest organisations, with the objective of creating a richer and more distributed evidence base for understanding water conditions and ecological risks. The project also aims to show that collaborative, data-driven water monitoring can be transferable to other river systems and bodies of water. The solution is implemented through sensor boxes deployed by non-governmental and citizen actors, whose data are then analysed together with official monitoring information. At a conceptual level, the system combines distributed environmental sensing, citizen-science participation and analytical models to identify patterns in water-quality conditions and improve interpretation of aquatic data. The collaboration with the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries and re:edu provides a bridge between grassroots monitoring and scientific expertise. The expected impact is broader data coverage, improved environmental awareness and stronger capacity to detect and understand water-quality issues. More broadly, AI.CAN creates value by making aquatic monitoring more participatory, scalable and evidence-based, while strengthening cooperation between citizens and scientific institutions in environmental stewardship.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: SUMM AI - Creating accessible information: End to end automated with AI
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Public administrations are increasingly expected to provide information that is not only accurate and timely, but also easy to understand and accessible to people with different communication needs. In practice, however, producing barrier-free content can be labour-intensive, particularly when staff must adapt texts, identify suitable illustrations and ensure that materials remain understandable for broad audiences. This use case, developed by the start-up SUMM AI in collaboration with the press office of the Senate of Hamburg, addresses that operational challenge by helping public-sector employees create accessible information with far less manual effort. The objective is to improve equal access to public information across Germany by making the production of clearer, more inclusive content faster and easier within everyday administrative workflows. The solution is implemented as an automated pipeline that analyses the meaning of a text and suggests suitable images from a curated database, with future functionality intended to generate new visuals where no appropriate image exists. At a conceptual level, the system combines text analysis, semantic matching and image recommendation within a content-production workflow tailored to public administration. This allows staff to move more quickly from raw written content to illustrated, accessible materials. The expected impact is reduced preparation time, improved consistency in accessible communication and broader reach for public information. More broadly, the project strengthens inclusion, enhances the usability of official communications and creates value by lowering the practical barriers to producing barrier-free content at scale.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Civic-Sync – Mapping platform for social offerings
source_description: Citizens and frontline organisations often struggle to navigate the wide range of social and cultural services available in a community, especially when information is fragmented across providers, difficult to search or inaccessible to people who face language or digital barriers. Civic-Sync addresses this problem by creating a shared platform through which social and cultural offerings can be collected, structured and made easier to find. The stakeholders include civil-society organisations, public institutions and the people seeking support, with the objective of improving visibility, accessibility and coordination across available services while ensuring that information remains easy to reuse and compliant with data-protection requirements. The solution is implemented as a collaborative database and mapping platform with open interfaces, multilingual access and low-barrier design. At a conceptual level, the platform combines shared data structures, translation tools and speech output to make information available to a broader set of users, while future development focuses on enhancing search, guidance and feedback functions through additional intelligent support features. This creates a common infrastructure through which providers can maintain and share service information more effectively. The expected impact is easier access to relevant social and cultural offerings, better discoverability for target groups and improved coordination between institutions and civil-society actors. More broadly, Civic-Sync supports inclusion, strengthens service visibility and creates value by turning dispersed local information into a more navigable, multilingual and citizen-friendly support ecosystem.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Claim - AI for social claims
source_description: Many people do not access state support simply because the system is difficult to understand, full of administrative language and fragmented across multiple schemes, forms and eligibility rules. Claim addresses this barrier by helping users determine, anonymously and more simply, which public benefits or funding they may be entitled to receive. The use case involves citizens, social workers and counsellors, with the objective of reducing bureaucratic and linguistic obstacles, saving time in advisory settings and making access to public support more equitable. Rather than requiring users to navigate numerous official sources, the tool is designed to guide them through a single process that clarifies possible entitlements and next steps. The solution is implemented through an interactive application that calculates individual claims on the basis of one structured form and delivers personalised guidance. At a conceptual level, it combines machine learning and natural language processing to support user interaction, extract relevant information dynamically and offer multilingual access, enabling both self-service use by citizens and guided use in advisory consultations. This allows complex eligibility logic to be translated into a more accessible user journey. The expected impact is quicker identification of relevant support, reduced consultation time for social workers and fewer missed entitlements for citizens. More broadly, Claim improves user experience, lowers access barriers and creates social value by making public financial assistance easier to understand and reach.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Comms4Good - AI for public relations work of social and non-profit organizations
source_description: Many social and non-profit organisations need to communicate professionally with the public, funders and local communities, yet they often lack dedicated communications staff, sufficient budgets or the specialist expertise needed to produce high-quality public-relations material. This challenge is particularly acute in organisations that depend on volunteers, where communication work competes with service delivery for time and attention. Comms4Good addresses this gap by supporting non-experts in carrying out essential PR tasks more effectively and at lower cost. The stakeholders include social organisations, non-profits, volunteers and communication leads, with the objective of improving visibility, strengthening outreach and making everyday communication work more manageable. The solution is implemented as a virtual assistant developed through a collaboration between IU International University, Producer Media UG and Phineo. At a conceptual level, the tool analyses an organisation’s existing public presence and generates practical recommendations and templates, such as draft press releases or poster ideas, to support communication activities. By embedding this support in an accessible digital tool, the project seeks to raise the baseline quality of communications without requiring extensive external expertise. The expected impact is improved visibility for social initiatives, more efficient communication workflows and a better working culture around outreach tasks. More broadly, Comms4Good creates value by helping mission-driven organisations communicate more professionally, consistently and affordably.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: CORRECTIV.Faktenforum - AI to combat disinformation
source_description: CORRECTIV.Faktenforum is Germany’s first fact-checking community, created to involve citizens in identifying, discussing and countering false claims. The societal problem is the rapid spread of disinformation online, which can outpace traditional journalistic fact-checking and undermine public debate. The platform therefore combines community participation, civic technology and professional guidance to scale prebunking and debunking activities. Stakeholders include CORRECTIV, participating citizens, journalists, online communities, civic-tech actors and the wider public exposed to misleading information. The implementation enables people, regardless of journalistic experience, to contribute from anywhere by identifying suspicious claims, collecting evidence, discussing facts and sharing findings under CORRECTIV’s guidance to maintain journalistic standards. AI technologies support the workflow through data analysis, machine learning and generative AI, while human-in-the-loop tools such as CORRECTIV.Checkbot assist community efforts. Conceptually, the system combines collaborative fact-checking, automated claim-support tools, content analysis, community moderation and editorial oversight. The expected impact is increased capacity to detect and respond to false claims, stronger public participation in information integrity and improved resilience against disinformation campaigns. By combining automation with human review and journalistic standards, the project can expand fact-checking capacity without fully outsourcing judgement to machines. Its value lies in linking civic engagement with structured, technology-supported verification processes.

title: BOTschafft Inclusion - AI for families with disability
source_description: Parents caring for children with disabilities or chronic illnesses often face a complex and exhausting landscape of support services, rehabilitation options, training opportunities and employment-related questions. Finding the right information at the right time can be difficult, and this can make it harder for families to stay in work, access assistance or participate fully in social life. BOTschafft Inclusion addresses this challenge by providing more accessible and responsive guidance for caregiving parents and, in some cases, for employers seeking relevant support information. The stakeholders include families, employers and support organisations, with the objective of helping parents remain professionally active, better informed and more connected to available services. The solution is implemented as a chatbot-based support system developed through a collaboration between Cologne University of Applied Sciences, Founders1 GmbH and Health Region CologneBonn e.V. At a conceptual level, the system uses language-understanding capabilities to interpret complex questions, recommend relevant services and adapt its responses over time as it learns from interactions and use patterns. This enables more tailored guidance than static information pages or conventional FAQ tools. The expected impact is easier access to counselling and support, reduced time spent searching for relevant assistance and a more personalised experience for caregiving families. More broadly, the project promotes inclusion, supports labour-market participation and creates social value by making support pathways more understandable and usable for parents under considerable practical pressure.

title: Deaf.AI - AI for social inclusion
source_description: Deaf people continue to face significant communication barriers in everyday social and professional life, particularly where information, services and interactions are not readily available in sign language. These barriers can limit participation, reduce independence and make access to public and private services more difficult. Deaf.AI addresses this problem by seeking to improve sign-language accessibility through tools developed around the actual needs of the deaf community. The stakeholders include deaf individuals, advocacy organisations and service environments where communication inclusion matters, with the objective of strengthening participation, reducing exclusion and expanding access to information and interaction in more accessible forms. The solution is implemented by training systems on extensive sign-language video data in order to develop avatars capable of automatically rendering sign-language output. At a conceptual level, the project combines video-based language modelling, avatar generation and translation functionality so that spoken or written information can be conveyed more effectively in sign language. A defining feature of the initiative is that it is led by deaf professionals, ensuring that development remains grounded in practical use and community priorities rather than abstract technical assumptions. The expected impact is improved accessibility, greater autonomy and stronger social and professional participation for deaf users. More broadly, Deaf.AI creates value by advancing inclusive communication tools that are community-led, need-based and focused on reducing structural barriers faced by deaf people.

title: Digitaler Erstkontakt (Digital Initial Contact) - AI for counseling services related to family and parenthood
source_description: People seeking advice on family and parenting issues do not always know which counselling service is appropriate for their situation, and this can delay support, create frustration and increase the burden on organisations that must redirect enquiries manually. Digitaler Erstkontakt addresses this problem by creating a constant first point of contact that can guide users more quickly to the counselling facility best suited to their needs. The stakeholders include people seeking advice, counselling organisations and service coordinators, with the objective of improving access, reducing misdirection and ensuring that enquiries are matched more efficiently to the right provider. The solution is implemented through an automated dialogue system called guide.me – smart paths to counseling, designed for deployment as both a chat bot and a telephone bot. At a conceptual level, the system uses natural-language-processing methods to interpret user input and connect it with curated response pathways and referral logic developed entirely by human experts. Unlike generative systems that produce new content on their own, this approach relies on controlled outputs, allowing organisations to retain a high degree of oversight over behaviour and service quality. Development, testing and evaluation are carried out through agile feedback cycles, enabling regular refinement. The expected impact is faster and more accurate referral to counselling, improved user experience and reduced administrative effort for service providers. More broadly, the project creates value by making first contact with counselling services more accessible, dependable and operationally efficient.

title: EdTech for Diversity in AI
source_description: As companies increasingly adopt digital applications in people-related processes such as recruitment, there is a growing need to ensure that these systems are introduced in ways that do not reproduce or reinforce discrimination. Many organisations recognise the risk, but lack the practical knowledge and internal capability required to implement diversity-sensitive solutions confidently. The DivAI project was created to address this gap by equipping companies and employees with the skills needed to introduce human-centred digital applications more responsibly. The stakeholders include employers, staff and organisations involved in workplace digitalisation, with the objective of reducing discriminatory risk, supporting fairer adoption practices and providing an accessible learning route for organisations that may not otherwise have specialist expertise in this area. The solution is implemented through an AI-supported learning platform offering low-threshold digital training packages. At a conceptual level, the project builds on the EdTech tool developed by platform3L, using adaptive digital-learning functionalities to deliver practical content on diversity-sensitive implementation and to support skills development in real workplace settings. This allows training to be embedded into everyday organisational learning rather than treated as a one-off intervention. The expected impact is better preparedness for fair digital adoption, improved awareness of discrimination risks and stronger internal capability among companies and employees. More broadly, DivAI creates value by supporting more inclusive workplace innovation and making diversity-sensitive implementation more scalable and accessible.

title: Harnessing 5G for innovation in higher education in Belgium
source_description: Higher-education institutions increasingly need digital infrastructures that can support advanced teaching, applied research and closer collaboration with industry, particularly in fields where real-time data exchange and connected devices are essential. HOGENT University in Ghent addresses this challenge through the 5GENIUS project, which aims to integrate private 5G networks into education and research in order to strengthen both learning and innovation. The stakeholders include students, teachers, researchers and industry partners, with the objective of familiarising them with the practical potential of 5G while improving the quality of training and experimentation in sectors such as healthcare, logistics and agriculture. The solution is implemented through private 5G infrastructure that provides high-speed, low-latency connectivity across educational and research environments. At a conceptual level, this enables use cases such as real-time healthcare training through smart glasses, remote guidance without transmission delays, and continuous data collection from drones and machinery in precision agriculture. By embedding these capabilities directly into teaching and research workflows, the university links technical experimentation with practical sectoral applications. The expected impact is richer student learning, stronger industry-academia collaboration and improved research capability in connected, data-intensive environments. More broadly, the initiative enhances institutional innovation capacity, helps prepare future professionals for emerging technologies and creates value by positioning higher education as a driver of smart, connected communities.

title: Consultation AI

Its implementation uses AI-driven analytics to support the analysis, synthesis and reporting of consultation responses, while preserving a human decision-making role for policymakers and public officials. Conceptually, the system combines text classification, clustering, summarisation, theme extraction and reporting support to help governments understand citizen input at scale. title: EKAPEx - AI for precipitation forecast
source_description: Forecasting extreme precipitation accurately is a growing operational challenge, particularly as severe weather events place increasing pressure on infrastructure, emergency planning and public safety. Traditional forecasting approaches can be computationally demanding and may not always extract the full value from long-term observational datasets. EKAPEx addresses this challenge by developing improved precipitation forecasts for Germany, with a particular focus on extreme weather events and the need for methods that are both effective and resource-efficient. The stakeholders include meteorological researchers, forecasting specialists and organisations that rely on timely weather intelligence, with the objective of improving predictive accuracy while controlling computational demands. The solution is implemented through analytical models trained on a distinctive long-term dataset derived from the Global Navigation Satellite System, covering the past 20 years. At a conceptual level, the project uses these historical atmospheric and positioning-related signals to support the development of new forecasting algorithms capable of identifying patterns linked to precipitation intensity and extreme-weather formation. By combining long-run data depth with efficient modelling techniques, the approach seeks to improve forecast quality without relying on unnecessarily heavy computational processes. The expected impact is more accurate precipitation prediction, better anticipation of extreme events and more efficient use of forecasting resources. More broadly, EKAPEx creates value by strengthening weather preparedness, improving the usability of specialised environmental datasets and supporting more resilient responses to high-impact rainfall events.

title: ErLeSen - Creation and Analysis of Easy Language through AI
source_description: Access to information remains uneven when official or public-facing texts are difficult to understand for people with cognitive impairments or limited proficiency in German. This creates barriers to participation in education, services and everyday social life, particularly where simplified language is not readily available at scale. ErLeSen addresses this challenge by developing tools that can convert complex German texts into Leichte Sprache so that more people can engage with information independently and effectively. The stakeholders include individuals who benefit from Easy Language, accessibility advocates and organisations seeking to communicate more inclusively, with the objective of improving societal participation through more understandable written content. The solution is implemented through open models and datasets designed to learn from pairs of complex and simplified texts. At a conceptual level, the project uses deep-learning methods based on artificial neural networks, supported by partially synthetic data generation and later refinement through reinforcement-learning techniques. This allows the models to capture patterns of simplification while improving output quality over time. The emphasis on open resources also supports reuse and broader accessibility in the field. The expected impact is easier access to information, stronger inclusion for users with specific language or comprehension needs and reduced effort in producing simplified texts manually. More broadly, ErLeSen creates value by supporting accessible communication as a scalable digital capability rather than a purely manual specialist service.

title: Helpme.ai - assisting asylum seekers with AI
source_description: Helpme.ai addresses the information barriers faced by refugees and asylum seekers who need reliable, understandable, and context-specific guidance when navigating administrative procedures, social services, accommodation, rights, and local support options in Germany. The operational problem is that relevant information is often dispersed across official websites, service providers, assistance organisations, and informal experiences, making it difficult for users to identify accurate answers in a language they understand. Stakeholders include asylum seekers, refugees, public administrations, social service providers, civil society organisations, and the Helpme.ai platform team. The objective is to provide a centralised, accessible support channel that can respond to user questions and guide people towards relevant resources. The implementation uses Large Language Models to deliver multilingual chatbot functionality, supported by advanced natural language processing and a privacy-conscious configuration. The system draws on an information vector database containing material from official websites, social service providers, assistance resources, and positive experiences shared by previous refugees and asylum seekers. Through retrieval-based techniques, the chatbot can search relevant content, generate contextual answers, and present information through a web interface. The expected impact includes improved access to support, reduced confusion, faster orientation, and better user experience for vulnerable groups. For service providers, the platform can reduce repeated enquiries, scale multilingual assistance, and improve the consistency of information delivered across different user situations.

title: KIA - AI-supported assistance for digital psychosocial counseling
source_description: Digital psychosocial counselling services often require counsellors to assess complex enquiries quickly while maintaining empathy, relevance and consistency in their responses. As demand grows, there is a practical need for tools that can support professionals during consultations without disrupting the human-centred nature of the interaction. KIA addresses this challenge by developing an assistive system for digital psychosocial counselling that helps practitioners interpret incoming requests and respond more effectively in real time. The stakeholders include counsellors, service providers and people seeking support, with the objective of improving the efficiency and quality of digital counselling while preserving professional judgement and relational care. The solution is implemented as an assistance system that analyses counselling enquiries as they arrive and provides targeted cues to the counsellor during the exchange. At a conceptual level, the platform combines several analytical methods to identify relevant themes, interpret user needs and generate support prompts that can help structure the consultation and surface useful response directions. title: Gefion - the new Supercomputer in Denmark
source_description: Gefion is Denmark’s national AI supercomputer, established to strengthen the country’s capacity for advanced research and innovation across healthcare, life sciences, biotechnology, environmental sustainability and quantum computing. The strategic problem is that frontier AI research requires large-scale computing infrastructure that may otherwise be inaccessible to Danish public and private researchers. The initiative is led by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark, in collaboration with NVIDIA, and is operated by the Danish Centre for AI Innovation. The implementation uses NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD infrastructure with 1,528 GPUs, creating a national platform for high-performance AI workloads. Conceptually, Gefion provides sovereign AI compute capacity, expert support and access mechanisms for Danish researchers and companies developing advanced AI applications. The expected impact is faster scientific discovery, stronger national technological capacity, more competitive AI research and better support for innovation in domains such as drug discovery, disease diagnosis, climate research and quantum technologies. The system was launched in Copenhagen in October 2024, when it was symbolically turned on by King Frederik X, NVIDIA’s CEO and DCAI’s CEO.

title: Navigard: the future of road safety on Italian motorways
source_description: Navigard is an advanced motorway safety platform developed by Autostrade per l’Italia and the Italian State Police to improve traffic monitoring, enforcement and incident detection on Italian highways. The operational challenge is that motorway safety depends on rapidly identifying risky behaviours and conditions, including dangerous overtaking by heavy vehicles, wrong-way driving, overloaded vehicles, accidents and abnormal traffic situations. The system integrates radars, high-definition cameras, sensors and centrally processed data to monitor traffic and driver behaviour in real time. Its implementation relies on complex algorithms, advanced sensing infrastructure and a central platform able to communicate with competent authorities. title: GovTech4All - Secure information in cross-border data spaces
source_description: GovTech4All Pilot 1 focused on the challenge of securely sharing sensitive public-sector data across borders while preparing digital public services for future cryptographic risks. Public administrations increasingly depend on data spaces that must remain confidential, interoperable, and resilient over time. Led by LANTIK with GRNET and DINUM, the pilot involved public authorities, infrastructure providers, and European institutions, aiming to protect shared data while preserving usability and compliance. The technical solution combined post-quantum cryptographic algorithms with fully homomorphic encryption, enabling data to be processed while remaining encrypted. An open-source framework was developed, deployable via Docker and accessible through APIs, allowing public bodies to integrate advanced encryption into existing systems without architectural disruption. Data exchanged within cross-border services could be analysed securely without exposing underlying information. The pilot was conducted between mid-2023 and mid-2024 under the Digital Europe Programme. Outcomes included improved long-term data security, reduced exposure to emerging cryptographic threats, and a reusable framework adaptable across administrations. The project strengthened trust in European data spaces while supporting scalability, interoperability, and regulatory alignment for future digital public services.

title: INDOOR – usINg Drones fOr Organ tRansportation
source_description: INDOOR tests whether drones can improve medical logistics for the transport of organs and biological material in urban areas. The operational challenge is that transplant logistics are extremely time-sensitive, while road-based transport can be affected by traffic, distance between hospital sites and coordination constraints. In Turin, the project demonstrated a drone connection between two hospital facilities, aiming to create a replicable model for faster and safer transport of organs, blood, medicines and biological samples. The experimental flight on 1 October 2024 covered around 500 metres between the CTO helipad and the Molinette Genetics building, crossing an urban section of the city and part of the Po river. The drone, developed by ABzero, used a dedicated smart capsule able to maintain appropriate transport conditions. Its implementation combines automatic drone navigation, protected biomedical transport, capsule-based monitoring and integrated AI for continuous control of temperature, humidity and material integrity. The expected impact is shorter medical transport times, improved reliability of transplant logistics and stronger capacity to manage urgent biological deliveries across dense urban environments. In Piedmont, the potential beneficiaries include transplant patients, with 496 organ transplants reported in 2024, 449 of them in Turin.

title: Rome's Digital Twin - Atlante di Roma Capitale
source_description: Managing Rome’s extensive territory and public assets requires municipal departments to access consistent, accurate and interoperable information. Previously, relevant data were distributed across fragmented databases, paper records and systems that could not communicate effectively. To address this challenge, Roma Capitale developed the Atlante di Roma Capitale, an integrated digital platform described by the municipality as the city’s digital twin. Launched in July 2026 as an expansion of the existing Atlante del Patrimonio, the platform aims to improve knowledge of the urban territory, strengthen public-asset management and progressively integrate data and services from across the municipal administration. The Atlante is based on a new aerial photogrammetric survey covering the entire municipal territory and provides high-definition cartography with a resolution of approximately 5–7.5 centimetres per pixel. The platform integrates three-dimensional mesh models, Building Information Modelling navigation and tools that allow users to perform measurements directly within the digital environment. Data integrity and verifiability are supported through SHA2-256 digital hashes and a precision photogrammetric processing chain. The platform currently incorporates more than 60% of Roma Capitale’s property portfolio, which can be consulted by category, address, condition and surface area. It also integrates the Atlante del Patrimonio, the three-dimensional Schools Atlas and the Underground Utilities Atlas, although access to the latter is restricted for security reasons. Its open architecture is designed to progressively accommodate additional datasets, services and information from all municipal departments. Roma Capitale intends to complete the digitalisation of its entire property portfolio by 2027. Expected benefits include more coordinated planning and maintenance activities, improved access to municipal information, more efficient management of public assets and greater administrative transparency.

title: Caddy - AI powered tool for customer service functions (part of the Humphrey toolkit)
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Caddy was piloted to support frontline customer service agents handling complex citizen enquiries under time pressure. Developed with Citizens Advice organisations, the objective was to improve response quality while reducing cognitive load on advisers. The system acted as a secure copilot, analysing queries and suggesting structured guidance drawn from trusted knowledge bases. Language models and retrieval techniques ensured responses were accurate, auditable, and aligned with organisational standards. Caddy integrated into existing case management systems without replacing human judgement. The pilot ran from mid-2023 to mid-2024. Results showed faster response times, improved advice consistency, and higher agent confidence. The tool enhanced service quality while maintaining accountability, demonstrating clear business value and scalability for public-facing advisory services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology and Infrastructure and Projects Authority (IPA)
title: Scout - AI-powered tool to improve government major project delivery
source_description: Oversight of major government projects in the United Kingdom requires the analysis of extensive documentation, often under time pressure and with high financial stakes. Review teams within the Infrastructure and Projects Authority face challenges in ensuring consistency, identifying recurring risks and retaining institutional knowledge. The objective of this pilot is to significantly improve the speed and quality of project reviews. The implementation introduces a document analysis system that processes large volumes of review material, extracts structured insights and stores them in a searchable vector-based repository. Two complementary modules support reviewers: one assesses compliance with official review guidelines using traceable citations, while another identifies cross-project patterns and potential risks. The system integrates into existing review workflows and relies exclusively on authoritative guidance. The pilot reduced review preparation time from several days to minutes, improved consistency across assessments and enhanced knowledge reuse. Qualitative benefits include better risk anticipation, more robust decision-making and improved working conditions for reviewers, supporting future scaling across government assurance functions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology
title: Connect - AI to match capacity to demand in the Grid connections queue
source_description: The transition to renewable energy is constrained by delays in connecting new projects to the electricity grid, creating long queues and uncertainty for investors. In the UK, grid operators require better tools to allocate limited capacity more effectively. The objective of Connect is to optimise the matching of available grid capacity with demand from connection applicants. The implementation is developing advanced matching and optimisation algorithms that analyse grid constraints, project readiness and demand characteristics. These tools aim to support planners in prioritising connections that deliver the greatest system and policy benefits. As the project is in development, evaluation focuses on decision-support quality rather than automated execution. Expected impacts include reduced connection delays, improved investment confidence and accelerated deployment of renewable energy. Qualitative outcomes include more transparent planning, better resource utilisation and a scalable approach to managing infrastructure constraints.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI to analyse X-ray images for bone fractures and joint injuries in the healthcare system
source_description: Emergency departments face increasing pressure from high patient volumes, particularly during out-of-hours periods, which can delay diagnosis and treatment. In Denmark, healthcare providers seek tools to support clinicians in analysing injury-related X-rays. The objective of this initiative is to improve diagnostic support for fractures and joint injuries while reducing waiting times. The implementation involves developing systems that analyse X-ray images and identify the likelihood of fractures with high accuracy, supporting clinical decision-making. The solution is currently deployed in pilot settings and is planned for gradual national rollout. Expected impacts include faster triage, reduced workload for staff and improved patient flow. Qualitative benefits include enhanced clinical confidence, improved service resilience and more equitable access to timely care.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: VisitMadridGPT - Transforming tourism in Madrid
source_description: Tourists visiting Madrid require timely, accurate, and personalised information to navigate attractions, transport, and services, while the city seeks better insight into visitor needs. VisitMadridGPT addresses both challenges by enhancing digital tourism services. The objective is to improve visitor experience, accessibility, and data-driven tourism management. The solution is implemented as a virtual assistant accessible online, providing real-time information and personalised recommendations in over 95 languages. It integrates official tourism data, city services, and content management systems, while capturing anonymised interaction data for analysis by city officials. The impact is reflected in strong user engagement, with an average session duration of four minutes and 18 seconds and a low bounce rate. The assistant improves accessibility for international visitors, reduces pressure on traditional information channels, and provides valuable insights into tourism behaviour. VisitMadridGPT delivers measurable improvements in user experience, supports smarter tourism planning, and strengthens Madrid’s position as an innovative, visitor-friendly destination.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Barcelona Supercomputing Center-Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS)
title: ALIA - European Supercomputing Public Infrastructure
source_description: ALIA is a pioneering initiative in the European Union that seeks to provide a public infrastructure of AI resources, such as open and transparent language models, to boost the promotion of Spanish and co-official languages ​​- Catalan and Valencian, Basque and Galician - in the development and deployment of AI in the world. This is the first European public infrastructure, open and multilingual, which, thanks to the unique supercomputing capabilities of the Barcelona Supercomputing Center, reinforces the technological sovereignty of Spain and Europe in the development of transparent, responsible AI at the service of people. This project is coordinated by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center-Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS), with the support and leadership of the Secretary of State for Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence. It is also part of the Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024 initiated by the Spanish Government
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-Code - GenAi against disinformation
source_description: The rapid proliferation of manipulated and synthetic media has increased the difficulty for journalists to verify content and maintain public trust in news reporting. Media organisations and fact-checking networks require tools that can operate at the speed of modern information flows while remaining transparent and reliable. The objective of this pilot is to support trustworthy journalism by enhancing the detection and assessment of disinformation across digital channels. The implementation develops a suite of interoperable services integrated into newsroom workflows, enabling the analysis of text, images and audiovisual material for credibility, provenance and signs of manipulation. These services draw on media archives, social platforms and verification datasets, and are evaluated against existing market solutions. The pilot is expected to improve verification speed, detection accuracy and transparency in content handling. Qualitative impacts include stronger editorial confidence, improved collaboration between journalists and fact-checkers, and increased audience trust. The project also contributes shared knowledge to the wider research and media communities, supporting responsible innovation in the fight against disinformation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Teaching Institute of Public Health “Dr. Andrija Štampar”
title: Tackling Air Pollution in the City of Zagreb
source_description: Air quality management in large urban areas requires accurate, granular and timely information to protect public health and guide environmental policy. In Zagreb, authorities and health institutions faced limitations in understanding pollution dynamics across the city. The objective of this pilot is to provide a comprehensive, real-time overview of air quality conditions and predictive insights to support decision-making. The implementation deploys a network of environmental sensors collecting data on key pollutants and meteorological factors, combined with modelling techniques that assess exposure levels and forecast trends. Results are presented through analytical tools and public dashboards accessible to policymakers and citizens. The pilot enabled more precise identification of pollution hotspots, improved forecasting capabilities and greater transparency of environmental data. Qualitative benefits include better-informed urban planning, increased public awareness and stronger institutional capacity to respond to environmental risks. The initiative demonstrates how continuous monitoring and predictive analysis can contribute to healthier and more sustainable urban environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Transforming Croatian Schools with Indoor Air Quality Monitoring
source_description: Learning environments are directly influenced by indoor air quality, yet many schools lack the tools to monitor and manage classroom conditions effectively. In Croatia, education authorities and school administrators sought to improve student wellbeing and learning outcomes through better environmental control. The objective of this pilot is to enhance indoor air quality across 400 schools nationwide. The implementation involves installing sensors that continuously measure parameters such as carbon dioxide levels, temperature and humidity, with real-time data transmitted to a centralised monitoring dashboard. Visual indicators and alerts enable staff to take timely actions, such as ventilating classrooms or adjusting heating systems. The pilot led to measurable improvements in classroom conditions and increased awareness among teachers and administrators. Qualitative outcomes include healthier learning environments, improved concentration for students and a stronger evidence base for school facility management. The project provides a scalable model for smart education infrastructure and supports broader digital transformation in the education sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-augmented system for predicting electricity consumption in Serbia
source_description: The Electric Power Company of Serbia (EPS) is responsible for balancing electricity generation, distribution, and consumption across a national grid subject to fluctuating demand, seasonal variation, and increasing sustainability requirements. Traditional forecasting methods limited the company’s ability to anticipate demand peaks accurately, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation and higher operational costs. This use case involves EPS grid operators, planners, and energy market stakeholders, with the objective of improving demand forecasting to support reliable supply, optimise grid operations, and reduce waste. The solution is implemented through an advanced forecasting system that combines historical consumption data, real-time grid measurements, weather information, and socio-economic indicators. Machine-learning models analyse these datasets to generate short- and medium-term demand predictions that are continuously updated as new data becomes available. The system is integrated into EPS operational platforms to support planning, dispatch, and decision-making. The impact includes more accurate demand forecasts, improved grid stability, and better optimisation of generation assets. EPS benefits from reduced operational risk, improved energy efficiency, and stronger support for sustainability objectives, contributing to smarter and more resilient national energy management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: exPEDite - Enabling Positive Energy Districts through Digital Twins
source_description: Achieving climate neutrality at district level requires coordinated management of energy production, consumption and mobility, which is difficult using fragmented planning tools. City planners and energy stakeholders need integrated solutions to manage complex urban systems. The objective of this pilot is to support the creation of Positive Energy Districts that produce more energy than they consume. The implementation develops digital twins of urban districts that combine real-time and historical data on buildings, energy networks and transport flows. Simulation and optimisation tools allow stakeholders to test scenarios, optimise energy balance and engage citizens through visualisation and gamification features. The pilot demonstrated improved energy efficiency, reduced emissions and enhanced planning capabilities. Qualitative impacts include better cross-sector collaboration, increased public engagement and transferable guidelines for replication in other cities. The project illustrates the value of digital twins in supporting sustainable urban transformation across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Blockchain.PT - Decentralize Portugal with Blockchain
source_description: Portugal aims to strengthen its position in emerging digital infrastructures by building a coordinated national blockchain ecosystem capable of supporting innovation, interoperability and new business opportunities across multiple sectors. Without such coordination, blockchain adoption can remain fragmented, limiting scale, reuse and broader economic impact. Blockchain.PT addresses this challenge by bringing together a large consortium of partners to create the foundations for a national ecosystem that supports both technological development and market-oriented application. The stakeholders include technology firms, research institutions, sectoral organisations and public and private actors involved in areas such as agriculture, digital asset management and interoperability, with the objective of positioning Portugal at the forefront of blockchain development in Europe. The solution is implemented as a collaborative national initiative led by VOID Software and involving 56 partners, including INESC-ID, funded through the Recovery and Resilience Plan and the European Union’s Next Generation EU framework. At a conceptual level, the project supports ecosystem building, experimentation and cross-sector development of blockchain-enabled solutions, creating shared momentum across research, deployment and business uptake. This model is intended to reduce fragmentation and accelerate capability-building at national level. The expected impact is stronger innovation capacity, improved cross-sector collaboration and greater readiness to capture global business opportunities linked to blockchain. More broadly, Blockchain.PT creates strategic value by supporting technological leadership, ecosystem coherence and long-term digital competitiveness.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smart City Logistics – Automating Last-Mile Delivery in Leuven
source_description: Urban last-mile delivery places growing pressure on cities, especially where mail, goods movement and mobility services compete for road space and where fragmented operations reduce efficiency. This use case addresses the challenge by exploring how delivery processes can be automated within a smart-city framework so that logistics and mobility operate more smoothly in dense urban environments. The stakeholders include public authorities, city administrations and business operators working in partnership, with the objective of improving delivery efficiency, supporting better urban mobility and creating a more coordinated model for last-mile operations. The solution is implemented through automation of delivery processes as part of the EU-funded TOKEN project, using a public-private partnership model that connects government actors, the city and a business operator. At a conceptual level, the approach combines digital coordination, automated logistics processes and smart-city service integration to streamline the movement of goods in the final stage of delivery. This allows last-mile operations to be linked more closely with wider urban mobility systems instead of being treated as a separate logistical problem. The expected impact is more efficient urban delivery, smoother interaction between logistics and city transport systems and stronger operational coordination among partners. More broadly, the initiative creates value by demonstrating how automation can support smarter city logistics, reduce friction in urban deliveries and contribute to more effective mobility management in connected city environments.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AMS Berufs Infomat - personalized career advice for job seekers
source_description: Job seekers often struggle to navigate complex information on occupations, training pathways, and reskilling opportunities, particularly in a rapidly changing labour market. Austria’s Public Employment Service (AMS) developed Berufs-Infomat to provide accessible, personalised career information to support informed decisions. The use case involves job seekers, students, career advisors, and AMS staff, with the objective of improving access to labour-market information and supporting lifelong learning. The solution is implemented as an interactive digital assistant that responds dynamically to user questions about professions, qualifications, and further education opportunities. It draws on structured labour-market data, occupational profiles, and training catalogues to generate tailored responses aligned with user interests and backgrounds. Integrated into AMS digital services, it complements human counselling rather than replacing it. The impact includes faster access to relevant career information, improved user engagement, and better alignment between individual aspirations and labour-market needs. AMS benefits from more scalable service delivery, while users gain clearer guidance and increased confidence in career planning, supporting employability and workforce adaptability.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Generative AI-Enhanced Knowledge Management in Business (GAIK)
source_description: Many organisations struggle with fragmented information and inefficient knowledge sharing, leading to duplicated work and reduced productivity among knowledge workers. Finnish companies participating in this pilot sought practical solutions to improve access to internal knowledge assets. The objective of the pilot is to reduce information bottlenecks and enhance organisational efficiency. The implementation delivers a modular toolkit that enables organisations to deploy intelligent knowledge services using their own business data. Reusable components, templates and process models support rapid integration into existing systems, enabling functions such as contextual search, summarisation and knowledge reuse. Early results indicate reduced time spent searching for information, improved decision-making and higher employee satisfaction. Qualitative benefits include better onboarding, stronger knowledge retention and improved customer-facing processes. The project demonstrates how flexible, reusable solutions can support scalable knowledge management across different organisational contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: GENAI4ED - A Platform for Assessing and Bridging Generative AI and Human Skills in Secondary Education
source_description: Secondary schools face growing pressure to adopt digital tools that enhance learning while supporting teachers rather than increasing their workload. Educators and policymakers require evidence-based guidance to select appropriate educational technologies. The objective of this pilot is to assess and recommend tools that best complement teaching practices and student needs. The implementation provides a digital evaluation platform that reviews widely used educational software against pedagogical, usability and skills-related criteria. Pilot schools involve both teachers and students in structured evaluations, generating comparative insights. The pilot improves alignment between technology adoption and educational objectives, supporting more informed procurement and classroom use. Qualitative outcomes include improved teacher confidence, better student engagement and enhanced learning experiences. The project contributes practical frameworks for responsible integration of advanced digital tools in education.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Generative-AI based chatbot for the Cypriot Government Portal
source_description: Citizens interacting with public administration often face fragmented information and limited service availability outside office hours. The Cypriot Government sought to improve digital access to public information through its central portal, gov.cy. This use case involves government departments, citizens, and businesses, with the objective of enabling faster, clearer, and more immediate communication with the state on a 24/7 basis. The solution is implemented as a generative digital assistant embedded within the government portal, capable of responding to a wide range of citizen enquiries in natural language. It draws on official government content, structured service information, and continuously updated policy data to provide accurate and consistent answers. The assistant is integrated with the portal’s information architecture and designed to scale as new services are added. The impact includes improved accessibility to government information, reduced pressure on call centres, and higher user satisfaction. Citizens benefit from timely responses and simplified navigation of public services, while the administration gains efficiency and insight into user needs, supporting a more responsive and citizen-centric digital government.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: European AI Factories for businesses
source_description: European businesses and public organisations increasingly require access to advanced computing, data, and expertise to develop and deploy competitive digital solutions, yet such resources are often fragmented or inaccessible. The European AI Factories initiative addresses this gap by creating interconnected innovation hubs across Europe. The use case involves supercomputing centres, universities, SMEs, large industry, financial actors, and public authorities, with the objective of accelerating innovation and adoption across strategic sectors. AI Factories are implemented as ecosystems that combine high-performance computing infrastructure, shared datasets, research expertise, and collaborative environments. They support the development, testing, and scaling of advanced digital models and applications across domains such as health, manufacturing, climate, finance, and space. The network includes national initiatives such as LUMI AIF in Finland, Meluxina-AI in Luxembourg, and IT4LIA in Italy, among others. The impact is increased innovation capacity, reduced barriers to entry for SMEs, and stronger cross-border collaboration. AI Factories enhance Europe’s digital sovereignty, improve competitiveness, and deliver long-term economic and societal value by enabling scalable, trustworthy, and high-impact innovation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
title: Norwegian University of Science and Technology testing the utility and safety of Microsoft's AI assistant in public sector organisations
source_description: Public sector organisations increasingly explore productivity assistants but lack clear guidance on organisational readiness, data protection and responsible deployment. In Norway, public institutions sought evidence-based insights before large-scale adoption. The objective of this pilot is to evaluate the utility, safety and governance implications of deploying Copilot for Microsoft 365. The implementation tests the tool in controlled organisational settings, examining impacts on workflows, information handling and compliance. A structured “readiness toolbox” is developed, providing guidelines, risk assessments and best practices. The pilot delivered practical recommendations, increased organisational awareness and clearer policy guidance. Qualitative benefits include reduced uncertainty, improved governance capacity and a foundation for responsible scaling across the public sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: x-CITE: Expanding the Experience of Citizens through Extended Reality and Metaverse in the City of Tampere
source_description: Cities increasingly seek new ways to engage citizens, improve access to culture, and support participatory urban development while ensuring that digital innovation remains human-centric and inclusive. The City of Tampere aims to enhance how residents and visitors experience urban spaces, cultural venues, and civic participation by blending physical and digital environments. This use case addresses the need to broaden access to culture, improve engagement in urban planning, and create new forms of social participation, involving the city administration, cultural institutions, event organisers, citizens, and visitors, with the objective of developing a shared CitiVerse as a practical tool for smart city innovation. The x-CITE project implements extended reality and metaverse technologies to create immersive experiences connected to real locations, events, and artworks, integrating physical spaces such as public areas and the Nokia Arena with digital layers. XR applications are developed for urban planning, museums, culture, and tourism, supported by city data platforms and tested through pilots such as immersive museum experiences at Vapriikki. The initiative enhances citizen engagement, reaches new audiences, and improves accessibility to cultural and civic spaces. It delivers richer user experiences, supports inclusive participation, and establishes scalable digital capabilities that strengthen Tampere’s position as a pioneer of human-centric smart cities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: TwIN - Urban Digital Twin in the Region of Navarra
source_description: Cities and regions increasingly need collaborative tools to address complex urban challenges while ensuring that innovation delivers tangible benefits to citizens. In the Region of Navarra, public authorities and local companies face fragmentation between policy needs, technological capabilities and skills development. The objective of this pilot is to foster structured collaboration between public administration, industry and the innovation ecosystem through the use of urban digital twin technologies. The implementation is organised around two complementary lines of work. TwIN GovTech operates as an open innovation programme that responds rapidly to concrete challenges defined by Pamplona City Council, enabling companies to test digital twin applications in real urban contexts. TwIN Lab functions as a training and experimentation environment, supporting skills development, prototyping and knowledge transfer across the regional ecosystem. Digital twin components integrate urban data, simulation tools and visualisation environments to support analysis and decision-making. The pilot has strengthened collaboration between public and private actors, accelerated experimentation cycles and increased institutional capacity to adopt advanced digital tools. Qualitative results include improved policy design, greater innovation readiness and a scalable framework for citizen-centred urban transformation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BasqueLLM research project launched the Llama-eus-8B neural model in Basque
source_description: Digital services often underrepresent minority and regional languages, limiting accessibility and cultural inclusion. The BasqueLLM research project addresses this challenge by strengthening digital language support for Basque. This use case involves researchers, public institutions, technology developers, and Basque-speaking communities, with the objective of enabling high-quality language understanding and generation for Basque in digital applications. The solution is implemented through Llama-eus-8B, a foundational neural language model specifically trained on curated Basque-language datasets. With fewer than 10 billion parameters, it balances performance and efficiency, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. The model is designed as a base layer for downstream tools such as chatbots, content generation systems, and public-sector digital services. The impact includes improved linguistic coverage, reduced dependency on non-European language technologies, and enhanced accessibility of digital services for Basque speakers. The project strengthens digital inclusion, supports cultural preservation, and enables innovation in public and private services using the Basque language.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI tool for industries' application of EU regulations on cybersecurity
source_description: Industrial companies face growing regulatory complexity in complying with EU cybersecurity requirements, particularly under new frameworks such as NIS2. Many organisations lack the internal expertise to interpret and apply regulations effectively. ZIUR, the Industrial Cybersecurity Centre of Gipuzkoa, developed a digital assistant to support companies in this process. The use case involves industrial firms, cybersecurity specialists, and regional authorities, with the objective of simplifying regulatory compliance and strengthening cyber resilience. The solution is implemented as an interactive advisory tool that guides users through regulatory requirements, assesses organisational maturity, and provides tailored recommendations based on company profiles. It draws on regulatory texts, best practices, and sector-specific risk scenarios. The impact includes improved understanding of obligations, reduced compliance costs, and more consistent application of cybersecurity measures. Companies benefit from clearer guidance and reduced risk exposure, while the region strengthens its industrial cybersecurity posture and regulatory readiness.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Streamlining Environmental Permitting Processes with Multi-Agent AI in Denmark
source_description: Environmental permitting processes are often complex, slow, and resource-intensive, creating uncertainty for project developers while placing pressure on regulators. Denmark’s Environmental Protection Agency modernised this process to improve efficiency and transparency. This use case involves regulators, developers, and environmental stakeholders, with the objective of accelerating permit decisions while maintaining regulatory integrity. The solution is implemented through a fully digital, centrally managed permitting platform that structures workflows, standardises documentation, and supports caseworkers with analytical tools and access to historical data. Automated checks and intelligent assistance help identify issues early and reduce bottlenecks. Applicants can track application status in real time, improving predictability. The impact includes faster processing times, improved coordination between agencies, and higher consistency in decisions. The system supports renewable energy deployment and climate goals, delivering a scalable, replicable model for modern regulatory administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-driven citizen engagement platform for the City of Prague
source_description: Municipal administrations often struggle to manage large volumes of citizen reports submitted through fragmented communication channels, leading to delays, misrouting and reduced public satisfaction. In Prague, residents and city departments required a more efficient and transparent mechanism for reporting and resolving urban issues. The objective of this pilot is to streamline citizen engagement and improve responsiveness of municipal services. The implementation delivers a digital engagement platform that allows residents to report issues through a single interface, where submissions are automatically categorised and routed to the responsible departments. Natural language processing techniques interpret citizen inputs, while workflow automation integrates with municipal back-office systems. The platform is developed within the CommuniCity initiative in collaboration with the city’s ICT organisation, ensuring alignment with existing governance structures. The pilot has reduced manual handling of reports, shortened response times and improved traceability of issue resolution. Qualitative benefits include increased citizen trust, better inter-departmental coordination and more consistent service delivery. The initiative demonstrates how digital engagement platforms can enhance participation while improving operational efficiency in large cities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Skendy - Multilingual Chatbot supporting Ukrainian refugees in the City of Amsterdam
source_description: Newly arrived refugees often face significant barriers in understanding administrative requirements, particularly when dealing with unfamiliar languages and complex bureaucratic processes. In the City of Amsterdam, Ukrainian refugees required accessible support to manage official communications and documentation. The objective of this pilot is to reduce administrative stress and improve access to essential services for displaced populations. The implementation adapts an existing digital assistant platform to provide multilingual document support, including translation, organisation and reminder functions. The system processes official letters, utility bills and other documents, presenting clear explanations and deadlines in the user’s preferred language. The solution integrates with mobile devices and existing municipal support services, ensuring ease of access. The pilot improved refugees’ ability to comply with administrative obligations, reduced reliance on informal assistance and eased pressure on frontline municipal staff. Qualitative outcomes include increased autonomy for users, improved inclusion and better access to public services. The project illustrates how targeted digital tools can support vulnerable groups while enhancing the effectiveness of city-level integration policies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: nShield - Predictive Maintenance for escalators downtimes in Prague
source_description: Escalator failures in public transport systems cause service disruptions, safety risks, and high maintenance costs. Prague’s public transport operator sought to reduce downtime and improve maintenance efficiency. This use case involves transport operators, maintenance teams, and passengers, with the objective of predicting failures before they occur. The solution is implemented through acoustic sensors installed on escalators, continuously collecting sound data. These signals are analysed in real time using mathematical models that detect anomalies and deviations from normal behaviour. The system identifies likely component failures and provides maintenance recommendations to operators. Integrated into maintenance workflows, it enables condition-based interventions rather than reactive repairs. The impact includes reduced downtime, lower maintenance costs, improved passenger experience, and increased asset lifespan. The system enhances operational reliability and supports smarter management of critical transport infrastructure.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Bundesdruckerei Group – Federal AI Competence Center
title: ADLER: Local Language Models for Sensitive Data
source_description: Public sector organisations frequently process confidential documents that cannot be transferred to external systems without risking data breaches or loss of sovereignty. Administrative staff require advanced text-processing capabilities while maintaining strict control over sensitive information. The objective of this pilot is to demonstrate that language models can be executed securely on local devices without network dependency. The implementation explores on-device deployment of compact language models on commercially available, resilient hardware. Documents are processed directly on the user’s workstation, enabling functions such as classification, extraction and summarisation without external data transmission. The approach is designed to comply with strict security classifications, including confidential government information. The pilot strengthens data sovereignty, reduces exposure to cyber risks and opens new usage contexts for secure document handling. Qualitative benefits include increased trust, broader applicability of advanced text processing in sensitive environments and reduced dependency on external infrastructure. The project provides a foundation for responsible deployment of advanced digital tools in security-critical administrative contexts.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Bundesdruckerei Group – Federal AI Competence Center
title: MÖVE: Benchmarking of Language Models for Public Administration
source_description: Public administrations face growing pressure to adopt language technologies while ensuring reliability, fairness and regulatory compliance. Decision-makers often lack objective criteria to compare available models for administrative use. The objective of this pilot is to establish a robust evaluation framework tailored to public sector needs. The implementation defines standardised benchmarks assessing model performance on administrative tasks in German, alongside governance criteria such as social fairness, hallucination rates and alignment with the EU AI Act. The framework supports transparent comparison of different models and deployment scenarios. The pilot provides evidence-based guidance for procurement and policy decisions. Qualitative impacts include improved risk awareness, stronger governance and increased confidence in technology adoption. The framework supports scalable, responsible use of language technologies across public administrations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Bundesdruckerei Group – Federal AI Competence Center
title: AI Language Assistant for the German Federal Administration: Efficient Information Processing
source_description: Administrative decision-making often depends on analysing large volumes of unstructured documents, which places significant strain on staff resources. Federal authorities require tools to extract relevant information efficiently while maintaining accountability. The objective of this pilot is to improve information processing and support evidence-based decisions. The implementation deploys a language-based assistant capable of summarising documents, identifying key topics and mapping responsibilities. The system integrates with existing document management systems and supports staff workflows. The pilot reduced processing time, improved consistency and enhanced transparency. Qualitative benefits include increased productivity, improved staff satisfaction and better-informed decisions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Bundesdruckerei Group – Federal AI Competence Center
title: PLAIN: a data analysis platform for the entire German federal administration
source_description: Effective public policy increasingly depends on the ability to analyse large and heterogeneous datasets across institutional boundaries. Federal ministries often lack a shared infrastructure to support advanced data analysis securely. The objective of this pilot is to establish a standard, cross-departmental data platform. The implementation delivers a secure infrastructure enabling storage, processing and analysis of diverse datasets without thematic restrictions. The platform supports advanced analytical applications and future data-driven projects. The pilot improved analytical capacity, reduced duplication and strengthened inter-ministerial collaboration. Qualitative outcomes include improved policy insight, scalability and strategic alignment with national digital strategies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: SOCIB - Balearic Islands Coastal Observing and Forecasting System
title: SOCIB 2030: Digital Twin of the Western Mediterranean
source_description: Understanding complex marine systems is essential for addressing climate change, biodiversity loss and coastal risks. Researchers and policymakers require integrated tools that combine data, modelling and visualisation. The objective of this pilot is to develop modular digital twin prototypes tailored to specific marine challenges in the Western Mediterranean. The implementation delivers three specialised prototypes focusing on marine protected areas, climate adaptation and early warning for extreme events. These integrate observational data, forecasting models and visual analytics. The pilot enhances scientific understanding, supports decision-making and fosters international collaboration. Qualitative impacts include improved preparedness, better environmental governance and scalable contributions to global ocean initiatives.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: VELVET - Italian AI Open Source model
source_description: European administrations and organisations require language technologies that reflect linguistic diversity, regulatory requirements and sustainability goals. The objective of this pilot is to develop an open-source model prioritising Italian language and content while supporting multilingual use. The implementation trains a multimodal model on high-performance computing infrastructure, optimised for efficiency and regulatory compliance. The pilot strengthens European technological autonomy, improves language coverage and supports diverse public and private applications. Qualitative benefits include transparency, energy efficiency and alignment with European values.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Smart Street Lighting
source_description: Urban lighting represents a major source of energy consumption and maintenance costs for municipalities. Hafnarfjörður sought to modernise its lighting infrastructure to improve efficiency and safety. The objective of this pilot is to enable adaptive, data-driven lighting management. The implementation deploys networked controllers connected via low-power communication, allowing real-time control and monitoring of 6,000 streetlights. Lighting levels adapt to conditions and schedules, and maintenance is optimised through monitoring data. The pilot achieved a 35% reduction in energy consumption and a 42% decrease in maintenance costs, while improving public safety. Qualitative impacts include reduced emissions, operational savings and a scalable foundation for broader smart city services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Preserving History with Smart Technology: IoT Monitoring at the Colosseum
source_description: Protecting world heritage sites requires continuous monitoring while avoiding invasive interventions that could compromise historical integrity. At the Colosseum in Rome, heritage authorities and conservation experts needed a reliable method to detect structural changes and environmental stress without physical alteration of the monument. The objective of this pilot is to support proactive preservation through non-invasive, real-time monitoring. The implementation deploys discreet LoRaWAN®-enabled sensors that collect structural and environmental data and transmit it continuously to a central network server. The system enables real-time detection of anomalies and supports the validation of satellite-based observations, integrating multiple data sources into a coherent monitoring framework. The pilot improved the ability to identify early warning signs of structural stress, reduced reliance on periodic manual inspections and enhanced situational awareness for conservation teams. Qualitative impacts include improved safeguarding of cultural heritage, more informed maintenance planning and a scalable approach for monitoring other sensitive historical sites while preserving their authenticity.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Water Network Monitoring
source_description: Ensuring reliable water supply and minimising losses is particularly challenging in areas with limited infrastructure and remote pumping stations. In Tápióság, Hungary, water utilities required better visibility of network performance without continuous on-site supervision. The objective of this pilot is to improve operational efficiency and sustainability of water distribution systems. The implementation installs autonomous monitoring devices at pumping stations to measure parameters such as pressure, energy consumption, pump operation time and water flow. Data is transmitted via low-power wide-area networks to a central management system, enabling real-time monitoring and alerts. The solution operates continuously without human intervention, even in hard-to-reach locations.
