The pilot enabled faster detection of faults, improved optimisation of pumping operations and reduced water losses. Qualitative benefits include lower operational costs, improved service reliability and stronger support for sustainable water management practices, demonstrating the value of remote monitoring for utilities with constrained resources.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Data-driven Wildfire Prevention System for Forest
source_description: Forest authorities face increasing risks from wildfires due to climate change, requiring early detection and accurate risk assessment over large areas. In Salzburg, managing forest safety demanded real-time environmental insights to support preventive action. The objective of this pilot is to enhance wildfire preparedness through continuous risk monitoring. The implementation deploys a dense network of environmental sensors across 350 square kilometres, collecting data on weather conditions and soil moisture. These inputs are processed to calculate the Fire Weather Index, providing real-time assessments of fire risk. Information is made available to authorities to guide prevention measures and resource allocation. The pilot improved situational awareness, enabled faster preventive responses and supported more informed decision-making. Qualitative impacts include increased forest resilience, improved safety for communities and a scalable framework for wildfire risk management in other regions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space (BMFTR)
title: German Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space provides a popular chatbot to make project funding regulations more accessible
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Research funding regulations are complex and difficult for applicants to interpret, often leading to incomplete applications and high enquiry volumes. The German Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space introduced a digital assistant to improve accessibility of funding information. This use case involves researchers, institutions, and ministry staff, with the objective of simplifying access to funding rules and guidance. The solution is implemented as a conversational assistant built on an enterprise-grade platform that retrieves answers from official funding documents and guidance materials. It supports natural language queries and provides clear, context-specific responses. Integrated into ministry websites, it complements existing support channels. The impact includes reduced administrative burden, faster access to information for applicants, and improved quality of submissions. The ministry benefits from efficiency gains and better stakeholder engagement, while applicants gain clarity and confidence in navigating funding opportunities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: City of Naples, Catania, and Perugia
title: Urban EVOLUTION (Earth obserVatiOn and nature-based soLUTions agaInst urban pollution)
source_description: Urban EVOLUTION addresses a pressing urban-management challenge: how to reduce air pollution and urban heat-island effects in dense city environments while planning interventions that are practical, evidence-based and replicable. Piloted over 12 months in Naples, Catania and Perugia, the initiative brings together municipalities, research partners and technical specialists to test how Nature-Based Solutions can respond to different climatic and urban conditions. The operational objective is to help cities understand where green infrastructure can deliver the greatest value in lowering emissions, reducing particulate matter and improving thermal comfort, while supporting longer-term planning aligned with climate targets. The solution is implemented through a combination of geospatial analysis, remote sensing and analytical models developed with technological partner Latitudo 40 and supported by WiseTown, TeamDev’s R&D division, and the Universities of Perugia and Palermo. At a conceptual level, Earth-observation data and urban-environment indicators are processed to assess pollution levels, map spatial patterns and estimate the impact of green spaces on CO₂ reduction, particulate capture and temperature mitigation. These outputs provide a decision-support layer for Nature-Based Solution planning across diverse city contexts. The expected impact is improved urban-planning precision, stronger evidence for climate adaptation measures and a scalable model for greener cities. More broadly, the project supports Paris Agreement goals, with the broader ambition of cutting emissions by 50% by 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2050, while showing that urban green spaces could offset up to 40% of city emissions and materially improve air quality.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MEDI:CUS – A Multi-Cloud-Based Platform Architecture for a Connected and Intersectoral Healthcare System
source_description: Baden-Württemberg launched MEDI:CUS in 2022 to tackle a structural weakness in Germany’s decentralised healthcare IT environment: fragmented systems, limited interoperability and inefficient data exchange across institutions and care sectors. This fragmentation makes it harder for hospitals and other healthcare actors to share information securely, scale digital services and innovate consistently across the system. Backed by five state ministries and a broad coalition that includes all university hospitals and the Baden-Württemberg Hospital Association, the initiative aims to establish by 2026 a connected digital foundation that supports more efficient, trusted and interoperable healthcare operations. The solution is being implemented through MEDI:core, a multi-cloud platform architecture designed to function like an app-store model for healthcare. At a conceptual level, the platform combines Infrastructure-as-a-Service and Software-as-a-Service components delivered through standardised interfaces and protocols, enabling interoperability at technical, semantic, organisational and legal levels. The architecture supports secure health-data exchange, cloud-based services and modular digital applications that can be adopted across institutions without each organisation building separate infrastructure from scratch. Early pilot testing has already demonstrated secure hospital connectivity and the deployment of initial services such as cloud storage and Nextcloud. The expected impact is a more scalable and reliable digital-health ecosystem, lower duplication of effort and faster service rollout across participating institutions. By the end of 2026, the project aims to connect 15 to 20 hospitals, provide usable digital solutions and establish a self-sustaining target organisation, creating both a reference model for health-system transformation and a broader blueprint for trusted public-sector platforms.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: PublicTwin for citizen engagement in Malmo for the renovation of the Nyhamnen harbor
source_description: Major urban-regeneration schemes often struggle to involve residents in a way that is timely, understandable and genuinely influential, which can weaken transparency, reduce public acceptance and leave planners without a clear view of community priorities. In Malmö’s Nyhamnen harbour redevelopment, the city sought to address this participation gap by creating a more open and engaging planning process in which citizens could explore proposals and contribute meaningfully to decisions shaping the area’s future. The stakeholders include municipal planners, local residents and other community actors, with the objective of improving dialogue, increasing transparency and ensuring that redevelopment choices are better aligned with public needs and expectations. The solution is implemented through PublicTwin, a digital twin platform that visualises proposed developments and enables interactive exploration of planning data. At a conceptual level, the system combines 3D urban representation, accessible user interfaces and feedback tools that allow residents to review proposed interventions, understand spatial implications and submit suggestions in real time. Public input can then be integrated into planning workflows as part of a more continuous and structured engagement process. The pilot’s impact has been qualitative but significant: it improved transparency, increased citizen participation and strengthened communication between planners and residents. More broadly, the initiative fostered greater trust, supported more inclusive decision-making and demonstrated the business and governance value of digital twins as scalable tools for participatory urban planning and more responsive city development.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-Tour guide in the City of Tampere
source_description: As visitor expectations shift towards immediate, personalised and multilingual support, cities face growing pressure to offer tourism services that are both more engaging and more adaptive than static signage or traditional information points. In Tampere, tourism stakeholders wanted to enrich the visitor journey while also creating stronger links between tourists, attractions and local businesses. The pilot therefore focused on improving how people experience the city in real time, with the objective of delivering accessible, immersive guidance that helps visitors discover services, museums and points of interest more easily and enjoyably. The stakeholders include tourists, tourism authorities, museums and local businesses, all of whom benefit from a more dynamic visitor-information system. The solution is implemented through smart glasses equipped with a virtual assistant that delivers location-based information as visitors move through the city. At a conceptual level, the system combines wearable interfaces, contextual content delivery and continuously updated destination information supplied by tourism organisations and local businesses. This enables visitors to receive relevant guidance in situ rather than searching separately for information, while also allowing business and cultural content to remain current. The pilot improved visitor satisfaction and increased engagement with local services, while also opening new promotional opportunities for participating businesses. More broadly, the use case enhanced accessibility, supported a more interactive tourism experience and demonstrated a scalable smart-tourism model capable of combining user convenience, local economic value and richer destination storytelling.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Bike sharing availability optimisation in the City of Kuopio
source_description: Keeping shared bicycles available where and when users need them is a persistent operational challenge for cities, particularly when demand fluctuates sharply by area and time of day. In Kuopio, the electric bike-sharing scheme regularly faced shortages in high-demand zones and surpluses elsewhere, undermining reliability and limiting its effectiveness as a sustainable mobility option. The pilot was designed to address this imbalance by helping the city and service operators manage fleet distribution more intelligently. The stakeholders include mobility operators, logistics teams, municipal transport planners and users of the bike-sharing system, with the objective of improving service reliability, increasing user satisfaction and encouraging wider uptake of cycling as part of the urban transport mix. The solution is implemented through analysis of historical usage data to identify recurring demand patterns by location and time, followed by predictive forecasting of likely shortages. At a conceptual level, these forecasts feed into an operational system that sends real-time redistribution instructions to logistics operators via SMS or digital channels, guiding targeted rebalancing actions. A feedback loop records completed interventions and reported outcomes, allowing the predictive models to be refined continuously. The pilot resulted in more consistent bike availability, fewer service disruptions and better operational efficiency. More broadly, it improved the user experience, strengthened the attractiveness of sustainable transport and demonstrated a scalable, data-driven approach to managing shared mobility assets more effectively across a city.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Regional AI Hubs/Centres for Health and Tourism
source_description: Several Italian regions are facing similar operational pressures in two high-impact service areas: healthcare and tourism. In healthcare, long waiting lists, uneven demand and constrained resources make it difficult to plan appointments and allocate capacity fairly and efficiently. In tourism, fluctuating visitor numbers, seasonal concentration and rising expectations for personalised services place strain on destinations and reduce the quality of the visitor experience. This pilot was created to address those shared challenges through regionally coordinated innovation hubs that bring together public administrations, service providers and technology partners. Its objective is to test common approaches that improve planning, service efficiency and user experience across both domains, while building a framework that can be replicated across regions. The solution is implemented through analytical tools for healthcare demand forecasting, adaptive resource allocation, appointment scheduling and booking support, combined with tourism-flow management tools designed to personalise visitor experiences and distribute demand more evenly across destinations and seasons. At a conceptual level, the system uses predictive analysis, optimisation techniques and shared governance mechanisms, while embedding ethical and regulatory safeguards into implementation. Early results show improved planning accuracy, reduced bottlenecks in access to care and stronger coordination in tourism services. More broadly, the pilot supports greater service equity, better quality of care and visitor experience, and a resilient, citizen-centred model for cross-regional public-sector innovation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Regional AI Hub/Centres for Environmental Data and Sustainable Mobility
source_description: Environmental protection and mobility planning increasingly require coordinated action across administrative boundaries, yet data fragmentation often limits policy effectiveness. Lombardy and Veneto regions sought to improve environmental and transport governance through shared analytical capabilities. The objective of this pilot is to create a “smart land” by enabling transregional analysis of environmental and mobility data. The implementation establishes a federated data architecture that allows regions to retain control over their datasets while enabling advanced analytical models to operate across jurisdictions. These models support evidence-based policymaking in areas such as emissions reduction, traffic management and sustainable transport planning. The pilot enhances interoperability between regional systems and supports scalable innovation. Qualitative impacts include improved policy insight, stronger coordination between regions and more effective sustainability strategies. The initiative demonstrates how federated data approaches can support advanced analytics while respecting governance and data sovereignty requirements.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Regional AI Hubs/Centres for the PA
source_description: Public administrations face increasing complexity in policy design and technical-administrative procedures, placing pressure on staff capacity and decision quality. Several Italian regions recognised the need for shared innovation to support administrative effectiveness. The objective of this pilot is to enhance the quality, consistency and efficiency of public sector work by supporting human decision-making. The implementation introduces analytical and decision-support tools tailored to public policy analysis and administrative processes, integrated into existing workflows. Regional hubs provide shared infrastructure, governance and expertise, enabling experimentation and responsible adoption. The pilot improved process efficiency, supported more informed decisions and reduced administrative burdens. Qualitative benefits include improved working conditions for public servants, stronger institutional capacity and better service outcomes for citizens, offering a scalable model for digital transformation in public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Regional AI Hubs/Centres for Resilience and Security of the Territory with 5G pilot action
source_description: Preventing environmental risks and ensuring the safety of infrastructure and communities requires timely data, advanced analysis and reliable connectivity. Tuscany and partner regions sought to strengthen territorial resilience and emergency preparedness. The objective of this pilot is to improve risk monitoring, intervention planning and emergency management across regions. The implementation combines advanced analytical models with 5G-enabled connectivity to support real-time data collection from sensors, infrastructure and construction sites. Analytical tools support risk assessment, scenario planning and coordination among authorities. The pilot enhances situational awareness, speeds up response planning and improves cross-agency collaboration. Qualitative impacts include increased safety, stronger resilience of critical infrastructure and improved spatial planning capabilities, demonstrating the value of combining advanced analytics and next-generation connectivity for territorial governance.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: "Roma 5G"" - extension of the 5G connection across Rome"
source_description: Rome faces the challenge of supporting digital services, public safety, and connectivity across a large, historic, and densely used urban environment. Roma 5G addresses this by upgrading citywide digital infrastructure. This use case involves the City of Rome, infrastructure providers, transport authorities, and citizens, with the objective of enabling a fast, secure, and sustainable smart city. The solution is implemented through the deployment of advanced 5G infrastructure, including small cells, fibre networks, public Wi-Fi, IoT sensors, and surveillance cameras. Coverage is extended across the entire metro system and key public spaces. A central Security Operations Centre coordinates data flows and supports crowd management, particularly for major events such as the 2025 Jubilee. The impact includes improved connectivity, enhanced public safety, better urban monitoring, and support for future digital services. Roma 5G positions Rome as a leading European smart city, delivering long-term social, economic, and environmental value.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Project Griffin - Drones to transport medical supplies in emergency situations
source_description: Rapid transport of medical samples and supplies is critical in emergency healthcare, yet traditional logistics can be slow or constrained by infrastructure. In Luxembourg, emergency services seek innovative solutions to reduce response times. The objective of Project Griffin is to explore the use of drones for transporting medical supplies in urgent situations. The implementation involves testing drone-based delivery routes, operational procedures and coordination with healthcare providers. Future development plans include integrating advanced automation for route planning, obstacle avoidance and fleet coordination. Expected impacts include faster sample transport, improved emergency response and reduced dependency on road transport. Qualitative outcomes include increased system resilience, innovation in healthcare logistics and a scalable foundation for future autonomous delivery networks.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: UNIC – Blockchain- and Metaverse-Based University Course
source_description: Universities are increasingly challenged to provide innovative, globally accessible education while ensuring the authenticity and portability of academic credentials. The University of Nicosia (UNIC) addressed this by redesigning how a course is delivered, accessed, and certified. The initiative involves the university, students worldwide, academic staff, and external experts from the digital economy, with the objective of experimenting with new models of online learning, certification, and learner engagement. The course “Introduction to NFTs and the Metaverse” is delivered entirely through decentralised digital environments, removing reliance on traditional learning management systems. Registration is enabled through the minting of a free course token, which grants access to learning materials and activities hosted in virtual spaces. Course participation, progress, and completion are recorded through blockchain-based mechanisms, and learners can optionally obtain a completion certificate issued as a non-fungible token on Ethereum. The impact has been significant, with more than 14,000 registrants, demonstrating global reach and strong engagement. The model enhances transparency, verifiability, and learner ownership of credentials, while reducing administrative overhead. It provides UNIC with a scalable, future-oriented education model and offers learners a portable, tamper-proof record of achievement aligned with emerging digital economies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU)
title: MareNostrum-Ona, Europe's first quantum annealer
source_description: Europe faces increasing demand for advanced computing capabilities to address complex optimisation problems that are difficult to solve using conventional supercomputing alone, particularly in areas such as logistics, materials science and advanced analytics. The objective of MareNostrum-Ona is to strengthen European technological sovereignty by providing researchers, industry and public sector organisations with access to novel quantum computing resources. The implementation involves the development of an analogue quantum annealer hosted at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center and integrated into the MareNostrum 5 infrastructure. The initial system will operate with at least ten physical qubits and will be progressively expanded in subsequent generations. It is designed to complement classical high-performance computing by addressing optimisation tasks through quantum annealing techniques. The project is co-funded by European and national partners and developed in collaboration with leading research institutions. Expected impacts include expanded research capabilities, early industrial experimentation with quantum optimisation and accelerated knowledge transfer within Europe. Qualitative outcomes include improved readiness for quantum adoption, strengthened collaboration between academia and industry, and a scalable foundation for future quantum–HPC hybrid systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: DeepHealth - Deep-Learning and HPC to Boost Biomedical Applications for Health
source_description: Biomedical research and healthcare increasingly depend on the ability to analyse large, complex datasets to support diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment, yet existing computing infrastructures often limit performance and scalability. Researchers and clinicians require integrated environments that can efficiently process imaging, genomic, and clinical data across diverse applications. This use case addresses these needs by supporting advanced biomedical applications through a unified computational framework, involving research institutions, healthcare providers, and technology partners, with the objective of accelerating innovation in diagnosis and treatment. The DeepHealth project implements a framework that combines high-performance computing infrastructures with deep learning and computer vision techniques, optimised to run on heterogeneous HPC and big data architectures. It supports data-intensive workflows and enables large-scale training and inference across multiple biomedical domains, piloted through 15 real-world applications. The project improves processing speed, scalability, and analytical accuracy, enabling more efficient analysis of complex biomedical data. It reduces time to insight, supports more precise clinical decision-making, and demonstrates how advanced computing infrastructures can be effectively leveraged to deliver tangible benefits in health research and clinical practice.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: PILOTING - PILOTs for robotic INspection and maintenance Grounded on advanced intelligent platforms and prototype applications
source_description: Ageing infrastructure such as bridges, tunnels and oil and gas facilities requires frequent inspection and maintenance, yet these activities are costly, labour-intensive and often expose workers to hazardous environments. PILOTING was created to address this operational challenge by improving how critical assets are inspected and maintained across Europe. The stakeholders included infrastructure owners, industrial operators, maintenance teams and standardisation actors, with the objective of increasing inspection quality, reducing operating costs and enhancing worker safety in sectors where asset failure can have major economic and public consequences. The solution was implemented through an integrated robotic platform combining aerial drones, ground robots, crawlers and advanced analytics within a common inspection and maintenance framework. At a conceptual level, the system brought together data capture, autonomous or semi-autonomous navigation and defect-analysis capabilities so that robots could operate in complex environments and support the detection of structural or operational issues. These technologies were validated in three large-scale pilots spanning civil infrastructure and oil and gas settings. The expected impact was safer inspections, improved consistency in asset assessment and lower reliance on risky manual intervention. More broadly, PILOTING strengthened the case for robotics in industrial inspection and maintenance, supported the development of standards in the field and created value through more efficient, scalable and safer infrastructure management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: FABULOS (Future Automated Bus Urban Level Operation Systems)
source_description: Many cities are interested in automated last-mile public transport, yet practical deployment depends on more than vehicle technology alone: it also requires integration with existing networks, regulatory clarity, financial viability and public acceptance. FABULOS addressed this challenge by helping cities test whether autonomous minibuses could become a realistic extension of urban transport systems rather than a stand-alone novelty. The stakeholders included municipalities, public-transport planners, technology suppliers and potential passengers, with the objective of exploring how self-driving shuttle services could improve first- and last-mile connectivity while fitting within real urban operating conditions. The solution was implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement process that engaged several consortia to design, prototype and pilot automated shuttle services in six European cities, including Helsinki, Gjesdal, Tallinn, Lamia and Helmond, as well as a site in Portugal. At a conceptual level, the project combined vehicle automation, service design, route integration and operational testing in live urban contexts to assess the technical, economic and societal feasibility of the model. This enabled cities to compare approaches and identify the conditions needed for broader adoption. The expected impact was improved understanding of autonomous public transport in practice, evidence on user acceptance and stronger readiness for future deployment decisions. More broadly, FABULOS created value by reducing uncertainty around automated mobility and supporting cities in planning more connected and innovative transport systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-EFFECT, Advancing AI Integration in the European Energy Sector - Multi energy and sector coupling
source_description: Energy systems are becoming increasingly complex as electricity, heating, and other energy vectors must be coordinated to reduce emissions while maintaining reliability and affordability. In regions such as Jutland and Bornholm, energy operators face challenges in optimising district heating and power grid operations simultaneously. This use case addresses the need for better coordination between energy systems, involving grid operators, heating network operators, and energy stakeholders, with the objective of improving efficiency and moving towards near-zero-emission energy supply. The initiative implements advanced analytical and forecasting tools to optimise sector coupling between electricity grids and district heating networks. These tools support demand forecasting, plant operation optimisation, and coordinated control across multiple energy vectors, validated through targeted demonstrations. The approach enables more efficient use of renewable energy, lowers operational costs, and reduces CO₂ emissions. It strengthens system flexibility, improves reliability of district heating operations, and provides a validated pathway for deploying advanced optimisation tools across multi-energy systems in Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-EFFECT, Advancing AI Integration in the European Energy Sector - Transmission Congestion Management Laboratory
source_description: Electricity transmission networks face growing congestion due to renewable integration, electrification, and increased demand, placing pressure on control rooms to manage grid stability in real time. Grid operators require safe environments to test and validate new operational approaches without risking live systems. This use case addresses these challenges by supporting the development and validation of congestion management solutions, involving transmission system operators, researchers, and control room specialists, with the objective of improving grid resilience and operational effectiveness. The Transmission Congestion Management Laboratory extends TU Delft’s Control Room of the Future with capabilities for synthetic grid data generation and algorithm testing. A digital-physical test environment enables rigorous verification of congestion management strategies, including sequential topological reconfigurations, under controlled conditions. The facility improves the robustness and reliability of congestion management solutions, reduces operational risk, and accelerates innovation by allowing experimentation before real-world deployment. It delivers clear value by strengthening grid security, supporting operator confidence, and enabling scalable validation of next-generation grid control tools.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: INESC TEC - Institute for Systems and Computer Engineering, Technology and Science
title: AI-EFFECT, Advancing AI Integration in the European Energy Sector - Energy efficiency, management and sharing for local energy communities
source_description: Local energy communities are playing a growing role in the energy transition, yet effective energy sharing and optimisation are hindered by fragmented data access, privacy concerns, and limited consumer engagement. Traditional data platforms led by system operators are not fully designed for collaborative, user-centric energy services. This use case addresses these barriers by enabling secure, trusted data sharing for local energy communities, involving consumers, grid operators, service providers, and technology developers, with the objective of improving energy efficiency and supporting new community-based services. The initiative implements an Energy Data Space that provides a common framework for sharing energy data with explicit consent, supported by governance, security, and certification mechanisms. This environment enables the development and testing of data-driven services for energy management, e-mobility, and smart appliances, while respecting privacy and data sovereignty. The approach increases consumer trust and participation, supports more flexible grid management, and fosters cross-sector innovation. It delivers improved energy efficiency, better use of local renewable resources, and scalable foundations for community-driven energy systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: AI-EFFECT, Advancing AI Integration in the European Energy Sector - Distribution Network Congestion Management for Renewable Integration
source_description: Electricity distribution networks are under increasing strain as renewable generation, electrification, and decentralised energy resources grow, leading to congestion and operational complexity at local grid level. Distribution system operators need more accurate, scalable, and real-time tools to manage congestion while maintaining high standards of safety, reliability, and security. This use case addresses these challenges by supporting the integration of advanced decision-support tools into distribution network operations, involving grid operators, engineers, and technology providers, with the objective of enabling efficient renewable integration and improved congestion management as part of business-as-usual operations. The solution is implemented through a flexible and reconfigurable laboratory environment that emulates real cyber-physical distribution systems, allowing advanced analytical and learning-based models to be developed, tested, and validated before deployment. The setup integrates simulators, synthetic data generation, and distribution system IT and OT components to assess performance, robustness, scalability, and real-time behaviour under realistic scenarios. This approach reduces operational risk, supports seamless integration with classical engineering methods, and accelerates innovation. It delivers improved grid efficiency, higher hosting capacity for renewables, stronger decision-making capabilities, and a validated framework for safely scaling advanced congestion management solutions across European distribution networks.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: ChatAmsterdam - AI assistant for civil servants
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Municipal employees increasingly work with large volumes of text, policy documents and complex information, which places pressure on time, consistency and quality of administrative work. At the same time, public organisations must ensure that sensitive information is handled securely and in line with public values. In the City of Amsterdam, civil servants required a trusted internal tool to support everyday tasks without relying on external commercial services that process data outside municipal control. The objective of this pilot is to improve productivity and information handling for municipal staff while maintaining full data sovereignty and compliance with public sector standards. The implementation delivers an internal digital assistant deployed within the municipality’s secure infrastructure. The system supports tasks such as drafting texts, summarising documents and analysing complex material, while ensuring that all inputs and outputs remain within the city’s digital environment and are not reused externally. The assistant was developed in alignment with the city’s Agenda Digitale Stad and integrated into existing work processes. During the six-month pilot, more than 800 civil servants used the tool for over 34,000 assignments. Results indicate time savings, improved consistency in document handling and high user acceptance. Qualitative impacts include increased trust in digital tools, enhanced staff efficiency and a reusable model that can be shared with other public administrations to support a resilient, human-centred digital public sector.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: LOQUI - participation by speech
source_description: Digital public services increasingly rely on text-based interfaces, which creates significant barriers for people with language deficits, low literacy levels, visual impairments or limited digital skills, including new Dutch citizens and status holders. These barriers reduce access to essential services and limit participation in digital society. The objective of this pilot is to enable inclusive access to digital government services through speech-based interaction. The implementation develops a multilingual speech control tool supporting Dutch, English and Arabic, allowing users to navigate and complete digital services using voice commands. The system recognises speech input, identifies language difficulties in real time and adapts interactions accordingly, enabling more intuitive and accessible service use. Integration with existing digital government platforms allows speech to act as a universal interface layer rather than a separate service. The pilot demonstrated improved accessibility for vulnerable user groups, reduced dependency on intermediaries and greater autonomy in interacting with public services. Qualitative impacts include enhanced digital inclusion, improved user confidence and a scalable approach for making digital public services accessible to diverse populations.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: VITE-A2 Video and Text AI Analysis for Political Debates
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Municipal council meetings are essential democratic forums, yet their length and complexity often discourage citizen engagement and limit transparency. In the Netherlands, local governments sought ways to make political debates more accessible to the public. The objective of this pilot is to improve understanding of municipal decision-making by transforming complex discussions into clear and engaging summaries. The implementation analyses video and textual recordings of council meetings, extracting key topics, arguments and emotional cues through multimodal analysis techniques. Outputs are presented in simplified formats that highlight relevant discussion points and sentiments, supporting easier interpretation by citizens. The pilot produced a paper prototype and feasibility studies informed by stakeholder feedback. Qualitative results include improved accessibility of political information, increased civic awareness and stronger potential for citizen engagement. The project demonstrates how advanced analysis of public meetings can support transparency and democratic participation at local level.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Accelerat.AI - Accelerating digital transformation in Portugal
source_description: Public administrations and businesses in Portugal face rising demand for efficient, accessible customer service across multiple channels, while language diversity, regional accents, and ageing populations limit the effectiveness of generic digital solutions. Accelerat.AI addresses this challenge by modernising customer service delivery in both public and private sectors, involving government bodies, enterprises, technology providers, and citizens, with the objective of significantly increasing automation while improving user experience in European Portuguese. The initiative is implemented through the development of advanced conversational agents and Contact Center as a Service platforms tailored to linguistic and demographic variation, trained on large-scale, high-quality language and speech datasets. These systems are integrated into existing customer service infrastructures to support voice and text interactions, automated case handling, and escalation to human agents when required. Funded with €35 million under Portugal’s Recovery and Resilience Plan and Next Generation EU, the project targets automation of up to 80% of customer interactions. The initiative delivers substantial efficiency gains, reduces operational costs, improves service accessibility, and strengthens digital sovereignty by developing language technologies aligned with European values and local needs.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: AtlanTTic research centre of the University of Vigo
title: FalAI - A Dataset for End-to-end Spoken Language Understanding in a Low-Resource Scenario
source_description: Many European languages remain underrepresented in voice-based digital services, limiting access to technology for speakers of minority languages. In Galicia, the lack of large, high-quality datasets constrained the development of conversational systems in Galician and Spanish. The objective of this pilot is to promote linguistic diversity and digital inclusion by creating open datasets for spoken language understanding. The implementation mobilised large-scale citizen participation through the #A30frases campaign, collecting voice recordings of prototype sentences across public sector domains such as healthcare and social care. The resulting dataset exceeds 260,000 recordings from around 12,000 contributors and is openly available for research and development. The pilot significantly improved the availability of training data for low-resource languages, supporting the development of inclusive voice technologies. Qualitative impacts include strengthened linguistic equality, increased research capacity and long-term benefits for public service accessibility across Europe.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
title: Virtual assistant for services - first step towards artificial intelligence in diplomacy
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Citizens and businesses interacting with diplomatic and consular services often face complex procedures and time-zone constraints, leading to delays and information gaps. The Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs sought to improve service accessibility and consistency across its global network. The objective of this pilot is to provide continuous, multilingual guidance for consular and administrative services. The implementation introduces a virtual assistant available on ministry, embassy and consulate websites, supporting six languages and operating around the clock. The assistant guides users through structured decision trees based on frequently asked questions and common procedures, optimised during development through analysis of historical enquiries. Initially deployed across 20 pilot locations, the system integrates with existing digital service channels. The pilot improved response availability, reduced pressure on frontline staff and enhanced user satisfaction. Qualitative benefits include more consistent service delivery, improved accessibility for international users and a foundation for future digital transformation in diplomatic services.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: OLI Chatbot across spanish airports
source_description: Airports manage complex passenger flows and high volumes of enquiries related to flights, terminals, and services, particularly during peak travel periods.
