title: Fasit Dialogstøtte – AI Assistant for Conversation Notes
source_description: Caseworkers in employment and social-service settings must listen carefully to citizens while also documenting conversations accurately for case files. This creates a practical tension: manual note-taking can reduce presence in the conversation, while incomplete documentation can weaken case quality and increase the risk of mistakes. Fasit Dialogstøtte addresses this problem by integrating an AI assistant into the Schultz Fasit case-management environment. The operational objective is to support caseworkers by automatically transcribing conversations with citizens and generating draft summaries, minutes or journal notes. At a conceptual level, the assistant acts as a documentation support tool rather than a case-decision system. It captures the spoken conversation, converts it to text and prepares a draft that the caseworker can review, correct and approve before it becomes part of the case record. This allows the professional to remain responsible for the final documentation while reducing the repetitive burden of manual note-taking. The expected impact is more focused citizen dialogue, more consistent records, reduced administrative workload and stronger documentation quality. The system may also support accuracy because key points from the conversation can be captured systematically rather than reconstructed from memory after the meeting. The case is relevant because it shows how AI can support front-line welfare administration in a relatively bounded way: it improves the production of case documentation while leaving professional judgement, case assessment and legal responsibility with the human caseworker.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Pluto – Road Analysis and Maintenance
source_description: Municipal road maintenance requires up-to-date information on potholes, surface wear, cracking and other defects, but manual inspections can be slow, expensive and unevenly prioritised. Pluto Technologies’ solution addresses this problem by using AI, smartphones and GPS to monitor road conditions and support more targeted maintenance planning. In Hvidovre Municipality, the tool is used through devices installed on municipal vehicles, such as refuse trucks, which already travel regularly across the road network. The operational problem is that municipalities often lack a continuous, objective and scalable picture of road condition. By collecting data from vehicles that are already operating, the system can reduce the need for dedicated inspection rounds and transform routine municipal driving into a source of infrastructure intelligence. The AI model detects damage and wear on road surfaces, while the results are visualised on a digital map for planners and maintenance teams. At a conceptual level, Pluto creates a data-driven road-management loop: sensor and image data are collected, AI identifies defects, maps show where action is needed, and maintenance resources can then be prioritised according to actual condition. The expected impact is faster detection of damage, better prioritisation of repairs, more preventive maintenance, lower costs and potentially longer road lifespan. The case is relevant because it applies AI to a very concrete municipal asset-management task, making infrastructure maintenance more proactive and evidence-based. Pluto describes its product as AI-powered software for detecting damage, planning repairs and managing road maintenance
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: InDialog Voicebot – Internal AI Support for ESDH and Topdesk
source_description: Hvidovre Municipality’s InDialog Voicebot supports municipal employees by making internal guidance easier to access through voice-based interaction. Public administrations rely on many internal systems, including electronic document and case-management systems and service-management platforms such as TOPdesk. Employees often need quick answers on how to use these systems correctly, but finding the relevant instruction can require searching manuals, intranet pages or previous support material. The InDialog Voicebot addresses this problem by allowing staff to ask questions through voice commands and receive guidance rapidly. The solution is used internally to support navigation and guidance in the municipality’s ESDH system and TOPdesk. At operational level, the voicebot works as an internal first-line assistant: employees can obtain immediate answers or locate relevant instructions without interrupting their workflow or submitting routine support requests. This reduces the time spent searching for procedural guidance and allows support staff to focus on more complex issues that require human expertise. The expected impact is faster internal support, more efficient use of digital systems, reduced friction in administrative work and improved productivity for municipal employees. The voice interface is also relevant because it lowers the threshold for using internal knowledge tools, especially in situations where typing a search query or navigating a system manually is inconvenient. The initiative demonstrates how AI can be used inside local government to improve the everyday experience of staff working with digital administrative systems.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: KAILA - AI tool for Danish legislation
context: Executive and legislative organs, financial and fiscal affairs, external affairs.
source_description: Municipal legal staff must interpret current legislation, prepare arguments, draft legal documents and ensure that advice is based on reliable and up-to-date sources. KAILA supports this work by providing an AI assistant grounded in Karnov’s legal content and, in the municipal case-management context, potentially combined with the municipality’s own uploaded documents. The operational problem is that legal professionals spend substantial time locating relevant provisions, guidance, case law and arguments before they can apply them to a concrete case. KAILA is designed to accelerate this research and drafting process while preserving source verification. It can help generate legal text, gather relevant sources and arguments, provide new perspectives and assist preparation for meetings or case discussions. At a conceptual level, the system works as a retrieval and drafting assistant for legal work: it uses AI to interpret the user’s question, search trusted legal materials and produce a response with references that the legal professional can verify. This is important because legal AI must not be treated as an uncheckable answer generator; the value lies in combining speed with transparent source grounding. The expected impact is faster legal research, more efficient preparation of legal documents, improved consistency in municipal legal work and reduced time spent on preliminary information gathering. The case is relevant because it applies generative AI to a high-accountability domain where human verification remains essential. KAILA should therefore be presented as decision support for legal professionals, not as an automated legal decision-maker. (karnovgroup.dk

title: AI-for-Søren: AI for work injuries
source_description: Work-related injuries and eye injuries involve specific reporting obligations, rights, responsibilities and procedural steps that can be difficult for employees and managers to understand quickly. AI-for-Søren addresses this problem by providing an AI assistant that answers questions about municipal procedures for handling occupational injury cases. The operational problem is that different users need different kinds of guidance: an injured employee may need to know what to do immediately, a manager may need to understand reporting obligations, and HR or working-environment staff may need consistent procedural information. The assistant communicates the municipality’s procedures and links users to supplementary information from relevant Danish authorities and professional sources, including the Danish Working Environment Authority and the National Board of Industrial Injuries. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as a specialised knowledge assistant for a narrow administrative domain. It does not decide whether an injury is compensable or replace formal case handling; instead, it helps users find correct guidance and understand the steps involved. The expected impact is easier access to accurate information, fewer procedural mistakes, more consistent handling of work-injury cases and reduced workload for staff who otherwise answer recurring questions manually. The intended users include managers, working-environment representatives, injured employees, HR staff, MED organisation representatives and the municipality’s occupational-injury function. The case is relevant because it shows how a municipality can create a focused AI assistant for a specific internal governance and employee-support process, where a well-defined knowledge base can reduce uncertainty and improve procedural compliance.

title: 5G launch in Lviv
source_description: Kyivstar, Ukraine's largest mobile operator, plans to launch its first commercial fifth-generation (5G) service in Lviv after completing pilot tests. Speaking at the Spring Business Forum, Business Development Director Kostiantyn Vechir confirmed the move, noting that previous 5G tests had been conducted in Kyiv. The launch is part of a coordinated effort with the Ministry of Digital Transformation, as Kyivstar works alongside state authorities and the telecommunications industry to implement a nationwide 5G transition plan.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: A Sovereign AI Model: National LLM to Enter Beta in 2026
source_description: Ukraine is developing its own sovereign large language model (LLM)—a national artificial intelligence system tailored to the Ukrainian language, culture and public-sector needs. The project has moved from concept to technical planning and is being built in partnership with Kyivstar, with the first beta version due in spring 2026. It uses Google’s open Gemma models as a base, which are being adapted and trained on extensive Ukrainian-language datasets drawn from government, academia, media and other sources. An independent expert panel is shaping quality, safety and linguistic benchmarks, while a legal framework for data use and intellectual-property compliance is under development. Once tested, the model will be made available to public institutions, researchers and developers, and is intended to bolster Ukraine’s digital sovereignty and reduce reliance on foreign AI technologies.

title: ELLI - Chatbot of the City of Linz
source_description: The City of Linz provides an AI-powered chatbot service called “ELLI” (short for Elektronische Linzerin) to help citizens find information about municipal services quickly and easily. ELLI is available 24/7 online and answers questions about topics like administrative services, opening hours, civic procedures, local information and more, using natural language understanding to interpret queries and point users to relevant details or external resources. The chatbot supports multilingual interaction, is continuously updated with new content, and helps reduce routine inquiries to the City’s Teleservice Center by providing instant responses to common questions.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Innovative Mathematics Learning Platform (Grades 5–12)
source_description: This AI-powered mathematics platform supports students in grades 5–12 by providing curriculum-aligned exercises, intelligent feedback, and adaptive learning paths. It helps students strengthen mathematical understanding, practice problem-solving skills, and prepare for assessments, while also supporting teachers with insights into student progress. The platform is integrated into the Learn on.ai initiative as one of the core learning tools used in participating schools. It is implemented directly in classroom and independent learning settings to demonstrate how AI can enhance mathematics education at scale. Learn on.ai is a national initiative by the Devbridge Foundation aimed at introducing AI-powered educational tools into Lithuanian schools. The project supports teachers and students by providing access to innovative digital solutions, fostering personalised learning, and reducing regional disparities in access to modern educational technologies.

title: Personalised Mathematics Learning Platform for Every Student (Grades 5–12)
source_description: This platform delivers personalised mathematics learning through adaptive tasks, interactive content, and gamified elements that respond to each student’s individual progress and knowledge gaps. It is designed to improve engagement, reinforce foundational skills, and support steady academic development. The platform is integrated withitn the Learn on.ai initiative, and it is used to demonstrate how artificial intelligence can individualise learning at scale. title: EditAI – AI Tool for Teachers
source_description: EditAI is an AI-powered tool designed to help teachers create lesson plans, assignments, and learning materials more efficiently. It supports modern teaching approaches such as problem-based and personalised learning, while allowing educators to adapt content to different student needs. EditAI is integrated into the Learn on.ai initiative as a teacher-focused solution that supports daily classroom work. title: AI solution in Roskilde Municipality helps create minutes of consultation responses
source_description: Roskilde Municipality uses generative AI to automatically create summaries of consultation responses from residents regarding planning decisions. When citizens submit feedback on municipal projects, employees manually had to summarize each response—a time-consuming and variable process. The AI solution uses Azure GPT to generate initial drafts of these summaries, which employees then review and refine to ensure accuracy. Testing shows the AI produces summaries of 75-80% quality initially, potentially saving up to one hour per consultation response. This allows staff to redirect time toward other citizen-facing tasks.

title: AI helps the Danish Digital Agency conduct analyses
source_description: Since 2021, large Danish companies must address data ethics in their annual reports. The Digital Agency needed to analyze thousands of reports to strengthen national data ethics guidance. The sheer volume—3,673 reports totaling approximately 88,000 pages from 2022-2023—made manual analysis impractical. The agency developed a generative AI solution using ChatGPT API with a custom prompt containing 30 classification categories. This enables systematic analysis of data ethics policies across entire company populations rather than just samples, allowing faster, more comprehensive insights for policy development.

title: AI solution in ATP writes journal notes of conversations with citizens
source_description: ATP, Denmark's labor market fund, receives approximately 2.5 million citizen calls annually, each requiring documentation as journal notes. The automated journaling solution converts call recordings to text, then summarizes conversations using generative AI. Results show the system generates draft notes in 5 seconds, with employees spending under 2 minutes correcting them in 70% of cases. This automation frees employees from time-consuming documentation tasks while maintaining consistent, high-quality records of citizen interactions.

title: Agrinio Environmental Digital Observatory: A Digital Twin Ecosystem for Sustainable and Data-Driven Governance
source_description: The Agrinio Environmental Digital Observatory establishes a unified digital twin and governance ecosystem operating as a decision-support system for evidence-based, climate-resilient and participatory governance in the Municipality of Agrinio. It integrates environmental monitoring, spatial planning, municipal intelligence and citizen engagement into a single interoperable platform. The system combines real-time IoT sensor networks, Copernicus Earth Observation data, GIS analytics and open data services with participatory planning tools, enabling continuous monitoring of environmental conditions, land-use dynamics and urban development in near real time. It functions as a single source of truth for municipal territory, improving coordination, efficiency and cross-departmental decision-making. A KPI framework aligned with ISO 37120 supports performance monitoring of municipal services. Citizens access environmental and spatial data, strengthening transparency and participation. organization: MINISTRY OF THE INTERIOR AND PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION
title: Skrinja: AI-Enhanced Business Intelligence for Evidence-Based Decision-Making and Policymaking in Slovenia
source_description: Skrinja is Slovenia’s national Business Intelligence (BI) and AI-enabled analytics platform, supporting evidence-based decision-making and policymaking across public administration. It provides strategic KPI dashboards, advanced analytics, standardised reports, real-time reporting, interactive visualisations and predictive analytics, transforming administrative data into actionable insights. Operating in a secure GDPR-compliant government environment since 2020, Skrinja integrates major national datasets, including the Common Agricultural Policy (covering over 80,000 farms), Administrative Procedures (more than 1 million cases annually), Market and Health Inspections, Public-Sector Salaries (over 180,000 employees and 2,000 budget users), Public Procurement, the Central Personnel Registry and Public Funding Programmes. organization: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development of the Republic of Latvia
title: Latvia enables legal recognition of Ukrainian trusted e-signatures
source_description: Latvia introduced a legal and technical solution enabling Ukrainian electronic signatures to be recognised and verified in Latvia. The initiative builds on Ukraine’s recognition of EU electronic signatures since January 2023, and on the European Commission’s Trusted List of third countries, which together created the legal and technical foundation for the acceptance of Ukrainian electronic signatures within Latvia’s digital environment. It responds to the needs of Ukrainian citizens, residents, entrepreneurs and business representatives who interact with Latvian public institutions and service providers but may not have Latvian digital credentials. It also benefits Latvian citizens and businesses cooperating with Ukrainian partners, by enabling legally valid remote transactions. By amending national legislation and integrating verification functionality into Latvia’s national e-signature infrastructure, documents signed with Ukrainian electronic signatures issued by trusted Ukrainian service providers can now be accepted for legally binding digital interactions. The solution removes administrative barriers, supports remote access to services, and strengthens secure cross-border digital cooperation.

organization: The Communications Regulatory Authority of the Republic of Lithuania
title: Matuok.lt: Open-Source Network Measurement and Data Platform for Public Internet Quality Monitoring
source_description: Matuok.lt is a public network measurement platform implemented and operated by the Communications Regulatory Authority of Lithuania (RRT), based on the open-source RTR-NetTest framework. It enables citizens and businesses to objectively assess the quality of their internet access services by measuring key parameters such as download/upload speed, latency, and additional quality indicators. The solution builds on an existing European open-source software and adapts it to national needs, providing detailed reports, historical data, and visualized statistics, including maps and open datasets. It empowers users to verify whether their service meets contractual conditions and supports complaint processes with evidence-based measurements. At the same time, aggregated data supports public authorities in monitoring national network performance, identifying coverage gaps, and informing infrastructure investment decisions. The platform is accessible via web and mobile applications, ensuring broad public access and usability.

title: Simple: A Semantic, Voice-Driven Procurement Intelligence and Training System for Auditing and Decision Support in Public Administration
source_description: Simple is a semantic, graph-based procurement intelligence system developed within a university-led public sector innovation context and currently in pilot phase. It integrates European (TED) and national (KIMDIS) procurement data into a unified knowledge graph aligned with the eProcurement Ontology (ePO), enabling large-scale audit and analysis across contracting authorities, time periods and CPV categories. The system supports automated generation of structured audit reports and provides multi-layer diagnosis of procurement markets (macro–meso–micro) through explainable indicators, enhancing audit, policy analysis and decision-making. It also incorporates legal knowledge into a graph-based reasoning framework, enabling structured interpretation within the regulatory context. A voice-driven interface allows non-technical users to interact naturally, while a human-supervised self-correction mechanism ensures continuous refinement and transparency. The solution improves efficiency, compliance and data-driven policymaking in public procurement.

title: Servizz.gov – Reimagining Public Service Delivery Through AI-Powered Citizen Engagement
source_description: Servizz.gov is Malta’s next-generation national public service platform, designed to transform how citizens discover, access and interact with government services. The platform consolidates 450-500 public services into a single AI-enabled experience where citizens can identify relevant services, discover benefits and entitlements, manage appointments, track applications and receive support through both AI-assisted and human-assisted channels. organization: Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia (CNMC): Deputy Directorate for Economic Analysis (Advocacy Department). Technical support: Deputy Directorate for Information Systems and ICT (SSTIC).
title: LExIA - AI-assisted regulatory screening for early detection of competition restrictions.
source_description: LExIA (“Lectura Experta con IA”) is an AI-based internal solution developed by the CNMC to support early detection of public regulatory restrictions to competition in Spanish official gazettes. It addresses a high-volume, time-sensitive process: thousands of legal texts are published across multiple official sources and must be screened quickly when they may require competition advocacy or, ultimately, legal action. LExIA combines preliminary filters, key information extraction, preliminary assessment of restrictions, retrieval of CNMC precedents through Retrieval Augmented Generation –RAG–, legal analysis against related official sources, prioritisation and automatic generation of Word reports and e-mail alerts. The system runs on real regulatory publications and sends daily results and filtering statistics for expert review. It does not replace legal or economic judgement; it structures, documents and prioritises cases, enabling CNMC to identify cases to challenge in court and engage authorities to amend anti-competitive rules, and has already helped remove restrictive regulation.

title: AI Playbook
source_description: The AI Playbook developed by Digitaal Vlaanderen establishes a practical operating model for trustworthy, scalable and interoperable AI adoption across the public sector. It was created in response to growing challenges faced by public administrations in adopting AI in a strategic and responsible manner, including fragmented experimentation, rapidly evolving technologies and regulations, and varying levels of organisational readiness. The Playbook supports public administrations across the entire AI lifecycle: defining strategy and roadmaps, identifying and prioritising AI use cases, implementing governance aligned with the EU AI Act, strengthening organisational readiness and skills, and embedding AI architecture. The Playbook turns policy ambitions into concrete tools, checklists and reusable guidance, enabling administrations to move from fragmented experimentation to coordinated and interoperable AI adoption. It provides a common framework and shared language for AI adoption, helping organisations move from fragmented experimentation towards coordinated, interoperable and value-driven AI implementation. The Playbook supports organisations at different stages of AI maturity, from initial exploration to large-scale operational adoption.

title: Prozorro.Sale
source_description: Prozorro.Sale is Ukraine’s national digital public infrastructure for the transparent sale and lease of public assets and rights. It addresses fragmented procedures, limited competition, unequal access to information, and integrity risks in public asset management. The solution combines a state-administered electronic trading system with more than 40 private e-marketplaces operating under common rules and standards. It uses APIs, open data, public BI dashboards, cloud infrastructure, and transparency-by-design principles to ensure equal access, accountability, and public oversight. Prozorro.Sale enables fair competition and market-based price discovery. Since 2016, the system has conducted over 860k auctions, generated more than UAH 130 billion, and attracted over 149k participants. It improves administrative efficiency and provides a scalable model for digital governance.

title: Medical Drone Transport Corridor in Catalonia
source_description: Rural and remote healthcare areas in Catalonia, particularly in the Pyrenees, face logistical challenges in the rapid transport of biological samples, blood products, medicines and medical equipment. The Medical Drone Transport Corridor in Catalonia, led by CTTI and the Department of Health, introduces a drone-based logistics service starting with the Lleida–Tremp corridor and Tremp-Sort corridor. It uses Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) to complement road transport with regular, on-demand and urgent aerial services between healthcare centres. The project combines certified drone operations, healthcare air corridors, vertiports, traceability and a digital platform for mission management. Building on two pilots in rural and urban areas, the solution has shown faster deliveries, lower emissions and better sample preservation, including up to 75% shorter delivery times, up to 98% lower emissions and a 50% reduction in sample hemolysis. It also provides a scalable model for future healthcare corridors.

title: BRISA: A Cross-Domain AI Foundation Model for Predictive Public Infrastructure Management
source_description: BRISA is an interoperable Artificial Intelligence solution that helps public administrations move from reactive management to predictive decision-making in energy and environmental policies. Based on a proprietary time-series foundation model trained on more than 11 billion energy, climate, mobility, occupancy and environmental data points, BRISA forecasts demand, detects anomalies, simulates intervention scenarios and prioritises actions with explainable and auditable outputs. organization: MKIFK Hungarian Gazette Publishing and Legal Translation Centre Ltd.
title: Artificial intelligence-based legal search service integrated in the Hungarian Gazette and National Legislation Database
source_description: The Gazette 2.0 project modernised IT systems supporting official gazette publication and integrated the National Legislation Database with an innovative AI platform accessible via jog.gov.hu, free of charge, implemented by co-financing of EU and hungarian Government. organization: The Danish Agency for Planning and Rural Development (Plan- og Landdistriktsstyrelsen)nddistriktsstyrelsen)
title: Transforming environmental assessment with AI for Denmark's state-designated energy parks
source_description: The green transition requires public authorities to make faster and better-informed planning decisions while maintaining high environmental standards. To support this ambition, The Danish Agency for Planning and Rural Development has developed an AI-assisted solution that helps prepare Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) reports for Denmark's state-designated energy parks. organization: Ajuntament de Sant Feliu de Llobregat
title: Implementation of the First Autonomous Traffic Light with Artificial Intelligence Functionalities
source_description: Sant Feliu de Llobregat City Council has an Innovation Unit, which operates through Sant Feliu Innova, the city’s public urban innovation laboratory. This space works to address urban challenges through innovation, experimentation and public-private collaboration. This approach is aligned with the Pla d’Actuació de Mandat 2023-2027, particularly with its 5th Horizon, focused on innovation and city promotion, which establishes the promotion of the economic and productive fabric through innovation as a priority. The initiative is also framed within the Agenda Urbana de Sant Feliu de Llobregat, specifically Objective 7.1, aimed at promoting local productivity, job creation, economic dynamism and the diversification of productive activity. Likewise, it is linked to the Agenda Digital de Sant Feliu de Llobregat, particularly Axis 4: Digital Economy, which promotes the modernisation and digitalisation of the productive fabric, SMEs and local businesses, with the aim of moving towards an agile, inclusive, climate-neutral, competitive and resource-efficient digital economy. In this context, the undergrounding of the railway tracks represents an unprecedented milestone for the city. The release of nearly 150,000 m² in the urban centre opens up a strategic opportunity to rethink the city model from an integrated perspective. The vision of the Ecodistrict, as a new urban centrality based on criteria of sustainability, safety, health and innovation, places the Innovation Unit before the challenge of prototyping sustainable technological solutions that can be applied to the future released space and generate a triple impact: social, environmental and economic. An example of this approach is the deployment of pilots in real urban environments, such as the autonomous traffic light installed in Sant Feliu de Llobregat. Since September 2025, the city has had a pedestrian crossing that operates independently from the electricity grid, thanks to a solar panel system that provides it with energy autonomy. In addition, the system incorporates local, technologically sovereign and sustainable artificial intelligence, designed to protect the most vulnerable pedestrians through voice assistance and to prevent potential failures. This patented technology emerged from CO-Innova Lab Sant Feliu, the city’s own centre for urban innovation and experimentation.

title: Automatic detection of impervious surfaces using AI
source_description: In the context of progressing climate change, a precise and up-to-date overview of impervious surfaces in municipalities is essential. Impervious surfaces (approximately 45% of settlement and transport areas in Germany) reduce rainwater infiltration and contribute to the formation of urban heat islands by acting as heat storage. To date, imperviousness has mainly been determined using: - Cadastral data, which only partially reflect the actual on-site situation. - Manual mapping, which is highly time-consuming, costly, and difficult to maintain. At the same time, AI-based methods—particularly deep convolutional neural networks for image analysis—have made significant performance advances. In parallel, the availability of high-resolution georeferenced data has increased, such as annual digital orthophotos (DOPs) with a ground resolution of up to 10 cm (RGB and near-infrared/NIR). These developments make the automated detection of impervious surfaces using AI a promising approach. The district of Recklinghausen, in cooperation with the Westphalian University of Applied Sciences, initiated a project to automatically detect and classify impervious surfaces.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: BronConnect: Reusable source access for European digital government services
source_description: Public authorities across Europe face a structural implementation challenge: the same authoritative source data is increasingly needed for OOTS, eIDAS 2.0, wallets and future cross-border public services, while source access is often still organised separately for each channel or legal obligation. This creates duplication, higher implementation costs and fragmented interoperability. BronConnect addresses this challenge by taking the authoritative source as the starting point: it defines one reusable way for trusted public-sector data to be made available securely, with the user in control, across multiple European digital government contexts. BronConnect is an initiative led by the Association of Netherlands Municipalities, the national organisation representing Dutch local authorities. It develops a uniform and reusable approach for making municipal source data available to European and national data exchange infrastructures. Rather than building a separate connection for each regulation or channel, BronConnect defines how trusted data from municipal sources can be accessed once and reused for multiple purposes, including OOTS, eIDAS 2.0 and future wallet-based services. The initiative builds on, and works with, the standard OOTS infrastructure. Its added value lies at the source-holder side: standardising source access, developing reusable DATA-API specifications, aligning with the Federated Data System, and creating an implementation model that municipalities and other public authorities can adopt without each designing their own solution. Led by the Association of Netherlands Municipalities, with Indra Henneman as project lead, BronConnect brings together municipalities and key partners in the Dutch SDG/OOTS ecosystem, including RINIS, EnableU, Cleverbase, the Federated Data System, Digilab/BZK and the national SDG/OOTS network. The project translates European legal and technical requirements into a practical model for source-side interoperability. By shifting the focus from individual channels to reusable source access, BronConnect helps make the Once-Only Principle operational in practice. It reduces duplication, supports secure cross-border public services and creates a scalable foundation for future European digital government obligations.

organization: Community of Madrid | Regional Ministry of Digitalization
title: SABIA & Sol: AI-Powered Citizen Assistant
source_description: SABIA Assistant & Avatar Sol is an Artificial Intelligence-based solution developed by the Community of Madrid to transform citizen access to public information and services. The system combines generative AI, semantic search and a conversational avatar to provide accurate, personalised and accessible responses through natural language interactions, available 24/7. Built on a secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, it retrieves and organises information from official government sources, ensuring reliable and up-to-date answers. The solution reduces information search times from several minutes to just a few seconds, improves digital inclusion through multilingual and voice-enabled interactions, and decreases reliance on traditional support channels. Fully aligned with the EU AI Act, GDPR and the Spanish National Security Framework, SABIA establishes a scalable and citizen-centric model for the responsible use of AI in public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Incubator for AI - Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
title: Extract: AI-powered planning data for every council in England
source_description: Extract is an AI tool that turns England's historic planning records — scanned Conservation Area appraisals, Article 4 Directions and Tree Preservation Orders, locked in old PDFs and paper maps — into accurate, standardised digital geospatial data. It combines vision language models, Meta's Segment Anything Model and automated geo-referencing in a modular pipeline, with a human-in-the-loop interface so officers review every output before use. Manual digitisation can take up to two hours per document; on average, Extract produces a draft in about two minutes. Built by DSIT's i.AI in partnership with MHCLG's Digital Planning Programme, it launched free to every local planning authority in England in June 2026. This unlocks decades of trapped planning data, speeds up planning decisions and supports the government's commitment to build 1.5 million new homes.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Digital Twins for Smart Territories
source_description: Digital Twins for Smart Territories contributes to the goals of the Portuguese National Strategy for Smart Territories, by promoting the development and implementation of digital twins in eight nationally prioritized thematic areas: Health, Mobility, Decarbonization, Tourism, Civil Protection, Climate Resilience, Agriculture, and Water Management. The initiative aims to support the development of reusable digital twins that, can be integrated by public administration entities, for the development ofinto public policies and decision-making processes. It also seeks to promote innovation and technological responsiveness across territories, while engaging the national scientific and technological ecosystem in the creation of digital solutions with a direct impact on public management and citizens’ quality of life.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: MesAides28: Digital twins of social welfare policies to improve social support through Rules as Code
source_description: MesAides28 is a digital benefits calculator that leverages OpenFisca's Rules-as-Code technology to help citizens of the Eure-et-Loir department in France determine their eligibility and potential benefit amounts across complex social welfare programs. By transforming legislation into machine-consumable rules, the solution simplifies access to social benefits, reduces administrative complexity, and increases policy uptake. It enables us as a local government to provide accurate information on both national and local benefits, and to better understand and explain the interaction of our policies with national ones. We can also use this resource to design reforms through precise impact simulation.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg – State Agency for Geoinformation and Surveying
title: From Urban Data to Simulated Decisions: Hamburg's AI-enabled Urban Digital Twin for Real-time Policy Simulation
source_description: Hamburg's Digital Twin turns open urban data into evidence for policy decisions. It combines the Urban Data Platform (UDP_HH), Urban Model Platform (UMP), open-source Masterportal and UDP-Agent into an AI-enabled urban digital twin for real-time policy simulation. UDP_HH provides governed geospatial, sensor and urban data through open APIs. UMP exposes models and simulations through standards such as OGC API Processes. Masterportal and its add-ons - 3D Projektplaner, Scenario Explorer and Data Narrator - let users create 3D planning scenarios, run and compare simulations, and explain results through maps and narratives. The UDP-Agent adds a natural-language and agentic layer for data discovery, spatial analysis and evidence generation. Public servants can move from a policy question - for example the impact of a new road layout on traffic noise, wind or heat - to a map-based scenario, simulation result and explainable decision basis. The stack is reusable for other European cities.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Courts
title: Intelligent Automation of Judicial Proceedings through AI and RPA
source_description: The Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Courts has developed a comprehensive Smart Automation strategy that combines Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and Hyperautomation to transform the management of judicial proceedings and improve the services provided to citizens. It currently has more than 30 lines of work and more than 60 active robots, which have allowed more than 23 million automated operations to be executed, saving more than 1.18 million working hours and generating economic savings of more than 26 million euros. AI-based initiatives streamline document management and facilitate access to legal information through solutions such as smart summaries, clear reading and easy reading. Currently, more than 600,000 AI processes have been executed. Hyperautomation combines both technologies to process up to 340 monitoring procedures per day from end to end.

title: Implementation of an Information System for the Optimization of Strategic Planning and Project Management Processes within the Druskininkai Municipality Administration
source_description: Druskininkai Municipality has developed an innovative Strategic Planning and Project Management Information System that transforms strategic governance, project administration, and planning processes in the public sector. It is one of the first integrated solutions of its kind among Lithuanian municipalities, bringing together strategic planning, project management, budget planning, and public procurement processes within a single digital platform. The project not only modernizes the municipality’s internal operations but also establishes a new model for public service management that can serve as a best-practice example for other municipalities. The implemented solution contributes to a smarter, more efficient, and data-driven transformation of the public sector, strengthens the institution’s ability to respond rapidly to change, and helps ensure higher-quality services for residents.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

organization: Ajuntament de Sant Feliu de Llobregat
title: SmartCityMAP: Sant Feliu de Llobregat's BIM-Based Digital Twin Platform for Municipal Asset Management
source_description: The Ajuntament de Sant Feliu de Llobregat has built an interoperable digital twin ecosystem connecting Building Information Modelling (BIM) with real-time IoT sensing and open data to manage municipal buildings and infrastructure. Centred on the open-source platform BIMROCKET (a common data environment for IFC models) and the open-source AI/rules engine Brain4it, the system links static 3D models with the real behaviour of assets, enabling automated lighting and climate control, remote energy monitoring, faster and cheaper technical audits, and a prototype for automated compliance-checking of building permits. Eighteen municipal facilities (33% of the building stock) are already digitised, with a roadmap to reach 75% by 2030, and the model is now being scaled to other Catalan and Spanish public administrations.

title: BärGPT: An Open-Source AI Assistant for a Sovereign Public Administration
source_description: BärGPT (https://www.baergpt.berlin) is an open-source AI assistant developed for Berlin’s public administration to support everyday work while ensuring digital sovereignty. Built on European technologies and infrastructure, it helps civil servants analyze documents, draft texts, prepare policy briefs, and evaluate administrative data. Developed through an iterative, user-centered design process involving civil servants, BärGPT combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), transparent source citations and persistent document management to deliver trustworthy results. Since its launch in November 2025, there have been over 16,000 account registrations, and BärGPT has enabled users to work more efficiently while complying with public sector requirements. As an open-source solution, BärGPT can be adapted and replicated by other public administrations. It’s the result of a collaboration between Berlin’s Senate Chancellery (Senatskanzlei Berlin) and Berlin’s public innovation lab CityLAB Berlin.

title: Gov.pt’s GenAI-powered Virtual Assistant
source_description: The Portuguese single digital gateway, Gov.pt, provides a multilingual GenAI virtual assistant (chatbot) that gives real-time guidanceinformation on +2400 public services, answering both in text and/or audio, in 12 different languages, with an animated avatar. It benefits citizens, foreign residents and businesses by making information easier to find and understand. It was developed to cut bureaucratic friction, such as complex navigation in over 5000 webpages, language barriers or long waits in onsite public attendance or support channels, while reducing workload on public administration.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: EUROCONTROL – AI-powered Digital Twins for Air Traffic Management
source_description: European Air Traffic Management is becoming increasingly complex, requiring new ways to anticipate the impact of operational decisions before they are implemented. To explore the potential of emerging technologies, EUROCONTROL partnered with Cronos Europa to develop an AI-powered Digital Twin Proof of Concept. The solution was designed and implemented by Mr. Watts, a competence center within De Cronos Groep specialising in Artificial Intelligence and advanced digital solutions. By combining Artificial Intelligence with Digital Twin technology, the project demonstrates how realistic operational simulations can support evidence-based decision-making, strengthen collaboration and improve operational resilience. The Proof of Concept also illustrates how interoperable digital technologies can complement existing operational environments while supporting future innovation in Air Traffic Management.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Artificial Intelligence for detecting legal overlaps and improving legislative harmonization in Albania
source_description: The AI-powered Law Overlap Detection System is an innovative solution developed by the National Agency for Information Society (NAIS) and the Ministry of Justice to improve the quality and consistency of Albania’s legal framework. Using artificial intelligence and large language models (LLMs), the system analyzes over 27,000 legal acts in the National Registry of Legislation to identify overlaps, contradictions, and inconsistencies between draft laws and existing legislation. Integrated with the Official Gazette, it enables legal experts to compare legal texts, generate structured comparison tables, and produce evidence-based legal analyses. By automating complex legislative reviews, the platform reduces processing time, improves drafting accuracy, and supports more transparent and reliable decision-making. The initiative modernizes legislative processes and strengthens Albania’s alignment with the EU acquis through AI-assisted legal harmonization.

title: eLys – Enabling Trusted Data Exchange for Better Public Services
source_description: The death of a loved one is one of life's most difficult moments. Administrative procedures should support citizens during this time, not add unnecessary complexity. Developed by Athumi in collaboration with the Flemish Government, eLys is a trusted digital platform that transforms the civil death registration process across Flanders. The implementation brought together Cronos Public Services, the De Cronos Groep entity specialised in digital transformation for the Belgian public sector, and Kunlabora, a De Cronos Groep competence center specialising in public sector innovation and service design. By replacing fragmented paper-based procedures with one secure digital workflow, eLys enables trusted data exchange between healthcare providers, local authorities and funeral directors. The platform reduces administrative burden, improves data quality and demonstrates how interoperability creates tangible public value.

organization: IdomSoft Zrt. (100% state-owned IT development company)
title: Digital Twin Scene: Rapid 3D Documentation for Public-Safety Investigations
source_description: Digital Twin Scene enables the AI-assisted creation of accurate, scale-aware 3D records of traffic accidents, crime and fire scenes, illegal-waste sites and evidence objects within minutes with ordinary cameras and drones. IdomSoft’s field-tested pilot was co-designed with police and fire-service professionals and replaces slow spatial documentation based on manual measurements, sketches and photo annexes. In parallel field testing, an average two-car accident was captured and modelled in under 15 minutes, versus 3–4 hours for the current documentation process. Professionals remain responsible for analysing the models and making decisions. The records support measurement, enlargement and immersive AR/VR review, and are already used in real cases and formal police and fire-investigator training. Over 100 case-related models demonstrate operational maturity. Affordable capture, compact outputs and low computing needs make the method fast, cost-effective, resource-efficient and reusable.

organization: Government of New Caledonia – Digital Transformation Directorate
title: A digital twin of policies to enable reform design and buy-in through Rules as Code
source_description: In early 2025, following a major social crisis, the New Caledonian territory faced a difficult situation: housing aid applications had surged by 30 percent while government revenue collapsed by 14 percent of GDP. A digital twin of New Caledonia's housing benefit laws, created with the Rules as Code engine OpenFisca and a simple user interface on top, allowed impact assessment of reform scenarios during this major economic crisis. The solution prevented austerity measures that would have backfired significantly by revealing their minimal fiscal impact, leading to a major redesign of the policy through stakeholder collaboration. On top, the resulting increase in taxation received strong buy-in from the taxed subjects once they were presented with the ability to interact with the digital twin themselves.

title: Form+: Reuse instead of rebuilding - A shared municipal forms service
source_description: Form+ is a shared digital form service provided by Kommuneforlaget for Norwegian municipalities and other public-sector organisations. Kommuneforlaget creates digital forms for common administrative and citizen-facing needs and publishes them in a shared form library. Participating organisations can select the forms they need from the library instead of independently designing and implementing equivalent forms. The solution supports reuse across the public sector. A form developed to address a recurring municipal need can be made available to multiple organisations through the same service. This reduces duplicated development work, supports more consistent digital services and gives municipalities access to forms created and maintained by a dedicated service provider. The model is particularly valuable for smaller administrations that may have limited internal capacity for form design, technical configuration and ongoing maintenance.

title: The Semantic Intelligence Services
source_description: The SIS project, developed by ISTAT with DXC Technology and Lutech, addresses the semantic gap in public sector interoperability. By integrating the transactional Piattaforma Digitale Nazionale Dati (PDND) and the authoritative National Data Catalog (schema.gov.it), SIS supports data providers, consumers, and governors by automating the verification and discovery of data meaning in API specifications and API-based exchanges to enhance ecosystem semantic quality. SIS deploys a collaborative Agent Crew orchestrated by a central Semantic Broker and supported by specialized agents like the Schema Assistant and API Catalog Assistant. These agents dynamically query technical API specifications and map fields onto standardized ontologies and vocabularies. The pilot demonstrates that public sector data can transition from machine-readable to machine-comprehensible, establishing the foundation for trust, automated semantic quality assurance, and seamless cross-border e-Government.

organization: Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies (Ministero del Lavoro e delle Politiche Sociali)
title: Digital Supervisory Intelligence for Private Pension Schemes
source_description: The Ministry of Labour and Social Policies (MLPS) supervises pension and social security institutions, including private-law entities established under D.Lgs No. 509/1994 and No. 103/1996. Its responsibilities cover both legal-administrative and financial oversight, including the approval of resolutions on contributions, benefits, governance, and appointments; the review of budgets, financial statements, actuarial reports, and investment plans; the assessment of financial sustainability and regulatory compliance in cooperation with other authorities, including MEF and COVIP. These activities generate large volumes of documentation and complex procedures, while being managed by a limited number of officials. The resulting administrative burden has increased processing times and highlighted the need for advanced digital tools to improve efficiency, consistency, knowledge sharing, and decision-making. The platform represents the first integrated digital environment specifically designed to enhance, streamline, and accelerate the supervisory and monitoring activities carried out by the MLPS overseeing private pension schemes. The platform has been conceived to support the supervision of 20 private pension funds currently operating in Italy, providing a comprehensive digital environment for the analysis, management, and assessment of both financial and governance-related information. The system is structured around two integrated modules. 1. Document Management, Analysis, and Knowledge Discovery Module The first module is dedicated to the collection, storage, processing, indexing, and intelligent analysis of all documents periodically submitted by pension funds to their supervisory authority. Through a centralized and highly searchable repository, supervisory staff can rapidly retrieve relevant information, navigate large volumes of documentation, and perform cross-document analyses that would otherwise require significant manual effort. The platform manages a wide range of documents, including annual budgets, financial statements, actuarial balance sheets, investment plans, board resolutions, minutes, reports issued by the Board of Statutory Auditors, and other regulatory filings. Advanced indexing and semantic-search capabilities enable users to identify specific information within seconds, compare data across multiple reporting periods, and conduct in-depth analyses of financial, governance, and operational trends. The system also includes sophisticated analytical tools that allow supervisors to generate reports, perform data aggregations, visualize historical developments through comparative tables and time-series analyses, and monitor key indicators over extended periods. These functionalities significantly improve the efficiency and consistency of supervisory activities while reducing the operational burden on staff. A particularly valuable feature concerns the assessment of board resolutions submitted for approval. In addition to the resolutions themselves, the platform incorporates a comprehensive and constantly updated repository of applicable legislation, regulatory provisions, pension-fund statutes, internal regulations, and governance rules adopted by each scheme. By combining this legal and regulatory framework with the economic, financial, and actuarial information extracted from the funds' reports, the platform leverages advanced Artificial Intelligence algorithms to support supervisory decision-making. Users can interact with the AI engine either through predefined prompts tailored to specific supervisory tasks or through a free-form conversational interface. The system can identify relevant regulatory references, highlighting potential inconsistencies or compliance issues, assessing the coherence of proposed decisions with applicable rules, and providing reasoned analyses to support the approval or rejection of board resolutions. Furthermore, it assists supervisory personnel in drafting technical opinions, advisory reports, and formal assessments, substantially reducing preparation time while improving the quality, consistency, and traceability of regulatory evaluations. 2. Appointment Management and Eligibility Assessment Module The second module issues invitations to complete application forms for appointments to the audit bodies of 20 pension schemes, the 36 administrative committees responsible for managing INPS (National Institute of Pension Schemes) funds, and four private complementary pension funds. Applications are transmitted to and verified by the Supervisory Authority’s staff. The module manages the full initial submission workflow, from the invitation sent to the candidate through the transmission of the completed application and supporting documents to the competent supervisory staff. This also supports efficient handling of each individual appointment procedure. Through a certified authentication system, selected individuals can complete an online form, upload a CV and an ID document and, after confirming the accuracy of the information entered, automatically generate the documents that the Administration must publish on its transparency portal. After applicants review and verify the submitted information, the platform performs a preliminary formal review using an artificial intelligence algorithm. It provides feedback indicating, for example, whether a document is expired, a file has the wrong format, a file submitted as a CV is not a curriculum vitae, the CV contains a name different from the applicant’s, or the CV lacks the declarations required for self-certifications and sworn statements. When formal errors are detected, the platform alerts applicants, enabling them to correct the issues and upload the appropriate documentation. This initial phase reduces completion errors and processing times. Consequently, applications reach the competent authority complete and formally compliant, allowing its staff to focus on substantive rather than formal checks. Immediately after submission, an officer of the Supervisory Authority can review the documentation and initiate automated checks to verify its completeness and formal correctness and, within the information available on the platform, identify potential risks concerning conflicts of interest, incompatibility, or ineligibility for appointment. For example, the platform examines candidates’ CVs and the positions they declare they currently hold or have held during the previous two years, to identify companies affiliated with or controlled by the pension institution concerned. This assessment is conducted by analysing the notes to the institution’s financial statements. If an officer needs to clarify additional issues, an AI-powered free-text chat function is available. It enables the officer to query all documentation stored on the platform, including declarations and supporting documents, conduct further analysis, and investigate matters requiring additional scrutiny. *** A core innovation of the platform is the transformation of previously siloed information into a shared institutional knowledge base. Historically, supervisory processes were managed by different offices, resulting in fragmented information, duplicated activities, and limited knowledge transfer. The platform overcomes these constraints by integrating documents, data, regulatory sources, and procedural information within a single digital environment. This substantially reduces the effort required to store, analyze, and retrieve relevant information, while enhancing collaboration, preserving institutional knowledge, and improving the overall effectiveness and efficiency of supervisory activities

title: OpenPA Local AI: A Modular AI and Document Automation Platform for Public Administration
source_description: OpenPA Local AI is a locally deployed, modular platform designed to increase the operational autonomy of public administration staff. Implemented within the Province of Reggio Emilia, it runs on Ubuntu and combines a locally deployed language model with Python applications built with free and open-source libraries. The platform supports document search and summarisation, assistance on procedures and services, audio and video transcription, PDF-to-Word conversion, OCR for scanned PDFs and images, PDF compression, and automation of repetitive administrative tasks. Local deployment gives the administration greater control over data, configuration and costs, while the modular architecture allows new applications to be added according to the needs of different offices and reused by other public bodies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: INPS ISAC – Generative Artificial Intelligence applied to social security contribution compliance.
source_description: INPS, in agreement with the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the National Labour Inspectorate (INL), has developed the Statistical Indicators of Contribution Reliability (Indicatori Statistici di Affidabilità Contributiva, known as ISAC) in order to promote preventive contribution compliance and to identify cases of under-declaration of employment, by means of indicators that compare tax and social security contribution data. The process provides for compliance letters to be sent to companies, setting out any deviations in the indicators, as determined by the Institute. Once the compliance letters have been sent, companies may justify and explain the deviations, including by attaching appropriate documentation, by submitting specific communications through the INPS channels. The generative AI component operates in the analysis of the communications submitted by companies: it analyses and assesses the replies and any attachments in line with the deviations determined by the Institute; it extracts the evidence provided by the company; it assigns the companies’ replies to specific clusters; it proposes an explainable justification of the analysis carried out and also prepares a draft reply to the company itself. INPS staff govern the entire process: they examine, modify, supplement and/or validate the output produced by the AI system, that is, they retain responsibility for the final decision in providing feedback to the company. The outcomes feed into monitoring, enabling continuous improvement of the system. The first application concerns the “Wholesale food trade” sector and the “Hotel and non-hotel accommodation facilities” sector, for a total of 35,491 companies analysed and 20,038 compliance letters sent. The solution improves consistency, timeliness and traceability and will be extended to six further production sectors, namely: - Bar, ice-cream parlour, pastry shop and confectionery production activities, for a total of 91,048 businesses; - Retail sale of medical and orthopaedic goods, for a total of 2,551 businesses; - Installation of electrical, plumbing and other building installations, for a total of 113,063 businesses; - Bespoke and mass production of clothing, accessories and household linen, and related processing, for a total of 17,543 businesses; - Hairdressing services, for a total of 38,794 businesses; - “Maintenance and repair of motor vehicles, motorcycles and mopeds”, for a total of 49,035 businesses. The legal entities affected will total 312,034, while approximately 176,000 letters will be sent. The proposed solution has been designed with features of flexibility and modularity that also allow it to be extended to further processes, promoting the standardisation of activities and the optimisation of the resources employed.

organization: Ministry of Labour and Social Policies (Ministero del Lavoro e delle Politiche Sociali)
title: SIO: AI-enabled evidence infrastructure for Italy's Observatory on Artificial Intelligence and Labour
source_description: Evidence on artificial intelligence and work evolves rapidly and remains fragmented across public institutions, research bodies, firms, workers and social partners. SIO (Sistema Intelligente dell’Osservatorio, the Intelligent System of the Observatory) is the AI-enabled evidence infrastructure of Italy’s Observatory on Artificial Intelligence and Labour, established within the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies. It combines a curated, source-linked knowledge base, a public conversational interface and an adaptive consultation environment for the Observatory’s bodies. Its governed architecture separates orchestration from generation, applies differentiated access and keeps validation and institutional responsibility with the Ministry and the Observatory. SIO supports a more structured, comparable and traceable evidence-to-policy cycle and provides a transferable model for public institutions addressing fast-moving technological change.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: IRIS Navarra: Turning Frontier Technologies into a Shared Public Resource for Regional Innovation
source_description: IRIS Navarra is a regional public innovation ecosystem promoted by the Government of Navarra and formally supported by a collaboration agreement involving 40 leading public and private organisations. Recognised as a European Digital Innovation Hub since 2023, IRIS has evolved into a permanent regional capability backed by €13 million in public investment. It gives companies and public organisations access to more than 220 services, 104 regional technology providers and advanced experimentation facilities in AI, supercomputing, synthetic biology, genomics, IoT, robotics and advanced manufacturing. More than 3,000 companies have already benefited from the Polo, while over 200 have used IRIS Lab infrastructures. By reducing the cost and risk of experimentation, IRIS enables organisations to test before investing and increasingly positions Navarra as a real-world testbed for frontier technologies.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: What's Next - The immersive orientation
source_description: The adoption of emerging technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence and Spatial Computing, in education has contributed to rethinking the learning experience. Within this context, Whatâ€™s Next was created: the immersive orientation service that guides students and families in exploring upper secondary school pathways and tertiary education. Through a co-design process involving schools, ITS Academies, and the General Directorates of the Italian Ministry of Education and Merit (MIM), the service use cases were identified and implemented across two releases: the first dedicated to ITS Academies and the second to upper secondary school. Integrated into Unica and accessible from PCs, tablets, smartphones, and headsets, the service offers Digital Human-guided tours through immersive environments enriched with 3D objects and interactive laboratories, combining generative AI, Virtual Reality, and Augmented Reality. Whatâ€™s Next ensures privacy and data protection in compliance with applicable regulations.

title: SyRCI-IA: Human-Supervised AI for Routing Suggestions, Complaints and Compliments
source_description: SyRCI-IA is Madrid City Council’s human-supervised artificial intelligence capability for classifying and routing suggestions, complaints and compliments to the competent municipal unit. Embedded in SYRCI, the corporate case-management system, it combines deterministic rules with three BERT-based classifiers. Municipal staff retain responsibility: receiving units validate or return routings, and corrections inform rules and retraining. In production since 4 November 2024, by 9 May 2026 it had supported 38,221 routings; 30,225 were validated as correct (79.08%). Within the measured scope, rules and AI automate 97.46% of routings; AI accounts for 47.06% of automated routings. A dashboard refreshed daily covers 84 units and 523 users; two full retraining cycles and a formal risk assessment support safe, accountable operation. Published on the Interoperable Europe Portal with a bilingual reuse and implementation guide, it offers public administrations a documented route to replication.
source_license: CC BY 4.0

title: Piacenza Smart: An Innovative and Inclusive City
source_description: The Piacenza Municipality Smart City project is a strategic tool for local governance, aimed at modernizing public administration and building a more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient city. The core of the project is the Territorial Information System (SIT), already used by the organization and now undergoing further advanced development, integrated with an urban Digital Twin. This system is conceived as a unified digital infrastructure able of collecting, integrating, and enhancing territorial, environmental, infrastructural, and energy data, transforming information into a concrete lever to support public decisions. Within this framework, the project plays an enabling and cross-cutting role, able of systematizing and enhancing further initiatives promoted by the Municipal Administration, such as the introduction of IoT sensor technology, projects financed under the PNRR (National Recovery and Resilience Plan)—particularly those related to the updating and georeferencing of street numbers and place names—as well as activities and collaborations with external entities, such as the PADRION project and other data survey and collection campaigns, ensuring coherence, interoperability, and reuse of information within a single shared digital infrastructure.

title: Privacy-safe synthetic test data: AI-generated replicas of statistical microdata for software development and testing at Statistics Netherlands
source_description: Statistics Netherlands (CBS) builds and maintains the software pipelines that produce official statistics. New software is developed in an environment that is less strictly secured than production, so real microdata about citizens and businesses may not be used there. Dummy or rule-based test data cannot capture the complexity of the real data. Together with technology partner BlueGen, CBS generated a synthetic replica of a large, complex relational dataset using generative AI (a diffusion transformer) trained entirely inside CBS's secure, air-gapped environment. The synthetic data mirrors the structure, statistical patterns and business rules of the real microdata while containing no real records. It enabled a new statistical pipeline to be developed and tested on realistic data, surfaced real defects before production, and removed the risk of a data leak from the development environment. Resemblance and utility scores exceeded 85%; measured privacy risk was zero

source_description: The Balanced Scorecard (BSC) is a business management tool that translates an organization’s strategy into a coherent set of relevant indicators aimed at achieving its objectives. Linked to the company’s mission, vision, values, and strategy, it offers significant advantages as a key tool in decision-making by management, making use of technology as a highly strategic asset. It is a strategic model implemented in the Human Resources management of the Provincial Council of Seville, based on three pillars: strategic planning, knowledge management, and process optimization. organization: Università degli Studi di Urbino Carlo Bo
title: Memento — auditable AI-assisted drafting of administrative documentation
source_description: A method for producing and reviewing complex administrative documentation with AI: vendor-neutral, at near-zero marginal cost, placing human-model collaboration inside a Git-versioned workflow that is traceable, reproducible and adoptable with tools an administration already owns. Four written registers, including a deterministic archive of the interactions, keep the work portable across people, offices and models. Applied twice by the university's administrative offices, to a technical manual required by national guidelines and to an internal regulation: about 1,370 pages of sources analysed, some 214,000 words produced, 13 effective working days, against the months of expert work a comparable document had previously required. Beyond drafting, the model reviews: examining the whole corpus it surfaced coverage gaps that human review had missed. Human validation and editorial responsibility remain with the officers. title: Synthetic datasets for Privacy-Friendly Education Research
source_description: DUO provides synthetic data as a privacy-friendly service for research into the Dutch education system. Machine-learning methods generate artificial records that preserve relevant statistical patterns without directly representing real individuals. This allows researchers and public-sector organisations to use detailed education data that could otherwise be difficult to share because of privacy restrictions. After a 2022–2025 pilot, DUO now uses this approach structurally for new and recurring data deliveries.

title: Madrid Digital Twin of Twins: a federated, semantic city digital twin for evidence-based policy decisions
source_description: Madrid, Digital Capital is building a Digital Twin of Digital Twins: a citywide, interoperable ecosystem that connects specialised digital twins, municipal data and real-world infrastructure through a common semantic framework. Building on multiple demonstrators across mobility, infrastructure, urban planning, public space and smart urban spaces, Madrid is now moving from individual use cases to city-scale integration. Open standards and a vendor-neutral architecture allow independently developed systems to work together, turning fragmented data into a shared city representation. This enables Madrid to integrate information across domains, simulate policy interventions, compare scenarios and assess trade-offs before committing public resources. The result is not simply a more detailed digital model, but a new municipal intelligence capability: understanding how policy decisions in one part of the city affect others, supporting more efficient, sustainable and people-centred public investment.

title: ASTRA: unlocking Italy's major terrorism-related and criminal case files through AI
source_description: ASTRA is an AI-powered system developed by the Emilia-Romagna Region to enhance access to digitized judicial records relating to some of Italy’s most significant terrorism-related cases of the late 20th century, including the Bologna (1980) and Italicus Express (1974) massacres, and the crimes of the White Uno Gang. Developed with the State Archives of Bologna, its first institutional user and custodian of the original records, ASTRA uses AI as an interface between users and textual and audiovisual heritage. Alongside traditional archival navigation and keyword search, AI enables semantic and conversational exploration, allowing users to query collections in natural language and retrieve relevant records, with links to sources that can be immediately viewed or played and contextualized within the archival hierarchy. ASTRA extends access to non-specialist users, facilitating their exploration and understanding of the records and events they document.

title: OmgevingsChat
source_description: OmgevingsChat is a location-aware generative AI platform that helps public-sector professionals interpret and apply the Dutch Environment and Planning Act. Users select a location and ask questions in natural language. The platform combines official DSO data, applicable legislation and organisation-specific sources to generate clear, traceable answers with verifiable references. Developed in partnership with Dutch public authorities and already used by ten clients across municipalities and provinces, it supports legal research, public service delivery, policy development and environmental planning. Human professionals remain responsible for interpretation and decisions. Its modular architecture, evaluation tools and responsible-AI safeguards make OmgevingsChat scalable and reusable across municipalities, provinces, water authorities and regional environmental agencies.

organization: Instituto para o Ensino Superior, I.P.
title: Auto Send Mails - PRR: An Integrated Low-Code Solution for Automating Public Administration Communications
source_description: Auto Send Mails - PRR is an internally developed low-code solution that transformed how official communications are managed across Portugal's Recovery and Resilience Plan (PRR). It replaced a fragmented and highly manual process (involving dispersed contact lists, individual email preparation and repetitive attachment handling) with a single, standardised and automated workflow. Built entirely with existing organisational resources, it integrates SharePoint, Excel, Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI and Microsoft Teams, without additional procurement, external development or software costs. The solution currently supports 7 PRR programmes and 99 projects, centralising contact management and enabling controlled recipient selection, content preparation and automated sending. For a communication to 33 projects, the end-to-end process was reduced from approximately 5 hours to 5 minutes (a time reduction of over 98%) while reducing manual errors, ensuring consistent institutional communication standards and freeing technical staff for higher-value tasks.

title: Regional e-portfolio of certified skills using blockchain technology
source_description: The use of Open Badges to track the acquisition of micro-credentials, both formal and informal, is becoming increasingly widespread. However, skills are often described without the use of specific and shared vocabularies, and without the possibility of assessing the duration of courses or the presence of final tests. This makes it difficult to certify the skills acquired and to evaluate them for the certification of specific professional profiles. The Marche Region has created a single regional e-portfolio, Marche Digital Open Badge, designed to build a digital learning portfolio for citizens of the Marche region, enabling them to certify their skills and share the related attestations in verifiable and standard formats. The system is made available to all organisations carrying out training activities in the regional territory, including schools, universities, companies, voluntary associations and local training providers. This allows each citizen-user to have a comprehensive overview of the training-related skills acquired throughout their lifetime.
